children.description:
Ze derives the EWMA smoothing factor from this window: alpha is
2 divided by the window plus 1. The default 300 gives an alpha
of 0.0066. A longer window makes the baseline slower and a short
burst more visible. Ze folds a tick into the baseline only when
the entity is not anomalous on that tick. A long anomaly cannot
drift the baseline up to meet it.
children.name: baseline-window
children.short-help: Per-entity baseline horizon in ticks (the EWMA smoothing factor is derived from it).

children.description:
One tick is one second. An active incident clears after this
many ticks in a row below the threshold, and one tick above it
resets the count to 0. The default 10 holds the incident for 10
seconds after the traffic stops.
children.name: clear-consecutive
children.short-help: Consecutive below-threshold ticks before an active incident clears.

children.description:
Ze masks the IPv4 address of the entity to this length and uses
the result as the cohort key. Ze compares each entity against
the other members of its cohort, which is how it scores rarity.
A shorter length makes a larger cohort. min-cohort-size sets the
smallest cohort Ze scores rarity in.
children.name: cohort-prefix-len-v4
children.short-help: Source-prefix length that buckets IPv4 entities into peer-group cohorts.

children.description:
Ze masks the IPv6 address of the entity to this length and uses
the result as the cohort key. The default 48 groups a site
together. Where the mask does not apply to the address, Ze
falls back to the whole address. That entity then forms a cohort
of one, and Ze scores it on its own baseline alone.
children.name: cohort-prefix-len-v6
children.short-help: Source-prefix length that buckets IPv6 entities into peer-group cohorts.

children.description:
One tick is one second. Ze needs this many ticks in a row above
the threshold, and one tick below it resets the count to 0. The
default 3 delays an incident by 3 seconds and it drops a
one-tick spike.
children.name: confirm-duration
children.short-help: Consecutive above-threshold ticks before an incident is confirmed and emitted.

children.description:
Discount applied to corroborating features when combining scores. The discount stops correlated
features from counting twice.
children.name: corroboration-weight
children.short-help: Discount applied to a corroborating feature when Ze combines scores.

children.description:
A feature fires when its z-score reaches this value. That score
is the larger of two numbers. The first is the deviation from
the entity own baseline. The second is the rarity of the value
in the cohort of the entity. A lower value fires more features
and raises the number of false incidents. The value also grades
the severity Ze puts on an incident.
children.name: deviation-threshold
children.short-help: Sigma at or above which a per-entity feature deviation fires.

children.description:
The default false leaves the detector idle: it starts no ticker
and it holds no baseline. Set it true and Ze attaches to the
traffic-feature service and starts the one-second ticker. An
entity needs 3 ticks of samples before Ze scores its deviation
from its own baseline.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the behavioral anomaly detector (report-only; emits incidents, takes no action).

children.description:
Minimum cohort members before peer-group rarity is scored. A cohort is a source-prefix bucket. A
smaller cohort uses self-deviation only.
children.name: min-cohort-size
children.short-help: Minimum members in a cohort before Ze scores peer-group rarity.

children.description:
Minimum distinct features that must fire on one entity and one window before Ze scores an incident.
The minimum correlates weak signals, so one feature alone raises no incident.
children.name: min-features-to-correlate
children.short-help: Minimum distinct features that must fire before Ze scores an incident.

children.description:
The detector reads one traffic-feature snapshot every second, and
one second is one tick. It holds a baseline for each entity on
three axes: the source address, the destination address, and the
port. It publishes an incident on the event bus, and it writes no
firewall rule. The shape subtree is what acts on an incident.
children.name: detect
children.short-help: Report-only behavioral anomaly detector (emits incidents, takes no action).

children.description: When the ring is full, the oldest finalized incident is dropped first.
children.name: incident-ring-size
children.short-help: Maximum number of incidents the ring keeps in memory.

children.description:
The detector stops reporting an entity that goes idle, and it sends no clear event for that entity.
This timeout is the limit on how long such an incident reads as active.
children.name: stale-incident-timeout
children.short-help: Seconds before an open incident with no clear event is finalized.

children.description:
The store keeps each confirmed incident from its start to its end. `show anomaly observe` reads the
store, so it can report the duration of a finished incident.
children.name: observe
children.short-help: Incident lifecycle store for confirmed anomaly incidents.

children.description:
limit writes an nftables counter and a rate limit on the source
prefix, and it reads limit-rate, limit-unit and limit-burst.
drop writes a counter and discards every packet from that
source. Ze applies the action to each armed source, and it
applies nothing while mode is shadow.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Armed action: rate-limit the source (surgical) or drop it (fallback).

values.name: drop
values.short-help: Discard every packet from the source prefix.

values.name: limit
values.short-help: Rate-limit the source prefix at limit-rate per limit-unit.

children.description:
The list guards against self-lockout, for management sources
and control-plane sources.
children.name: allowlist
children.short-help: Protected source prefixes that ze never arms an action against.

children.description:
This ceiling holds whether or not a clear event arrives, so an
armed action can never stay in place indefinitely.
children.name: auto-revert-ttl
children.short-help: Seconds after the last signal before an armed action reverts by itself.

children.description:
Ze counts the sources that carry a live action. At this cap Ze
refuses to arm one more source, writes a warning, and raises the
arm-refused metric. A source that is armed already costs the
count nothing, because that path only refreshes its
auto-revert-ttl. The cap bounds the firewall table an incident
storm can produce.
children.name: blast-radius-cap
children.short-help: Maximum concurrently-armed live actions; further arm attempts are refused.

children.description:
Ze runs the revert when it reads the config, so it also removes
what an earlier instance of the responder left in the firewall.
The responder then answers every incident as shadow does, and it
writes a log line in place of a rule. Set the leaf back to false
to let the responder arm again.
children.name: kill-switch
children.short-help: When true, revert every armed action and force the responder to shadow.

children.description:
The burst is the number of packets Ze lets through above the
rate before it starts to drop. The default 0 gives no
allowance, so the rate applies from the first packet. Ze gives
the value to the nftables limit expression. The leaf changes
nothing while the action is drop.
children.name: limit-burst
children.short-help: Burst allowance for the limit action.

children.description:
The rate counts packets, and limit-unit gives the time. The
default 1000, with the default unit second, lets 1000 packets a
second through from each armed source. A value of 0 is refused
at commit while the action is limit. The leaf changes nothing
while the action is drop.
children.name: limit-rate
children.short-help: Rate for the limit action, in packets per limit-unit.

children.description:
The unit divides limit-rate. A rate of 1000 with the unit minute
lets 1000 packets a minute through. Ze gives the word to the
nftables limit expression, and a word outside the four is
refused at commit. The leaf changes nothing while the action is
drop.
children.name: limit-unit
children.short-help: Time unit for limit-rate.

values.name: day
values.short-help: Allow limit-rate packets each day.

values.name: hour
values.short-help: Allow limit-rate packets each hour.

values.name: minute
values.short-help: Allow limit-rate packets each minute.

values.name: second
values.short-help: Allow limit-rate packets each second.

children.description:
shadow, the default, logs the action it would take and installs
nothing. armed installs live per-source firewall actions.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Responder mode: shadow or armed.

values.name: armed
values.short-help: Install live per-source firewall actions.

values.name: shadow
values.short-help: Log the action the responder would take and install nothing.

children.description:
The responder reads the incidents the detect subtree publishes,
and it acts on a source incident alone. In armed mode it writes an
nftables table named ze_anomaly-shape, with one term for each
armed source. The chain of that table attaches to the input hook
at priority -200, so it acts on the traffic addressed to this
host.
children.name: shape
children.short-help: Autonomous responder: shadow (log-only) or armed (live per-source firewall actions).

anomaly.description:
Two plugins fill this container. anomaly-detect owns the detect
subtree and reports incidents on the event bus. anomaly-shape adds
the shape subtree and acts on those incidents. Remove a plugin and
its subtree disappears from the config.
anomaly.name: anomaly
anomaly.short-help: Behavioral anomaly detection and response subsystem.

children.description:
When this leaf is true, the BFD plugin also binds an IPv6 socket (::0) alongside the IPv4 socket for
every (vrf, mode) loop. The paired sockets share the same RX channel through a transport.Dual
wrapper, and send routes by destination address family. Stage 2b (spec-bfd-2b-ipv6-transport) ships
this leaf. A pinned IPv6 session requires the leaf to be set explicitly, so an operator who does not
need IPv6 does not open a second socket per loop.
children.name: bind-v6
children.short-help: Bind an IPv6 socket beside the IPv4 socket on every loop.

children.description:
The default is true. false stops Ze from starting the sessions pinned in this bfd
container. A reload to false stops the pinned sessions already running. It does not stop
the BFD service. Ze publishes that service whatever this leaf holds, so a BGP peer that
carries a bfd container still gets a BFD session. To stop the session of a peer, remove
the bfd container from that peer or set its enabled leaf to false.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Master switch for the BFD plugin.

children.description:
Ze refuses an entry that omits this leaf. The address is the source of every
Control packet Ze sends, and it is part of the session key. RFC 5883 Section 4.1
states that two sessions between the same pair of systems must differ in at least
one endpoint address. The reason is that the first packet carries a Your
Discriminator of 0.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Local source address. Required for multi-hop.

children.description:
Ze discards a Control packet whose TTL is less than this value, and the test is
inclusive, so a TTL equal to it passes. A peer sends with a TTL of 255, so 254 allows
one router between the peer and Ze. Raise the value toward 255 when the peer is
fewer hops away, because a higher floor rejects a packet sent from further away.
children.name: min-ttl
children.short-help:
Minimum acceptable TTL on receive. Weak replacement
for GTSM on multi-hop paths.

children.description:
The value is the first word after the list name, so multi-hop-session
203.0.113.9 names this peer. Ze refuses an address it cannot parse, and IPv4 and
IPv6 are both accepted. The peer, the local address and the VRF together identify
the session.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: Address of the remote system this session runs to.

children.description:
Ze refuses a name that no profile declares, and it refuses a profile that
enables echo. Without this leaf the session takes the engine values: a detect
multiplier of 3, and 1000000 microseconds for both the transmit target and the
receive floor.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: Name of the timer profile this session takes its intervals from.

children.description:
The session stays configured and stops sending control packets, so a
peer sees it go down. Delete the list entry to remove it instead.
children.name: shutdown
children.short-help: Hold the session administratively down and keep its configuration.

children.description:
A name other than default binds the socket to the VRF device of that name. Ze
runs one socket for each pair of VRF and hop mode, so every multi-hop session in one
VRF shares it. An empty value is read as default.
children.name: vrf
children.short-help: Routing instance the session runs in. The default instance is named default.

children.description:
The 255-TTL test of a single-hop session cannot work over several hops. The
min-ttl leaf is the cheap protection here, and authentication is the strong one. Ze
refuses an entry whose profile enables echo. RFC 5883 Section 3 states that the Echo
function MUST NOT be used over multiple hops. The local leaf is required here, and it
is optional on a single-hop session.
children.name: multi-hop-session
children.short-help: Multi-hop BFD session (RFC 5883). Port 4784, no GTSM.

children.description:
DEPRECATED, retained for back-compat and scheduled for removal. The value is no longer interpreted
as a directory. TX sequence numbers for Meticulous Keyed authentication now persist to the shared
managed state store (database.zefs), instead of a loose file. A non-empty value still opts a session
into persistence. RFC 5880 Section 6.7.3 requires the sequence to survive process restarts. Without
this leaf set, Meticulous sessions still work at runtime, but a fresh process loses its sequence
floor until the peer's replay window slides forward.
children.name: persist-dir
children.short-help: DEPRECATED. A non-empty value opts a session into sequence persistence.

children.description:
Ze writes the value into the authentication section of every Control packet
it sends. Ze discards a received packet that carries another value, which RFC 5880
Section 6.7.2 requires for Simple Password. Both ends must name the same key-id
and the same secret. The range is 0 to 255.
children.name: key-id
children.short-help: Auth Key ID (RFC 5880 Section 6.7.1).

children.description:
Shared secret. Redacted from `ze config show` output. MD5 variants use the first 16 bytes of the
secret, SHA1 variants the first 20, and both pad a shorter secret with zeros. The simple-password
type carries the secret itself on the wire, so it must be 1 to 16 bytes, and a longer one is refused
at parse time (RFC 5880 Section 6.7.2).
children.name: secret
children.short-help: Shared secret, redacted from `ze config show` output.

children.description:
Authentication type. There is no default. The operator names the type, and simple-password is never
selected on their behalf. simple-password is RFC 5880 Section 6.7.2 Simple Password. The password
travels in clear in every Control packet and the section never changes, so it protects against a
misconfigured peer and against nothing else. It does not protect against a listener on the path, who
reads the password from one packet, and it carries no Sequence Number, so a captured packet can be
replayed. Choose a keyed type wherever the path is not already trusted.
children.name: type
children.short-help: Authentication type, which the operator must name.

values.name: keyed-md5
values.short-help: RFC 5880 Section 6.7.3 Keyed MD5.

values.name: keyed-sha1
values.short-help: RFC 5880 Section 6.7.4 Keyed SHA1.

values.name: meticulous-keyed-md5
values.short-help: RFC 5880 Section 6.7.3 Meticulous Keyed MD5 (strict sequence increase).

values.name: meticulous-keyed-sha1
values.short-help: RFC 5880 Section 6.7.4 Meticulous Keyed SHA1 (strict sequence increase).

values.name: simple-password
values.short-help: RFC 5880 Section 6.7.2 Simple Password, sent in clear in every Control packet.

children.description:
RFC 5880 Section 6.7 authentication parameters. Sessions inheriting this profile sign every outgoing
Control packet with the configured type, and verify incoming packets with the same key. There is no
default type, and authentication runs only on the type the operator names here.
children.name: auth
children.short-help: Authentication parameters (RFC 5880 Section 6.7).

children.description:
Local target transmit rate in microseconds. The slow-start floor of 1 000 000 us applies while the
session is not Up, per RFC 5880 Section 6.8.3.
children.name: desired-min-tx-us
children.short-help: Local target transmit rate in microseconds.

children.description: Number of consecutive missed Control packets that trigger a Down transition. RFC 5880 Section 6.8.4.
children.name: detect-multiplier
children.short-help: Consecutive missed Control packets that trigger a Down transition.

children.description:
Local target echo transmit rate in microseconds. The effective echo rate is max(local desired, peer
RequiredMinEchoRx).
children.name: desired-min-echo-tx-us
children.short-help: Local target echo transmit rate in microseconds.

children.description:
RFC 5880 Section 6.4 / RFC 5881 Section 5 Echo mode. Echo mode is single-hop only, because RFC 5883
Section 4 explicitly prohibits multi-hop echo, and the parser rejects echo on a multi-hop session.
When echo is active, the engine sends echo packets on UDP port 3785 at the peer's advertised
RequiredMinEchoRxInterval. The engine then slows its async Control TX to the peer's
RequiredMinRxInterval.
children.name: echo
children.short-help: BFD Echo mode (RFC 5880 Section 6.4, RFC 5881 Section 5).

children.description:
Active, which is the default, transmits from session creation. Passive transmits nothing until a
Control packet arrives from the peer. RFC 5883 Section 4.3.
children.name: passive
children.short-help: Wait for a peer Control packet before this session transmits.

children.description:
Ze advertises the value as Required Min RX Interval, and a peer that obeys it
does not transmit faster. The detection time is the peer's Detect Multiplier times
the larger of this value and the peer's Desired Min TX Interval. While echo mode
runs, Ze raises the advertised value to 1000000 microseconds and starts a Poll
sequence, because the echo packets already prove the path.
children.name: required-min-rx-us
children.short-help:
Minimum inter-packet gap the local end can handle,
in microseconds.

children.description:
Reusable timer and feature profile. Sessions reference a profile by name and inherit every field
below.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: Reusable timer and feature profile.

children.description:
Ze binds the socket of the loop to this interface with SO_BINDTODEVICE. One
socket serves every session of one VRF and hop mode. Ze binds it only when each
session in the default VRF names the same interface. A mix of names leaves the
socket unbound, with a warning in the log. In a VRF other than default the VRF
device wins, and this leaf is dropped.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Egress interface name.

children.description:
While the leaf is absent, the kernel selects the source address. The address
is part of the session key. A change to it therefore releases the running session,
and creates a new one at the next config load.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Local source address (optional).

children.description:
The value is the first word after the list name, so single-hop-session
203.0.113.9 names this peer. Ze refuses an address it cannot parse, and IPv4 and IPv6
are both accepted. RFC 5881 Section 5 requires a received TTL of 255, so Ze discards
a Control packet from this peer that crossed a router.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: Peer IPv4 or IPv6 address.

children.description:
Ze refuses a name that no profile declares. Without this leaf the session takes
the engine values: a detect multiplier of 3, and 1000000 microseconds for both the
transmit target and the receive floor.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: Named profile to inherit timer parameters from.

children.description:
The session keeps its configuration and its place in the list, and Ze holds it
in AdminDown. Ze applies the value again at each reload, so a change from true to
false brings the session back with no restart. Delete the list entry to remove the
session instead.
children.name: shutdown
children.short-help:
When true, the session stays in AdminDown state.
RFC 5880 Section 6.8.16.

children.description:
A name other than default binds the socket to the VRF device of that name. The
interface leaf of every session in that VRF is then dropped, and Ze logs the names it
dropped once for each loop. An empty value is read as default.
children.name: vrf
children.short-help: Routing instance the session runs in. The default instance is named default.

children.description:
Per-link BFD session (RFC 5881). Port 3784, TTL=255. A protocol client MUST NOT use this list. A
protocol client calls the plugin Service interface at runtime.
children.name: single-hop-session
children.short-help: Per-link BFD session on port 3784 with TTL 255 (RFC 5881).

bfd.description:
The container holds the plugin switch, the reusable profiles, and the sessions an
operator pins. A session that BGP or a static route asks for at runtime does not appear
here. A protocol client reaches the plugin through its Service interface instead.
bfd.name: bfd

children.description:
RFC 5396 Section 2 names the three notations. Take AS 65546 and AS 100. asplain
writes them 65546 and 100. asdot writes 1.10 and 100, leaving an AS number less than 65536
alone, and asdot+ writes 1.10 and 0.100. The leaf changes the text Ze WRITES, and the
wire value stays the same 4-octet number (RFC 6793). Ze READS all three notations wherever
an AS number is configured, and asplain is the default RFC 5396 Section 3 recommends.
children.name: as-notation
children.short-help: How Ze writes an AS number in the output an operator reads.

values.name: asdot
values.short-help: An AS number of 65536 or more is X.Y, and a lower one is a decimal integer

values.name: asdot+
values.short-help: Every AS number is X.Y

values.name: asplain
values.short-help: Every AS number is a decimal integer

children.description:
Discard traffic sent toward a prefix this peer announces
carrying one of these communities. Ze installs that prefix as
a discard route directly. There is no next-hop to allocate and
no static route to pre-create.

Write ASN:VAL, for example 65001:666, or a well-known name.
blackhole and 65535:666 are one value, the one RFC 7999
registers. Section 4 suggests that keyword. An operator's own
community is the common case, which is why this is a list.

A listed community IS the agreement RFC 7999 Section 3.3
requires the receiving party to make 'on that particular BGP
session'.

An empty list beside a set prefixes list means the well-known
value alone. Stating the prefixes a peer CAN blackhole within
IS the explicit configuration directive Section 4 asks for.
The same act is Section 3.3's agreement on that session, so
standard RTBH takes one line. Section 4's default holds: a
container with neither list discards nothing, and so does a
peer with no container.

A STATED list is taken exactly. The well-known value is NOT
added to it. An operator who names 65001:666 and not 65535:666
means it, and Section 3.1 makes that their choice.

The parser applies that default, not a YANG default statement.
The default is conditional on a SIBLING leaf, which a leaf-list
default cannot express. A value materialised into the schema
would also make every peer read as having agreed to 65535:666
on the send side.

One community is not enough on its own. RFC 7999 Section 3.3
states two conditions, and the prefixes list is the other. A
peer with a community and no covering prefix blackholes
nothing.

The list governs the SEND side too. RFC 7999 Section 3.1
requires the two networks to agree on use of the BLACKHOLE
community before a speaker advertises it. Naming it here is
this speaker's half. `send bgp <selector> blackhole` reaches only the
sessions that hold 65535:666, under either spelling. A session
that named its own value alone is left out of the
announcement, and is not sent the prefix untagged.
children.name: communities
children.short-help: Communities that make Ze discard traffic toward a prefix this peer announces.

children.description:
The prefixes this PEER is authorized to advertise. Ze honors a
received blackhole announcement only when one of them covers
it and is equal or shorter. That is RFC 7999 Section 3.3's
first condition, in the RFC's own words. The announced prefix
is 'covered by an equal or shorter IP prefix that the
neighboring network is authorized to advertise'.

The container already says blackhole, so the leaf does not
repeat it.

Coverage is not prefix-list membership. A list entry
192.0.2.0/24 authorizes a 192.0.2.1/32 blackhole inside it,
because the /24 is a shorter covering prefix the neighbor may
advertise. That is the RFC test, and it does not depend on any
ge or le bound.

An empty list authorizes nothing, so honoring never happens.
That is the closed state on purpose: RFC 7999 Section 6 names
unauthorized addition of BLACKHOLE as a denial-of-reachability
vector, and an open default would let any peer discard traffic
for any prefix it names.
children.name: prefixes
children.short-help: The prefixes this peer is authorized to advertise.

children.description:
The RFC 7999 agreement on this BGP session, in both directions.
It states what this speaker does with a received route carrying
the BLACKHOLE community, 65535:666. It also states whether this
speaker CAN advertise that community to this peer. Section 4 uses
the suggested shorthand keyword for the value.

A later revision adds an as-sets leaf-list here. It answers a
DIFFERENT question from session/irr/as-set. That one states what
the peer CAN advertise at all. This one would state what the peer
CAN blackhole within. Whether one deployment puts the same set in
both is the operator's business, not this model's.
children.name: blackhole
children.short-help: RFC 7999 blackhole agreement on this BGP session, in both directions.

children.description:
The leaf is mandatory, because a collector with no address has nothing to dial.
The address is part of the session identity. A reload that changes it ends the session
with a Termination message, then opens a new one.
children.name: address
children.short-help: Collector IP address

children.description:
11019 is also the default port of the BMP receiver of Ze, under environment bmp
server. Two Ze boxes therefore connect with no port written on either side. The port is
part of the session identity, so a reload that changes it opens a new session.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Collector TCP port

children.description:
Ze binds the address on the outbound connection. When the leaf is absent, the kernel
picks the source address of the route to the collector. The address is part of the
session identity, so a reload that changes it opens a new session.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IP address for outbound BMP connections

children.description:
Ze dials each collector from its own session. Ze retries a failed connection after 30
seconds, then doubles the wait to a limit of 720 seconds. A collector whose address, port
and source-address a reload does not change keeps its session, and keeps everything the
collector learned on it.
children.name: collector
children.short-help: BMP collector endpoints to connect to

children.description:
Ze streams each best-path change of the local RIB to the collectors as a Route Monitoring message.
The message carries a Loc-RIB peer header, which RFC 9069 gives PeerType 3.
children.name: loc-rib
children.short-help: Enable Loc-RIB monitoring (RFC 9069).

children.description:
Ze mirrors every OPEN, UPDATE, NOTIFICATION, KEEPALIVE and ROUTE-REFRESH message it
processes, in a TLV of type 0. The stream carries every message of every peer, so the
default is false. A change to the leaf bounces every monitored peer with a Peer Down and a
Peer Up, which RFC 8671 Section 7.2 requires.
children.name: route-mirroring
children.short-help: Enable Route Mirroring (RFC 7854 S4.7): stream verbatim copies of all BGP messages to collectors

children.description:
pre-policy streams the UPDATE messages Ze received, post-policy streams the UPDATE
messages Ze sent, and all streams both. A change to the leaf bounces every monitored peer
with a Peer Down and a Peer Up, which RFC 8671 Section 7.2 requires. The BMP session itself
stays up.
children.name: route-monitoring-policy
children.short-help: Which routes to stream: pre-policy (Adj-RIB-In), post-policy (Adj-RIB-Out, RFC 8671), or all

values.name: all
values.short-help: Stream both the received and the sent UPDATE messages.

values.name: post-policy
values.short-help: Stream the UPDATE messages Ze sent, the Adj-RIB-Out (RFC 8671).

values.name: pre-policy
values.short-help: Stream the UPDATE messages Ze received, the Adj-RIB-In.

children.description:
The unit is seconds and the range is 0 to 65535. The default is 0, and Ze sends no
Statistics Report (RFC 7854 Section 4.8) at any value. The periodic timer this leaf
configures is not implemented, so the leaf changes what the sender configuration carries and
nothing on the wire. A change to the leaf still bounces every session of the sender with a
Peer Down and Peer Up sequence. Ze does this because it compares the whole declared
sender behavior.
children.name: statistics-timeout
children.short-help: Interval for periodic statistics reports (0 = disabled)

children.description:
The container carries presence, so Ze starts the sender when you write it and stops every
collector session when you delete it. Ze sends an Initiation message first on each connection,
which RFC 7854 Section 4.3 requires.
children.name: sender
children.short-help: Stream BMP data to external collectors

children.description:
The container holds the sender. The BMP receiver of Ze listens under environment bmp, so a box
that only receives BMP writes nothing here.
children.name: bmp
children.short-help: BMP sender and protocol options

children.description:
An extended community is eight octets, and its type
decides how Ze reads the value (RFC 4360).
children.name: value
children.short-help: Extended community values.

children.description:
Each entry holds one or more extended community values under one name.
An ingress or egress tag or strip list names the entry
in place of the values. Ze refuses a set that holds no
value. It refuses a name a second entry of the
standard, large or extended list already holds. It
refuses a tag or a strip list that names a set no
entry declares.
children.name: extended
children.short-help: Named sets of extended communities a tag or a strip list names.

children.description:
A large community is three 32-bit numbers, written
GA:LD1:LD2 (RFC 8092).
children.name: value
children.short-help: Large community values, in GA:LD1:LD2 format.

children.description:
Each entry holds one or more GA:LD1:LD2 triples under one name.
An ingress or egress tag or strip list names the entry
in place of the values. Ze refuses a set that holds no
value. It refuses a name a second entry of the
standard, large or extended list already holds. It
refuses a tag or a strip list that names a set no
entry declares.
children.name: large
children.short-help: Named sets of large communities a tag or a strip list names.

children.description:
A standard community is two 16-bit numbers, written
ASN:value (RFC 1997).
children.name: value
children.short-help: Standard community values, in ASN:value format.

children.description:
Each entry holds one or more ASN:value pairs under one name.
An ingress or egress tag or strip list names the entry
in place of the values. Ze refuses a set that holds no
value. It refuses a name a second entry of the
standard, large or extended list already holds. It
refuses a tag or a strip list that names a set no
entry declares.
children.name: standard
children.short-help: Named sets of standard communities a tag or a strip list names.

children.description:
A filter rule names a set from this container rather than
repeating the community values. The three lists hold standard,
large and extended communities.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Named community definitions referenced by filter rules.

children.description:
RFC 4271 Section 9.1.1 supplies no number: "The exact nature of this policy information,
and the computation involved, is a local matter." 100 is the value FRR
(BGP_DEFAULT_LOCAL_PREF) and BIRD (default_local_pref) use, and it is the default here for
that reason alone. The leaf governs the modifier arithmetic. It does NOT supply the LOCAL_PREF
an eBGP-learned route carries into iBGP readvertisement, which ze does not do.
children.name: local-preference
children.short-help: The LOCAL_PREF value policy arithmetic starts from when the route carries none.

children.description:
RFC 4271 Section 9.1.2.2 supplies this number: "Routes that do not have the
MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute are considered to have the lowest possible MULTI_EXIT_DISC value."
A larger value makes an increment write a larger metric onto a route that arrived without one,
and the speaker that receives it reads a larger metric as a worse path. The Decision Process
comparison stays at 0 whatever this leaf holds.
children.name: med
children.short-help: The MULTI_EXIT_DISC value policy arithmetic starts from when the route carries none.

children.description:
The leaves govern the arithmetic in bgp { policy { modify NAME { increment } } } and its
decrement sibling alone. They do NOT move the Decision Process: RFC 4271 Section 9.1.2.2 compares
an absent MULTI_EXIT_DISC as 0 whatever med says here.

There is deliberately no aigp leaf. RFC 7311 Section 4.1 removes a route with no AIGP TLV from
consideration rather than scoring it, so no number stands in for the absence. Section 3.4.1
forbids ze to add the attribute to a route whose path leads outside the AIGP administrative
domain.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: The value policy arithmetic starts from when the route carries no such attribute.

children.description:
The container holds attribute alone today. A default that is not an attribute value gets its own
container beside it, so an operator's existing leaves never move.
children.name: defaults
children.short-help: Values ze supplies when a route carries no such attribute.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze removes every community of that set from the route.
children.name: strip
children.short-help: Named communities to remove on egress.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze adds every community of that set to the route.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: Named communities to add on egress.

children.description: The container holds the tag list and the strip list.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Community filter for egress.

children.description:
The container holds the filters Ze runs over a route it sends to
this peer.
children.name: egress
children.short-help: Egress direction filters.

children.description:
Ze runs the global chain first, then the group chain, then the peer chain. An RFC 9234
role can require this chain to name a filter that catches a transit leak.
children.name: export
children.short-help: Global export filter chain

children.description:
Ze runs the global chain first, then the group chain, then the peer chain. Each name
references a filter instance declared under bgp/policy. A plain name that no instance declares
is refused at config load.
children.name: import
children.short-help: Global import filter chain

children.description:
The community stops the prefix propagating outside the local
AS, which RFC 7999 Section 3.2 asks for. The choice between
the two values is the operator routing policy, so neither is
forced. This leaf adds the community. It does not discard
traffic.
children.name: blackhole-propagation
children.short-help: Community to add to a route that carries BLACKHOLE (65535:666).

values.name: no-advertise
values.short-help: Add NO_ADVERTISE (65535:65282).

values.name: no-export
values.short-help: Add NO_EXPORT (65535:65281).

values.name: none
values.short-help: Add nothing. RFC 7999 Section 3.1 makes ignoring the community conformant.

children.description:
RFC 8195 Section 3.2 leaves this number to each AS and gives
3 as its example. The number is a local convention, not a
protocol constant. Change it here when the AS already uses 3
for something else.
children.name: relation-function
children.short-help: Function number of the relation tag.

children.description:
RFC 8195 Section 3.2 defines the community. The Global
Administrator is the session local AS. The parameter comes
from what the peer IS to us: 2 for a customer, 3 for a
peer, 4 for a provider. A route-server session and a
route-server-client session write nothing, because RFC 7947
requires transparency there. An iBGP session writes nothing.
Its sender is inside the local AS and has no such
relation.
children.name: relation-tag
children.short-help: Write the relation-to-origin large community of RFC 8195 on each route from this peer.

children.description:
The list is RFC 7454 Section 11's exception for what
customers and peers use to signal. An empty list keeps

nothing. The relation-tag function number is never kept,
whatever this list says: a kept relation function would let
a peer state its own relation to this AS.
children.name: scrub-keep-function
children.short-help: Function numbers a peer can send with the local AS as the Global Administrator.

children.description:
Only the function numbers listed in scrub-keep-function
survive. RFC 7454 Section 11 asks for the scrub. It covers
standard and large communities. It runs on eBGP sessions
only. On an iBGP session an own-AS value is this network's
own signal to itself. Well-known communities are never
reached, so NO_EXPORT, NO_ADVERTISE and BLACKHOLE always
survive.
children.name: scrub-own-ga
children.short-help: Remove inbound communities whose Global Administrator is the local AS.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze removes every community of that set from the route.
children.name: strip
children.short-help: Named communities to remove on ingress.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze adds every community of that set to the route.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: Named communities to add on ingress.

children.description:
The container holds the tag list, the strip list, and the
RFC 8195, RFC 7454 and RFC 7999 leaves.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Community filter for ingress.

children.description:
The container holds the filters Ze runs over a route it receives
from this peer.
children.name: ingress
children.short-help: Ingress direction filters.

children.description:
The group level and the peer level append to this base chain. A name references a filter instance
defined in bgp/policy.
children.name: filter
children.short-help: Global route filter chains for import and export.

children.description:
The BGP reactor reads no value from the leaf. It takes encoding and format off the content container and
nothing else, so an event carries every attribute of the route whatever the leaf holds.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: Filter expression to select which BGP attributes are included in events.

children.description:
Ze resolves the value in three steps: this leaf first, then the default encoder the program registered,
then text. Ze lowercases the value before it passes the value to the program binding.
children.name: encoding
children.short-help: Wire encoding for events sent to the process (e.g., json, text).

children.description:
Ze uses parsed when the leaf is absent. Ze lowercases the value before it passes the value to the program
binding.
children.name: format
children.short-help: Output format template for event rendering.

children.description:
Ze reads encoding and format from the container. A binding that names neither takes
the encoder the program registered, and the parsed format.
children.name: content
children.short-help: Controls the encoding and filtering of events sent to this process.

children.description: The events are up, down, and reset. The process can therefore react to a peer lifecycle transition.
children.name: neighbor-changes
children.short-help: Send session state change events to this process.

children.description:
The config migration rewrites the leaf. Ze creates one attach process entry per name
in the list, and it deletes the block that carried the leaf. The BGP reactor reads no value
from the leaf.
children.name: processes
children.short-help: Legacy ExaBGP process reference list. Use 'receive' and 'send' instead.

children.description:
The config migration treats each pattern as a process name, and it creates one attach
process entry per pattern. Ze matches nothing against the pattern. The BGP reactor reads no
value from the leaf.
children.name: processes-match
children.short-help: Legacy ExaBGP process match patterns for event filtering.

children.description:
The base types are update, open, notification, keepalive, refresh, state, and negotiated. A plugin
registers more, for example update-rpki. A type carries the direction it is fed in: 'update' means
both directions, and 'update-received' and 'update-sent' each mean one direction. A registered type
keeps its whole name, so a plugin type that ends in -sent is never read as a direction. '*' feeds
every type, in both directions. 'all' is not accepted, because a word that reads like a type would
grant a type that a plugin registers later, which '*' says on purpose. Ze validates the list at
runtime against the registered event types.
children.name: receive
children.short-help: Event types this peer feeds the program.

children.description: Ze pipes the BGP events to the stdin of the process, and reads the commands from its stdout.
children.name: run
children.short-help: Shell command that starts the external process.

children.description:
The valid types are update, refresh, raw, and enhanced-refresh. raw is a whole BGP message that the
program builds itself. enhanced-refresh carries the BORR and EORR markers of RFC 7313. '*' names
every type. A direction has no meaning here, because every send type is sent. Ze validates the list
at runtime against the known send types.
children.name: send
children.short-help: Message types this program can send toward the peer.

children.description: Ze starts the process, and communicates with it over stdin and stdout, in JSON.
children.name: process
children.short-help: External process that receives BGP events and can inject a message.

children.description:
Each attachment names one program declared under plugin/external. It states what that program
receives from this peer, and what the program can send to the peer. Write one statement per program:
`attach process <name> { ... }`.
children.name: attach
children.short-help: Programs this peer attaches.

children.description:
When the leaf is disabled, a route stays until it is withdrawn explicitly, or until the hold timer
expires. This is a legacy ExaBGP option, kept for migration.
children.name: auto-flush
children.short-help: Withdraw every route advertised to this peer when the session goes down.

children.description:
Packing reduces the number of UPDATE messages from O(routes) to O(unique-attribute-sets). Disable it
for a peer that requires one prefix per UPDATE.
children.name: group-updates
children.short-help: Pack several NLRI into one UPDATE message when they share the same path attributes.

children.description:
When the leaf is enabled, End-of-RIB must be triggered from outside, through the process API. Use
the leaf when an external controller manages the convergence signaling.
children.name: manual-eor
children.short-help: Do not send End-of-RIB automatically after the initial route advertisement.

children.description:
Forward received UPDATEs directly inside the reactor for RS-client peers, and bypass the plugin
dispatch chain. This path gives lower latency for route server forwarding. A peer with an export
filter is excluded and uses the normal path.
children.name: rs-fast-path
children.short-help: Forward a received UPDATE inside the reactor for an RS-client peer.

children.description: Most operators can keep the defaults.
children.name: behavior
children.short-help: Controls how the reactor processes and forwards an UPDATE for this peer.

children.description:
Discard traffic sent toward a prefix this peer announces
carrying one of these communities. Ze installs that prefix as
a discard route directly. There is no next-hop to allocate and
no static route to pre-create.

Write ASN:VAL, for example 65001:666, or a well-known name.
blackhole and 65535:666 are one value, the one RFC 7999
registers. Section 4 suggests that keyword. An operator's own
community is the common case, which is why this is a list.

A listed community IS the agreement RFC 7999 Section 3.3
requires the receiving party to make 'on that particular BGP
session'.

An empty list beside a set prefixes list means the well-known
value alone. Stating the prefixes a peer CAN blackhole within
IS the explicit configuration directive Section 4 asks for.
The same act is Section 3.3's agreement on that session, so
standard RTBH takes one line. Section 4's default holds: a
container with neither list discards nothing, and so does a
peer with no container.

A STATED list is taken exactly. The well-known value is NOT
added to it. An operator who names 65001:666 and not 65535:666
means it, and Section 3.1 makes that their choice.

The parser applies that default, not a YANG default statement.
The default is conditional on a SIBLING leaf, which a leaf-list
default cannot express. A value materialised into the schema
would also make every peer read as having agreed to 65535:666
on the send side.

One community is not enough on its own. RFC 7999 Section 3.3
states two conditions, and the prefixes list is the other. A
peer with a community and no covering prefix blackholes
nothing.

The list governs the SEND side too. RFC 7999 Section 3.1
requires the two networks to agree on use of the BLACKHOLE
community before a speaker advertises it. Naming it here is
this speaker's half. `send bgp <selector> blackhole` reaches only the
sessions that hold 65535:666, under either spelling. A session
that named its own value alone is left out of the
announcement, and is not sent the prefix untagged.
children.name: communities
children.short-help: Communities that make Ze discard traffic toward a prefix this peer announces.

children.description:
The prefixes this PEER is authorized to advertise. Ze honors a
received blackhole announcement only when one of them covers
it and is equal or shorter. That is RFC 7999 Section 3.3's
first condition, in the RFC's own words. The announced prefix
is 'covered by an equal or shorter IP prefix that the
neighboring network is authorized to advertise'.

The container already says blackhole, so the leaf does not
repeat it.

Coverage is not prefix-list membership. A list entry
192.0.2.0/24 authorizes a 192.0.2.1/32 blackhole inside it,
because the /24 is a shorter covering prefix the neighbor may
advertise. That is the RFC test, and it does not depend on any
ge or le bound.

An empty list authorizes nothing, so honoring never happens.
That is the closed state on purpose: RFC 7999 Section 6 names
unauthorized addition of BLACKHOLE as a denial-of-reachability
vector, and an open default would let any peer discard traffic
for any prefix it names.
children.name: prefixes
children.short-help: The prefixes this peer is authorized to advertise.

children.description:
The RFC 7999 agreement on this BGP session, in both directions.
It states what this speaker does with a received route carrying
the BLACKHOLE community, 65535:666. It also states whether this
speaker CAN advertise that community to this peer. Section 4 uses
the suggested shorthand keyword for the value.

A later revision adds an as-sets leaf-list here. It answers a
DIFFERENT question from session/irr/as-set. That one states what
the peer CAN advertise at all. This one would state what the peer
CAN blackhole within. Whether one deployment puts the same set in
both is the operator's business, not this model's.
children.name: blackhole
children.short-help: RFC 7999 blackhole agreement on this BGP session, in both directions.

children.description:
Ze creates the directory when it is absent. Ze writes one file per peer, named
bgp-<peer-address>.jsonl. Choose a filesystem with room for the configured maximum-size, and with
twice that room when on-limit is rotate. 'ze doctor' reports whether the directory is writable.
children.name: directory
children.short-help: Directory that holds the capture files of this peer.

children.description:
When the leaf is true, Ze refuses the config if the directory is empty, and it refuses the
config if maximum-size is zero. Both refusals happen at config load, before the peer starts.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Capture this peer's inbound protocol events to a file. Off by default.

children.description:
The writer refuses a record that would cross the cap, and it never writes part of a record, so a
file never exceeds this value. With on-limit rotate, a peer uses at most twice this value on disk.
With on-limit stop, a peer uses at most this value.
children.name: maximum-size
children.short-help: Hard cap on the size of one capture file.

children.description:
'rotate' renames the file to <file>.1, which replaces any earlier rotation, and starts a fresh file.
Capture continues, and the newest events are kept. 'stop' closes the file and captures nothing more,
so the oldest events are kept. Either value leaves the daemon unaffected, and the file ends with a
capture-stop record.
children.name: on-limit
children.short-help: What happens when a capture file reaches maximum-size.

values.name: rotate
values.short-help: Rename the full file to <file>.1 and start a fresh one, keeping the newest events.

values.name: stop
values.short-help: Close the full file and capture nothing more, keeping the oldest events.

children.description:
When capture is enabled, Ze writes every message the peer sends to a JSONL file, as raw wire bytes
with arrival metadata. The file also carries the config operations applied while the capture runs.
Replay the file on a developer machine with 'le test replay <file>', which drives the same state
machine over the same input. Capture is a diagnostic aid, so leave it off in steady state. The file
holds the routing data of the peer: prefixes, AS paths, communities, and next hops. It holds no
local secret, because a TCP-MD5 key never appears on the wire, and a captured config payload is
redacted. Handle a capture file the way you handle a routing-table dump.
children.name: capture
children.short-help: Protocol event capture for this peer.

children.description:
Set the leaf false to keep the config in place and suspend the BFD client. This is useful during
maintenance.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Master switch for the BFD session of this peer.

children.description:
How long the BFD session must stay Up before Ze lets the BGP session establish. Zero, the default,
establishes on the first Up and is the behaviour of a peer that sets no hold-down. A non-zero value damps
a flapping link: a BFD session that goes down again inside the interval never completes it. Set the
negotiated BGP hold time long enough to cover this interval, or the far end times out waiting.
children.name: hold-down
children.short-help: BFD hold-down interval for strict mode (draft-ietf-idr-bgp-bfd-strict-mode Section 10).

children.description:
The maximum time Ze waits for BFD to come Up after the peer's OPEN, and only when the negotiated BGP
hold time is zero. A non-zero BGP hold time bounds the wait already, so this timer does not run. On
expiry Ze sends a NOTIFICATION with Cease and subcode BFD Down, and the peer returns to Idle.
children.name: hold-time
children.short-help: BfdHoldTime for strict mode (draft-ietf-idr-bgp-bfd-strict-mode Section 3).

children.description:
The leaf is optional. When the leaf is absent, the BFD plugin derives the interface from the local
address of the peer. Ze ignores the leaf for multi-hop.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Single-hop egress interface for the BFD session.

children.description: Ze ignores the leaf for single-hop. Zero selects the plugin default, which is 254.
children.name: min-ttl
children.short-help: Multi-hop minimum acceptable TTL (RFC 5883 Section 5).

children.description:
Single-hop is the common case for an eBGP peer on a direct link. Multi-hop is for iBGP over an IGP,
and for any peering that crosses more than one IP hop.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: BFD hop mode for this peer: single-hop or multi-hop.

values.name: multi-hop
values.short-help: RFC 5883 multi-hop BFD on UDP 4784 with min-TTL.

values.name: single-hop
values.short-help: RFC 5881 single-hop BFD on UDP 3784 with GTSM.

children.description:
The referenced profile supplies detect-multiplier, desired-min-tx-us, and required-min-rx-us. An
empty value selects the BFD plugin defaults.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: Name of a profile defined under the top-level bfd { profile ... } block.

children.description:
Ze advertises BGP capability 74 in its OPEN and does not let the BGP session go past OpenSent until
the BFD session is Up. Both speakers must advertise the capability: against a peer that does not, Ze
establishes the session on the normal path and BFD stays a failure detector. Ze opens the BFD session
before it starts the BGP FSM, and keeps it open while the BGP session is down.
children.name: strict
children.short-help: BFD strict mode (draft-ietf-idr-bgp-bfd-strict-mode).

children.description:
When the container is present, the BGP reactor calls the Service interface of the BFD plugin at
session establishment. The reactor stops the BGP session when BFD reports Down. The BFD plugin must
be loaded through a top-level bfd { ... } block. When the plugin is absent, the BGP peer starts
without BFD and Ze logs a warning.
children.name: bfd
children.short-help: Bidirectional Forwarding Detection options for this peer (RFC 5880).

children.description:
The BGP reactor reads no value from the leaf, so the leaf changes no TCP connection and
discovers no address. session > link-local is the leaf that carries a link-local address, and
Ze writes that address after the global next hop (RFC 2545 Section 3). ze exabgp migrate sets
this leaf true and writes the address into session > link-local for an ExaBGP peer that states
local-link-local.
children.name: link-local
children.short-help: Auto-discover IPv6 link-local address for TCP connection

children.description:
The default is true. Set the leaf false for a peer Ze dials and never answers. accept
and connect cannot both be false, and Ze refuses that config.
children.name: accept
children.short-help: Accept inbound TCP connections at this local endpoint (RFC 4271 Section 8.1.1)

children.description:
auto leaves the source address to the operating system. An address binds the outbound
connection to it, which fixes the source address that a next-hop self rewrite uses. Ze
refuses an IPv6 link-local address here.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Local address for connection (use IP address or 'auto')

values.name: auto
values.short-help: Let the operating system choose the source address of the connection.

children.description:
Ze opens a listener of its own for this peer on the local address and this port, and
answers an inbound connection there. The default is 179, and a peer at 179 shares the
global listener. The range is 1 to 65535, and Ze refuses a config outside it. Ze binds no
local source port on an outbound connection, so the value applies to the listener alone.
connection > remote > port is the port Ze dials, and the two are independent.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Local listen port

children.description: The container controls the bind address, the port, and whether Ze accepts an inbound connection.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Local endpoint for the TCP session.

children.description:
The default is the peer address. Set the leaf for a multi-hop peer whose key is bound
to another address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: MD5 authentication IP

children.description:
The leaf is marked sensitive, so the CLI and the web UI hide the value. The key never
reaches the wire, because RFC 2385 carries a digest in a TCP option.
children.name: password
children.short-help: MD5 authentication password

children.description:
Ze applies TCP_MD5SIG to the dialing socket and to the listening socket. A peer with no
matching key cannot open the TCP connection, so the session never reaches OPEN.
children.name: md5
children.short-help: TCP MD5 authentication (RFC 2385)

children.description:
The default is true. Set the leaf false for a passive peer that Ze answers and never
dials. connect and accept cannot both be false, and Ze refuses that config.
children.name: connect
children.short-help: Initiate outbound TCP connections to this remote endpoint (RFC 4271 Section 8.1.1)

children.description:
dynamic is valid at the group level alone. Ze then creates a peer when a connection
arrives from an address inside one of the ranges, up to max-peers. The address must be
unique over every peer.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Peer IP address or 'dynamic' for dynamic peer groups

values.name: dynamic
values.short-help: Accept BGP sessions from any IP in the group's range.

children.description:
The default is 1000, and the range is 1 to 100000. The leaf has a meaning when ip is
dynamic alone. Ze refuses a connection that would take the group past the value.
children.name: max-peers
children.short-help: Maximum number of dynamic peers for this group

children.description:
The default is 179. Ze dials the peer at this port. Set the leaf for a peer that
listens on another port, and for a test peer on one host. connection > local > port is
the port Ze listens on, and the two are independent.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Remote connection port

children.description:
The list has a meaning when ip is 'dynamic' alone. A connection from an IP address inside one of
these ranges creates a dynamic peer.
children.name: range
children.short-help: IP prefix ranges for a dynamic peer group.

children.description:
The container controls the peer address, the port, the outbound connection, and the dynamic peer
ranges.
children.name: remote
children.short-help: Remote endpoint for the TCP session.

children.description:
The value is a hop count. Ze sends every packet with TTL 255, and the kernel refuses a
packet that arrives with less than 256 minus the value. max 1 therefore accepts a directly
connected peer alone.
children.name: max
children.short-help: TTL security / GTSM (RFC 5082)

children.description:
0 installs no receive-side gate in the kernel. A value makes the kernel refuse a
packet whose IP TTL, or IPv6 Hop Limit, is less than it.
children.name: min
children.short-help: Minimum incoming TTL

children.description:
0 leaves the operating system default in place. A value sets the IP TTL, or the IPv6
Hop Limit, on every packet Ze sends to this peer.
children.name: set
children.short-help: Outgoing TTL value

children.description:
max is the hop-count form of RFC 5082 GTSM. set and min are the two raw values. Ze refuses
max together with set, and max together with min.
children.name: ttl
children.short-help: TTL settings for BGP sessions

children.description:
The container holds the local endpoint, the remote endpoint, the TCP MD5 key, the TTL
controls, and the BFD opt-in. connect and accept cannot both be false, and Ze refuses that config.
children.name: connection
children.short-help: Transport-level connection settings

children.description:
The CLI, the web UI, and the logs show the label. It usually names the role or the location of the
peer, for example 'upstream-transit-provider'.
children.name: description
children.short-help: Free-text label for this peer.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze removes every community of that set from the route.
children.name: strip
children.short-help: Named communities to remove on egress.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze adds every community of that set to the route.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: Named communities to add on egress.

children.description: The container holds the tag list and the strip list.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Community filter for egress.

children.description:
The container holds the filters Ze runs over a route it sends to
this peer.
children.name: egress
children.short-help: Egress direction filters.

children.description:
Ze runs the global chain, then the group chain, then this chain. Prefix a name with
inactive: to record that this session runs without a check an RFC 9234 role requires.
children.name: export
children.short-help: Export filter chain (filter instance names)

children.description:
Ze runs the global chain, then the group chain, then this chain. A plain name references a
filter instance declared under bgp/policy. A name that carries a colon names a plugin filter,
which Ze validates at runtime.
children.name: import
children.short-help: Import filter chain (filter instance names)

children.description:
The community stops the prefix propagating outside the local
AS, which RFC 7999 Section 3.2 asks for. The choice between
the two values is the operator routing policy, so neither is
forced. This leaf adds the community. It does not discard
traffic.
children.name: blackhole-propagation
children.short-help: Community to add to a route that carries BLACKHOLE (65535:666).

values.name: no-advertise
values.short-help: Add NO_ADVERTISE (65535:65282).

values.name: no-export
values.short-help: Add NO_EXPORT (65535:65281).

values.name: none
values.short-help: Add nothing. RFC 7999 Section 3.1 makes ignoring the community conformant.

children.description:
RFC 8195 Section 3.2 leaves this number to each AS and gives
3 as its example. The number is a local convention, not a
protocol constant. Change it here when the AS already uses 3
for something else.
children.name: relation-function
children.short-help: Function number of the relation tag.

children.description:
RFC 8195 Section 3.2 defines the community. The Global
Administrator is the session local AS. The parameter comes
from what the peer IS to us: 2 for a customer, 3 for a
peer, 4 for a provider. A route-server session and a
route-server-client session write nothing, because RFC 7947
requires transparency there. An iBGP session writes nothing.
Its sender is inside the local AS and has no such
relation.
children.name: relation-tag
children.short-help: Write the relation-to-origin large community of RFC 8195 on each route from this peer.

children.description:
The list is RFC 7454 Section 11's exception for what
customers and peers use to signal. An empty list keeps

nothing. The relation-tag function number is never kept,
whatever this list says: a kept relation function would let
a peer state its own relation to this AS.
children.name: scrub-keep-function
children.short-help: Function numbers a peer can send with the local AS as the Global Administrator.

children.description:
Only the function numbers listed in scrub-keep-function
survive. RFC 7454 Section 11 asks for the scrub. It covers
standard and large communities. It runs on eBGP sessions
only. On an iBGP session an own-AS value is this network's
own signal to itself. Well-known communities are never
reached, so NO_EXPORT, NO_ADVERTISE and BLACKHOLE always
survive.
children.name: scrub-own-ga
children.short-help: Remove inbound communities whose Global Administrator is the local AS.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze removes every community of that set from the route.
children.name: strip
children.short-help: Named communities to remove on ingress.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze adds every community of that set to the route.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: Named communities to add on ingress.

children.description:
The container holds the tag list, the strip list, and the
RFC 8195, RFC 7454 and RFC 7999 leaves.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Community filter for ingress.

children.description:
The container holds the filters Ze runs over a route it receives
from this peer.
children.name: ingress
children.short-help: Ingress direction filters.

children.description: A name references a filter instance defined in bgp/policy.
children.name: filter
children.short-help: Route filter chains for import and export.

children.description:
The BGP reactor reads no value from the leaf. It takes encoding and format off the content container and
nothing else, so an event carries every attribute of the route whatever the leaf holds.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: Filter expression to select which BGP attributes are included in events.

children.description:
Ze resolves the value in three steps: this leaf first, then the default encoder the program registered,
then text. Ze lowercases the value before it passes the value to the program binding.
children.name: encoding
children.short-help: Wire encoding for events sent to the process (e.g., json, text).

children.description:
Ze uses parsed when the leaf is absent. Ze lowercases the value before it passes the value to the program
binding.
children.name: format
children.short-help: Output format template for event rendering.

children.description:
Ze reads encoding and format from the container. A binding that names neither takes
the encoder the program registered, and the parsed format.
children.name: content
children.short-help: Controls the encoding and filtering of events sent to this process.

children.description: The events are up, down, and reset. The process can therefore react to a peer lifecycle transition.
children.name: neighbor-changes
children.short-help: Send session state change events to this process.

children.description:
The config migration rewrites the leaf. Ze creates one attach process entry per name
in the list, and it deletes the block that carried the leaf. The BGP reactor reads no value
from the leaf.
children.name: processes
children.short-help: Legacy ExaBGP process reference list. Use 'receive' and 'send' instead.

children.description:
The config migration treats each pattern as a process name, and it creates one attach
process entry per pattern. Ze matches nothing against the pattern. The BGP reactor reads no
value from the leaf.
children.name: processes-match
children.short-help: Legacy ExaBGP process match patterns for event filtering.

children.description:
The base types are update, open, notification, keepalive, refresh, state, and negotiated. A plugin
registers more, for example update-rpki. A type carries the direction it is fed in: 'update' means
both directions, and 'update-received' and 'update-sent' each mean one direction. A registered type
keeps its whole name, so a plugin type that ends in -sent is never read as a direction. '*' feeds
every type, in both directions. 'all' is not accepted, because a word that reads like a type would
grant a type that a plugin registers later, which '*' says on purpose. Ze validates the list at
runtime against the registered event types.
children.name: receive
children.short-help: Event types this peer feeds the program.

children.description: Ze pipes the BGP events to the stdin of the process, and reads the commands from its stdout.
children.name: run
children.short-help: Shell command that starts the external process.

children.description:
The valid types are update, refresh, raw, and enhanced-refresh. raw is a whole BGP message that the
program builds itself. enhanced-refresh carries the BORR and EORR markers of RFC 7313. '*' names
every type. A direction has no meaning here, because every send type is sent. Ze validates the list
at runtime against the known send types.
children.name: send
children.short-help: Message types this program can send toward the peer.

children.description: Ze starts the process, and communicates with it over stdin and stdout, in JSON.
children.name: process
children.short-help: External process that receives BGP events and can inject a message.

children.description:
Each attachment names one program declared under plugin/external. It states what that program
receives from this peer, and what the program can send to the peer. Write one statement per program:
`attach process <name> { ... }`.
children.name: attach
children.short-help: Programs this peer attaches.

children.description:
When the leaf is disabled, a route stays until it is withdrawn explicitly, or until the hold timer
expires. This is a legacy ExaBGP option, kept for migration.
children.name: auto-flush
children.short-help: Withdraw every route advertised to this peer when the session goes down.

children.description:
Packing reduces the number of UPDATE messages from O(routes) to O(unique-attribute-sets). Disable it
for a peer that requires one prefix per UPDATE.
children.name: group-updates
children.short-help: Pack several NLRI into one UPDATE message when they share the same path attributes.

children.description:
When the leaf is enabled, End-of-RIB must be triggered from outside, through the process API. Use
the leaf when an external controller manages the convergence signaling.
children.name: manual-eor
children.short-help: Do not send End-of-RIB automatically after the initial route advertisement.

children.description:
Forward received UPDATEs directly inside the reactor for RS-client peers, and bypass the plugin
dispatch chain. This path gives lower latency for route server forwarding. A peer with an export
filter is excluded and uses the normal path.
children.name: rs-fast-path
children.short-help: Forward a received UPDATE inside the reactor for an RS-client peer.

children.description: Most operators can keep the defaults.
children.name: behavior
children.short-help: Controls how the reactor processes and forwards an UPDATE for this peer.

children.description:
Discard traffic sent toward a prefix this peer announces
carrying one of these communities. Ze installs that prefix as
a discard route directly. There is no next-hop to allocate and
no static route to pre-create.

Write ASN:VAL, for example 65001:666, or a well-known name.
blackhole and 65535:666 are one value, the one RFC 7999
registers. Section 4 suggests that keyword. An operator's own
community is the common case, which is why this is a list.

A listed community IS the agreement RFC 7999 Section 3.3
requires the receiving party to make 'on that particular BGP
session'.

An empty list beside a set prefixes list means the well-known
value alone. Stating the prefixes a peer CAN blackhole within
IS the explicit configuration directive Section 4 asks for.
The same act is Section 3.3's agreement on that session, so
standard RTBH takes one line. Section 4's default holds: a
container with neither list discards nothing, and so does a
peer with no container.

A STATED list is taken exactly. The well-known value is NOT
added to it. An operator who names 65001:666 and not 65535:666
means it, and Section 3.1 makes that their choice.

The parser applies that default, not a YANG default statement.
The default is conditional on a SIBLING leaf, which a leaf-list
default cannot express. A value materialised into the schema
would also make every peer read as having agreed to 65535:666
on the send side.

One community is not enough on its own. RFC 7999 Section 3.3
states two conditions, and the prefixes list is the other. A
peer with a community and no covering prefix blackholes
nothing.

The list governs the SEND side too. RFC 7999 Section 3.1
requires the two networks to agree on use of the BLACKHOLE
community before a speaker advertises it. Naming it here is
this speaker's half. `send bgp <selector> blackhole` reaches only the
sessions that hold 65535:666, under either spelling. A session
that named its own value alone is left out of the
announcement, and is not sent the prefix untagged.
children.name: communities
children.short-help: Communities that make Ze discard traffic toward a prefix this peer announces.

children.description:
The prefixes this PEER is authorized to advertise. Ze honors a
received blackhole announcement only when one of them covers
it and is equal or shorter. That is RFC 7999 Section 3.3's
first condition, in the RFC's own words. The announced prefix
is 'covered by an equal or shorter IP prefix that the
neighboring network is authorized to advertise'.

The container already says blackhole, so the leaf does not
repeat it.

Coverage is not prefix-list membership. A list entry
192.0.2.0/24 authorizes a 192.0.2.1/32 blackhole inside it,
because the /24 is a shorter covering prefix the neighbor may
advertise. That is the RFC test, and it does not depend on any
ge or le bound.

An empty list authorizes nothing, so honoring never happens.
That is the closed state on purpose: RFC 7999 Section 6 names
unauthorized addition of BLACKHOLE as a denial-of-reachability
vector, and an open default would let any peer discard traffic
for any prefix it names.
children.name: prefixes
children.short-help: The prefixes this peer is authorized to advertise.

children.description:
The RFC 7999 agreement on this BGP session, in both directions.
It states what this speaker does with a received route carrying
the BLACKHOLE community, 65535:666. It also states whether this
speaker CAN advertise that community to this peer. Section 4 uses
the suggested shorthand keyword for the value.

A later revision adds an as-sets leaf-list here. It answers a
DIFFERENT question from session/irr/as-set. That one states what
the peer CAN advertise at all. This one would state what the peer
CAN blackhole within. Whether one deployment puts the same set in
both is the operator's business, not this model's.
children.name: blackhole
children.short-help: RFC 7999 blackhole agreement on this BGP session, in both directions.

children.description:
Ze creates the directory when it is absent. Ze writes one file per peer, named
bgp-<peer-address>.jsonl. Choose a filesystem with room for the configured maximum-size, and with
twice that room when on-limit is rotate. 'ze doctor' reports whether the directory is writable.
children.name: directory
children.short-help: Directory that holds the capture files of this peer.

children.description:
When the leaf is true, Ze refuses the config if the directory is empty, and it refuses the
config if maximum-size is zero. Both refusals happen at config load, before the peer starts.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Capture this peer's inbound protocol events to a file. Off by default.

children.description:
The writer refuses a record that would cross the cap, and it never writes part of a record, so a
file never exceeds this value. With on-limit rotate, a peer uses at most twice this value on disk.
With on-limit stop, a peer uses at most this value.
children.name: maximum-size
children.short-help: Hard cap on the size of one capture file.

children.description:
'rotate' renames the file to <file>.1, which replaces any earlier rotation, and starts a fresh file.
Capture continues, and the newest events are kept. 'stop' closes the file and captures nothing more,
so the oldest events are kept. Either value leaves the daemon unaffected, and the file ends with a
capture-stop record.
children.name: on-limit
children.short-help: What happens when a capture file reaches maximum-size.

values.name: rotate
values.short-help: Rename the full file to <file>.1 and start a fresh one, keeping the newest events.

values.name: stop
values.short-help: Close the full file and capture nothing more, keeping the oldest events.

children.description:
When capture is enabled, Ze writes every message the peer sends to a JSONL file, as raw wire bytes
with arrival metadata. The file also carries the config operations applied while the capture runs.
Replay the file on a developer machine with 'le test replay <file>', which drives the same state
machine over the same input. Capture is a diagnostic aid, so leave it off in steady state. The file
holds the routing data of the peer: prefixes, AS paths, communities, and next hops. It holds no
local secret, because a TCP-MD5 key never appears on the wire, and a captured config payload is
redacted. Handle a capture file the way you handle a routing-table dump.
children.name: capture
children.short-help: Protocol event capture for this peer.

children.description:
Set the leaf false to keep the config in place and suspend the BFD client. This is useful during
maintenance.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Master switch for the BFD session of this peer.

children.description:
How long the BFD session must stay Up before Ze lets the BGP session establish. Zero, the default,
establishes on the first Up and is the behaviour of a peer that sets no hold-down. A non-zero value damps
a flapping link: a BFD session that goes down again inside the interval never completes it. Set the
negotiated BGP hold time long enough to cover this interval, or the far end times out waiting.
children.name: hold-down
children.short-help: BFD hold-down interval for strict mode (draft-ietf-idr-bgp-bfd-strict-mode Section 10).

children.description:
The maximum time Ze waits for BFD to come Up after the peer's OPEN, and only when the negotiated BGP
hold time is zero. A non-zero BGP hold time bounds the wait already, so this timer does not run. On
expiry Ze sends a NOTIFICATION with Cease and subcode BFD Down, and the peer returns to Idle.
children.name: hold-time
children.short-help: BfdHoldTime for strict mode (draft-ietf-idr-bgp-bfd-strict-mode Section 3).

children.description:
The leaf is optional. When the leaf is absent, the BFD plugin derives the interface from the local
address of the peer. Ze ignores the leaf for multi-hop.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Single-hop egress interface for the BFD session.

children.description: Ze ignores the leaf for single-hop. Zero selects the plugin default, which is 254.
children.name: min-ttl
children.short-help: Multi-hop minimum acceptable TTL (RFC 5883 Section 5).

children.description:
Single-hop is the common case for an eBGP peer on a direct link. Multi-hop is for iBGP over an IGP,
and for any peering that crosses more than one IP hop.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: BFD hop mode for this peer: single-hop or multi-hop.

values.name: multi-hop
