values.short-help: RFC 5883 multi-hop BFD on UDP 4784 with min-TTL.

values.name: single-hop
values.short-help: RFC 5881 single-hop BFD on UDP 3784 with GTSM.

children.description:
The referenced profile supplies detect-multiplier, desired-min-tx-us, and required-min-rx-us. An
empty value selects the BFD plugin defaults.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: Name of a profile defined under the top-level bfd { profile ... } block.

children.description:
Ze advertises BGP capability 74 in its OPEN and does not let the BGP session go past OpenSent until
the BFD session is Up. Both speakers must advertise the capability: against a peer that does not, Ze
establishes the session on the normal path and BFD stays a failure detector. Ze opens the BFD session
before it starts the BGP FSM, and keeps it open while the BGP session is down.
children.name: strict
children.short-help: BFD strict mode (draft-ietf-idr-bgp-bfd-strict-mode).

children.description:
When the container is present, the BGP reactor calls the Service interface of the BFD plugin at
session establishment. The reactor stops the BGP session when BFD reports Down. The BFD plugin must
be loaded through a top-level bfd { ... } block. When the plugin is absent, the BGP peer starts
without BFD and Ze logs a warning.
children.name: bfd
children.short-help: Bidirectional Forwarding Detection options for this peer (RFC 5880).

children.description:
The BGP reactor reads no value from the leaf, so the leaf changes no TCP connection and
discovers no address. session > link-local is the leaf that carries a link-local address, and
Ze writes that address after the global next hop (RFC 2545 Section 3). ze exabgp migrate sets
this leaf true and writes the address into session > link-local for an ExaBGP peer that states
local-link-local.
children.name: link-local
children.short-help: Auto-discover IPv6 link-local address for TCP connection

children.description:
The default is true. Set the leaf false for a peer Ze dials and never answers. accept
and connect cannot both be false, and Ze refuses that config.
children.name: accept
children.short-help: Accept inbound TCP connections at this local endpoint (RFC 4271 Section 8.1.1)

children.description:
auto leaves the source address to the operating system. An address binds the outbound
connection to it, which fixes the source address that a next-hop self rewrite uses. Ze
refuses an IPv6 link-local address here.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Local address for connection (use IP address or 'auto')

values.name: auto
values.short-help: Let the operating system choose the source address of the connection.

children.description:
Ze opens a listener of its own for this peer on the local address and this port, and
answers an inbound connection there. The default is 179, and a peer at 179 shares the
global listener. The range is 1 to 65535, and Ze refuses a config outside it. Ze binds no
local source port on an outbound connection, so the value applies to the listener alone.
connection > remote > port is the port Ze dials, and the two are independent.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Local listen port

children.description: The container controls the bind address, the port, and whether Ze accepts an inbound connection.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Local endpoint for the TCP session.

children.description:
The default is the peer address. Set the leaf for a multi-hop peer whose key is bound
to another address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: MD5 authentication IP

children.description:
The leaf is marked sensitive, so the CLI and the web UI hide the value. The key never
reaches the wire, because RFC 2385 carries a digest in a TCP option.
children.name: password
children.short-help: MD5 authentication password

children.description:
Ze applies TCP_MD5SIG to the dialing socket and to the listening socket. A peer with no
matching key cannot open the TCP connection, so the session never reaches OPEN.
children.name: md5
children.short-help: TCP MD5 authentication (RFC 2385)

children.description:
The default is true. Set the leaf false for a passive peer that Ze answers and never
dials. connect and accept cannot both be false, and Ze refuses that config.
children.name: connect
children.short-help: Initiate outbound TCP connections to this remote endpoint (RFC 4271 Section 8.1.1)

children.description:
dynamic is valid at the group level alone. Ze then creates a peer when a connection
arrives from an address inside one of the ranges, up to max-peers. The address must be
unique over every peer.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Peer IP address or 'dynamic' for dynamic peer groups

values.name: dynamic
values.short-help: Accept BGP sessions from any IP in the group's range.

children.description:
The default is 1000, and the range is 1 to 100000. The leaf has a meaning when ip is
dynamic alone. Ze refuses a connection that would take the group past the value.
children.name: max-peers
children.short-help: Maximum number of dynamic peers for this group

children.description:
The default is 179. Ze dials the peer at this port. Set the leaf for a peer that
listens on another port, and for a test peer on one host. connection > local > port is
the port Ze listens on, and the two are independent.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Remote connection port

children.description:
The list has a meaning when ip is 'dynamic' alone. A connection from an IP address inside one of
these ranges creates a dynamic peer.
children.name: range
children.short-help: IP prefix ranges for a dynamic peer group.

children.description:
The container controls the peer address, the port, the outbound connection, and the dynamic peer
ranges.
children.name: remote
children.short-help: Remote endpoint for the TCP session.

children.description:
The value is a hop count. Ze sends every packet with TTL 255, and the kernel refuses a
packet that arrives with less than 256 minus the value. max 1 therefore accepts a directly
connected peer alone.
children.name: max
children.short-help: TTL security / GTSM (RFC 5082)

children.description:
0 installs no receive-side gate in the kernel. A value makes the kernel refuse a
packet whose IP TTL, or IPv6 Hop Limit, is less than it.
children.name: min
children.short-help: Minimum incoming TTL

children.description:
0 leaves the operating system default in place. A value sets the IP TTL, or the IPv6
Hop Limit, on every packet Ze sends to this peer.
children.name: set
children.short-help: Outgoing TTL value

children.description:
max is the hop-count form of RFC 5082 GTSM. set and min are the two raw values. Ze refuses
max together with set, and max together with min.
children.name: ttl
children.short-help: TTL settings for BGP sessions

children.description:
The container holds the local endpoint, the remote endpoint, the TCP MD5 key, the TTL
controls, and the BFD opt-in. connect and accept cannot both be false, and Ze refuses that config.
children.name: connection
children.short-help: Transport-level connection settings

children.description:
The CLI, the web UI, and the logs show the label. It usually names the role or the location of the
peer, for example 'upstream-transit-provider'.
children.name: description
children.short-help: Free-text label for this peer.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze removes every community of that set from the route.
children.name: strip
children.short-help: Named communities to remove on egress.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze adds every community of that set to the route.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: Named communities to add on egress.

children.description: The container holds the tag list and the strip list.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Community filter for egress.

children.description:
The container holds the filters Ze runs over a route it sends to
this peer.
children.name: egress
children.short-help: Egress direction filters.

children.description:
Ze runs the global chain, then the group chain, then this chain. Prefix a name with
inactive: to record that this session runs without a check an RFC 9234 role requires.
children.name: export
children.short-help: Export filter chain (filter instance names)

children.description:
Ze runs the global chain, then the group chain, then this chain. A plain name references a
filter instance declared under bgp/policy. A name that carries a colon names a plugin filter,
which Ze validates at runtime.
children.name: import
children.short-help: Import filter chain (filter instance names)

children.description:
The community stops the prefix propagating outside the local
AS, which RFC 7999 Section 3.2 asks for. The choice between
the two values is the operator routing policy, so neither is
forced. This leaf adds the community. It does not discard
traffic.
children.name: blackhole-propagation
children.short-help: Community to add to a route that carries BLACKHOLE (65535:666).

values.name: no-advertise
values.short-help: Add NO_ADVERTISE (65535:65282).

values.name: no-export
values.short-help: Add NO_EXPORT (65535:65281).

values.name: none
values.short-help: Add nothing. RFC 7999 Section 3.1 makes ignoring the community conformant.

children.description:
RFC 8195 Section 3.2 leaves this number to each AS and gives
3 as its example. The number is a local convention, not a
protocol constant. Change it here when the AS already uses 3
for something else.
children.name: relation-function
children.short-help: Function number of the relation tag.

children.description:
RFC 8195 Section 3.2 defines the community. The Global
Administrator is the session local AS. The parameter comes
from what the peer IS to us: 2 for a customer, 3 for a
peer, 4 for a provider. A route-server session and a
route-server-client session write nothing, because RFC 7947
requires transparency there. An iBGP session writes nothing.
Its sender is inside the local AS and has no such
relation.
children.name: relation-tag
children.short-help: Write the relation-to-origin large community of RFC 8195 on each route from this peer.

children.description:
The list is RFC 7454 Section 11's exception for what
customers and peers use to signal. An empty list keeps

nothing. The relation-tag function number is never kept,
whatever this list says: a kept relation function would let
a peer state its own relation to this AS.
children.name: scrub-keep-function
children.short-help: Function numbers a peer can send with the local AS as the Global Administrator.

children.description:
Only the function numbers listed in scrub-keep-function
survive. RFC 7454 Section 11 asks for the scrub. It covers

only. On an iBGP session an own-AS value is this network's

children.name: scrub-own-ga
children.short-help: Remove inbound communities whose Global Administrator is the local AS.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze removes every community of that set from the route.
children.name: strip
children.short-help: Named communities to remove on ingress.

children.description:
Each value names a set in the bgp community container.
Ze adds every community of that set to the route.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: Named communities to add on ingress.

children.description:
The container holds the tag list, the strip list, and the
RFC 8195, RFC 7454 and RFC 7999 leaves.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Community filter for ingress.

children.description:
The container holds the filters Ze runs over a route it receives
from this peer.
children.name: ingress
children.short-help: Ingress direction filters.

children.description: A name references a filter instance defined in bgp/policy.
children.name: filter
children.short-help: Route filter chains for import and export.

children.description:
The table makes inbound soft reconfiguration possible, which re-applies the import filters without a
session reset. It uses more memory, in proportion to the number of received routes.
children.name: in
children.short-help: Store received routes in Adj-RIB-In, before policy.

children.description:
Route-refresh (RFC 2918) needs the table to re-send the routes at the request of the peer. It uses
more memory, in proportion to the number of advertised routes.
children.name: out
children.short-help: Store advertised routes in Adj-RIB-Out, after policy.

children.description:
These tables hold the raw routes before policy and after policy. They make route-refresh and
soft-reconfiguration possible.
children.name: adj
children.short-help: Adjacency RIB storage for this peer.

children.description:
The delay batches rapid successive changes into fewer UPDATE messages. 0 flushes immediately on each
change.
children.name: auto-commit-delay
children.short-help: Milliseconds to wait before Ze flushes pending route changes to the peer.

children.description: The leaf does what the behavior-level group-updates does, for the Adj-RIB-Out of this peer alone.
children.name: group-updates
children.short-help: Pack routes with identical attributes into one UPDATE.

children.description:
0 means no limit, so Ze flushes every pending change at once. A limit reduces the CPU cost of one
cycle, and raises the convergence latency.
children.name: max-batch-size
children.short-help: Maximum number of route changes in one flush cycle.

children.description:
The three leaves act on the Adj-RIB-Out of this peer alone. They trade the number of
UPDATE messages and the CPU cost against the convergence latency.
children.name: out
children.short-help: Outbound RIB batching: how route changes are grouped and flushed to the peer.

children.description: The container controls which RIB tables Ze maintains, and how the outbound route batching works.
children.name: rib
children.short-help: Route Information Base settings for this peer.

children.description:
An empty list filters nothing, and the ingress and egress rules of RFC 9234 Section 5 still
run. default expands to the set RFC 9234 Section 5 gives the local role. provider sends to
customer and rs-client. customer sends to provider, rs and peer. rs sends to rs-client,
rs-client sends to rs and provider, and peer sends to customer and rs-client. unknown matches a
peer that sent no Role capability, and a peer whose OPEN Ze never recorded.
children.name: export
children.short-help: Controls which destination peer roles may receive routes from this peer

values.short-help: RFC 9234: Customer (3)

Ze sends the role in the Role capability, code 9, and it is the only leaf that makes Ze

peer with peer. Ze rejects any other pair with a NOTIFICATION of code 2 and subcode 11.

children.short-help: Declares local role and enables RFC 9234 ingress rules (replaces Phase 1 name keyword)

values.short-help: RFC 9234: Route Server (1)

values.name: rs-client
values.short-help: RFC 9234: RS-Client (2)

children.description:
The default false accepts a peer that sends no Role capability, which RFC 9234 Section 4.2
asks for. true rejects that session with a NOTIFICATION of code 2 and subcode 11. The leaf needs
import beside it, because Ze validates no OPEN for a peer that declares no local role.
children.name: strict
children.short-help: Require peer to send Role capability

children.description:
The container turns on the role rules for this peer. A peer with no role container sends no
Role capability, and Ze accepts whatever role the peer declares.
children.name: role
children.short-help: RFC 9234 BGP Role configuration

A leaf here carries no default, so an unset leaf falls through to the
group value and then to the global value.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Origin-validation action overrides of this peer or group.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description:
invalid names the action of an ASPA Invalid path and unknown that of an ASPA Unknown path.
Neither leaf carries a default, so an unset leaf falls through to the group value and then to the global value.
children.name: action
children.short-help: ASPA path-state action overrides of this peer or group.

children.description: These overrides apply only when ASPA validation is enabled globally.
children.name: aspa
children.short-help: ASPA action overrides for this peer or group.

children.description:
The route carries the RFC 7999 BLACKHOLE community, and a covering VRP allows a
shorter prefix than the route announces.

RFC 7999 Section 3.3 states that an operator MUST ensure origin validation does not
inadvertently block legitimate announcements carrying BLACKHOLE. A blackhole prefix is
as long as possible, usually a /32 or a /128. A ROA for the covering block carries its
maxLength at the aggregate. RFC 6811 then makes the announcement Invalid, and a session
running action invalid reject drops the route before anything can honor it.

The exemption is narrow. It applies only when a covering VRP names the route's own
origin AS and disagrees on nothing but the length. A wrong origin AS stays Invalid,
which is the hijack RFC 6811 exists to catch. A prefix with no covering VRP is NotFound
rather than Invalid, so the exemption never reaches it.

The default is false. Enable it together with the blackhole honor leaf of the peer, on
the same session. On its own it accepts a route it would have rejected, and it discards
nothing.
children.name: blackhole-exempt
children.short-help: Keep a BLACKHOLE route when its only origin-validation fault is the prefix length.

children.description:
Ze resolves every leaf on its own. A leaf set on the peer wins. A leaf that
is unset falls through to the group value, then to the global value.
children.name: rpki
children.short-help: RPKI action overrides of this peer or group.

children.description:
RFC 8669 Section 4 states that a PrefixSID from an EBGP peer outside the SR domain MUST be
discarded, unless the speaker is configured to accept it. The leaf has no effect on IBGP, where Ze
always accepts the attribute.
children.name: accept-srv6-prefix-sid
children.short-help: Accept the BGP Prefix-SID attribute (code 40) with SRv6 TLVs from this EBGP peer.

children.description:
Use the leaf in a VPN design, or in a multi-site design, where the same customer ASN appears at more
than one site.
children.name: as-override
children.short-help: Replace the ASN of the peer with the local ASN in the outbound AS_PATH.

children.description:
Ze sends this value in OPEN in place of the global ASN. Ze keeps the global ASN too,
and local-options decides how the two appear in AS_PATH.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Local AS (overrides global)

children.description:
The two options act in different directions, so each one is set on its own. no-prepend acts inbound:
the local-as is not added to a route received from this peer. replace-as acts outbound: this peer
sees the local-as alone instead of the local-as followed by the globally configured ASN. With
neither option, this peer sees the local-as followed by the globally configured ASN.
children.name: local-options
children.short-help: Modifiers for the local-as behavior of this peer.

values.name: no-prepend
values.short-help: Do not add the local-as to a route received from this peer.

values.name: replace-as
values.short-help: Send the local-as alone toward this peer, without the global ASN.

children.description:
RFC 7705 Section 4.2 'Internal BGP AS Migration'. Set the leaf to the other ASN of the
pair the router runs while it moves from one ASN to another: the local ASN is one of the two
and this leaf is the other. Ze then accepts an OPEN whose My Autonomous System carries either
ASN, and treats the session as native iBGP whichever ASN won. Ze sends the local ASN first and
falls back to this one only after the peer answers Bad Peer AS, which is what keeps two
speakers that both run the mechanism from deadlocking. remote must name one of the two ASNs,
and Ze refuses a config where it names a third. Remove the leaf when the migration ends.
children.name: migration
children.short-help: Second local AS this iBGP session accepts and sends during an AS migration.

children.description:
Ze compares the value with the local ASN. A different value makes the session eBGP,
and an equal value makes it iBGP. That verdict decides the AS_PATH prepend, the auto
next-hop rewrite, and whether Ze sends LOCAL_PREF.
children.name: remote
children.short-help: Peer Autonomous System Number

children.description:
local overrides the global ASN for this session. remote names the peer ASN. Ze compares
the two to decide whether the session is eBGP or iBGP. migration names a second local ASN this
iBGP session also accepts while the router moves from one ASN to another.
children.name: asn
children.short-help: AS number configuration

children.description:
send offers more than one path to the peer. receive accepts more than one path
from the peer. send/receive does both. Ze applies the value to every negotiated family
that carries no family entry of its own.
children.name: direction
children.short-help: Default ADD-PATH direction for all negotiated families.

values.name: receive
values.short-help: Receive multiple paths

values.name: send
values.short-help: Send multiple paths

values.name: send/receive
values.short-help: Both send and receive multiple paths

children.description:
The value replaces the container direction for this family. An absent value
keeps the container direction.
children.name: direction
children.short-help: ADD-PATH direction override for this family.

values.name: receive
values.short-help: Receive ADD-PATH

values.name: send
values.short-help: Send ADD-PATH

values.name: send/receive
values.short-help: Both send and receive ADD-PATH

children.description:
Use a value from 1 through 65535. Omit this leaf to inherit the container limit.
Ze advertises no limit for a disabled or refused ADD-PATH family. This is a request
to the sender, not local receive-side policing.
children.name: limit
children.short-help: Maximum paths per prefix requested from the peer (PATHS-LIMIT capability).

children.description:
enable and disable act on this family alone. require refuses the session when
the peer does not offer ADD-PATH. refuse refuses the session when the peer offers
it. Ze takes the most restrictive mode over the whole list.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: ADD-PATH negotiation mode for this family.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: refuse
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer offers it

values.name: require
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer does not offer it

children.description:
The list key is the family name. An entry with no direction takes the container
direction. Ze skips an entry whose family name is not registered.
children.name: family
children.short-help: Per-family ADD-PATH overrides with optional path count limit.

children.description:
Ze advertises this receive request for each enabled ADD-PATH family. A per-family
limit overrides it. This setting does not enforce a local receive-side limit.
children.name: limit
children.short-help: Default maximum paths per prefix requested from the peer (PATHS-LIMIT).

children.description:
PATHS-LIMIT is draft-abraitis-idr-addpath-paths-limit. The default direction applies to every
negotiated multiprotocol family. A per-family entry overrides the default direction.
children.name: add-path
children.short-help: ADD-PATH capability (RFC 7911), with an optional PATHS-LIMIT.

children.description:
The capability is required for an ASN of more than 65535. Disable it only for a peer that runs a
legacy implementation, which speaks 2-byte ASNs alone. require refuses the session when the
peer does not offer it, and refuse refuses the session when the peer offers it.
children.name: asn4
children.short-help: 4-byte ASN capability mode (RFC 6793): enable, disable, require or refuse.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: refuse
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer offers it

values.name: require
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer does not offer it

children.description:
The capability raises the BGP message size limit from 4096 bytes to 65535 bytes. A large UPDATE that
carries many attributes needs it.
children.name: extended-message
children.short-help: Extended Message capability (RFC 8654).

children.description:
Long-Lived Stale Time in seconds (RFC 9494 Section 3). When this leaf is set, Ze advertises the LLGR
capability (code 71). The maximum value is 16777215, because the field is 24 bits, which is about
194 days. Ze applies the value to every negotiated address family of the peer.
children.name: long-lived-stale-time
children.short-help: Long-Lived Stale Time for the peer, in seconds (RFC 9494 Section 3).

children.description:
The value is what Ze advertises to the peer. It does not set the timer Ze runs when the peer
restarts: that timer takes the Restart Time the peer itself advertised. Ze deletes every stale
route of the peer when that timer expires, unless the peer also negotiated LLGR.
children.name: restart-time
children.short-help:
Restart Time in seconds (RFC 4724 Section 3).
Maximum value is 4095 (12-bit field).

children.description:
The container carries presence, so writing it makes Ze send the Graceful Restart capability,
code 64, to this peer. Ze lists no address family in that capability, because Ze runs the Receiving
Speaker procedures of RFC 4724 and preserves no forwarding state of its own. A container on the peer
replaces the container on the group rather than adding to it.
children.name: graceful-restart
children.short-help: Graceful Restart capability configuration.

children.description:
The capability carries host and domain as two separate strings, and Ze joins neither. Ze
writes the domain after the host, with its own 1-byte length, which is why 255 bytes is the
limit.
children.name: domain
children.short-help: Domain name (max 255 bytes).

children.description:
Ze writes the value with a 1-byte length in front of it, which is why 255 bytes is the
limit. Ze does not read the hostname of the box, so an empty leaf sends an empty string.
children.name: host
children.short-help: System hostname (max 255 bytes).

children.description:
Ze sends the FQDN capability, code 73 of draft-walton-bgp-hostname, in the OPEN message. Ze
sends no capability when host and domain are both empty. A container on the peer replaces the
container on the group rather than adding to it.
children.name: hostname
children.short-help: FQDN capability configuration.

children.description:
The capability advertises that ze accepts IPv6 link-local
next-hops in MP_REACH_NLRI (RFC 2545 Section 3).
children.name: link-local-nexthop
children.short-help: Link-local next-hop capability.

children.description:
Ze takes the most restrictive mode over the whole list, where require wins against
refuse, and refuse wins against enable. enable and require both advertise the family.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Extended next hop negotiation mode

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: refuse
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer offers it

values.name: require
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer does not offer it

children.description: Ze reads ipv4 and ipv6 alone, and it skips an entry that names another value.
children.name: nhafi
children.short-help: Next-hop AFI (e.g. ipv6)

values.name: ipv4
values.short-help: IPv4 (AFI 1)

values.name: ipv6
values.short-help: IPv6 (AFI 2)

children.description:
The list key is the NLRI family, and nhafi is the next-hop AFI. The pair lets an IPv4
route carry an IPv6 next hop, so an IPv6-only session can hold IPv4 reachability.
children.name: nexthop
children.short-help: Extended Next Hop capability (RFC 8950)

children.description:
The capability lets the peer request a full re-advertisement of the routes, without a session
teardown.
children.name: route-refresh
children.short-help: Route Refresh capability (RFC 2918).

children.description:
enable is the default, and Ze sends the capability. disable sends none. Ze treats require
as enable and refuse as disable: the plugin decides only whether to send code 75, and it holds
the peer to nothing. So a peer that sends no Software Version stays up under require, and a peer
that sends one stays up under refuse. Set the leaf on the peer to override the group value.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Capability negotiation mode.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: refuse
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer offers it

values.name: require
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer does not offer it

children.description:
The container carries presence, so writing it makes Ze send the capability of
draft-abraitis-bgp-version-capability to this peer. The value is the fixed string Ze/0.1.0, and no
leaf changes it. A container on the peer replaces the container on the group rather than adding to
it.
children.name: software-version
children.short-help: Software Version capability (code 75).

children.description:
Every capability here takes four modes. enable advertises it. disable does not advertise
it. require advertises it and refuses the session when the peer does not offer it. refuse does
not advertise it and refuses the session when the peer offers it.
children.name: capability
children.short-help: BGP capability negotiation

children.description: The default is the router-id. Ze prepends the cluster ID to CLUSTER_LIST on a reflected route.
children.name: cluster-id
children.short-help: Override the cluster ID for route reflection (RFC 4456 Section 7).

children.description:
The default is all, which sends every community type. Name an individual type to control the set.
none suppresses every community attribute.
children.name: send
children.short-help: Community types Ze includes in an outbound UPDATE.

values.name: all
values.short-help: Send all community types (default)

values.name: extended
values.short-help: Send extended communities (type 16, RFC 4360)

values.name: large
values.short-help: Send large communities (type 32, RFC 8092)

values.name: none
values.short-help: Suppress all community attributes

values.name: standard
values.short-help: Send standard communities (type 8, RFC 1997)

children.description:
The container holds the send leaf-list alone. send names the community types Ze puts in an
outbound UPDATE, and it acts on no inbound message.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Community attribute control for this session

children.description:
Ze reads the leaf after capability > hostname > domain and replaces that value with it, so a
peer that writes both leaves sends this one. The capability writes a 1-byte length in front of the
domain name, which is the 255-byte limit. Write capability > hostname > domain in a new config:
ze exabgp migrate produces that spelling and never this one.
children.name: domain-name
children.short-help: Legacy: Domain name for FQDN capability.

children.description: The default route is 0.0.0.0/0 for IPv4, and ::/0 for IPv6.
children.name: default-originate
children.short-help: Originate the default route to this peer for this address family.

children.description:
When the filter rejects, Ze does not send the default route. An empty value, or an absent leaf,
originates the default route without a condition.
children.name: default-originate-filter
children.short-help: Named filter that must accept before Ze originates the default route.

children.description:
enable advertises the family. disable does not advertise it. require advertises it and
refuses the session when the peer does not offer it. ignore advertises the family and
relaxes the UPDATE check. Ze then drops an UPDATE that names a family the two peers did
not negotiate, and the session stays up.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Address family negotiation mode

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Disable this address family

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Enable this address family

values.name: ignore
values.short-help: Ignore this address family

values.name: require
values.short-help: Require this address family

children.description:
offered counts wire events. Every announcement raises the count, and every withdrawal lowers it. A
peer that re-announces a prefix to change an attribute raises the count again, although it holds the
same route. The count can therefore be more than the maximum. Ze then drops every later announce of
this family, until the peer withdraws enough prefixes. installed counts the set of prefixes Ze
currently holds for this family, which no re-announcement and no unmatched withdrawal can move.
installed keeps one entry per prefix for this family, so its memory is the size of what the peer
sends, up to the maximum. Neither value is the size of the RIB, because import policy can reject a
counted prefix.
children.name: count
children.short-help: Which prefixes the count compared against maximum holds.

values.name: installed
values.short-help: Count the prefixes this family holds now.

values.name: offered
values.short-help: Count every announcement the peer sends, repeats included.

children.description:
The wait doubles on each repeat teardown, up to one hour. 0 keeps the peer down. See the reconnect
leaf.
children.name: idle-timeout
children.short-help: Seconds to wait before reconnect after this family stopped the session.

children.description:
The NOTIFICATION data carries the AFI, the SAFI, and this value as the upper bound
(RFC 4486 Section 4). The count leaf decides which prefixes the count holds.
children.name: maximum
children.short-help: Hard maximum number of prefixes accepted

children.description: No value means timer when idle-timeout is more than 0, and never when idle-timeout is 0.
children.name: reconnect
children.short-help: What the peer does after this family stopped the session.

values.name: backoff
values.short-help: Reconnect on the usual connect backoff of the peer.

values.name: never
values.short-help: Keep the peer down. An operator restarts it.

values.name: timer
values.short-help: Reconnect after idle-timeout seconds.

children.description:
The default is true, and an absent value also reads as true. With false Ze keeps
the session up and drops the UPDATE that crossed the maximum.
children.name: teardown
children.short-help: Tear down session when prefix maximum exceeded (false = warn only)

children.description:
ze:hidden keeps the leaf out of the CLI completion. The peer command reports the
date, and it marks the peer prefix-stale when the date is more than 180 days old.
children.name: updated
children.short-help: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) when prefix maximum was last updated from PeeringDB. Hidden leaf.

children.description:
Crossing the threshold raises a metric and a login-banner warning, and it leaves
the session up. Ze refuses a warning value that is not less than maximum.
children.name: warning
children.short-help: Warning threshold. Defaults to 90% of maximum when not set.

children.description:
The limit is the defense against a peer that floods the RIB. When the count crosses
maximum, Ze sends a Cease NOTIFICATION with subcode 1, Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached
(RFC 4486).
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Prefix limit configuration for this address family

children.description:
Ze advertises one Multiprotocol Extensions capability per entry (RFC 4760). A list with no
entry sends no such capability. Each entry also carries the prefix limit and the
default-originate switch of that family.
children.name: family
children.short-help: Address families to negotiate

children.description:
Ze reads the leaf after capability > hostname > host and replaces that value with it, so a
peer that writes both leaves sends this one. The capability writes a 1-byte length in front of the
host name, which is the 255-byte limit. Write capability > hostname > host in a new config:
ze exabgp migrate produces that spelling and never this one.
children.name: host-name
children.short-help: Legacy: Host name for FQDN capability.

children.description:
The IRR filter queries an IRR database for the prefixes of one AS-SET.
This leaf names that AS-SET. If this leaf is empty, Ze reads the remote ASN of the
peer and discovers the AS-SET from PeeringDB.
children.name: as-set
children.short-help: Explicit AS-SET name for the IRR prefix lookup.

children.description:
disable takes the peer out of the resolution, so Ze runs no whois query and no PeeringDB
query for it. The other peers of the same remote ASN keep their list.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable or disable IRR filtering for this peer.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Disable IRR filtering for this peer.

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Enable IRR filtering for this peer (default).

children.description:
Ze resolves the prefixes of a peer only when the peer asked for it. A filter chain that names
bgp-filter-irr asks for it, and so does an as-set written here. A peer that states no remote ASN is
never resolved.
children.name: irr
children.short-help: Per-peer IRR filter settings.

children.description:
The address goes in the MP_REACH Next Hop field. The leaf supplies the address, and it does not
decide that the address is sent. Ze appends the address only when this speaker shares a locally
connected subnet with the peer, and with the entity that the global next hop names. That is the 'if
and only if' condition of Section 3. In every other case the field carries the global address alone.
Set the leaf on a session that faces a peer on a shared link. It has no effect on any other session.
children.name: link-local
children.short-help: IPv6 link-local address advertised after the global next hop (RFC 2545 Section 3).

children.description:
auto rewrites the next hop for an eBGP peer, and preserves it for an iBGP peer. self always rewrites
the next hop to the local address. unchanged never rewrites it, so the original next hop is
preserved. An IP address sets the next hop to that address.
children.name: next-hop
children.short-help: Next-hop rewriting policy for a forwarded UPDATE (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.3).

values.name: auto
values.short-help: RFC 4271 default: rewrite for eBGP, preserve for iBGP

values.name: self
values.short-help: Rewrite next-hop to local address (common for iBGP)

values.name: unchanged
values.short-help: Never rewrite next-hop (route-server, third-party NH)

children.description:
RFC 8669 Section 8 states that the propagation to another AS MUST be configured explicitly. Ze
therefore removes the attribute from every UPDATE sent to an EBGP peer that does not set this leaf.
Set the leaf on an EBGP peer inside the same SR domain. An SR domain can span more than one AS, and
Ze cannot derive that membership from the ASN. The leaf has no effect on IBGP, where Ze always
advertises the attribute.
children.name: propagate-srv6-prefix-sid
children.short-help: Advertise the BGP Prefix-SID attribute (code 40) to this EBGP peer.

children.description:
Ze forwards a route from a client to every client and to every non-client. Ze forwards a route from
a non-client to the clients alone.
children.name: route-reflector-client
children.short-help: Mark this peer as a route reflector client (RFC 4456).

children.description: RFC 6286 Section 2.1 defines the BGP Identifier as a 4-octet, unsigned, non-zero integer.
children.name: router-id
children.short-help: Override the router ID for this peer.

children.description:
Mark this peer as an RS-client for transparent AS-path forwarding. RFC 7947 Section 2.2.2: the route
server MUST NOT modify AS_PATH or any other transitive attribute. When this leaf is true, the
reactor skips AS-path prepending for this peer on the forwarding path.
children.name: rs-client
children.short-help: Mark this peer as an RS-client for transparent AS-path forwarding.

children.description:
The container holds the ASN, the capabilities, the address families, the next-hop policy, and the
community control. A peer inherits these from its group, and a peer value overrides the group value.
children.name: session
children.short-help: BGP session parameters for this peer or group.

children.description:
Ze removes a disconnected dynamic peer after this delay when no connection comes back. A
static peer reconnects on an exponential backoff from 5 seconds to 60 seconds, and this leaf
does not change that backoff.
children.name: connect-retry
children.short-help: Connect retry interval in seconds. Ze reads it for a dynamic peer alone.

children.description:
Ze refuses a value that is not less than receive-hold-time, because the hold timer must be
able to detect a lost KEEPALIVE. 0 derives the interval from the negotiated hold time.
children.name: keepalive
children.short-help: Keepalive interval in seconds (RFC 4271 Section 10). 0 = auto: hold-time/3.

children.description:
Ze puts the value in the Hold Time field of OPEN. The two peers then hold the lower of the
two values (RFC 4271 Section 4.2). Ze refuses 1 and 2, because the RFC permits 0, or 3 seconds
and more.
children.name: receive-hold-time
children.short-help: Receive hold time in seconds (RFC 4271: 0 or >= 3). Proposed in OPEN.

children.description:
RFC 9687 Section 4.4 requires a non-zero Send Hold Time to be more than the negotiated
hold time. Ze therefore refuses a value that is not more than receive-hold-time. Ze also
refuses a non-zero value of less than 480 seconds.
children.name: send-hold-time
children.short-help: Send hold time in seconds (RFC 9687). 0 = auto: max(480, 2x receive-hold-time).

children.description:
The speaker proposes the hold time in OPEN. The two peers negotiate it to the lower of their two
values.
children.name: timer
children.short-help: BGP session timers: hold time, keepalive interval, and connect retry delay.

children.description: The attribute identifies the AS and the router that formed the aggregate.
children.name: aggregator
children.short-help: AGGREGATOR attribute (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.7). The format is AS:IP.

children.description:
The list is an ordered sequence. A repeated ASN is a prepend that counts, so Ze does not deduplicate
it (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.2). AS_PATH decides loop detection, and it decides path selection, where
the shorter path is preferred.
children.name: as-path
children.short-help: AS_PATH segments prepended to the route, as space-separated ASNs.

children.description: The flag signals that aggregation formed the route, and that AS_PATH information was lost.
children.name: atomic-aggregate
children.short-help: ATOMIC_AGGREGATE flag (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.6).

children.description: The list carries an attribute that no named field covers.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: Raw BGP attributes in hex encoding, as flags:type:hex-value.

children.description:
The attribute carries an MPLS label index for Segment Routing. A node can therefore advertise its
SID without a per-prefix label allocation.
children.name: bgp-prefix-sid
children.short-help: Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 8669).

children.description:
The attribute carries SRv6 SID information for IPv6 Segment Routing, and it includes the SRv6 L3
Service TLVs.
children.name: bgp-prefix-sid-srv6
children.short-help: SRv6 Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 9252).

children.description: Each reflector prepends its cluster ID. The list detects a loop between reflectors.
children.name: cluster-list
children.short-help: CLUSTER_LIST for route reflection (RFC 4456).

children.description:
The format is AS:value, for example 65000:100. A well-known name is also accepted, such as no-export
or no-advertise.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Standard BGP communities (RFC 1997).

children.description: An extended community carries a route target, a site-of-origin, or VPN semantics.
children.name: extended-community
children.short-help: Extended communities (RFC 4360). The format is type:admin:value.

children.description:
Ze accepts a decimal number from 0 to 1048575, which is the 20-bit label field. It accepts no keyword.
Write the labels leaf-list for a stack of more than one label.
children.name: label
children.short-help: MPLS label value for a labeled unicast route (RFC 3107). The value is a number.

children.description:
The list is an ordered sequence from bottom to top. Ze keeps a repeated label, and it does not
deduplicate the stack.
children.name: labels
children.short-help: MPLS label stack for a multi-label route (RFC 8277).

children.description:
Each value is three 32-bit numbers separated by colons, which is 12 octets on the wire. The global part
holds a 4-byte ASN, which a standard community of RFC 1997 cannot hold.
children.name: large-community
children.short-help: Large BGP communities (RFC 8092). Format: global:local1:local2. Supports 4-byte ASNs natively.

children.description: LOCAL_PREF has a meaning inside a single AS alone (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.5). The default is 100.
children.name: local-preference
children.short-help: LOCAL_PREF value for iBGP best-path selection. The higher value wins.

children.description: MED influences the inbound path selection that an external peer makes (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.4).
children.name: med
children.short-help: Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED). The lower value is preferred.

children.description:
self resolves at send time to the local address of the session, so each peer reads its
own next hop. An IP address reaches every peer of the block unchanged. Ze refuses an IPv6
link-local address here, because RFC 2545 Section 3 puts the global address in that field.
children.name: next-hop
children.short-help: Next hop address or 'self'

values.name: self
values.short-help: Resolve the next hop at send time to the local address of each session.

children.description:
RFC 4271 Section 4.3 gives three values. igp is reachability interior to the
originating AS. egp is reachability learned through the EGP protocol. incomplete is
reachability learned by some other means, for example a redistributed static route.
children.name: origin
children.short-help: ORIGIN attribute (RFC 4271 Section 4.3)

values.name: egp
values.short-help: Exterior Gateway Protocol

values.name: igp
values.short-help: Interior Gateway Protocol

values.name: incomplete
values.short-help: Incomplete origin

children.description:
The reflector sets the attribute to the router ID of the originating router. The attribute prevents
a loop.
children.name: originator-id
children.short-help: ORIGINATOR_ID for route reflection (RFC 4456).

children.description: The identifier separates the several paths that one peer sends for the same prefix.
children.name: path-information
children.short-help: ADD-PATH path identifier (RFC 7911).

children.description: Ze prepends the Route Distinguisher to the prefix, which makes a unique VPN route.
children.name: rd
children.short-help: Route Distinguisher (RFC 4364). The format is ASN:nn or IP:nn.

children.description: The format is /length. For example, /24 splits a /16 into 256 prefixes of /24.
children.name: split
children.short-help: Split one prefix into more-specific prefixes for the announcement.

children.description:
Every NLRI of the block takes the same attributes. To announce two prefixes that carry
different attributes, write two update blocks.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: Path attributes for routes in this block

children.description:
The list carries no key, so the CLI and the web UI show this label in place of one. The
label reaches no BGP message.
children.name: name
children.short-help: Optional label for this update block (display only)

children.description:
The form is an operation keyword, then an optional rd and label, then one or more prefixes. add, del and
eor are the operation keywords, and one of them is required. A block that carries del or eor announces nothing
at config load.
children.name: content
children.short-help: Operation, qualifiers, and payload

children.description:
Every entry takes the attribute block of the update block. The key is the family name, and
content carries the operation keyword and the prefixes. An update block that declares no nlri
entry is refused at config load.
children.name: nlri
children.short-help: Routes this update block announces, one entry for each address family.

children.description:
request bgp watchdog announce <name> announces every route that carries the name, and request bgp
watchdog withdraw <name> withdraws them. Ze skips a block whose name is empty.
children.name: name
children.short-help: Watchdog group name

children.description:
The bgp-watchdog plugin reads the PRESENCE of the leaf and not its value, so withdraw false starts every
route of the block withdrawn exactly as withdraw true does. Delete the leaf to announce the routes as soon as
the session reaches Established. request bgp watchdog announce <name> announces a withdrawn route.
children.name: withdraw
children.short-help: Start in withdrawn state (default true)

children.description:
The bgp-watchdog plugin owns every route of the block, so the BGP engine holds none of
them as a static route. The plugin sends a route that is not withdrawn when the session reaches
Established.
children.name: watchdog
children.short-help: Watchdog-controlled route - held until 'bgp watchdog announce <name>'

children.description:
Ze announces every route of the block to the peers the block applies to. The block is written
at the global level, the group level, and the peer level, and the three accumulate.
children.name: update
children.short-help: Native Ze route announcements

children.description:
The list key is the peer name. connection/remote/ip must be unique over every peer, and Ze
refuses the config when that address, session/asn/local or session/asn/remote is absent.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: BGP peer in this group

children.description:
The table makes inbound soft reconfiguration possible, which re-applies the import filters without a
session reset. It uses more memory, in proportion to the number of received routes.
children.name: in
children.short-help: Store received routes in Adj-RIB-In, before policy.

children.description:
Route-refresh (RFC 2918) needs the table to re-send the routes at the request of the peer. It uses
more memory, in proportion to the number of advertised routes.
children.name: out
children.short-help: Store advertised routes in Adj-RIB-Out, after policy.

children.description:
These tables hold the raw routes before policy and after policy. They make route-refresh and
soft-reconfiguration possible.
children.name: adj
children.short-help: Adjacency RIB storage for this peer.

children.description:
The delay batches rapid successive changes into fewer UPDATE messages. 0 flushes immediately on each
change.
children.name: auto-commit-delay
children.short-help: Milliseconds to wait before Ze flushes pending route changes to the peer.

children.description: The leaf does what the behavior-level group-updates does, for the Adj-RIB-Out of this peer alone.
children.name: group-updates
children.short-help: Pack routes with identical attributes into one UPDATE.

children.description:
0 means no limit, so Ze flushes every pending change at once. A limit reduces the CPU cost of one
cycle, and raises the convergence latency.
children.name: max-batch-size
children.short-help: Maximum number of route changes in one flush cycle.

children.description:
The three leaves act on the Adj-RIB-Out of this peer alone. They trade the number of
UPDATE messages and the CPU cost against the convergence latency.
children.name: out
children.short-help: Outbound RIB batching: how route changes are grouped and flushed to the peer.

children.description: The container controls which RIB tables Ze maintains, and how the outbound route batching works.
children.name: rib
children.short-help: Route Information Base settings for this peer.

children.description:
An empty list filters nothing, and the ingress and egress rules of RFC 9234 Section 5 still
run. default expands to the set RFC 9234 Section 5 gives the local role. provider sends to
customer and rs-client. customer sends to provider, rs and peer. rs sends to rs-client,
rs-client sends to rs and provider, and peer sends to customer and rs-client. unknown matches a
peer that sent no Role capability, and a peer whose OPEN Ze never recorded.
children.name: export
children.short-help: Controls which destination peer roles may receive routes from this peer

values.name: customer
values.short-help: RFC 9234: Customer (3)

values.name: default
values.short-help: RFC 9234 Section 5 default egress rules for the declared role

values.name: peer
values.short-help: RFC 9234: Peer (4)

values.name: provider
values.short-help: RFC 9234: Provider (0)

values.name: rs
values.short-help: RFC 9234: Route Server (1)

values.name: rs-client
values.short-help: RFC 9234: RS-Client (2)

values.name: unknown
values.short-help: Also send to peers with no role configured

children.description:
Ze sends the role in the Role capability, code 9, and it is the only leaf that makes Ze
send it. RFC 9234 Section 4.2 Table 2 permits provider with customer, rs with rs-client, and
peer with peer. Ze rejects any other pair with a NOTIFICATION of code 2 and subcode 11.
children.name: import
children.short-help: Declares local role and enables RFC 9234 ingress rules (replaces Phase 1 name keyword)

values.name: customer
values.short-help: RFC 9234: Customer (3)

values.name: peer
values.short-help: RFC 9234: Peer (4)

values.name: provider
values.short-help: RFC 9234: Provider (0)

values.name: rs
values.short-help: RFC 9234: Route Server (1)

values.name: rs-client
values.short-help: RFC 9234: RS-Client (2)

children.description:
The default false accepts a peer that sends no Role capability, which RFC 9234 Section 4.2
asks for. true rejects that session with a NOTIFICATION of code 2 and subcode 11. The leaf needs
import beside it, because Ze validates no OPEN for a peer that declares no local role.
children.name: strict
children.short-help: Require peer to send Role capability

children.description:
The container turns on the role rules for this peer. A peer with no role container sends no
Role capability, and Ze accepts whatever role the peer declares.
children.name: role
children.short-help: RFC 9234 BGP Role configuration

children.description: An unset leaf inherits the group value, then the global value.
children.name: invalid
children.short-help: Action Ze applies to a route in the Invalid validation state.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: log-only
values.short-help: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description: An unset leaf inherits the group value, then the global value.
children.name: not-found
children.short-help: Action Ze applies to a route in the NotFound validation state.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: log-only
values.short-help: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description:
A leaf here carries no default, so an unset leaf falls through to the
group value and then to the global value.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Origin-validation action overrides of this peer or group.

children.description: An unset leaf inherits the group value, then the global value.
children.name: invalid
children.short-help: Action Ze applies to a route in the ASPA Invalid path state.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: log-only
values.short-help: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description: An unset leaf inherits the group value, then the global value.
children.name: unknown
children.short-help: Action Ze applies to a route in the ASPA Unknown path state.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: log-only
values.short-help: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description:
invalid names the action of an ASPA Invalid path and unknown that of an ASPA Unknown path.
Neither leaf carries a default, so an unset leaf falls through to the group value and then to the global value.
children.name: action
children.short-help: ASPA path-state action overrides of this peer or group.

children.description: These overrides apply only when ASPA validation is enabled globally.
children.name: aspa
children.short-help: ASPA action overrides for this peer or group.

children.description:
The route carries the RFC 7999 BLACKHOLE community, and a covering VRP allows a
shorter prefix than the route announces.

RFC 7999 Section 3.3 states that an operator MUST ensure origin validation does not
inadvertently block legitimate announcements carrying BLACKHOLE. A blackhole prefix is
as long as possible, usually a /32 or a /128. A ROA for the covering block carries its
maxLength at the aggregate. RFC 6811 then makes the announcement Invalid, and a session
running action invalid reject drops the route before anything can honor it.

The exemption is narrow. It applies only when a covering VRP names the route's own
origin AS and disagrees on nothing but the length. A wrong origin AS stays Invalid,
which is the hijack RFC 6811 exists to catch. A prefix with no covering VRP is NotFound
rather than Invalid, so the exemption never reaches it.

The default is false. Enable it together with the blackhole honor leaf of the peer, on
the same session. On its own it accepts a route it would have rejected, and it discards
nothing.
children.name: blackhole-exempt
children.short-help: Keep a BLACKHOLE route when its only origin-validation fault is the prefix length.

children.description:
Ze resolves every leaf on its own. A leaf set on the peer wins. A leaf that
is unset falls through to the group value, then to the global value.
children.name: rpki
children.short-help: RPKI action overrides of this peer or group.

children.description:
RFC 8669 Section 4 states that a PrefixSID from an EBGP peer outside the SR domain MUST be
discarded, unless the speaker is configured to accept it. The leaf has no effect on IBGP, where Ze
always accepts the attribute.
children.name: accept-srv6-prefix-sid
children.short-help: Accept the BGP Prefix-SID attribute (code 40) with SRv6 TLVs from this EBGP peer.

children.description:
Use the leaf in a VPN design, or in a multi-site design, where the same customer ASN appears at more
than one site.
children.name: as-override
children.short-help: Replace the ASN of the peer with the local ASN in the outbound AS_PATH.

children.description:
Ze sends this value in OPEN in place of the global ASN. Ze keeps the global ASN too,
and local-options decides how the two appear in AS_PATH.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Local AS (overrides global)

children.description:
The two options act in different directions, so each one is set on its own. no-prepend acts inbound:
the local-as is not added to a route received from this peer. replace-as acts outbound: this peer
sees the local-as alone instead of the local-as followed by the globally configured ASN. With
neither option, this peer sees the local-as followed by the globally configured ASN.
children.name: local-options
children.short-help: Modifiers for the local-as behavior of this peer.

values.name: no-prepend
values.short-help: Do not add the local-as to a route received from this peer.

values.name: replace-as
values.short-help: Send the local-as alone toward this peer, without the global ASN.

children.description:
RFC 7705 Section 4.2 'Internal BGP AS Migration'. Set the leaf to the other ASN of the
pair the router runs while it moves from one ASN to another: the local ASN is one of the two
and this leaf is the other. Ze then accepts an OPEN whose My Autonomous System carries either
ASN, and treats the session as native iBGP whichever ASN won. Ze sends the local ASN first and
falls back to this one only after the peer answers Bad Peer AS, which is what keeps two
speakers that both run the mechanism from deadlocking. remote must name one of the two ASNs,
and Ze refuses a config where it names a third. Remove the leaf when the migration ends.
children.name: migration
children.short-help: Second local AS this iBGP session accepts and sends during an AS migration.

children.description:
Ze compares the value with the local ASN. A different value makes the session eBGP,
and an equal value makes it iBGP. That verdict decides the AS_PATH prepend, the auto
next-hop rewrite, and whether Ze sends LOCAL_PREF.
children.name: remote
children.short-help: Peer Autonomous System Number

children.description:
local overrides the global ASN for this session. remote names the peer ASN. Ze compares
the two to decide whether the session is eBGP or iBGP. migration names a second local ASN this
iBGP session also accepts while the router moves from one ASN to another.
children.name: asn
children.short-help: AS number configuration

children.description:
send offers more than one path to the peer. receive accepts more than one path
from the peer. send/receive does both. Ze applies the value to every negotiated family
that carries no family entry of its own.
children.name: direction
children.short-help: Default ADD-PATH direction for all negotiated families.

values.name: receive
values.short-help: Receive multiple paths

values.name: send
values.short-help: Send multiple paths

values.name: send/receive
values.short-help: Both send and receive multiple paths

children.description:
The value replaces the container direction for this family. An absent value
keeps the container direction.
children.name: direction
children.short-help: ADD-PATH direction override for this family.

values.name: receive
values.short-help: Receive ADD-PATH

values.name: send
values.short-help: Send ADD-PATH

values.name: send/receive
values.short-help: Both send and receive ADD-PATH

children.description:
Use a value from 1 through 65535. Omit this leaf to inherit the container limit.
Ze advertises no limit for a disabled or refused ADD-PATH family. This is a request
to the sender, not local receive-side policing.
children.name: limit
children.short-help: Maximum paths per prefix requested from the peer (PATHS-LIMIT capability).

children.description:
enable and disable act on this family alone. require refuses the session when
the peer does not offer ADD-PATH. refuse refuses the session when the peer offers
it. Ze takes the most restrictive mode over the whole list.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: ADD-PATH negotiation mode for this family.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: refuse
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer offers it

values.name: require
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer does not offer it

children.description:
The list key is the family name. An entry with no direction takes the container
direction. Ze skips an entry whose family name is not registered.
children.name: family
children.short-help: Per-family ADD-PATH overrides with optional path count limit.

children.description:
Ze advertises this receive request for each enabled ADD-PATH family. A per-family
limit overrides it. This setting does not enforce a local receive-side limit.
children.name: limit
children.short-help: Default maximum paths per prefix requested from the peer (PATHS-LIMIT).

children.description:
PATHS-LIMIT is draft-abraitis-idr-addpath-paths-limit. The default direction applies to every
negotiated multiprotocol family. A per-family entry overrides the default direction.
children.name: add-path
children.short-help: ADD-PATH capability (RFC 7911), with an optional PATHS-LIMIT.

children.description:
The capability is required for an ASN of more than 65535. Disable it only for a peer that runs a
legacy implementation, which speaks 2-byte ASNs alone. require refuses the session when the
peer does not offer it, and refuse refuses the session when the peer offers it.
children.name: asn4
children.short-help: 4-byte ASN capability mode (RFC 6793): enable, disable, require or refuse.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: refuse
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer offers it

values.name: require
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer does not offer it

children.description:
The capability raises the BGP message size limit from 4096 bytes to 65535 bytes. A large UPDATE that
carries many attributes needs it.
children.name: extended-message
children.short-help: Extended Message capability (RFC 8654).

children.description:
Long-Lived Stale Time in seconds (RFC 9494 Section 3). When this leaf is set, Ze advertises the LLGR
capability (code 71). The maximum value is 16777215, because the field is 24 bits, which is about
194 days. Ze applies the value to every negotiated address family of the peer.
children.name: long-lived-stale-time
children.short-help: Long-Lived Stale Time for the peer, in seconds (RFC 9494 Section 3).

children.description:
The value is what Ze advertises to the peer. It does not set the timer Ze runs when the peer
restarts: that timer takes the Restart Time the peer itself advertised. Ze deletes every stale
route of the peer when that timer expires, unless the peer also negotiated LLGR.
children.name: restart-time
children.short-help:
Restart Time in seconds (RFC 4724 Section 3).
Maximum value is 4095 (12-bit field).

children.description:
The container carries presence, so writing it makes Ze send the Graceful Restart capability,
code 64, to this peer. Ze lists no address family in that capability, because Ze runs the Receiving
Speaker procedures of RFC 4724 and preserves no forwarding state of its own. A container on the peer
replaces the container on the group rather than adding to it.
children.name: graceful-restart
children.short-help: Graceful Restart capability configuration.

children.description:
The capability carries host and domain as two separate strings, and Ze joins neither. Ze
writes the domain after the host, with its own 1-byte length, which is why 255 bytes is the
limit.
children.name: domain
children.short-help: Domain name (max 255 bytes).

children.description:
Ze writes the value with a 1-byte length in front of it, which is why 255 bytes is the
limit. Ze does not read the hostname of the box, so an empty leaf sends an empty string.
children.name: host
children.short-help: System hostname (max 255 bytes).

children.description:
Ze sends the FQDN capability, code 73 of draft-walton-bgp-hostname, in the OPEN message. Ze
sends no capability when host and domain are both empty. A container on the peer replaces the
container on the group rather than adding to it.
children.name: hostname
children.short-help: FQDN capability configuration.

children.description:
The capability advertises that ze accepts IPv6 link-local
next-hops in MP_REACH_NLRI (RFC 2545 Section 3).
children.name: link-local-nexthop
children.short-help: Link-local next-hop capability.

children.description:
Ze takes the most restrictive mode over the whole list, where require wins against
refuse, and refuse wins against enable. enable and require both advertise the family.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Extended next hop negotiation mode

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: refuse
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer offers it

values.name: require
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer does not offer it

children.description: Ze reads ipv4 and ipv6 alone, and it skips an entry that names another value.
children.name: nhafi
children.short-help: Next-hop AFI (e.g. ipv6)

values.name: ipv4
values.short-help: IPv4 (AFI 1)

values.name: ipv6
values.short-help: IPv6 (AFI 2)

children.description:
The list key is the NLRI family, and nhafi is the next-hop AFI. The pair lets an IPv4
route carry an IPv6 next hop, so an IPv6-only session can hold IPv4 reachability.
children.name: nexthop
children.short-help: Extended Next Hop capability (RFC 8950)

children.description:
The capability lets the peer request a full re-advertisement of the routes, without a session
teardown.
children.name: route-refresh
children.short-help: Route Refresh capability (RFC 2918).

children.description:
enable is the default, and Ze sends the capability. disable sends none. Ze treats require
as enable and refuse as disable: the plugin decides only whether to send code 75, and it holds
the peer to nothing. So a peer that sends no Software Version stays up under require, and a peer
that sends one stays up under refuse. Set the leaf on the peer to override the group value.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Capability negotiation mode.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; no enforcement

values.name: refuse
values.short-help: Do not advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer offers it

values.name: require
values.short-help: Advertise the capability; refuse the session when the peer does not offer it

children.description:
The container carries presence, so writing it makes Ze send the capability of
draft-abraitis-bgp-version-capability to this peer. The value is the fixed string Ze/0.1.0, and no
leaf changes it. A container on the peer replaces the container on the group rather than adding to
it.
children.name: software-version
children.short-help: Software Version capability (code 75).

children.description:
Every capability here takes four modes. enable advertises it. disable does not advertise
it. require advertises it and refuses the session when the peer does not offer it. refuse does
not advertise it and refuses the session when the peer offers it.
children.name: capability
children.short-help: BGP capability negotiation

children.description: The default is the router-id. Ze prepends the cluster ID to CLUSTER_LIST on a reflected route.
children.name: cluster-id
children.short-help: Override the cluster ID for route reflection (RFC 4456 Section 7).

children.description:
The default is all, which sends every community type. Name an individual type to control the set.
none suppresses every community attribute.
children.name: send
children.short-help: Community types Ze includes in an outbound UPDATE.

values.name: all
values.short-help: Send all community types (default)

values.name: extended
values.short-help: Send extended communities (type 16, RFC 4360)

values.name: large
values.short-help: Send large communities (type 32, RFC 8092)

values.name: none
values.short-help: Suppress all community attributes

values.name: standard
values.short-help: Send standard communities (type 8, RFC 1997)

children.description:
The container holds the send leaf-list alone. send names the community types Ze puts in an
outbound UPDATE, and it acts on no inbound message.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Community attribute control for this session

children.description:
A member peer that states no domain-name of its own takes this value. Ze reads the leaf after
capability > hostname > domain and replaces that value with it. The capability writes a 1-byte length
in front of the domain name, which is the 255-byte limit. Write capability > hostname > domain in a new
config: ze exabgp migrate produces that spelling and never this one.
children.name: domain-name
children.short-help: Legacy: Domain name for FQDN capability (group default).

children.description: The default route is 0.0.0.0/0 for IPv4, and ::/0 for IPv6.
children.name: default-originate
children.short-help: Originate the default route to this peer for this address family.

children.description:
When the filter rejects, Ze does not send the default route. An empty value, or an absent leaf,
originates the default route without a condition.
children.name: default-originate-filter
children.short-help: Named filter that must accept before Ze originates the default route.

children.description:
enable advertises the family. disable does not advertise it. require advertises it and
refuses the session when the peer does not offer it. ignore advertises the family and
relaxes the UPDATE check. Ze then drops an UPDATE that names a family the two peers did
not negotiate, and the session stays up.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Address family negotiation mode

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Disable this address family

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Enable this address family

values.name: ignore
values.short-help: Ignore this address family

values.name: require
values.short-help: Require this address family

children.description:
offered counts wire events. Every announcement raises the count, and every withdrawal lowers it. A
peer that re-announces a prefix to change an attribute raises the count again, although it holds the
same route. The count can therefore be more than the maximum. Ze then drops every later announce of
this family, until the peer withdraws enough prefixes. installed counts the set of prefixes Ze
currently holds for this family, which no re-announcement and no unmatched withdrawal can move.
installed keeps one entry per prefix for this family, so its memory is the size of what the peer
sends, up to the maximum. Neither value is the size of the RIB, because import policy can reject a
counted prefix.
children.name: count
children.short-help: Which prefixes the count compared against maximum holds.

values.name: installed
values.short-help: Count the prefixes this family holds now.

values.name: offered
values.short-help: Count every announcement the peer sends, repeats included.

children.description:
The wait doubles on each repeat teardown, up to one hour. 0 keeps the peer down. See the reconnect
leaf.
children.name: idle-timeout
children.short-help: Seconds to wait before reconnect after this family stopped the session.

children.description:
The NOTIFICATION data carries the AFI, the SAFI, and this value as the upper bound
(RFC 4486 Section 4). The count leaf decides which prefixes the count holds.
children.name: maximum
children.short-help: Hard maximum number of prefixes accepted

children.description: No value means timer when idle-timeout is more than 0, and never when idle-timeout is 0.
children.name: reconnect
children.short-help: What the peer does after this family stopped the session.

values.name: backoff
values.short-help: Reconnect on the usual connect backoff of the peer.

values.name: never
values.short-help: Keep the peer down. An operator restarts it.

values.name: timer
values.short-help: Reconnect after idle-timeout seconds.

children.description:
The default is true, and an absent value also reads as true. With false Ze keeps
the session up and drops the UPDATE that crossed the maximum.
children.name: teardown
children.short-help: Tear down session when prefix maximum exceeded (false = warn only)

children.description:
ze:hidden keeps the leaf out of the CLI completion. The peer command reports the
date, and it marks the peer prefix-stale when the date is more than 180 days old.
children.name: updated
children.short-help: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) when prefix maximum was last updated from PeeringDB. Hidden leaf.

children.description:
Crossing the threshold raises a metric and a login-banner warning, and it leaves
the session up. Ze refuses a warning value that is not less than maximum.
children.name: warning
children.short-help: Warning threshold. Defaults to 90% of maximum when not set.

children.description:
The limit is the defense against a peer that floods the RIB. When the count crosses
maximum, Ze sends a Cease NOTIFICATION with subcode 1, Maximum Number of Prefixes Reached
(RFC 4486).
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Prefix limit configuration for this address family

children.description:
Ze advertises one Multiprotocol Extensions capability per entry (RFC 4760). A list with no
entry sends no such capability. Each entry also carries the prefix limit and the
default-originate switch of that family.
children.name: family
children.short-help: Address families to negotiate

children.description:
A member peer that states no host-name of its own takes this value. Ze reads the leaf after
capability > hostname > host and replaces that value with it. The capability writes a 1-byte length
in front of the host name, which is the 255-byte limit. Write capability > hostname > host in a new
config: ze exabgp migrate produces that spelling and never this one.
children.name: host-name
children.short-help: Legacy: Host name for FQDN capability (group default).

children.description:
The IRR filter queries an IRR database for the prefixes of one AS-SET.
This leaf names that AS-SET. If this leaf is empty, Ze reads the remote ASN of the
peer and discovers the AS-SET from PeeringDB.
children.name: as-set
children.short-help: Explicit AS-SET name for the IRR prefix lookup.

children.description:
disable takes the peer out of the resolution, so Ze runs no whois query and no PeeringDB
query for it. The other peers of the same remote ASN keep their list.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable or disable IRR filtering for this peer.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Disable IRR filtering for this peer.

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Enable IRR filtering for this peer (default).

children.description:
Ze resolves the prefixes of a peer only when the peer asked for it. A filter chain that names
bgp-filter-irr asks for it, and so does an as-set written here. A peer that states no remote ASN is
never resolved.
children.name: irr
children.short-help: Per-peer IRR filter settings.

children.description:
