the shorter path is preferred.
children.name: as-path
children.short-help: AS_PATH segments prepended to the route, as space-separated ASNs.

children.description: The flag signals that aggregation formed the route, and that AS_PATH information was lost.
children.name: atomic-aggregate
children.short-help: ATOMIC_AGGREGATE flag (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.6).

children.description: The list carries an attribute that no named field covers.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: Raw BGP attributes in hex encoding, as flags:type:hex-value.

children.description:
The attribute carries an MPLS label index for Segment Routing. A node can therefore advertise its
SID without a per-prefix label allocation.
children.name: bgp-prefix-sid
children.short-help: Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 8669).

children.description:
The attribute carries SRv6 SID information for IPv6 Segment Routing, and it includes the SRv6 L3
Service TLVs.
children.name: bgp-prefix-sid-srv6
children.short-help: SRv6 Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 9252).

children.description: Each reflector prepends its cluster ID. The list detects a loop between reflectors.
children.name: cluster-list
children.short-help: CLUSTER_LIST for route reflection (RFC 4456).

children.description:
The format is AS:value, for example 65000:100. A well-known name is also accepted, such as no-export
or no-advertise.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Standard BGP communities (RFC 1997).

children.description: An extended community carries a route target, a site-of-origin, or VPN semantics.
children.name: extended-community
children.short-help: Extended communities (RFC 4360). The format is type:admin:value.

children.description:
Ze accepts a decimal number from 0 to 1048575, which is the 20-bit label field. It accepts no keyword.
Write the labels leaf-list for a stack of more than one label.
children.name: label
children.short-help: MPLS label value for a labeled unicast route (RFC 3107). The value is a number.

children.description:
The list is an ordered sequence from bottom to top. Ze keeps a repeated label, and it does not
deduplicate the stack.
children.name: labels
children.short-help: MPLS label stack for a multi-label route (RFC 8277).

children.description:
Each value is three 32-bit numbers separated by colons, which is 12 octets on the wire. The global part
holds a 4-byte ASN, which a standard community of RFC 1997 cannot hold.
children.name: large-community
children.short-help: Large BGP communities (RFC 8092). Format: global:local1:local2. Supports 4-byte ASNs natively.

children.description: LOCAL_PREF has a meaning inside a single AS alone (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.5). The default is 100.
children.name: local-preference
children.short-help: LOCAL_PREF value for iBGP best-path selection. The higher value wins.

children.description: MED influences the inbound path selection that an external peer makes (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.4).
children.name: med
children.short-help: Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED). The lower value is preferred.

children.description:
self resolves at send time to the local address of the session, so each peer reads its
own next hop. An IP address reaches every peer of the block unchanged. Ze refuses an IPv6
link-local address here, because RFC 2545 Section 3 puts the global address in that field.
children.name: next-hop
children.short-help: Next hop address or 'self'

values.name: self
values.short-help: Resolve the next hop at send time to the local address of each session.

children.description:
RFC 4271 Section 4.3 gives three values. igp is reachability interior to the
originating AS. egp is reachability learned through the EGP protocol. incomplete is
reachability learned by some other means, for example a redistributed static route.
children.name: origin
children.short-help: ORIGIN attribute (RFC 4271 Section 4.3)

values.name: egp
values.short-help: Exterior Gateway Protocol

values.name: igp
values.short-help: Interior Gateway Protocol

values.name: incomplete
values.short-help: Incomplete origin

children.description:
The reflector sets the attribute to the router ID of the originating router. The attribute prevents
a loop.
children.name: originator-id
children.short-help: ORIGINATOR_ID for route reflection (RFC 4456).

children.description: The identifier separates the several paths that one peer sends for the same prefix.
children.name: path-information
children.short-help: ADD-PATH path identifier (RFC 7911).

children.description: Ze prepends the Route Distinguisher to the prefix, which makes a unique VPN route.
children.name: rd
children.short-help: Route Distinguisher (RFC 4364). The format is ASN:nn or IP:nn.

children.description: The format is /length. For example, /24 splits a /16 into 256 prefixes of /24.
children.name: split
children.short-help: Split one prefix into more-specific prefixes for the announcement.

children.description:
Every NLRI of the block takes the same attributes. To announce two prefixes that carry
different attributes, write two update blocks.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: Path attributes for routes in this block

children.description:
The list carries no key, so the CLI and the web UI show this label in place of one. The
label reaches no BGP message.
children.name: name
children.short-help: Optional label for this update block (display only)

children.description:
The form is an operation keyword, then an optional rd and label, then one or more prefixes. add, del and
eor are the operation keywords, and one of them is required. A block that carries del or eor announces nothing
at config load.
children.name: content
children.short-help: Operation, qualifiers, and payload

children.description:
Every entry takes the attribute block of the update block. The key is the family name, and
content carries the operation keyword and the prefixes. An update block that declares no nlri
entry is refused at config load.
children.name: nlri
children.short-help: Routes this update block announces, one entry for each address family.

children.description:
request bgp watchdog announce <name> announces every route that carries the name, and request bgp
watchdog withdraw <name> withdraws them. Ze skips a block whose name is empty.
children.name: name
children.short-help: Watchdog group name

children.description:
The bgp-watchdog plugin reads the PRESENCE of the leaf and not its value, so withdraw false starts every
route of the block withdrawn exactly as withdraw true does. Delete the leaf to announce the routes as soon as
the session reaches Established. request bgp watchdog announce <name> announces a withdrawn route.
children.name: withdraw
children.short-help: Start in withdrawn state (default true)

children.description:
The bgp-watchdog plugin owns every route of the block, so the BGP engine holds none of
them as a static route. The plugin sends a route that is not withdrawn when the session reaches
Established.
children.name: watchdog
children.short-help: Watchdog-controlled route - held until 'bgp watchdog announce <name>'

children.description:
Ze announces every route of the block to the peers the block applies to. The block is written
at the global level, the group level, and the peer level, and the three accumulate.
children.name: update
children.short-help: Native Ze route announcements

children.description:
A standalone peer takes the global level and its own level, so no group value reaches it. The
list key is the peer name, and connection/remote/ip must be unique over every peer.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: BGP peer configuration (standalone, no group)

children.description:
An absent leaf leaves the upper bound open, so a filter that states neither bound accepts
every route. Ze counts every ASN of the path, so a member of an AS_SET counts as one hop.
children.name: max
children.short-help:
Maximum allowed AS-path length (inclusive).
Routes with longer paths are rejected.

children.description:
An absent leaf leaves the lower bound open. A route that carries no AS_PATH counts 0
hops. min 1 therefore rejects a route Ze originated, and a route an iBGP peer sent with an
empty path.
children.name: min
children.short-help:
Minimum required AS-path length (inclusive).
Routes with shorter paths are rejected.

children.description:
Ze rejects a route whose AS-path length falls outside the
configured min..max range. Both min and max are optional,
and an omitted bound is open.
children.name: as-path-length
children.short-help: Named AS-path length filter instance.

children.description:
The first entry whose pattern matches decides the UPDATE, and no later entry is read. A
route whose path matches no entry is rejected, so a list needs no closing reject entry.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Action applied when this entry's regex matches.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Accept a route whose AS-path matches.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Reject a route whose AS-path matches.

children.description:
Ze matches each entry against the space-separated AS-path string,
in the configured order. The first entry that matches wins.
children.name: entry
children.short-help: One regex entry of the ordered list.

children.description:
Each list holds an ordered set of regex entries. Ze evaluates the
entries in order, and the first match wins. No match is an implicit deny, so Ze rejects
the route.
children.name: as-path-list
children.short-help: Named AS-path regex filter instance.

children.description:
The first entry whose community the route carries decides the UPDATE, and no later
entry is read. A route that carries none of the listed communities is rejected, so a list
needs no closing reject entry.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Action applied when this community is found in the route.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Accept routes containing this community

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Reject routes containing this community

children.description:
Ze reads the one attribute the leaf names. An entry of type standard therefore does
not see a value that sits in the LARGE COMMUNITIES attribute. Write one entry for each
attribute the route can carry the value in.
children.name: type
children.short-help: Which community attribute type to check.

values.name: extended
values.short-help: Match in extended community attribute (type 16)

values.name: large
values.short-help: Match in large community attribute (type 32)

values.name: standard
values.short-help: Match in standard community attribute (type 8)

children.description:
Ze reads the entries in order, and the first match wins.
An entry checks whether the named community value is
present in the route's community attributes.
children.name: entry
children.short-help: Ordered match entry, checked against the route's community attributes.

children.description:
Each list holds an ordered set of match entries. Ze reads
the entries in order, and the first match wins. No match is
an implicit deny, so the route is rejected.
children.name: community-match
children.short-help: Named community match filter instance.

children.description:
remove strips the MP_REACH NLRI and the MP_UNREACH NLRI of the
matched family from the UPDATE, on import and on export. If that removal empties the
UPDATE, Ze drops the whole UPDATE for that peer.

tear-down sends a BGP NOTIFICATION that carries the Cease code and the Connection
Rejected subcode, then closes the session. tear-down acts on import only.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Action to apply when the family matches.

values.name: remove
values.short-help: Strip the MP_REACH NLRI and the MP_UNREACH NLRI of the matched family.

values.name: tear-down
values.short-help: Close the session with a BGP NOTIFICATION when a received UPDATE carries the family.

children.description:
Ze treats an UPDATE with no MP_REACH attribute and no MP_UNREACH
attribute as ipv4/unicast.
children.name: family
children.short-help: Address family to match, for example ipv4/flowspec.

children.description:
One instance matches one family, because family holds one value and is mandatory. A chain that
must catch two families names two instances.
children.name: family-filter
children.short-help: Named address-family filter instance.

children.description:
Ze reads the AS-SET of a peer from the PeeringDB API when the
as-set leaf is empty. Set this leaf to the URL of a mock server to test the IRR filter
without a query to the public PeeringDB service.
children.name: peeringdb-url
children.short-help: Base URL of the PeeringDB API that Ze queries.

children.description:
Ze re-queries every enrolled AS-SET on this period. The first query runs in the background
at startup, so a slow IRR server never blocks the start of Ze. A failed query leaves the prefix
list of the last query in force.
children.name: refresh-interval
children.short-help: Seconds between automatic IRR re-queries.

children.description:
Ze speaks whois to the server and adds port 43 when the value carries no port. A query that
gets no answer in 10 seconds fails, and the prefix list of the last query stays in force.
children.name: server
children.short-help: IRR whois server hostname or host:port.

children.description:
Ze binds the address on the whois connection only. The PeeringDB query does not read the
leaf. When the leaf is absent, the kernel picks the source address of the route to the server.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IP address for outbound IRR whois connections.

children.description:
The container holds the IRR server, the PeeringDB endpoint and the refresh period. One
resolution serves every peer of the same remote ASN, so two peers of one ASN cost one query.
children.name: irr
children.short-help: Global IRR filtering settings.

children.description:
The default is 0, which rejects the route on the first
occurrence (RFC 4271 Section 9).
children.name: allow-own-as
children.short-help: Own-AS occurrences permitted in AS_PATH before ze rejects the route.

children.description:
When this leaf is unset, ze uses the BGP Router ID
(RFC 4456 Section 7).
children.name: cluster-id
children.short-help: Override Router ID for CLUSTER_LIST loop detection.

children.description:
The instance configures AS loop detection and cluster-list
loop detection, for each peer that references it.
children.name: loop-detection
children.short-help: Named loop detection filter instance.

children.description:
Ze runs the operation only on a route that already carries an AIGP TLV. A route with
none is left alone, because RFC 7311 Section 3.4.1 forbids Ze to add the attribute.
children.name: aigp
children.short-help: Decrement AIGP metric by this value.

children.description:
A route that carries no LOCAL_PREF counts as 100 before the subtraction. A decrement
larger than the current value writes 0 rather than wrapping.
children.name: local-preference
children.short-help: Decrement LOCAL_PREF by this value.

children.description:
A route that carries no MULTI_EXIT_DISC counts as 0, so the result is 0 and Ze writes a
metric the route did not have. Use del med to remove the attribute instead.
children.name: med
children.short-help: Decrement MED by this value.

children.description:
Ze subtracts the stated value from the current value of the
attribute. The result floors at 0, so it never underflows. decrement is mutually
exclusive with set for the same attribute.
children.name: decrement
children.short-help: Attributes to decrement on a matching route.

children.description:
RFC 4271 Section 5.1.4 requires a mechanism, based on local
configuration, that removes MULTI_EXIT_DISC from a route. The same section requires the
removal to happen before the route reaches Decision Process phase 1 and phase 2. The
del med operation is that mechanism, so it applies on an IMPORT chain only, and the
route enters the decision process with no metric. Ze refuses del med on an export chain
and writes a log line, because Section 9.1.2.2 states that a comparison on
MULTI_EXIT_DISC followed by advertisement without it causes route loops. del med is
mutually exclusive with set med, increment med and decrement med. Ze already keeps a
metric received from one neighboring AS off another one with no configuration (RFC 4271
Section 5.1.4), so del med is for the operator who wants the metric removed from the
route itself.
children.name: med
children.short-help: Remove the MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute (RFC 4271 type 4) from the route.

children.description:
Ze applies only the leaves that are present in this container,
and keeps every other attribute unchanged.
children.name: del
children.short-help: Attributes Ze deletes from a matching route.

children.description:
Ze runs the operation only on a route that already carries an AIGP TLV, and creates
none. RFC 7311 Section 3.4.1 forbids a speaker to add the attribute to a route whose path
leaves the AIGP domain. Section 4.1 removes a route with no AIGP from the decision rather
than scoring it.
children.name: aigp
children.short-help: Increment AIGP metric by this value.

children.description:
A route that carries no LOCAL_PREF counts as 100, which is the value FRR and BIRD use
for a route with none. RFC 4271 Section 9.1.1 leaves that number to local policy.
children.name: local-preference
children.short-help: Increment LOCAL_PREF by this value.

children.description:
A route that carries no MULTI_EXIT_DISC counts as 0, which RFC 4271 Section 9.1.2.2
gives as the value of an absent metric. The result therefore equals the increment.
children.name: med
children.short-help: Increment MED by this value.

children.description:
Ze adds the stated value to the current value of the attribute.
The result saturates at the uint32 maximum, 4294967295. increment is mutually exclusive
with set for the same attribute.
children.name: increment
children.short-help: Attributes to increment on a matching route.

children.description:
The COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 1997, type 8. The value takes
the form ASN:VAL, for example 65001:666, or a well-known name. The well-known names are
blackhole, no-export, no-advertise, no-export-subconfed and nopeer. The two spellings
of a well-known value are equivalent, so 65535:666 and blackhole select the same
community. RFC 7999 registers that community, and RFC 7999 Section 4 names it with that
suggested keyword.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Apply only to a route whose COMMUNITIES attribute carries this value.

children.description:
The EXTENDED COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 4360, type 16. The
value takes the form target:ASN:NN or origin:ASN:NN, or it is a hex string.
children.name: extended-community
children.short-help: Apply only to a route whose EXTENDED COMMUNITIES attribute carries this value.

children.description:
The LARGE COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 8092, type 32. The value
takes the form GA:LD1:LD2, for example 65001:100:200.
children.name: large-community
children.short-help: Apply only to a route whose LARGE COMMUNITIES attribute carries this value.

children.description:
A route that meets none of the stated values passes through
unchanged, and Ze does not reject it. The chain drops a rejected route, and a
conditional modifier exists so that the routes it does not touch keep flowing. An
absent match container applies the operations to every route that reaches the modifier.
The values across the three leaf-lists are alternatives, so one value present in the
route satisfies the condition.
children.name: match
children.short-help: Condition a route meets before the operations apply.

children.description:
Ze prepends the local-as of the peer, which the session config
holds. The range 1 to 32 stops the path from growing without a limit.
children.name: as-path-prepend
children.short-help: Prepend the local AS to AS_PATH this many times.

children.description:
Ze adds the values to the COMMUNITIES attribute of RFC 1997 and keeps every community
already on the route. Ze reads each value at config load, and refuses the modifier when one
does not parse.
children.name: community-add
children.short-help: Standard community values to add (ASN:VAL format).

children.description:
Ze removes only the values named here, and keeps every other community of the route.
A value the route does not carry costs nothing. Ze reads each value at config load, and
refuses the modifier when one does not parse.
children.name: community-remove
children.short-help: Standard community values to remove (ASN:VAL format).

children.description:
The EXTENDED COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 4360, type 16, and each value is 8 bytes.
target names a Route Target and origin names a Route Origin. A hex string writes the 8 bytes
Ze has no keyword for.
children.name: extended-community-add
children.short-help: Extended community values to add (target:ASN:NN or hex).

children.description:
Ze removes only the values named here, and leaves the standard and large communities of
the route untouched. A value the route does not carry costs nothing.
children.name: extended-community-remove
children.short-help: Extended community values to remove (target:ASN:NN or hex).

children.description:
The LARGE COMMUNITIES attribute is RFC 8092, type 32, and it carries three 4-byte
fields. A 4-byte ASN therefore fits, which a standard community cannot hold.
children.name: large-community-add
children.short-help: Large community values to add (GA:LD1:LD2 format).

children.description:
Ze removes only the values named here, and leaves the standard and extended communities
of the route untouched. A value the route does not carry costs nothing.
children.name: large-community-remove
children.short-help: Large community values to remove (GA:LD1:LD2 format).

children.description:
Ze replaces the value the route carried. RFC 4271 Section 5.1.5 forbids the attribute
in an UPDATE to an external peer, so the value serves the local decision process and the
internal peers. The leaf is mutually exclusive with increment local-preference and decrement
local-preference.
children.name: local-preference
children.short-help: Set LOCAL_PREF attribute (RFC 4271 type 5).

children.description:
Ze replaces the metric the route carried, and writes one on a route that carried none.
The leaf is mutually exclusive with del med, increment med and decrement med, and Ze refuses
a modifier that carries two of them.
children.name: med
children.short-help: Set MULTI_EXIT_DISC attribute (RFC 4271 type 4).

children.description:
NEXT_HOP is RFC 4271 type 3, and it carries an IPv4 address
only. An IPv6 next-hop travels in the MP_REACH attribute instead, so this leaf does not
set one.
children.name: next-hop
children.short-help: Set the NEXT_HOP attribute of the route.

children.description:
The decision process reads the attribute at step 3, after LOCAL_PREF and the AS_PATH
length. igp wins over egp, and egp wins over incomplete. Ze replaces whatever the route
carried.
children.name: origin
children.short-help: Set ORIGIN attribute (RFC 4271 type 1).

values.name: egp
values.short-help: The route came from the retired EGP protocol.

values.name: igp
values.short-help: The route started inside the local AS.

values.name: incomplete
values.short-help: The route came from another source, such as redistribution.

children.description:
Ze applies only the leaves that are present in this container,
and keeps every other attribute unchanged.
children.name: set
children.short-help: Attributes Ze sets on a matching route.

children.description:
Ze modifies only the declared leaves, and keeps every undeclared
attribute unchanged. One modifier can change several attributes.
children.name: modify
children.short-help: Named route attribute modifier instance.

children.description:
The first entry that matches a route prefix decides it, and no later entry is read for
that prefix. A prefix that matches no entry is rejected, so a list needs no closing reject
entry.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Action applied when this entry matches a route prefix.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Accept route prefixes matching this entry.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Reject route prefixes matching this entry.

children.description:
Ze refuses a value of more than 32 on an IPv4 entry, and more than 128 on an IPv6
entry. Ze also refuses a ge greater than the le of the same entry. Write 0.0.0.0/0 with ge 8
and le 24 to accept every route between /8 and /24.
children.name: ge
children.short-help:
Minimum match length (greater-than-or-equal).
Defaults to the prefix length of this entry.

children.description:
The default accepts every length inside the entry, so an entry with no le and no ge
matches the prefix and everything under it. Ze refuses a value greater than the family
maximum rather than letting the entry match nothing.
children.name: le
children.short-help:
Maximum match length (less-than-or-equal).
Defaults to 32 for IPv4 or 128 for IPv6.

children.description:
Ze judges each prefix of an UPDATE on its own. An UPDATE whose prefixes are all accepted
passes unchanged, and one whose prefixes are all rejected is dropped. A mixed UPDATE is
rewritten to carry the accepted prefixes only. An UPDATE that carries no prefix is accepted.
children.name: entry
children.short-help: Ordered match entry. First match wins per route prefix.

children.description:
Each list holds an ordered set of match entries. Ze evaluates
the entries in order, and the first match wins. A route prefix
that matches no entry is denied.
children.name: prefix-list
children.short-help: Named prefix-list filter instance.

children.description:
The keyword is the union of the other three, so it rejects the ASN wherever it sits. The
reject log line still names which of the three caught the route.
children.name: anywhere
children.short-help: Reject these ASNs at any position: direct, transit and origin together.

children.description:
The position is the leading run of tokens equal to the ASN of the sending peer, so four
prepends are one direct position. On export no ASN is direct, because the filter input carries
the destination peer rather than the sender. A path that starts with another ASN is a leak, and
direct does not catch it.
children.name: direct
children.short-help: Reject these ASNs where they are the peer we are talking to, prepends collapsed.

children.description:
The keyword covers transit and origin together. It is the leaf an operator writes for RFC
7454 Section 9. The route reached you through the ASN, and a direct session with that ASN is
still fine. On export the sender is unknown, so indirect covers the whole path.
children.name: indirect
children.short-help: Reject these ASNs anywhere they are NOT the peer we are talking to.

children.description:
The completion of the leaf offers a curated table of transit-free networks, and that
table constrains nothing. Every ASN the type admits stays valid, and an ASN the table never
held is accepted with no warning. show bgp reject-asn known transit-free prints the table.
children.name: asn
children.short-help: The ASNs this position rejects.

children.description:
Ze counts the positions from us, and 1 is the ASN we are talking to. A run of consecutive
identical ASNs counts once, so a peer cannot move your rule by a prepend. The keyword cuts
across the other five, because an ASN at position 2 CAN also be transit.
children.name: nth
children.short-help: Reject the listed ASNs at one collapsed position of the AS_PATH.

children.description:
The last ASN of the path announced the route. The leading run of the sender wins over that
last position, so a lone ASN sent by the peer that owns it is direct rather than the origin.
children.name: origin
children.short-help: Reject these ASNs where they are the last ASN of the AS_PATH.

children.description:
No position applies to a pattern. Ze matches it against the flat path, so a pattern reaches
an ASN inside an AS_SET and meets no bracket. The 512-character bound is the bound
bgp-filter-aspath applies to a regex. Ze reads the patterns only when no position matched.
children.name: regex
children.short-help: Go RE2 patterns matched against the whole space-separated AS_PATH string.

children.description:
A token is transit when it sits neither inside the leading run of the sender nor at the
end of the path. Ze gives every token exactly one of direct, transit and origin.
children.name: transit
children.short-help: Reject these ASNs where they sit past the peer and are not the last ASN of the AS_PATH.

children.description:
Every ASN written under the list is looked for in the AS_PATH of the route. The keyword it
sits under decides which positions reject it. The list is an unordered reject set, so any keyword
that matches rejects the route and no keyword wins over another. Ze reads the positions first and
the patterns after them.
children.name: reject-asn
children.short-help: Named list of ASNs rejected by their position in the AS_PATH.

children.description:
RFC 6996 Section 5 gives the ranges, which are 64512 to 65534 and 4200000000 to
4294967294. An absent leaf strips each of those ASNs, so the path loses one hop for each.
peer-as writes the ASN of the peer in its place, so the path keeps its length.
children.name: replace-with
children.short-help: Replacement mode. When absent, Private Use ASNs are stripped.

values.name: peer-as
values.short-help: Replace Private Use ASNs with the neighbor peer ASN.

children.description:
Ze rewrites AS_PATH and AS4_PATH, and the filter runs on an import chain and on an export
chain. A path that carries no Private Use ASN passes through unchanged.
children.name: remove-private-as
children.short-help: Named action filter that removes RFC 6996 Private Use ASNs.

children.description:
Each filter type is a list that its plugin adds through an augment. A peer filter chain references a
filter instance by name.
children.name: policy
children.short-help: Named filter definitions for the route policy framework.

children.description:
The count covers every address family of the peer. show bgp rib status answers it
as the in value under route-counts, where a family filter scopes the number to
one family.
children.name: route-count
children.short-help: Number of routes from this peer.

children.description:
One entry for each peer that holds a route, keyed by the peer address. show bgp rib
status answers the same numbers under route-counts, which carries an in value and an out
value for each peer address.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: Per-peer Adj-RIB-In.

children.description:
RFC 4271 Section 3.2 states that the Adj-RIBs-In "contains unprocessed routing information that has
been advertised to the local BGP speaker by its peers". show bgp rib received reports those
routes, and clear bgp rib in <peer> discards the routes of one peer. No code answers a read of
this subtree.
children.name: adj-rib-in
children.short-help: Routes received from peers.

children.description:
The count covers every address family of the peer. show bgp rib status answers it
as the out value under route-counts, where a family filter scopes the number to
one family.
children.name: route-count
children.short-help: Number of routes to this peer.

children.description:
One entry for each peer that holds a route, keyed by the peer address. show bgp rib
status answers the same numbers under route-counts, which carries an in value and an out
value for each peer address.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: Per-peer Adj-RIB-Out.

children.description:
RFC 4271 Section 3.2 states that the Adj-RIBs-Out "stores information the local BGP speaker
selected for advertisement to its peers". show bgp rib sent reports those routes. No code
answers a read of this subtree.
children.name: adj-rib-out
children.short-help: Routes sent to peers.

children.description:
The subtree is read-only, so the CLI refuses set on every node under it. No code answers a
read of it today. show bgp rib status reports the live per-peer counts, and show bgp rib
reports the routes. request bgp rib inject and request bgp rib withdraw change what the RIB
holds.
children.name: rib
children.short-help: RIB plugin state and operations.

children.description:
Per-source-peer worker channel capacity. The ze.bgp.route-server.worker-queue-size environment
variable overrides this value.
children.name: worker-queue-size
children.short-help: Worker channel capacity per source peer, overridden by ze.bgp.route-server.worker-queue-size.

children.description:
The route server forwards an UPDATE from one client to every other client. Each source peer
gets its own worker, and the worker stops after 5 seconds with no work. A peer joins the client set
with the rs-client leaf of its session, not with this container.
children.name: route-server
children.short-help: Route server plugin tuning parameters

children.description:
RFC 6286 Section 2.1 defines the BGP Identifier as a 4-octet, unsigned, non-zero integer. Ze
therefore rejects 0.0.0.0. A peer that implements RFC 6286 Section 2.2 answers an OPEN that carries
0.0.0.0 with Bad BGP Identifier.
children.name: router-id
children.short-help: BGP Router ID for this speaker. The leaf is required.

children.description:
The default is reject, which excludes the route from the Adj-RIB-In and
the decision process.
children.name: invalid
children.short-help: Action Ze applies to a route in the Invalid validation state.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: log-only
values.short-help: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description: The default is accept, which keeps the route and writes no log line.
children.name: not-found
children.short-help: Action Ze applies to a route in the NotFound validation state.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: log-only
values.short-help: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description:
RFC 6811 Section 3 makes the action of each validation state
configurable by the operator.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Global origin-validation actions.

children.description:
The default is log-only, which keeps the route, marks it with its
state, and writes a log line.
children.name: invalid
children.short-help: Action Ze applies to a route in the ASPA Invalid path state.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: log-only
values.short-help: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description: The default is accept, which keeps the route and writes no log line.
children.name: unknown
children.short-help: Action Ze applies to a route in the ASPA Unknown path state.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Keep the route and write no log line.

values.name: log-only
values.short-help: Keep the route, marked with its state, and write a log line.

values.name: reject
values.short-help: Exclude the route from the Adj-RIB-In and the decision process.

children.description:
invalid holds the action of an ASPA Invalid path and unknown that of an ASPA Unknown path. Both
apply only while aspa validation is true. A peer or a group overrides each leaf.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Global action Ze applies for each ASPA path state.

children.description: Ze reads the ASPA records over version 2 of the RTR protocol.
children.name: validation
children.short-help: Verify the AS path of a route against the ASPA records.

children.description:
validation turns the verification on and its default is false. Ze reads an ASPA record over
version 2 of the RTR protocol alone. A session Ze downgrades to version 1 carries none. Ze refuses an ASPA PDU
on a version 1 session as a protocol violation. action holds the action of each path state, and a peer or a
group overrides those two leaves.
children.name: aspa
children.short-help: AS_PATH verification against the ASPA records, and the action of each result.

children.description:
Ze opens a TCP connection to this port on the cache server. The default
is 323.
children.name: port
children.short-help: TCP port of the RTR cache server.

children.description:
Ze runs a session to every cache server at the same time and selects none of them, so the value
changes no behavior today. show bgp rpki status reports it for each server.
children.name: preference
children.short-help: Preference of this cache server.

children.description:
Set this leaf when the RTR connection MUST leave the box from one
specific local address.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IP address of an outbound RTR connection.

children.description:
The list key is the address, which is an IP address or a hostname. Ze opens one RTR session to
every entry at the same time, and merges what the entries send into one cache. A second entry gives redundancy.
Each entry carries the port, the preference and the source address. An empty list leaves validation off.
children.name: cache-server
children.short-help: RTR cache servers Ze reads the validated ROA and ASPA records from.

children.description:
The default is 30 seconds. A longer timeout holds a route in the pending
state for longer.
children.name: validation-timeout
children.short-help: Fail-open timeout of a route whose validation is pending.

children.description:
The container carries presence. Ze validates a route only when cache-server holds at least one
entry, so an empty container validates nothing. The container also holds the validation timeout, the
origin-validation actions, and the ASPA block. A peer and a group override an action leaf of their own. Neither
can name a cache server, because the RTR transport is global.
children.name: rpki
children.short-help: RPKI origin validation of a received route (RFC 6811).

children.description:
The default is false, which enforces AS-wide uniqueness: Ze rejects the second OPEN with Bad BGP
Identifier. RFC 6286 Section 2.1 makes AS-wide uniqueness a SHOULD alone, so a shared identifier is
conformant. Set the leaf true when the duplication is intentional, for example one anycast speaker
(AS112) that peers over both IPv4 and IPv6 with the same router-id. When the leaf is true, Ze skips
the AS-wide uniqueness claim alone. RFC 6286 Section 2.2 validation still applies, and it rejects a
zero identifier, and this speaker's own identifier from an internal peer. Section 2.3 connection
collision resolution is implemented, and this leaf does not disable it.
children.name: allow-shared-router-id
children.short-help: Accept a peer whose BGP Identifier duplicates another established peer in the same AS.

children.description:
Ze sends the value as My Autonomous System in OPEN. A group or a peer can override it.
Ze keeps this global value for the local-as modifiers, which need the real AS number.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Local Autonomous System Number (required)

children.description:
At this global level the container holds the local ASN alone. The same container under a
group or a peer also holds remote and local-options.
children.name: asn
children.short-help: AS number configuration

children.description:
A group value overrides this global value, and a peer value overrides the group value. The
container holds the local ASN and the shared-router-id switch.
children.name: session
children.short-help: Global BGP session defaults

children.description: The attribute identifies the AS and the router that formed the aggregate.
children.name: aggregator
children.short-help: AGGREGATOR attribute (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.7). The format is AS:IP.

children.description:
The list is an ordered sequence. A repeated ASN is a prepend that counts, so Ze does not deduplicate
it (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.2). AS_PATH decides loop detection, and it decides path selection, where
the shorter path is preferred.
children.name: as-path
children.short-help: AS_PATH segments prepended to the route, as space-separated ASNs.

children.description: The flag signals that aggregation formed the route, and that AS_PATH information was lost.
children.name: atomic-aggregate
children.short-help: ATOMIC_AGGREGATE flag (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.6).

children.description: The list carries an attribute that no named field covers.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: Raw BGP attributes in hex encoding, as flags:type:hex-value.

children.description:
The attribute carries an MPLS label index for Segment Routing. A node can therefore advertise its
SID without a per-prefix label allocation.
children.name: bgp-prefix-sid
children.short-help: Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 8669).

children.description:
The attribute carries SRv6 SID information for IPv6 Segment Routing, and it includes the SRv6 L3
Service TLVs.
children.name: bgp-prefix-sid-srv6
children.short-help: SRv6 Prefix-SID attribute (RFC 9252).

children.description: Each reflector prepends its cluster ID. The list detects a loop between reflectors.
children.name: cluster-list
children.short-help: CLUSTER_LIST for route reflection (RFC 4456).

children.description:
The format is AS:value, for example 65000:100. A well-known name is also accepted, such as no-export
or no-advertise.
children.name: community
children.short-help: Standard BGP communities (RFC 1997).

children.description: An extended community carries a route target, a site-of-origin, or VPN semantics.
children.name: extended-community
children.short-help: Extended communities (RFC 4360). The format is type:admin:value.

children.description:
Ze accepts a decimal number from 0 to 1048575, which is the 20-bit label field. It accepts no keyword.
Write the labels leaf-list for a stack of more than one label.
children.name: label
children.short-help: MPLS label value for a labeled unicast route (RFC 3107). The value is a number.

children.description:
The list is an ordered sequence from bottom to top. Ze keeps a repeated label, and it does not
deduplicate the stack.
children.name: labels
children.short-help: MPLS label stack for a multi-label route (RFC 8277).

children.description:
Each value is three 32-bit numbers separated by colons, which is 12 octets on the wire. The global part
holds a 4-byte ASN, which a standard community of RFC 1997 cannot hold.
children.name: large-community
children.short-help: Large BGP communities (RFC 8092). Format: global:local1:local2. Supports 4-byte ASNs natively.

children.description: LOCAL_PREF has a meaning inside a single AS alone (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.5). The default is 100.
children.name: local-preference
children.short-help: LOCAL_PREF value for iBGP best-path selection. The higher value wins.

children.description: MED influences the inbound path selection that an external peer makes (RFC 4271 Section 5.1.4).
children.name: med
children.short-help: Multi-Exit Discriminator (MED). The lower value is preferred.

children.description:
self resolves at send time to the local address of the session, so each peer reads its
own next hop. An IP address reaches every peer of the block unchanged. Ze refuses an IPv6
link-local address here, because RFC 2545 Section 3 puts the global address in that field.
children.name: next-hop
children.short-help: Next hop address or 'self'

values.name: self
values.short-help: Resolve the next hop at send time to the local address of each session.

children.description:
RFC 4271 Section 4.3 gives three values. igp is reachability interior to the
originating AS. egp is reachability learned through the EGP protocol. incomplete is
reachability learned by some other means, for example a redistributed static route.
children.name: origin
children.short-help: ORIGIN attribute (RFC 4271 Section 4.3)

values.name: egp
values.short-help: Exterior Gateway Protocol

values.name: igp
values.short-help: Interior Gateway Protocol

values.name: incomplete
values.short-help: Incomplete origin

children.description:
The reflector sets the attribute to the router ID of the originating router. The attribute prevents
a loop.
children.name: originator-id
children.short-help: ORIGINATOR_ID for route reflection (RFC 4456).

children.description: The identifier separates the several paths that one peer sends for the same prefix.
children.name: path-information
children.short-help: ADD-PATH path identifier (RFC 7911).

children.description: Ze prepends the Route Distinguisher to the prefix, which makes a unique VPN route.
children.name: rd
children.short-help: Route Distinguisher (RFC 4364). The format is ASN:nn or IP:nn.

children.description: The format is /length. For example, /24 splits a /16 into 256 prefixes of /24.
children.name: split
children.short-help: Split one prefix into more-specific prefixes for the announcement.

children.description:
Every NLRI of the block takes the same attributes. To announce two prefixes that carry
different attributes, write two update blocks.
children.name: attribute
children.short-help: Path attributes for routes in this block

children.description:
The list carries no key, so the CLI and the web UI show this label in place of one. The
label reaches no BGP message.
children.name: name
children.short-help: Optional label for this update block (display only)

children.description:
The form is an operation keyword, then an optional rd and label, then one or more prefixes. add, del and
eor are the operation keywords, and one of them is required. A block that carries del or eor announces nothing
at config load.
children.name: content
children.short-help: Operation, qualifiers, and payload

children.description:
Every entry takes the attribute block of the update block. The key is the family name, and
content carries the operation keyword and the prefixes. An update block that declares no nlri
entry is refused at config load.
children.name: nlri
children.short-help: Routes this update block announces, one entry for each address family.

children.description:
request bgp watchdog announce <name> announces every route that carries the name, and request bgp
watchdog withdraw <name> withdraws them. Ze skips a block whose name is empty.
children.name: name
children.short-help: Watchdog group name

children.description:
The bgp-watchdog plugin reads the PRESENCE of the leaf and not its value, so withdraw false starts every
route of the block withdrawn exactly as withdraw true does. Delete the leaf to announce the routes as soon as
the session reaches Established. request bgp watchdog announce <name> announces a withdrawn route.
children.name: withdraw
children.short-help: Start in withdrawn state (default true)

children.description:
The bgp-watchdog plugin owns every route of the block, so the BGP engine holds none of
them as a static route. The plugin sends a route that is not withdrawn when the session reaches
Established.
children.name: watchdog
children.short-help: Watchdog-controlled route - held until 'bgp watchdog announce <name>'

children.description:
Ze announces every route of the block to the peers the block applies to. The block is written
at the global level, the group level, and the peer level, and the three accumulate.
children.name: update
children.short-help: Native Ze route announcements

children.description:
The leaf is optional, and an absent leaf lets only max-delay and full convergence end
the hold. When these seconds elapse and one or more peers are held, Ze ends the hold and
advertises to them, whether or not they sent an End-of-RIB marker. When no peer is held, Ze
keeps waiting until max-delay, because there is no peer to advertise to yet. Ze refuses a
configuration where this value is more than max-delay.
children.name: establish-wait
children.short-help: Seconds after which the peers that are held end the hold. Must not exceed max-delay.

children.description:
0 is the default and disables the feature. A value of more than 0 arms the hold when the
daemon starts its peers. The hold ends when every configured peer sends its End-of-RIB
marker, or when establish-wait ends it early, or when these seconds elapse, whichever comes
first. Ze waits for the marker and not for Established, because Established says only that
the neighbor answered. RFC 4724 Section 4.1 excludes a peer that advertised no
graceful-restart capability and a peer that is itself restarting, and Ze excludes the same
two. A peer that never comes up cannot extend the wait past this number.
children.name: max-delay
children.short-help: Seconds to hold the first advertisement. 0 disables the hold.

children.description:
An absent container is the default, and it keeps the behavior Ze had before the container
existed: each peer advertises as soon as it reaches Established. The container holds max-delay,
which enables the feature and bounds the wait, and establish-wait, which can end the wait early.
While Ze holds, sessions negotiate, reach Established and receive UPDATE messages as usual. Ze
sends no UPDATE and no End-of-RIB marker until the hold ends. RFC 4724 Section 4.1 prescribes
the same deferral for a speaker that restarts, and requires the configurable upper bound
max-delay supplies. The hold applies at startup alone: a reload validates a changed value and
Ze keeps the hold it already armed, or none, so a new value takes effect at the next restart.
Ze does not enforce a relation between max-delay and the Restart Time it advertises in its
graceful-restart capability, so keep max-delay below that number yourself. A neighbor whose own
restart timer expires first discards the routes it kept for Ze. Read `show bgp update-delay` to
see whether a speaker is holding and what it waits for.
children.name: update-delay
children.short-help: Hold the first advertisement at startup until the RIB settles.

bgp.description: A peer inherits from its group defaults. A group inherits from this global level.
bgp.name: bgp

children.description:
IEEE 802.1Q defines the Priority Code Point field, which
is 3 bits wide and holds a value from 0 to 7.
children.name: pcp
children.short-help: PCP value Ze stamps in the 802.1Q header.

children.description:
The list key is the internal priority, so the list holds at
most one entry for each of the eight priorities.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Map one internal priority to a transmitted PCP value.

children.description:
Ze reads this mapping when it stamps the PCP field of a frame it
transmits.
children.name: egress
children.short-help: Priority-to-PCP mapping of a transmitted tagged frame.

children.description: The value runs from 0 to 7.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Internal priority Ze gives to a matching frame.

children.description:
The list key is the PCP value, so the list holds at most one
entry for each of the eight values.
children.name: pcp
children.short-help: Map one received PCP value to an internal priority.

children.description:
Ze reads this mapping when it takes the internal priority of a
frame it receives.
children.name: ingress
children.short-help: PCP-to-priority mapping of a received tagged frame.

children.description:
The profile defines the mapping between the 3-bit PCP field in the
802.1Q header and the internal priorities. It covers the ingress direction and the
egress direction.
children.name: ieee-802.1p
children.short-help: An 802.1p QoS profile.

class-of-service.description:
A profile maps the 3-bit PCP field of an 802.1Q header to an internal
priority, in the ingress direction and in the egress direction. An interface leaf and a
unit leaf name the profile they use.
class-of-service.name: class-of-service

connected.description:
The container carries no leaf, so writing it is the whole configuration.
The plugin watches each interface address event and emits the network
prefix of that address on the redistribute event bus. It counts the
addresses of one prefix, so two addresses in one subnet announce the prefix
once. The withdrawal waits for the last address of that prefix. The plugin
registers the connected route source, and a redistribute statement names
that source.
connected.name: connected
connected.short-help: Connected route redistribution. Presence enables the plugin.

children.description:
The unit follows the unit of rate: a packet count where rate counts
packets, and a byte count where rate names a byte unit. The leaf
has no default, and Ze gives the kernel a burst of 0 when it is
absent.
children.name: burst
children.short-help: Burst size (packets or bytes matching the rate unit).

children.description:
accept, the default, counts the over-limit packets and lets them through. The
limit then reports load and stops nothing. drop discards a new TCP connection
to a protected port once the rate is exceeded. Either setting reaches the
over-limit packets alone. The input chain keeps an accept policy, so SSH, ICMP
and every service this table never names stay reachable. The first term accepts
an established session before the limit is read, so drop never closes a session
that is already up.
children.name: over-limit-policy
children.short-help: What Ze does with the packets that exceed the rate limit.

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Accept over-limit packets (safe default).

values.name: drop
values.short-help: Drop over-limit packets.

children.description:
TCP port(s) to protect. Ze uses 179, the BGP port, when this leaf is omitted. Set a different value
when the BGP listener uses another port.
children.name: protected-port
children.short-help: TCP port(s) the control-plane policing rules protect, 179 (BGP) by default.

children.description:
The leaf is mandatory, so Ze refuses the container without it. The
value is a count, an optional byte unit, and a time unit, as in
100/second or 1mbytes/second. The limit reaches a new TCP
connection to a protected port alone, because the chain accepts an
established connection before it.
children.name: rate
children.short-help: Rate limit for new connections (e.g., 100/second).

children.description:
Ze adds one accept term for each prefix, above the rate limit term.
The term matches TCP from that source to a protected port, so a
trusted peer never meets the limit. Ze refuses a value that is not
an IPv4 prefix or an IPv6 prefix.
children.name: trusted-source
children.short-help:
Source prefixes that bypass the rate limit.
Typically the addresses of configured BGP peers.

children.description:
The container carries presence, so Ze builds the ze_copp table when you
write it and removes the table when you delete it. The chain accepts an
established or related connection first, then a connection from each
trusted-source prefix, and applies the rate to what is left.
children.name: bgp
children.short-help: Rate-limit new TCP connections to the BGP listen port.

control-plane-protection.description:
Ze compiles the containers under it into one nftables table named ze_copp,
which carries a base input chain at priority 0. The ze_ prefix is what
makes the firewall backend own that table and withdraw it when you delete
the configuration. The bgp container is the only policy Ze builds today.
control-plane-protection.name: control-plane-protection

children.description:
Minimum threshold in PPS regardless of baseline, default 5000. A quiet link cannot trigger on a small
burst, because the threshold never falls under this value. Five times this value is also the packet-rate
escape from startup-grace, so a rate over 25000 PPS triggers at the default while the grace period
runs.
children.name: absolute-floor
children.short-help: Minimum threshold in PPS regardless of baseline.

children.description:
Rolling baseline window size in samples, and one sample is one evaluation, so one check-interval. The
window p99 is recalculated every 10 admitted samples, so a cold detector runs on absolute-floor alone for
its first 10 evaluations. A
sample taken while the rate is over the threshold is refused, so an attack cannot raise the threshold
that detects it. One sample in 3600 consecutive refused samples is admitted, which lets a lasting rise
in traffic move the baseline. A persisted baseline is restored only when it carries 50 samples or
more.
children.name: baseline-window
children.short-help: Rolling baseline window size in samples.

children.description:
Minimum bandwidth in bits/sec below which the BPS trigger is inert. The default is 50 Mbps. The
value is expressed in bits/sec, which is the operator unit. The detector's internal rate is
bytes/sec, and it converts the value.
children.name: bps-floor
children.short-help: Minimum bandwidth in bits/sec below which the BPS trigger is inert.

children.description:
Baseline p99 multiplier for the bandwidth (BPS) trigger. The trigger catches low-PPS, high-bandwidth
amplification, such as NTP, memcached and CLDAP, that the packet-rate threshold misses.
children.name: bps-threshold-multiplier
children.short-help: Baseline p99 multiplier for the bandwidth (BPS) trigger.

children.description:
Enable the bandwidth (BPS) trigger alongside the PPS threshold. When this leaf is false, only the
packet-rate threshold can trigger detection.
children.name: bps-trigger-enable
children.short-help: Enable the bandwidth (BPS) trigger beside the PPS threshold.

children.description:
Run Stage-2 flow characterization. The stage classifies the family and the narrowest vector from the
flow-export recent-flow ring, and emits AttackCharacterized. When this leaf is false, the detector
still emits the coarse AttackDetected target from traffic-usage.
children.name: characterize-enable
children.short-help: Run Stage-2 flow characterization on a detected attack.

children.description:
Milliseconds budget for the on-trigger traffic-usage and flow-recent queries. On timeout, the
detector falls back to the best available target.
children.name: characterize-timeout
children.short-help: Milliseconds budget for the on-trigger queries.

children.description:
Seconds of recent flows to consider when characterizing. Flows last seen before this window are
ignored. Flows with no timestamp are always kept.
children.name: characterize-window
children.short-help: Seconds of recent flows to consider when characterizing an attack.

children.description:
Seconds between detection evaluations. Both rate feeds publish once a second: the
traffic-statistics service, and the interface rate collector Ze falls back to when that service
is absent. The detector folds this many samples and evaluates their PEAK, so a flood shorter
than the interval still reaches the threshold. Every leaf that counts ticks against the
threshold counts evaluations, so its wall-clock meaning is multiplied by this value. The
default 1 evaluates every second.
children.name: check-interval
children.short-help: Seconds between detection evaluations.

children.description:
The count of consecutive evaluations under the threshold that ends an attack. The first one under the
threshold moves an active detector to the clearing state and counts as the first check. The default 10
therefore holds the attack live for ten evaluations, which is ten seconds at the default check-interval.
One evaluation back over the threshold returns the detector to active and drops the count.
children.name: clear-consecutive-checks
children.short-help: Consecutive evaluations below threshold before clearing.

children.description:
The count of consecutive evaluations over the threshold that arms the detector. One evaluation is
check-interval seconds, one second at the default. The default 3 needs three unbroken
evaluations over the threshold. A value of 0 or 1 triggers on the first one. One evaluation back under the
threshold returns the detector to idle and restarts the count.
children.name: confirm-duration
children.short-help: Consecutive evaluations above threshold before triggering.

children.description:
Enable the DDoS detector. Left false, the detector subscribes to no rate feed, so it takes no sample
and its baseline stays cold. A commit rebuilds the detector and restores the persisted baseline either
way, and the subscription is what this leaf controls.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the DDoS detector.

children.description:
Source-address Shannon entropy (bits) at or above which an attack is logged as distributed or
spoofed. A value of 0 is a single source, and a higher value is more sources.
children.name: entropy-threshold
children.short-help: Source-address Shannon entropy in bits that marks an attack distributed.

children.description:
Disposition when no rule matches. deny means defend, which is detection plus mitigation. allow means
exempt from detection entirely.
children.name: default-action
children.short-help: Disposition when no rule matches the attack.

values.name: allow
values.short-help: Exempt an attack no rule matches from detection entirely.

values.name: deny
values.short-help: Detect and mitigate an attack no rule matches.

children.description:
allow exempts the matched traffic and deny subjects it to DDoS handling. The scope leaf decides how
far each one reaches. allow at mitigation scope records the incident and installs no block, and allow
at detection scope suppresses the incident. deny at detection scope also records without a block, and
deny at mitigation scope is full handling.
children.name: action
children.short-help: allow exempts matching traffic and deny subjects it to DDoS handling.

values.name: allow
values.short-help: Exempt the matched traffic, as far as the scope leaf reaches.

values.name: deny
values.short-help: Subject the matched traffic to DDoS handling, as far as the scope leaf reaches.

children.description:
Whether the prefix matches the attack source, the victim destination, or either. A source rule takes
effect once the attack sources are characterized.
children.name: match
children.short-help: Whether the prefix matches the attack source, the destination, or either.

values.name: any
values.short-help: Match the prefix against the attack sources or the destination.

values.name: destination
values.short-help: Match the prefix against the victim destination.

values.name: source
values.short-help: Match the prefix against the attack sources, once they are characterized.

children.description:
Stage the action governs. mitigation means detect and record, and for allow it does not block.
detection means that for allow the incident is suppressed entirely.
children.name: scope
children.short-help: Stage the action governs, mitigation or detection.

values.name: detection
values.short-help: The action governs detection, so allow suppresses the incident entirely.

values.name: mitigation
values.short-help: The action governs mitigation, so the incident is recorded and allow blocks nothing.

children.description:
One allow/deny rule matched against an attack, keyed by prefix. Precedence is longest-prefix match,
so a /24 rule beats a covering /16 with no ordering.
children.name: rule
children.short-help: One allow or deny rule matched against an attack, keyed by prefix.

children.description:
Allow/deny traffic policy applied to detected attacks, indexed by prefix. Ze evaluates the policy by
longest-prefix match, where the most specific rule wins, and not by config order. The policy
replaces the removed per-responder allowlists. The detector enforces it once and encodes the exempt
or mitigate decision on the emitted event, so the responders obey it with no config read.
children.name: policy
children.short-help: Allow and deny traffic policy applied to a detected attack.

children.description:
Seconds after startup where only extreme spikes trigger, default 90. The count follows the rate feed,
one per second, so check-interval does not change it.
A cold baseline warms during the grace period, and the grace stops that warm-up from firing on itself.
Two things still trigger: a packet rate over five times absolute-floor, and the bandwidth trigger once
its own baseline is ready.
children.name: startup-grace
children.short-help: Seconds after startup where only extreme spikes trigger.

children.description:
Baseline p99 multiplier for the dynamic threshold. The threshold is the larger of two numbers: the
window p99 multiplied by this leaf, and absolute-floor. The default 3.00 therefore triggers at three
times the p99 of normal traffic. A changed value reaches the threshold at the next recalculation, which
is within 10 admitted samples.
children.name: threshold-multiplier
children.short-help: Baseline p99 multiplier for the dynamic threshold.

children.description:
Maximum number of attacker source addresses ranked into TopSources by packet volume, default 10. Ties
are broken by address. The same ranked list is what a source-matching policy rule reads, and every
address in it has to fall inside the rule prefix before that rule matches.
children.name: top-n-sources
children.short-help: Maximum number of attacker source addresses ranked into TopSources by packet volume.

children.description:
Detection is separate from mitigation: this container decides that an
attack is happening and emits an event. A responder under flowspec or
local is what acts on that event, and none is armed by default.
children.name: detect
children.short-help: Detect a volumetric attack from the traffic Ze already sees.

children.description:
Neither discard nor rate-limit is universally safe, so this leaf
has no default. discard announces an RFC 8955 traffic-rate of 0,
which drops the characterized attack flow. rate-limit announces
a byte rate, and it requires an explicit rate-limit-bytes. A
rate-limit-bytes of 0 is a valid choice, and it is equivalent to
discard on the wire.
children.name: action
children.short-help: FlowSpec traffic-action: discard or rate-limit. Mandatory, with no default.

values.name: discard
values.short-help: Announce a traffic-rate of 0, which drops the attack flow.

values.name: rate-limit
values.short-help: Announce a traffic-rate of rate-limit-bytes, which that leaf must then carry.

children.description:
The most FlowSpec announcements Ze sends in any 60 second window. An announcement over
the limit is refused and logged, and the responder stays idle, so the next attack
characterization inside the window announces nothing upstream and the one after the
window rolls does. The limit protects the BGP sessions the rule goes to: a peer that
drops the session over announce churn loses every rule it holds. 10 is the default, and
the range is 1 to 600.
children.name: announce-rate-limit
children.short-help: Maximum FlowSpec announcements per minute.

children.description:
Each probe that saturates doubles the current hold-down, and this value stops the
doubling. Ze refuses a backoff-cap under hold-down, and the upper bound is 604800
seconds. 3600 is the default, which stops the wait at one hour.
children.name: backoff-cap
children.short-help: Maximum hold-down after exponential backoff.

children.description:
When true, a critical-severity AttackDetected (a peak of 5x the
threshold or more) engages an immediate upstream discard, in the
style of RTBH, and it does not wait for characterization. When
false, the default, ze announces the upstream rule only from
AttackCharacterized. The rule is then precise before the box
goes blind behind the filter.
children.name: blackhole-fallback
children.short-help: Announce an immediate upstream discard on a critical-severity AttackDetected.

children.description:
The default is 0, which accepts any confidence. The
blackhole-fallback fast path never applies this minimum,
because AttackDetected carries no confidence.
children.name: confidence-min
children.short-help: Minimum incident confidence (0-100) to announce an upstream rule from a characterized attack.

children.description:
The responder counts one second for each AttackOngoing event the detector emits, and
the detector emits one for each traffic sample. The rule stays at full strength for
this long, and the first leak-probe follows. A probe that saturates doubles the wait,
up to backoff-cap. The range is 1 to 86400 seconds, and 300 is the default.
children.name: hold-down
children.short-help: Minimum seconds before the first leak-probe after announcement.

children.description:
The responder measures this against the wall clock, and not against the probe. An
attack that goes quiet stops the AttackOngoing events the probe counts, which is the
case the probe cannot see. 0 removes the cap, so the rule then stays until a probe
withdraws it. 3600 is the default, and the range is 0 to 604800 seconds.
children.name: max-mitigation-duration
children.short-help: Maximum seconds a FlowSpec rule stays announced (0 = no cap).

children.description:
After the hold-down ends the responder waits this long. It then narrows the rule to
probe-rate and watches what arrives. 60 is the default, and the range is 1 to 3600
seconds. A shorter interval finds the end of an attack sooner, and it also lets more
attack traffic through each time.
children.name: probe-interval
children.short-help: Seconds between leak-probe attempts after hold-down.

children.description:
The responder compares the rate it measures behind the filter against this value. At
or above it, the attack still runs: the rule is tightened again and the hold-down
doubles. Under it for a whole probe-window, the rule is withdrawn. 1000000 bits per
second is the default, and the value must be 1 or more.
children.name: probe-rate
children.short-help: Bits per second to allow during a leak-probe.

children.description:
The responder withdraws the rule when the observed rate stays under probe-rate for
this whole window. One second at or above probe-rate ends the probe at once, and the
rule goes back to full strength. 10 is the default, and the range is 1 to 300
seconds.
children.name: probe-window
children.short-help: Seconds to observe leaked traffic during a probe.

children.description:
This leaf is required, and validated, when action is rate-limit.
It has no default, because no rate is universally safe. A value
of 0 is valid, and it encodes the same traffic-rate-0 as
discard. Ze does not read the leaf when action is discard. Set
it to the per-flow rate you accept toward the victim during
mitigation.
children.name: rate-limit-bytes
children.short-help: Bytes per second announced in the RFC 8955 traffic-rate extended community.

children.description:
alert is the default. The responder then logs the announcement it would make, and
announces nothing. enforce is the value that puts a rule on the wire. The leaf gates
every announce path, the blackhole-fallback fast path included.
children.name: response-level
children.short-help: Action on attack detection: alert (log only) or enforce (announce FlowSpec).

values.name: alert
values.short-help: Log the FlowSpec rule the responder would announce, and announce nothing.

values.name: enforce
values.short-help: Announce the FlowSpec rule to the peer.

children.description:
The rule is announced to a peer, so the traffic is dropped upstream and
never reaches this router. It needs a peer that accepts FlowSpec, which
is what separates it from the local responder.
children.name: flowspec
children.short-help: Answer a detected attack by announcing a BGP FlowSpec rule.

children.description:
Ze appends a path to this value, so a trailing slash gives a double slash in the
request. /agent/incidents opens and closes an incident, and /agent/heartbeat reports
the baseline. Each request has a timeout of 10 seconds. After 5 failures Ze stops
posting for 60 seconds, then tries again.
children.name: api-base
children.short-help: Flowtriq API base URL.

children.description:
Ze sends the value in the Authorization header of each request, as a Bearer token.
The length is 1 to 512 characters. The leaf is required when enabled is true, and Ze
refuses the config without it. The leaf is marked sensitive, so every display path
prints a placeholder in place of the token. A $9$-encoded value written by hand is
decoded on read. Ze does not encode it for you, so a token typed into the editor is
written to the config file as you typed it.
children.name: api-key
children.short-help: Flowtriq API bearer token.

children.description:
false is the default, and the reporter then posts nothing. true makes api-key and
node-uuid required, and Ze refuses the config when either one is empty. The reporter
answers an attack with one HTTP POST, and it stops no traffic.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable reporting DDoS incidents to the Flowtriq cloud API.

children.description:
Ze sends the value in the X-Node-UUID header of each request, which is how the
service tells this router from another. The length is 1 to 128 characters. The leaf
is required when enabled is true.
children.name: node-uuid
children.short-help: Node UUID for Flowtriq agent identification.

children.description:
It reports and mitigates nothing on its own. The traffic still needs a
responder under flowspec or local to be stopped.
children.name: flowtriq
children.short-help: Feed detected attacks to the FlowTriq reporting service.

children.description:
Ze installs a drop rule from a characterized attack only when the
confidence of the incident reaches this value. The default is 0, which disables the
check. A higher value stops mitigation on a borderline detection.
children.name: confidence-min
children.short-help: Minimum incident confidence, from 0 to 100, to install a drop rule.

children.description:
The default is false. The responder then guards only a local victim, one
the box owns, on the netfilter INPUT hook. The responder leaves a remote victim to the
flowspec upstream announce. Set this leaf to true to protect a downstream host as well.
The ddos/detect policy makes the exempt decision and the mitigate decision.
children.name: forward-mitigation
children.short-help: Drop the traffic of a remote transit victim on the netfilter FORWARD hook.

children.description:
A drop rule that reaches this age is removed, and the plugin checks the age once a
second. The clock starts when the rule goes in and a narrowing of the same rule does not
restart it. The cap is the second removal trigger: the first is the AttackCleared event,
and the cap is what bounds a rule when that event never arrives. Set the leaf to 0 for no
cap, and the rule then stays until the attack clears. The leaf of the same name under ddos
flowspec caps the upstream announce in the same way.
children.name: max-mitigation-duration
children.short-help: Maximum seconds a drop rule stays installed (0 = no cap).

children.description:
alert is the default. The responder then logs the rule it would install, and installs
nothing. enforce is the value that puts a drop rule in nftables, on a base chain at
priority -200. The traffic policy of ddos/detect can still exempt a target from the
action.
children.name: response-level
children.short-help: Action on attack detection: alert (log only) or enforce (install drop rule).

values.name: alert
values.short-help: Log the drop rule the responder would install, and install nothing.

values.name: enforce
values.short-help: Install the drop rule in nftables.

children.description:
The rule drops the traffic where it arrives, so the link into this router
still carries the attack. Announce a FlowSpec rule instead to have it
dropped upstream.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Answer a detected attack with a firewall rule on this router.

children.description:
The ring holds this many incidents. A new incident past the bound deletes the oldest
closed one. When every incident in the ring is still open, the oldest open one is
deleted instead. 1000 is the default, and the range is 1 to 100000.
children.name: incident-ring-size
children.short-help: Maximum number of incidents to retain in memory.

children.description:
The value reaches the incident store as its stale timeout, and no worker of ddos
observe applies that timeout. The store closes an incident on the AttackCleared event that
matches it. An incident that gets no clear event stays open until incident-ring-size evicts
it. The default is 3600 seconds and the range is 1 to 86400. A value other than the default
changes no behavior.
children.name: stale-incident-timeout
children.short-help: Seconds before an open incident without a clear event is auto-finalized.

children.description:
The ring is bounded and in memory, so it holds recent incidents and not a
history, and a restart empties it.
children.name: observe
children.short-help: Keep a ring of recent incidents for an operator to read back.

ddos.description:
Distributed denial-of-service detection and mitigation subsystem. This module declares the container,
and the flowtriq, observe, local and flowspec plugins each augment it. The detect subtree decides
that an attack is present, and a responder under one of those subtrees acts on the event.
ddos.name: ddos
ddos.short-help: Distributed denial-of-service detection and mitigation subsystem.

children.description:
The default is false, so config starts no gRPC listener until
the leaf is true. The environment variable
ze.api-server.grpc.enabled starts the transport with no leaf
written. Ze parses the addresses and the TLS pair even when the
transport stays off.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable gRPC API server

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:
The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a
free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation
collects each endpoint and refuses a second listener that binds
the same protocol, port and address. An empty list still binds
one endpoint, 0.0.0.0 port 50051, from the refine defaults
under it.
children.name: server
children.short-help: gRPC API listen endpoints

children.description:
Write tls-cert and tls-key together. Ze refuses to start the
server when one of the two is written and the other is not. Ze
reads the pair from disk at start, so a path that names no file
stops the server with an error.
children.name: tls-cert
children.short-help: Path to TLS certificate file for gRPC

children.description:
The leaf names the file that holds the private key of tls-cert,
and Ze reads the two together at start. Ze marks the leaf
ze:sensitive, so ze config dump prints the value $9$-encoded.
children.name: tls-key
children.short-help: Path to TLS private key file for gRPC

children.description:
A listen address that is not loopback must carry authentication and
TLS, and Ze refuses to start the server without them. Without TLS
the bearer token that gates each call crosses the network in clear.
Ze accepts TLS 1.2 as its lowest version.
children.name: grpc
children.short-help:
gRPC API transport. Authenticated non-loopback listeners
require tls-cert and tls-key.

children.description:
Ze copies the value into the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header
of each API answer, and validates nothing in it. An empty leaf sends no
