CORS header, and a preflight request then gets 204 with no
header. A preflight answer permits GET, POST, PUT, DELETE and
OPTIONS, permits the Authorization and Content-Type headers,
and holds for 86400 seconds.
children.name: cors-origin
children.short-help: CORS allowed origin (empty disables CORS headers)

children.description:
The default is false, so config starts no REST listener until
the leaf is true. The environment variable
ze.api-server.rest.enabled starts the transport with no leaf
written. Ze parses the addresses and the CORS origin even when
the transport stays off.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable REST API server

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:
The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a
free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation
collects each endpoint and refuses a second listener that binds
the same protocol, port and address. An empty list still binds
one endpoint, 0.0.0.0 port 8081, from the refine defaults under
it.
children.name: server
children.short-help: REST API listen endpoints

children.description:
A plain HTTP listener is restricted to loopback. To reach the API from another host, put a TLS
terminator in front of the listener.
children.name: rest
children.short-help: REST and HTTP transport for the API server.

children.description:
When the token is set, a client MUST send the header
'Authorization: Bearer <token>'. Leave the leaf empty to
allow unauthenticated access.
children.name: token
children.short-help: Bearer token for API authentication.

children.description:
The token leaf here is shared by both transports. Each transport starts
only when its own enabled leaf is true, or when
ze.api-server.rest.enabled or ze.api-server.grpc.enabled starts it.
Ze parses the addresses, the CORS origin and the TLS pair even when
the transport stays off.
children.name: api-server
children.short-help: API engine settings (shared parent for the REST/gRPC transports)

children.description:
The environment variable ze.bgp.announce.delay overrides the leaf. Ze holds every peer
start for the delay after the reactor is otherwise Ready, which staggers route emission over a
restart.
children.name: announce-delay
children.short-help: Delay between reactor Ready and first UPDATE (duration, 0s-1h)

children.description:
The environment variable ze.bgp.openwait overrides the leaf. Ze arms the hold timer with
the value after it sends OPEN. Ze resets that timer to the negotiated hold time when the peer
OPEN arrives.
children.name: openwait
children.short-help: Seconds to wait for peer OPEN after TCP connect

children.description: The container controls the OPEN wait timeout and the initial announce delay.
children.name: bgp
children.short-help: BGP protocol environment settings, applied before any peer-level config.

children.description:
The default is false. The receiver needs this leaf true and one
server entry at least, so enabled true on its own binds no address.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable BMP receiver

children.description:
The default is 100 and the range is 1 to 1000. The count is per
listener, so two server entries admit twice this number of
sessions. Over the limit Ze closes the new connection and logs a
warning, and the sessions already open keep running.
children.name: max-sessions
children.short-help: Maximum concurrent BMP sessions

children.description:
monitor is the default and is the only action Ze performs. redistribute is
accepted by the schema and is not implemented: Ze writes a warning in the log and acts
as monitor. Under monitor the routes of a BMP Route Monitoring message go to the BMP
RIB, which show bmp rib reads. They reach neither BGP best-path selection nor the
FIB.
children.name: route-action
children.short-help: Action for received BMP Route Monitoring messages

values.name: monitor
values.short-help: Store in BMP RIB for visibility (show bmp rib), isolated from BGP best-path and FIB

values.name: redistribute
values.short-help: Store in BMP RIB and redistribute into BGP best-path selection

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:
The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a
free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
The ze:listener extension marks this list, so config validation
refuses a second listener that binds the same protocol, port and
address. Ze opens one TCP listener for each entry. A bind that
fails is logged, and the other entries keep their listener. An
empty list binds nothing, because the receiver has no default
endpoint.
children.name: server
children.short-help: BMP receiver listen endpoints

children.description:
The receiver starts only when enabled is true and the server list holds
one entry at least. Ze stores each Route Monitoring message it accepts
in the BMP RIB, and show bmp rib reads that RIB.
children.name: bmp
children.short-help: BMP receiver settings

children.description:
0.1 injects a fault into one operation in ten. Ze uses 0.1 for a value that is
not a number, and for a value outside 0.0 to 1.0. The leaf does nothing while seed
is 0.
children.name: rate
children.short-help: Fault probability per operation (0.0-1.0)

children.description:
Ze builds the fault injector only while the seed is not 0. The same seed replays
the same sequence of faults, so a failed run can be repeated. A seed of -1 takes the
seed from the clock, and Ze logs the value it took. Ze applies the ze command line
after the config load, so a seed given there replaces the seed in this leaf.
children.name: seed
children.short-help: PRNG seed (0 = disabled)

children.description:
Ze wraps the clock, the dialer and the listener factory with a fault injector while
seed is not 0. The block exists to test Ze against slow timers and failed connections.
A production config leaves the block out.
children.name: chaos
children.short-help: Chaos fault injection settings

children.description:
text writes space-aligned columns, table draws a box around them, json
pretty-prints, yaml writes YAML, and ndjson writes one JSON object on each line.
A format operator on the command line, such as | json, wins over this leaf, and
so does set cli format. Ze falls back to text for a value it does not know.
children.name: default
children.short-help: Default output format when no pipe operator is specified

values.name: json
values.short-help: JSON output (pretty-printed)

values.name: ndjson
values.short-help: Newline-delimited JSON (one object per line)

values.name: table
values.short-help: Nushell-style table with box-drawing characters

values.name: text
values.short-help: Space-aligned columns without box-drawing

values.name: yaml
values.short-help: YAML output

children.description:
The container holds the default leaf alone. A session overrides it with set cli
format, which changes that one session and no other.
children.name: format
children.short-help: Default output format settings

children.description:
enabled writes one file for each session, named transcript-DATE-TIME-PID.log,
with mode 0600 in a directory with mode 0700. Each entry holds the time, the command
with its pipe operators, and the answer. Ze writes under $HOME/.local/share while
XDG_DATA_HOME is unset, and it reports a directory it cannot create on stderr.
children.name: transcript
children.short-help: CLI session transcript recording to $XDG_DATA_HOME/ze/transcripts/

values.name: disabled
values.short-help: No transcript recording

values.name: enabled
values.short-help: Record CLI session commands and output to local transcript file

children.description:
The container holds the default output format and the transcript switch. Both leaves
apply to every CLI session this daemon serves.
children.name: cli
children.short-help: CLI session settings

children.description:
Ze writes its own process ID to this path at startup and removes the file at a
clean shutdown. The create refuses an existing file, so a second daemon that names
the same path stops at startup with an error. When the user leaf is also set, Ze
gives the file to that user, because the shutdown path runs after the change of user.
Ze writes no PID file while the leaf is absent.
children.name: pid
children.short-help: PID file path

children.description:
Ze starts as root to bind port 179, then changes to this user before it starts a
plugin or accepts a connection. A user name and a numeric UID are both accepted, and
the user's primary group is used. Ze keeps root while the leaf is absent.
children.name: user
children.short-help: System user for privilege drop

children.description:
The container holds the path of the PID file and the user Ze changes to. Ze reads
both leaves at startup, in that order, and neither one changes a running daemon.
children.name: daemon
children.short-help: Daemon settings

children.description:
true matches ExaBGP, and it lets the program wait for done before it sends
the next command. false keeps the bridge silent, and a program that waits for
done then stops. The bridge reads false, 0, no, off, disable and disabled as
false, and every other value as true.
children.name: ack
children.short-help: Emit done/error ack lines on plugin stdin after each dispatched command

children.description:
The container holds the ack leaf alone. The bridge reads the leaf once, when it
starts, so a change reaches the bridge at the next daemon start.
children.name: api
children.short-help: ExaBGP bridge API settings

children.description:
The bridge runs an unchanged ExaBGP API program against Ze, and the container holds
the settings of the channel to that program.
children.name: exabgp
children.short-help: ExaBGP compatibility settings for the migration bridge

children.description:
The default is false, so Ze opens no gNMI listener until this
leaf is true.
children.name: enabled

answers Get, Set, Subscribe and Capabilities over gRPC.

children.description:
The web interface and the looking glass both stamp X-Ze-Version on a
response. The banner gives the release, the git commit, the Go version and the
OS, which tells a client the exact build it speaks to. With true, neither
server sends the header, and no other header changes. The default false keeps
the banner, so a tool that reads it continues to operate. Ze reads the leaf at
startup, so a new value applies at the next daemon start.
children.name: hide-version
children.short-help: Hide the X-Ze-Version banner on every HTTP response (ze.hide-version)

the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.

children.description:
Each entry is one UDP socket Ze binds for L2TPv2, and RFC 2661 assigns port
1701. Config validation refuses two listeners that share a protocol and a port
where their addresses overlap. `ze doctor` tries to bind each entry and names
the one the host refuses.
children.name: server
children.short-help: L2TP server listen endpoints (UDP)

children.description:
The container holds the UDP endpoints the L2TP subsystem listens on, and
nothing about a tunnel. A change to an endpoint is restart-only. The reload logs
that it ignored the change and asks for a restart, and Ze keeps the socket it
holds.
children.name: l2tp
children.short-help: L2TP listener endpoints

children.description:
syslog reads the destination leaf for its address, and it is the one value that
does not write to a file descriptor. Ze writes to stderr when the syslog dial fails,
and also while the leaf is absent.
children.name: backend
children.short-help: Log output backend (default: stderr)

values.name: stderr
values.short-help: Standard error output

values.name: stdout
values.short-help: Standard output

values.name: syslog
values.short-help: Syslog daemon

children.description:
NO_COLOR and TERM=dumb win over this leaf, and each one removes color whatever
the leaf holds. While neither is set and the leaf is absent, Ze writes color only
when the log writer is a terminal.
children.name: color
children.short-help: Force color log output on (true) or off (false). When unset, auto-detected from terminal.

children.description:
An empty value reaches the local syslog daemon. A value that starts with /
names a Unix socket. Any other value is a UDP address, so 127.0.0.1:514 sends to a
collector on this host. Ze writes to stderr when the dial fails. The crash log reads
the same address, and it reads it once at startup.
children.name: destination
children.short-help: Syslog address used when backend is syslog: empty, a socket path, or host:port

children.description:
warn is the level Ze uses while no config leaf and no environment variable set
one. warning, error and err name the same two levels, and disabled silences every
subsystem. Ze refuses any other word with a warning on stderr and keeps the level it
already has. A subsystem name written beside this leaf overrides it for that
subsystem alone.
children.name: level
children.short-help: Base log level for all subsystems: disabled, debug, info, warn, or err (case-insensitive)

children.description:
A plugin runs as its own process and writes to its own stderr. Ze relays a line
at this level or above into its own log, and drops the rest. warn is the level Ze
uses while the leaf is absent, and disabled silences a plugin's stderr completely.
children.name: relay
children.short-help: Plugin stderr relay level: disabled, debug, info, warn, or err (case-insensitive)

children.description:
A name this container does not declare becomes a subsystem level: bgp.routes debug
sets the level of the bgp.routes subsystem alone. Ze reads a subsystem level from the
longest matching name to the shortest, so bgp covers bgp.fsm until bgp.fsm is set too.
children.name: log
children.short-help: Logging settings

children.description:
The listener sends the leaf certificate and every
intermediate certificate the store entry holds, so a client
can build the full chain.
When this leaf is not set, ze generates a self-signed
certificate and serves that.
If the store holds no entry with that name, or the entry
holds no private key, ze exits with an error and rejects a
reload. ze never falls back to a self-signed certificate
for a configured name.
A named certificate needs no blob storage, because the
material comes from the pki container.
Environment variable: ze.looking-glass.certificate.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: PKI store certificate served on the looking-glass listener (ze.looking-glass.certificate).

children.description:
The looking glass does not start while this leaf is false,
and false is the default.

children.short-help: Enable the looking glass.

overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,

children.description:
Each entry names one listen endpoint. The default endpoint
is 0.0.0.0 on port 8443.

children.short-help: Looking glass listen endpoints.

children.description:
TLS needs blob storage for the certificates. The default
true holds because the looking glass binds 0.0.0.0 and
publishes route data. Set it to false to serve plaintext,
for example when a proxy in front of Ze serves TLS.
children.name: tls
children.short-help: Enable TLS. Override with the ze.looking-glass.tls variable.

children.description:
Ze compares the token in constant time, with sha256 and
subtle.ConstantTimeCompare. An empty token leaves the
looking glass open, and that is the default: a looking
glass is a public read-only surface.
children.name: token
children.short-help: Bearer token checked on every /api/ and /lg/ route (ze.looking-glass.token).

children.description:
The container holds the enable switch, the listen endpoints, the
TLS switch and the bearer token.
children.name: looking-glass
children.short-help: Looking glass HTTP server settings.

children.description:
In oauth mode, Ze validates a token locally against the JWKS of
the configured authorization server. If the token leaf is set and the auth-mode leaf is
absent, Ze infers 'bearer' for backward compatibility. In every other case the default
is 'none'.

bearer is the legacy mode, which reads one shared token from the token leaf. bearer-list
replaces it: each entry of the identity list names one principal and carries its own
token.
children.name: auth-mode
children.short-help: Authentication strategy for the MCP server.

values.name: bearer
values.short-help: One shared bearer token, read from the token leaf.

values.name: bearer-list
values.short-help: One bearer token for each entry of the identity list.

values.name: none
values.short-help: No authentication, permitted on a loopback bind only.

values.name: oauth
values.short-help: OAuth 2.1 resource server.

children.description:
The default is false, which keeps the Phase 1 clamp. That clamp
forces every server entry to 127.0.0.1. When this leaf is true, Ze honors the ip the
operator configured, and auth-mode MUST be set to a value other than 'none'. The verify
step rejects a config that does not meet that condition.
children.name: bind-remote
children.short-help: Allow the MCP server to bind to a non-loopback address.

children.description:
The default is false, so Ze opens no MCP listener until this leaf
is true.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Start the MCP server.

children.description:
This leaf-list is optional. An empty leaf-list carries no
scope.
children.name: scope
children.short-help: Scopes Ze carries on a request this identity authenticates.

children.description:
Ze compares the token in constant time, so the duration of a
comparison tells an attacker nothing about the value.
children.name: token
children.short-help: Bearer token value of this identity.

children.description:
The token of each entry grants access to the named principal.
Authentication runs on every request, so the name and the scopes of the matching entry
ride that one authenticated request. A change takes effect on the next request.
children.name: identity
children.short-help: Per-identity bearer entries, for auth-mode=bearer-list.

children.description:
Ze rejects a token whose 'aud' claim does not match this URL.
Set this leaf explicitly. Ze never derives the value from the Host header of the
request.
children.name: audience
children.short-help: Canonical URL that identifies this MCP endpoint (RFC 8707).

children.description:
The resource server reads the metadata of the authorization
server from <url>/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server (RFC 8414), and discovers the
jwks_uri there.
children.name: authorization-server
children.short-help: HTTPS URL of the authorization server.

children.description:
Ze rejects a token that does not carry every scope in this
list. An empty leaf-list accepts any valid token.
children.name: required-scopes
children.short-help: Scopes an accepted token MUST carry.

children.description:
Ze does not run an authorization server. Ze validates a bearer
token that the external authorization server issued.
children.name: oauth
children.short-help: OAuth 2.1 resource-server settings, for auth-mode=oauth.

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:

free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
Each entry binds one address and one port. The address defaults
to 127.0.0.1 and the port defaults to 8080. The bind-remote leaf decides whether an
address other than loopback is kept.
children.name: server
children.short-help: Listen endpoints of the MCP server.

children.description:
Ze serves the endpoint over HTTPS only when cert and key are
both set, and over HTTP when one of the two is empty. Ze reads
the pair at start and accepts TLS 1.2 as its lowest version. A
pair that fails to load stops the MCP server, and Ze prints the
reason. ze doctor reads the file and reports it missing, or
near its expiry date.
children.name: cert
children.short-help: Path to PEM-encoded certificate file (or a chain).

children.description:
Ze refuses a key file that group or other can read, and refuses
a symbolic link, when it runs as a user other than root. The
MCP server does not start in that case. Under root Ze reads the
file whatever its mode, because root reads every file anyway.
children.name: key
children.short-help: Path to PEM-encoded private-key file.

children.description:
This container is required when auth-mode is oauth and a listen
endpoint is not a loopback address. ze config verify rejects a config that leaves the
cert leaf empty in that case, and one that sets cert without key.
children.name: tls
children.short-help: TLS certificate that serves the MCP endpoint over HTTPS.

children.description:
When this leaf is set and no auth-mode leaf is present, Ze infers
auth-mode 'bearer'. Leave this leaf empty for bearer-list mode and for oauth mode.
children.name: token
children.short-help: Bearer token for auth-mode=bearer.

children.description:
MCP is the Model Context Protocol. The Ze MCP server is the interface
an AI assistant uses to read state from Ze and to control it.
children.name: mcp
children.short-help: Settings of the MCP server.

children.description:
The default is false, so Ze leaves the system clock alone until
this leaf is true.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Synchronize the system clock with an NTP server.

children.description: The range is 60 to 86400 seconds, and the default is 3600.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Seconds between two clock synchronizations.

children.description:
Ze refuses a step larger than this value, which keeps a wrong
server answer from moving the clock far. A value of 0 removes the limit, so Ze accepts
a step of any size.
children.name: max-step
children.short-help: Largest clock step in seconds that Ze accepts.

children.description:
Ze writes the current time to this file at shutdown, and reads it
at startup. The stored time gives the clock a sane value before the first NTP answer
arrives.
children.name: persist-path
children.short-help: Path of the file that holds the time across a restart.

children.description:
The value is an IPv4 address, an IPv6 address, or a
hostname.
children.name: address
children.short-help: Hostname or IP address of the NTP server.

children.description:
The list key is the name leaf, so one entry exists for each
server.
children.name: server
children.short-help: The NTP servers Ze queries.

children.description:
Ze corrects an offset up to this threshold with Adjtimex, which slews
the clock gradually. Ze corrects a larger offset with Settimeofday, which steps the
clock. A value of 0 disables the slew, so Ze always steps the clock.
children.name: slew-threshold
children.short-help: Maximum offset in milliseconds for a gradual clock slew.

children.description:
The presence of these settings does not start the client. Set the
enabled leaf to true.
children.name: ntp
children.short-help: Settings of the NTP client.

children.description:
Ze starts the Go pprof handlers on this address at startup. The host must be
127.0.0.1, ::1 or localhost, and Ze stops with an error for any other host. An address
that carries no host, such as :6060, binds every interface, so Ze stops on it too. Ze
starts no pprof server while the leaf is absent. When the ze command line gives a
pprof address, Ze uses that address and ignores this leaf.
children.name: pprof
children.short-help: Address of the pprof HTTP server, which must be a loopback address

children.description:
The value bounds the memory that the encoding cache uses. 0 means unlimited, so the cache grows with
the route table.
children.name: cache-max
children.short-help: Maximum number of cached UPDATE wire messages.

children.description:
Ze reuses a cached UPDATE for a peer with the same encoding context, which removes a repeated
serialization. 0 disables the cache, so Ze builds every UPDATE fresh.
children.name: cache-ttl
children.short-help: Seconds Ze keeps a built UPDATE wire message in the encoding cache.

children.description:
The environment variable ze.fwd.batch.limit overrides the leaf. The limit bounds how long one drain holds
the session write lock, so a large batch cannot block another writer for long.
children.name: forward-batch-limit
children.short-help: Max items per drain batch. Bounds writeMu hold time during forward dispatch. 0 means unlimited.

children.description: The maximum is about 4GB. Ze ignores the leaf when forward-pool-max-bytes is set explicitly.
children.name: forward-pool-headroom
children.short-help: Extra bytes beyond the auto-sized pool baseline.

children.description:
The maximum is about 4GB. 0 means unlimited, and Ze then sizes the pools from the prefix maximums of
the peers.
children.name: forward-pool-max-bytes
children.short-help: Combined byte budget for the 4K and 64K buffer pools, in bytes.

children.description:
The value is the number of UPDATE items Ze buffers for one destination peer before backpressure
starts.
children.name: forward-queue-size
children.short-help: Per-destination forward channel capacity.

children.description:
The environment variable ze.fwd.teardown.grace overrides the leaf. Ze starts the period when the forward
pool is more than 95% full and the peer holds more than twice its weight. A peer that does not drain inside
the period is torn down.
children.name: forward-teardown-grace
children.short-help: Grace period before forced teardown on congestion (duration string, e.g. 5s, 1m).

children.description:
The environment variable ze.buf.read.size overrides the leaf. Ze sizes one buffered reader per session at
connection time, so a change reaches a session at its next connection. The kernel receive buffer is a separate
256KB.
children.name: read-buffer-size
children.short-help: Per-session TCP read buffer size in bytes.

children.description:
A value of less than 1.0 runs the loop faster, which lowers the latency and raises the CPU cost. A
value of more than 1.0 runs the loop slower, which raises the latency and lowers the CPU cost.
children.name: speed
children.short-help: Reactor loop cycle time multiplier, from 0.1 to 10.0.

children.description:
The encoding context is the negotiated capabilities and the address families. Grouping reduces the
CPU cost from O(peers x routes) to O(groups x routes). Disable it for debugging alone.
children.name: update-groups
children.short-help: Build each UPDATE once for every peer with the same encoding context.

children.description:
The environment variable ze.buf.write.size overrides the leaf. A larger buffer packs more BGP messages
into one write to the socket. The kernel send buffer is a separate 64KB.
children.name: write-buffer-size
children.short-help: Per-session TCP write buffer size in bytes.

children.description:
The reactor is the core event loop. It processes an incoming message, runs the peer FSMs, and
dispatches an outbound UPDATE.
children.name: reactor
children.short-help: BGP reactor engine tuning.

children.description:
The SSH server does not start while this leaf is false, and
false is the default.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the SSH server.

children.description:
A client that trusts the CA verifies the host on the
first connection. It does not have to trust the host key
on first use.
children.name: host-certificate
children.short-help: Path to the SSH host certificate file, signed by a CA.

children.description:
The default path is the config directory plus
ssh_host_ed25519_key. Ze generates that key when the
file is missing.
children.name: host-key
children.short-help: Path to the SSH host key file.

children.description:
Ze passes the value to the SSH server as the maximum
duration of one session. The default is 600 seconds.
children.name: idle-timeout
children.short-help: Idle timeout in seconds. The default is 600.

children.description:
Ze answers a session past this limit with 'maximum sessions
reached', and closes it. The default limit is 8 sessions.
children.name: max-sessions
children.short-help: Maximum number of concurrent SSH sessions.

two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.

listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and

children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.short-help: SSH server listen endpoints.

host key, the host certificate, the idle timeout and the session

children.short-help: Name of the PKI store certificate served on the HTTPS listener (ze.web.certificate).

children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the web interface.

children.description:
With true, the web interface asks for no credentials. Ze
then binds it to 127.0.0.1, so only a user on the host
reaches it.
children.name: insecure
children.short-help: Disable authentication, which forces the host to 127.0.0.1.

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.

children.description:

free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port

children.description:
Each entry names one listen endpoint. The default endpoint
is 0.0.0.0 on port 3443.
children.name: server
children.short-help: Web server listen endpoints.

children.description:
finder is the default file-browser UI. workbench is the
experimental one.
children.name: ui-mode
children.short-help: Web UI mode.

values.name: finder
values.short-help: Default file-browser style UI.

values.name: workbench
values.short-help: Experimental workbench UI.

children.description:
The container holds the enable switch, the listen endpoints, the
insecure switch, the certificate name and the UI mode.
children.name: web
children.short-help: Web interface settings.

environment.description:
The api-server container under it is the shared parent of the REST and gRPC
transports. ze-rest-conf and ze-grpc-conf merge their rest and grpc
containers into it, so a transport compiled out leaves no container to
configure.
environment.name: environment

children.description:
RFC 7911 defines ADD-PATH. none disables it. receive accepts more
than one path from the peer. send advertises more than one path to the peer. both does
each of the two.
children.name: add-path
children.short-help: ADD-PATH mode for the families the bridge negotiates.

values.name: both
values.short-help: Send/Receive value 3: accept and advertise more than one path.

values.name: none
values.short-help: Advertise no ADD-PATH capability.

values.name: receive
values.short-help: Send/Receive value 1: accept more than one path from the peer.

values.name: send
values.short-help: Send/Receive value 2: advertise more than one path to the peer.

children.description:
One example is ipv4/unicast. If this leaf-list is empty, the
bridge negotiates ipv4/unicast.
children.name: family
children.short-help: Address families the bridge negotiates for the script.

children.description:
json writes one JSON object per event. text writes ExaBGP's
one-event-per-line format, such as 'neighbor 127.0.0.1 receive update announced 10.0.0.0/24
next-hop 10.0.0.1 origin igp'. ExaBGP spells this leaf the same way and declares it per process,
so one bridge can feed a text script and a JSON script at once. The default is json because the
envelope Ze declares is 6.0.0, and ExaBGP 6 answers every process in JSON.
children.name: encoder
children.short-help: Format the script's events are written in.

values.name: json
values.short-help: Write each event as one JSON object.

values.name: text
values.short-help: Write each event as one line in the ExaBGP text format.

children.description:
ExaBGP's own event names: 'receive-update', 'send-update',
'receive-open', 'send-keepalive', 'receive-notification', 'send-refresh', 'receive-operational'
and their siblings, plus 'neighbor-changes', 'negotiated', 'fsm' and 'signal'. An EMPTY list
feeds no event from this peer, which is what an ExaBGP api block that names a process and no
message kind does.
children.name: event
children.short-help: Events this peer feeds this script.

children.description:
An ExaBGP neighbor names the processes it feeds in
'api { processes [ ... ] }' and the message kinds it feeds them in the same block, so the
relation is per peer AND per script. The migration writes one block here for each neighbor that
named this script. Ze also sends a command that names no neighbor to these peers alone. A
process with NO feed block is fed by every peer with every event, which is what one script and
one neighbor means.
children.name: feed
children.short-help: One peer that feeds this script, and the events it feeds.

children.description:
true starts the script again the moment it exits. false leaves it
stopped, which is what a script that does its work once and exits needs. A script that exits
more than five times in 64 seconds stays stopped whatever this leaf holds, and Ze logs that it
did. ExaBGP spells this leaf the same way and applies the same limit.
children.name: respawn
children.short-help: Start the script again when it exits.

children.description:
Two examples are './plugin.py' and 'python3 /opt/plugin.py'. Ze
splits the line on whitespace. The first token is the executable, and the rest are its
arguments. A block with no run command is refused.
children.name: run
children.short-help: Command line of the script.

children.description:
One block per script. An ExaBGP configuration declares the same set as
'process <name> { run ... }', and the migration writes one block here for each of them. Ze
starts every block, sends every event to every script, and reads commands from every script.
The bridge does nothing until one block names a run command.
children.name: process
children.short-help: One ExaBGP-format script the bridge runs as a subprocess.

children.description:
RFC 2918 defines the route-refresh capability. When this leaf is
true, Ze advertises the capability on every session the bridge feeds.
children.name: route-refresh
children.short-help: Advertise the BGP route-refresh capability.

children.description:
Present this container to configure the internal exabgp-bridge
plugin.
children.name: bridge
children.short-help: In-process ExaBGP bridge settings.

exabgp.description:
The bridge itself lives in the bridge container under this root, which
keeps the root free for other ExaBGP compatibility settings. The plugin is
registered as exabgp-bridge, so plugin { internal exabgp-bridge } starts
it. The bridge refuses to start until bridge run names a script.
exabgp.name: exabgp

children.description:
When true, the plugin removes every route it installed as it
stops. The default false keeps those routes in the kernel
after shutdown, which supports graceful restart.
children.name: flush-on-stop
children.short-help: Remove every ze-installed route when the plugin stops.

children.description:
The delay lets BGP reconverge and refresh the matching routes
before Ze removes the stale ones. The default is 30 seconds.
children.name: sweep-delay
children.short-help: Time to wait after startup before Ze sweeps stale routes.

children.description:
Ze writes each best route from the system RIB into the OS with
netlink, and it stamps rtm_protocol 250 on every route it
writes. That number separates a ze route from a route another
daemon owns, so `ip route show proto 250` lists them. The plugin
also watches the kernel, and it writes its route again where
something else overwrote one of them.
children.name: kernel
children.short-help: OS kernel route programming via netlink (Linux).

children.description:
P4Runtime addresses one forwarding pipeline on a target by
its device id, and the switch assigns that number. The
default 1 matches a target that carries one pipeline. The
type is a 64-bit unsigned number. The plugin opens no
P4Runtime session yet, so the value reaches no switch.
children.name: device-id
children.short-help: P4Runtime device ID.

children.description:
When true, the plugin deletes every forwarding entry it
installed as it stops. The default false leaves those
entries in the switch after shutdown, which supports
graceful restart. The plugin does not read this leaf yet:
the stop path keeps the entries whatever you write, and the
backend programs no switch. The kernel backend carries the
same leaf at fib/kernel/flush-on-stop.
children.name: flush-on-stop
children.short-help: Remove all forwarding entries when the plugin stops.

children.description:
The value names the P4Runtime gRPC server on the switch as
host:port, and 9559 is the port P4Runtime listens on by
convention. There is no default, so the leaf stays unset
until you write it. The plugin opens no connection to this
address yet, because the gRPC client is not written.
children.name: target
children.short-help:
P4Runtime gRPC target address (host:port).
Example: 127.0.0.1:9559

children.description:
fib-p4 subscribes to the best-change event of the system RIB
and holds every route it would program into a P4 switch with
P4Runtime. The gRPC client is not written yet. The plugin
writes a log line for each route it adds, replaces and deletes,
and it programs no switch. The command `show fib p4` prints the
prefix and the next hop of each entry the plugin holds. No leaf
in this container reaches a switch today.
children.name: p4
children.short-help: P4 switch route programming via gRPC/P4Runtime.

children.description:
The leaf declares how long a partial batch would wait
before dispatch, in milliseconds, and the plugin implements
no batching. A config that writes this leaf fails to parse,
with an error naming batch-interval-ms as not yet
implemented, so the default 10 never applies. The leaf
batch-size is deferred for the same reason.
children.name: batch-interval-ms
children.short-help:
Maximum time in milliseconds before dispatching
a partial batch.

children.description:
The leaf declares how many routes one batch dispatch would
carry, and the plugin implements no batching. A config that
writes this leaf fails to parse, with an error naming
batch-size as not yet implemented, so the default 256 never
applies. The system RIB already delivers one batch per
address family, and the VPP call IPRouteAddDel programs one
route per call. The plugin programs each route as it
arrives.
children.name: batch-size
children.short-help: Maximum number of routes per batch dispatch.

children.description:
The plugin programs the VPP FIB for as long as it runs, and
it does not read this leaf. The config parser accepts the
name and stores no value. Programming starts when the
plugin loads and stops when it unloads, so the default
false disables nothing. Unload the fib-vpp plugin to stop
programming the VPP FIB.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help:
Enable VPP FIB programming. Routes from system RIB
are programmed directly into VPP's FIB.

children.description:
The value names the VPP VRF that Ze programs, and the
default 0 is the default VRF. Ze gives it to the IP backend
and to the MPLS and SRv6 backends at the moment it builds
them. A new value reaches VPP when the plugin builds a
backend again, which happens when VPP connects.
children.name: table-id
children.short-help:
VRF table ID for route programming.
0 is the default VRF.

children.description:
Ze writes each best route from the system RIB into the VPP FIB
with the GoVPP call IPRouteAddDel. The plugin needs a live VPP
connector. With none it falls back to a backend that programs
nothing and writes a warning. Ze asks the system RIB to replay
the whole table each time VPP connects, so a VPP restart
reprograms every route.
children.name: vpp
children.short-help: VPP FIB programming via GoVPP binary API.

fib.description:
The FIB is where Ze writes the best routes the system RIB chose.
Each container under it is one backend: kernel programs the OS with
netlink, and vpp programs VPP with the GoVPP binary API. A backend
runs only while its plugin is loaded. Admin distance is not here,
because it belongs to the rib container.
fib.name: fib

children.description:
Firewall backend implementation. The default is nft, which is nftables through libnftnl. A future
backend can declare itself through firewall.RegisterBackend. The ze:backend YANG extension on
feature nodes declares per-feature backend support, so the commit-time gate rejects a config that
uses an unsupported primitive.
children.name: backend
children.short-help: Firewall backend implementation, nft by default.

children.description:
Ze asks for the A and the AAAA record of each name and puts every
address it gets into the group. Each name and each family keeps
its own schedule, so a name with a short TTL does not pull the
others with it. Ze accepts at most 64 addresses from one name and
one family, and logs a warning when it drops the rest.
children.name: domain-names
children.short-help: DNS names whose addresses are the members of this group.

children.description:
A name answering with a very short TTL would otherwise drive a
query and a set rewrite every few seconds. Ze waits this long at
least, whatever the answer says. A TTL of 0 means 'do not cache'
and Ze also waits the floor for it, rather than treating it as
already expired.
children.name: ttl-floor
children.short-help: Shortest interval Ze waits before it resolves a name again.

children.description:
Ze resolves each name in the group and puts the addresses into an
nftables set a rule can match with source-domain-group or
destination-domain-group. Each name is resolved again when its own
answer expires, and the set is reprogrammed only when the addresses
changed. A commit naming a group Ze has never resolved is refused:
run 'update firewall domain-group <name>' first. A permit rule keyed
on a DNS name trusts whoever controls that name.
children.name: domain-group
children.short-help: Address group whose members are what its DNS names resolve to.

children.description:
Remove ze-owned nftables tables from the kernel when the ze process stops in an orderly way
(SIGTERM). The default is true, so a stopped daemon leaves no rules behind. Set the leaf to false to
use ze as a one-shot provisioner: program the rules, let the process exit, and leave them running in
the kernel, like nft -f. The leaf keys off how the process exits, and it is unrelated to BGP
graceful restart. A crash never runs the shutdown path, so tables always persist across a crash
whatever this leaf holds. The leaf governs every ze table producer (firewall,
control-plane-protection, policy-routes, ddos-local), which share one backend.
children.name: flush-on-shutdown
children.short-help: Remove ze-owned nftables tables when the ze process stops in an orderly way.

children.description:
The keyword writes net.ipv4.icmp_echo_ignore_all. The sysctl is inverted, so enable
writes 0 and disable writes 1. A router set to disable answers no ICMP echo request.
A monitoring system that pings it sees no reply.
children.name: all-ping
children.short-help: Control ICMP echo (ping) responses.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Ignore all ICMP echo requests (icmp_echo_ignore_all=1)

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Allow ICMP echo replies (icmp_echo_ignore_all=0)

children.description:
Control broadcast ICMP echo responses. The sysctl is inverted, so enable sets
icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts to 0.
children.name: broadcast-ping
children.short-help: Control broadcast ICMP echo responses.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Ignore broadcast ICMP echo (icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts=1)

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Allow broadcast ICMP echo (icmp_echo_ignore_broadcasts=0)

children.description:
The keyword writes net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_redirects. The value enable writes 1,
and disable writes 0. The leaf governs IPv6 alone. The IPv4 sysctl stays under
receive-redirects.
children.name: ipv6-receive-redirects
children.short-help: Control acceptance of IPv6 ICMP redirect messages.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Reject IPv6 ICMP redirects (accept_redirects=0)

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Accept IPv6 ICMP redirects (accept_redirects=1)

children.description:
The keyword writes net.ipv6.conf.all.accept_source_route. The value enable writes 1,
and disable writes 0. A source-routed packet carries a routing header that names
hops it MUST pass. An accepted one lets the sender pick the path through this
router.
children.name: ipv6-src-route
children.short-help: Control acceptance of IPv6 packets with source routing headers.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Reject IPv6 source-routed packets (accept_source_route=0)

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Accept IPv6 source-routed packets (accept_source_route=1)

children.description:
The keyword writes net.ipv4.conf.all.log_martians. The value enable writes 1, and
disable writes 0. A martian packet carries a source address that no route can reach.
The kernel writes one line for each such packet, and a flood of them fills the log.
children.name: log-martians
children.short-help: Log packets with impossible source addresses.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not log martian packets (log_martians=0)

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Log martian packets (log_martians=1)

children.description:
The keyword writes net.ipv4.conf.all.accept_redirects. The value enable writes 1,
and disable writes 0. An accepted ICMP redirect installs a host route in the kernel.
A neighbor on the same segment can then change where this router sends the traffic.
children.name: receive-redirects
children.short-help: Control acceptance of IPv4 ICMP redirect messages.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Reject ICMP redirects (accept_redirects=0)

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Accept ICMP redirects (accept_redirects=1)

children.description:
The keyword writes net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects. The value enable writes 1, and
disable writes 0. A router sends an ICMP redirect when it forwards a packet back out
the interface the packet arrived on.
children.name: send-redirects
children.short-help: Control sending of IPv4 ICMP redirect messages.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Do not send ICMP redirects (send_redirects=0)

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Send ICMP redirects (send_redirects=1)

children.description:
The keyword writes net.ipv4.conf.all.rp_filter. The value disable writes 0, strict
writes 1, and loose writes 2. Strict drops a packet when the best route back to its
source does not use the interface it arrived on. Loose drops it only when no route
back to the source exists.
children.name: source-validation
children.short-help: Reverse path filtering mode for source address validation.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: No source address validation (rp_filter=0)

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Loose reverse path filtering (rp_filter=2)

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Strict reverse path filtering (rp_filter=1)

children.description:
The keyword writes net.ipv4.tcp_syncookies. The value enable writes 1, and disable
writes 0. A kernel with cookies on answers a SYN that overflows the accept queue. It
keeps no state for that half-open connection until the third packet returns the
cookie.
children.name: syn-cookies
children.short-help: TCP SYN cookie protection against SYN flood attacks.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Disable TCP SYN cookies (tcp_syncookies=0)

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Enable TCP SYN cookies (tcp_syncookies=1)

children.description:
Network security defaults mapped to kernel sysctls. The container provides VyOS-compatible keyword
toggles for common settings. At apply time each keyword translates to a sysctl key and value pair
emitted to the sysctl plugin. An explicit sysctl setting always overrides these.
children.name: global-options
children.short-help: Network security defaults mapped to kernel sysctls.

children.description:
The prefixes the IRR resolves for this AS-SET form the
allowed source-address set of the interface. The match
needs cached prefix data. A config commit is refused
when no cached data exists.
children.name: source-as-set
children.short-help: AS-SET whose IRR-resolved prefixes are the allowed source addresses.

children.description:
Ze drops a packet that arrives on this interface when its
source address is not in the IRR-resolved prefixes of the
AS-SET.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Per-interface AS-SET binding for ingress source validation.

children.description:
The default is https://www.peeringdb.com. Ze adds /api/net?asn=<N>
to this value for each query, and holds each answer for one hour.
Ze skips TLS verification for the host 127.0.0.1 alone, which is
what makes a local test server work.
children.name: peeringdb-url
children.short-help:
Base URL for PeeringDB API queries.
Override for testing with a mock server.

children.description:
The default 0 disables the automatic refresh, and the
operator then runs 'update firewall irr' by hand. A value
in 60..86400 starts the periodic refresh. That refresh
fails closed: a failed query keeps the last-good cache.
children.name: refresh-interval
children.short-help: Seconds between automatic IRR re-queries.

children.description:
The default is whois.radb.net. Ze adds port 43 when the value names
no port, so a host:port value reaches the port you name. One query
waits 10 seconds at most, and Ze holds each answer for one hour.
children.name: server
children.short-help: IRR whois server hostname or host:port.

children.description:
The settings under it reach every IRR reference of the firewall, in a
term and on an interface alike. Ze keeps the resolved prefixes in a
zefs prefix store that the BGP IRR filter shares, so one query serves
both. A commit that names a reference with no cached prefixes is
refused.
children.name: irr
children.short-help: IRR policy settings for firewall prefix-list resolution.

children.description:
A base chain MUST carry a hook, and verify refuses one that does not. The hook
decides where in the kernel path the chain sees the packet. The values input,
output, forward, prerouting and postrouting serve every family. The value
ingress serves a netdev or inet table, and egress serves a netdev table.
children.name: hook
children.short-help: Netfilter hook point (base chains only)

values.name: egress
values.short-help: Egress hook (netdev)

values.name: forward
values.short-help: Forward hook

values.name: ingress
values.short-help: Ingress hook (netdev/inet)

values.name: input
values.short-help: Input hook

values.name: output
values.short-help: Output hook

values.name: postrouting
values.short-help: Postrouting hook

values.name: prerouting
values.short-help: Prerouting hook

children.description:
The policy decides a packet that reaches the end of the chain with no verdict
from a term. A base chain MUST carry accept or drop, and verify refuses a base
chain that carries neither. A regular chain takes no policy, and the packet
returns to the chain that jumped to it.
children.name: policy
children.short-help: Default policy (base chains only)

values.name: accept
values.short-help: Accept by default

values.name: drop
values.short-help: Drop by default

children.description:
The chain with the lower number runs first at the same hook. Verify accepts -400
to 400 and refuses a number outside that range, which catches a typo such as 500
for 50. The well-known nftables values all fit: raw -300, mangle -150, filter 0,
security 50, nat prerouting -100 and nat postrouting 100. An absent leaf means
0.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Chain priority (base chains only)

children.description:
The mark lives on the conntrack entry, so every packet of one flow reads the same value
in both directions. The mark leaf beside it reads the per-packet mark instead, which
starts at 0 for each packet. The match is conntrack-driven, and it needs a backend that
integrates with the kernel nf_conntrack module.
children.name: connection-mark
children.short-help: Connection mark value with an optional mask.

children.description:
Connection tracking state(s). The match is conntrack-driven, and it requires a backend that
integrates with the kernel nf_conntrack module.
children.name: connection-state
children.short-help: Connection tracking state(s) the rule matches.

children.description:
The value takes the same two forms the source-address leaf takes. Ze reads the IPv4
destination at network-header offset 16 and the IPv6 destination at offset 24. An inet
table therefore carries an nfproto guard in front of the match, so an IPv4 rule never
reads IPv6 bytes.
children.name: destination-address
children.short-help: Destination IP prefix or @set-name

children.description:
The cache rule is the one source-as-set states. The match
needs cached prefix data, so run 'update firewall irr as-set
<name>' first. A config commit is refused when no cached data
exists.
children.name: destination-as-set
children.short-help: Match the destination address against the IRR-resolved prefixes of this AS-SET.

children.description:
The cache rule is the one source-asn states. The match needs
cached prefix data, so run 'update firewall irr asn <N>'
first. A config commit is refused when no cached data
exists.
children.name: destination-asn
children.short-help: Match the destination address against the IRR-resolved prefixes of this ASN.

children.description:
The cache rule is the one source-domain-group states. The match needs
the group's names to have resolved at least once, so a commit is
refused when they have not: run 'update firewall domain-group <name>'
first.
children.name: destination-domain-group
children.short-help: Match the destination address against the addresses of this domain group.

children.description:
The value takes the same four forms the source-port leaf takes. The match reads the
transport header at a fixed offset and carries no protocol guard of its own. Name the
protocol leaf in the same from block, or the term reads those two bytes out of any
protocol the chain sees.
children.name: destination-port
children.short-help: Destination port, range, or list

children.description:
The value is a number 0 to 63, or a symbolic name such as ef, af41 or cs6. The match is
IPv4-only. Verify refuses it in a table of family ip6, arp, bridge or netdev, and names
the family it read.
children.name: dscp
children.short-help: DSCP value

children.description:
ICMPv4 type. It accepts symbolic names from nftables, such as echo-request, echo-reply,
destination-unreachable and time-exceeded. It also accepts a numeric byte value 0..255.
children.name: icmp-type
children.short-help: ICMPv4 type, as an nftables symbolic name or a byte value 0..255.

children.description:
ICMPv6 type. It accepts symbolic names from nftables, such as echo-request, nd-neighbor-solicit and
packet-too-big. It also accepts a numeric byte value 0..255.
children.name: icmpv6-type
children.short-help: ICMPv6 type, as an nftables symbolic name or a byte value 0..255.

children.description:
Input interface name. A trailing asterisk, for example 'l2tp*', matches any interface whose name
begins with the given prefix.
children.name: input-interface
children.short-help: Input interface name, with a trailing asterisk for a prefix match.

children.description:
The value is decimal or 0x-prefixed, and an optional /mask follows in the same form. An
absent mask means 0xffffffff, so the whole 32-bit mark MUST be equal. With a mask, Ze
ANDs the packet mark with it before the compare, so the other bits do not matter. The
mark lives for one packet.
children.name: mark
children.short-help: Packet mark value/mask

children.description:
Output interface name. A trailing asterisk, for example 'veth*', matches any interface whose name
begins with the given prefix.
children.name: output-interface
children.short-help: Output interface name, with a trailing asterisk for a prefix match.

children.description:
The names are tcp, udp, icmp, icmpv6, sctp, gre, esp, ah, ospf and vrrp. The match reads
the kernel meta field l4proto rather than an IP header byte, so one term serves IPv4 and
IPv6 alike.
children.name: protocol
children.short-help: L4 protocol

values.name: ah
values.short-help: Match IPsec AH, IP protocol 51.

values.name: esp
values.short-help: Match IPsec ESP, IP protocol 50.

values.name: gre
values.short-help: Match GRE, IP protocol 47.

values.name: icmp
values.short-help: Match ICMP, IP protocol 1.

values.name: icmpv6
values.short-help: Match ICMPv6, IP protocol 58.

values.name: ospf
values.short-help: Match OSPF, IP protocol 89.

values.name: sctp
values.short-help: Match SCTP, IP protocol 132.

values.name: tcp
values.short-help: Match TCP, IP protocol 6.

values.name: udp
values.short-help: Match UDP, IP protocol 17.

values.name: vrrp
values.short-help: Match VRRP, IP protocol 112.

children.description:
A prefix carries its length, so write 10.0.0.0/24 or 10.0.0.1/32. A bare address is
refused. The form @name matches against a named set of the same table, and that set MUST
be of type ipv4 or ipv6. Ze reads the IPv4 source at network-header offset 12 and the
IPv6 source at offset 8.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IP prefix or @set-name

children.description:
The match needs cached prefix data, so run 'update firewall
irr as-set <name>' first. A config commit is refused when no
cached data exists.
children.name: source-as-set
children.short-help: Match the source address against the IRR-resolved prefixes of this AS-SET.

children.description:
The match needs cached prefix data, so run 'update firewall
irr asn <N>' first. A config commit is refused when no cached
data exists.
children.name: source-asn
children.short-help: Match the source address against the IRR-resolved prefixes of this ASN.

children.description:
Names a domain-group defined under firewall. The match needs the
group's names to have resolved at least once, so a commit is refused
when they have not: run 'update firewall domain-group <name>' first.
children.name: source-domain-group
children.short-help: Match the source address against the addresses of this domain group.

children.description:
The value is one port, a range such as 80-90, a comma list such as 22,80,443, or @name
for a named set of type inet-service. Verify refuses a port of 0, an inverted range, an
overlapping pair and more than 128 comma entries. Several ranges lower to one anonymous
interval set in the kernel.
children.name: source-port
children.short-help: Source port, range, or list

children.description:
Every match in this container MUST hold at the same time for the term to
act, because they lower into one kernel rule. A from block that declares no
match matches every packet the chain sees.
children.name: from
children.short-help: Match criteria

children.description:
The verdict ends the evaluation of the packet in this chain, so a later term of the same
chain never sees it. A packet that reaches the end of the chain with no verdict takes
the chain policy instead.
children.name: accept
children.short-help: Accept the packet

children.description:
The form is the one mark-set takes. With a mask Ze reads the current conntrack mark,
clears the masked bits, puts the new value in and writes it back. The mark then
holds for every later packet of that flow.
children.name: value
children.short-help: Mark value with optional mask

children.description:
The mark lives on the conntrack entry, so it survives for the whole flow and both
directions read it. The mark-set action writes the per-packet mark instead, and that
mark starts at 0 on each packet. The nft backend is required.
children.name: connection-mark-set
children.short-help: Write the conntrack mark of the packet's flow.

children.description:
Verify refuses a non-empty value today. An nftables named counter is a table-scoped
object plus an objref expression, and Ze emits an anonymous counter instead. Leave
the leaf unset.
children.name: name
children.short-help: Counter name, reserved for a future named-counter feature.

children.description:
Anonymous per-rule counter. A non-empty `name` leaf is reserved for a future named-counter feature,
and verify rejects it today.
children.name: counter
children.short-help: Anonymous per-rule counter.

children.description:
The value takes the same form the snat leaf takes. Both ends of an address range
MUST be of one family, and neither range can be inverted. With no port in the value
Ze programs the address alone, so the destination port stays as the sender wrote it.
children.name: to
children.short-help: NAT target address:port

children.description:
Translation happens before the routing decision. The packet is then
forwarded toward the rewritten address, and not toward the address
the sender wrote.
children.name: dnat
children.short-help: Rewrite the destination address of a packet arriving at this router.

children.description:
The packet is discarded and nothing goes back to the sender. The sender waits for its
own timeout to learn. Use a reject term instead when the sender MUST learn at once.
children.name: drop
children.short-help: Drop the packet

children.description:
Ze rewrites the top 6 bits of the IPv4 TOS byte and keeps the 2 ECN bits below them. It
then recomputes the IPv4 header checksum. Verify refuses the action in a table of family
ip6, arp, bridge or netdev. An inet table programs the term as two kernel rules, one for
each family, because the field sits at a different offset in each.
children.name: dscp-set
children.short-help: Set DSCP field value

children.description:
In a NAT chain term, skip NAT for matching traffic. It lowers to the same `return` verdict the
operator could have written directly. The keyword exists for VyOS-config parity.
children.name: exclude
children.short-help: In a NAT chain term, skip NAT for the matching traffic.

children.description:
The value is the bare flowtable name, and verify refuses a name the same table does
not declare. A leading @ is part of the nft command syntax and not part of this
value.
children.name: flowtable
children.short-help: Flowtable name declared in this table.

children.description:
Hardware or software flow offload through an nftables flowtable. The VPP dataplane is itself the
fast path, and it does not expose a flowtable surface.
children.name: flow-offload
children.short-help: Hardware or software flow offload through an nftables flowtable.

children.description:
The target chain MUST be declared in the same table, and verify refuses a name the table
does not hold. Evaluation does not come back, so the terms after this one never run for
that packet.
children.name: goto
children.short-help: Goto target chain (no return)

children.description:
The target chain MUST be declared in the same table, and verify refuses a name the table
does not hold. Evaluation comes back to the term after this one when the target chain
ends or returns.
children.name: jump
children.short-help: Jump to target chain

children.description:
The burst is the allowance the term carries over from an idle period. It counts
packets under a packet rate and bytes under a byte rate, which follows the dimension
the rate leaf sets. An absent leaf means 0.
children.name: burst
children.short-help: Burst size

children.description:
The value is a count, a slash, then second, minute, hour or day. A plain count
limits packets, and a byte form such as 1mbytes/second limits bytes. The byte
prefixes scale as kbytes=1024, mbytes=1024^2 and gbytes=1024^3.
children.name: rate
children.short-help: Rate limit, as a count and a time unit, such as 10/second.

children.description:
Traffic past the limit stops matching the term, so it falls through to
what follows rather than being dropped here. Put the drop in the next
term when that is what you want.
children.name: limit-rate
children.short-help: Match only while the packet rate stays under a stated limit.

children.description:
The number is a syslog severity, 0 for emerg through 7 for debug. An absent leaf
leaves the kernel default in place. Ze holds the level as a pointer, so it tells an
explicit 0 apart from an absent leaf and sets NFTA_LOG_LEVEL only for the explicit
one.
children.name: level
children.short-help: Log level (syslog severity)

children.description:
The kernel writes the string in front of each logged packet, so a search over the
log finds the rule that wrote the line. The length is 0 to 127 characters. Ze sets
the NFTA_LOG_PREFIX attribute only when the string is not empty.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Log prefix string

children.description:
Logging does not decide the packet, so the term still needs an accept
or a drop beside it. A rule that logs every packet of a busy link
costs the kernel a line per packet.
children.name: log
children.short-help: Record the packet and go on evaluating the term.

children.description:
With no mask Ze writes all 32 bits. With a mask Ze reads the current mark, clears
the masked bits, puts the new value in and writes the mark back, so the bits outside
the mask survive. The value is decimal or 0x-prefixed, and the mask follows a slash
in the same form.
children.name: value
children.short-help: Mark value with optional mask

children.description:
Write the kernel skb mark. Different backends carry per-packet metadata differently. The VPP
classifier's equivalent uses opaque keys through ClassifyAddDelSession.
children.name: mark-set
children.short-help: Write the kernel skb mark.

children.description:
The flag cannot be combined with port-range, and verify refuses a term that sets
both. Ze reads the leaf as a presence flag, so it takes no value.
children.name: persistent
children.short-help: Program the masquerade with the NF_NAT_RANGE_PERSISTENT flag.

children.description:
The kernel picks the translated source port inside this range. Verify refuses a port
of 0 and an inverted range. The leaf cannot be combined with random or persistent,
and verify refuses a term that sets both.
children.name: port-range
children.short-help: Source port or port range for the translated source, such as 1024-65535.

children.description:
The leaf turns the random flag into NF_NAT_RANGE_PROTO_RANDOM_FULLY, which is
the wider randomization the kernel offers. Ze sets one of the two flags, never
both.
children.name: full
children.short-help: Use full randomization

children.description:
Ze sets NF_NAT_RANGE_PROTO_RANDOM on the masquerade. Add the full leaf under it for
NF_NAT_RANGE_PROTO_RANDOM_FULLY, and Ze then sets that flag alone. Neither flag can
be combined with port-range.
children.name: random
children.short-help: Randomize the translated source port.

children.description:
Masquerade (source NAT with outgoing interface address). Restrict the source port range with
port-range, or set the randomization and persistence flags. Port mapping and flags are mutually
exclusive.
children.name: masquerade
children.short-help: Masquerade, which is source NAT with the outgoing interface address.

children.description:
The packet skips conntrack, so the kernel opens no entry for its flow. A
connection-state or a connection-mark match in a later term cannot see that packet. NAT
needs a conntrack entry, so a NAT term cannot translate it either.
children.name: notrack
children.short-help: Disable connection tracking for the packet.

children.description:
The value is 1 to 65535. Ze rewrites the destination port to it, and the destination
address becomes an address of this router. A term that names no port cannot be
written, because the leaf is mandatory.
children.name: to
children.short-help: Local port number

children.description:
It is a destination NAT whose target is this machine, so the local
service sees the original source address and can answer it.
children.name: redirect
children.short-help: Send the packet to a port on this router instead of its destination.

children.description:
The number is the code byte of the ICMP unreachable message, and an absent leaf
sends 0, which means network unreachable. Ze passes the number to the kernel
whatever the reject type is, so set the leaf only beside an ICMP reject type.
children.name: code
children.short-help: ICMP code

children.description:
An absent leaf and the value icmp both send an ICMP unreachable message. The value
icmpv6 selects the ICMPX unreachable form, which the kernel renders for the family
of the packet. The value tcp-reset sends a TCP reset, which a TCP client sees at
once.
children.name: with
children.short-help: Reject response type

values.name: icmp
values.short-help: Answer with an ICMP destination unreachable message.

values.name: icmpv6
values.short-help: Answer with the unreachable message of the packet's own IP family.

values.name: tcp-reset
values.short-help: Answer a TCP packet with a TCP reset.

children.description:
The sender learns at once rather than waiting for a timeout, and the
reply costs one packet per dropped packet. Use a drop term when the
sender SHOULD learn nothing.
children.name: reject
children.short-help: Drop the packet and answer the sender with an ICMP or TCP reset.

children.description:
In a regular chain the packet returns to the term after the jump that reached this
chain. In a base chain the chain policy decides the packet. The exclude keyword lowers
to this same verdict.
children.name: return
children.short-help: Return to caller chain

children.description:
The value is an address, or an address and a port after a colon, such as 1.2.3.4:80.
An address range and a port range are both accepted, and Ze programs each as a
minimum and a maximum register. A comma list of ports is refused. With no port in
the value Ze translates the address alone.
children.name: to
children.short-help: NAT target address:port

children.description:
The reply is translated back on the same conntrack entry. A flow that
started before the rule was installed keeps its old translation. It
changes when that entry expires.
children.name: snat
children.short-help: Rewrite the source address of a packet leaving this router.

children.description:
The value is 1 to 65535, and verify refuses 0. The table MUST be of family ip, ip6 or
inet, because arp, bridge and netdev carry no TCP header to rewrite. A clamp repairs a
path whose smallest link cannot carry the segment size the two ends agreed.
children.name: tcp-mss-set
children.short-help: Clamp TCP Maximum Segment Size option to the given value

children.description:
The term MUST carry at least one action here, and verify refuses one that
carries none. Ze writes the modifiers first and the NAT and verdict actions
after them. A counter or a log in the same term therefore runs before the
packet is accepted or dropped.
children.name: then
children.short-help: Actions and modifiers

children.description:
The list is ordered-by user, and the backend writes one kernel rule for each
term in that order. A term MUST carry at least one action, and verify refuses
one that carries none.
children.name: term
children.short-help: Named rule (from/then structure)

children.description:
A base chain MUST carry a type, and verify refuses one that does not. The value
filter selects packet filtering, nat selects network address translation, and
route selects the routing decision override. Each lowers to the nftables chain
type of the same name.
children.name: type
children.short-help: Chain type (base chains only)

values.name: filter
values.short-help: Packet filtering

values.name: nat
values.short-help: Network address translation

values.name: route
values.short-help: Routing decision override

children.description:
A chain that carries a type or a hook is a base chain, and the kernel attaches it to
that hook. A chain with neither is a regular chain, and only a jump or a goto from
another chain of the same table reaches it.
children.name: chain
children.short-help: Named chain within table

children.description:
The value inet carries IPv4 and IPv6 in one table. Ze puts an nfproto guard in front
of each address match there, so an IPv4 rule never reads IPv6 header bytes. The
values ip and ip6 carry one family each. The values arp, bridge and netdev carry no
IP header, so a dscp match, dscp-set and tcp-mss-set are refused in them.
children.name: family
children.short-help: Address family

values.name: arp
values.short-help: ARP

values.name: bridge
values.short-help: Bridge

values.name: inet
values.short-help: Dual-stack IPv4+IPv6

values.name: ip
values.short-help: IPv4 only

values.name: ip6
values.short-help: IPv6 only

values.name: netdev
values.short-help: Netdev

children.description:
Each entry is a kernel interface name. The flowtable takes flows from those
interfaces alone, and a flowtable that names none takes nothing.
children.name: device
children.short-help: Devices for offload

children.description:
The leaf takes the chain-hook type, so the parser accepts every hook name. Apply
refuses each one except ingress and names the value it read.
children.name: hook
children.short-help: Hook point, which MUST be ingress.

values.name: egress
values.short-help: Egress hook (netdev)

values.name: forward
values.short-help: Forward hook

values.name: ingress
values.short-help: Ingress hook (netdev/inet)

values.name: input
values.short-help: Input hook

values.name: output
values.short-help: Output hook

values.name: postrouting
values.short-help: Postrouting hook

values.name: prerouting
values.short-help: Prerouting hook

children.description:
Ze passes the number to the kernel with no range check, so the -400 to 400 range
that a base chain takes does not apply here. The leaf is mandatory, so a
flowtable states its priority even when it is the only one.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Flowtable priority at the ingress hook.

children.description:
Hardware offload flowtable. The flowtable is nftables-specific. The VPP dataplane is itself the fast
path, and it does not expose a flowtable surface.
children.name: flowtable
children.short-help: Hardware offload flowtable, which is nftables-specific.

children.description:
The kernel deletes the element when the timeout runs out. The enclosing set
MUST carry flags-timeout, and the timeout reaches the kernel only under that
flag.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: Per-element timeout in seconds, where 0 means no timeout.

children.description:
Static set elements. The value form is interpreted per set type. ipv4 and ipv6 accept addresses, or
prefixes when flags-interval is set. inet-service accepts port numbers. mark accepts a numeric or
0x-prefixed value. ether accepts aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff. ifname accepts an interface name.
children.name: element
children.short-help: Static set elements, whose value form follows the set type.

children.description:
Ze programs the kernel set with the constant flag. The elements of a ze set come
from config, and Ze writes no rule that adds one at runtime.
children.name: flags-constant
children.short-help: Immutable after creation

children.description:
Ze programs the kernel set with the dynamic flag. Ze writes no rule that adds an
element, so the elements still come from config.
children.name: flags-dynamic
children.short-help: Dynamically populated

children.description:
Ze programs the kernel set with the interval flag. An element written in config
still carries one value: Ze drops the length of a prefix written there and
programs the bare address. The irr plugin is what fills an interval set with
ranges today.
children.name: flags-interval
children.short-help: Enable interval ranges

children.description:
The flag MUST be set for a per-element timeout to reach the kernel. The netlink
library writes the element timeout attribute only when the parent set carries
the flag, so a timeout under a set without it is dropped on the way down.
children.name: flags-timeout
children.short-help: Enable per-element timeouts

children.description:
The type decides the element form and which match can read the set. An address
match reads an ipv4 or ipv6 set, and a port match reads an inet-service set.
Verify refuses any other pairing. No match keyword reads an ether, mark or
ifname set today, so Ze creates that set and no term uses it.
children.name: type
children.short-help: Element data type

values.name: ether
values.short-help: Ethernet addresses

values.name: ifname
values.short-help: Interface names

values.name: inet-service
values.short-help: TCP/UDP ports

values.name: ipv4
values.short-help: IPv4 addresses

values.name: ipv6
values.short-help: IPv6 addresses

values.name: mark
values.short-help: Packet marks

children.description:
A term matches against the set with @name in place of an address or a port. Ze
applies the sets of a table before its chains, so a term can reference a set the
same commit creates. A reference never crosses a table.
children.name: set
children.short-help: Named set

children.description:
The kernel table is ze_<name>. Ze changes and deletes only a table that carries the ze_
prefix, so a table another tool wrote stays untouched. The chains, the named sets and
the flowtables of one table reference each other by name, and no reference crosses a
table.
children.name: table
children.short-help: Named firewall table

firewall.description:
Ze-managed nftables firewall tables. Table names are bare in config, and the component adds the ze_
prefix.
firewall.name: firewall

children.description:
Collector IP address, and the leaf is mandatory. The address and port together are where Ze
sends every datagram of this collector. A commit that gives a value Ze cannot parse as an
