children.name: rdnss
children.short-help: Recursive DNS servers advertised to hosts (RFC 8106 Section 5.1).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvReachableTime. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: reachable-time
children.short-help: How long a host treats a neighbor as reachable after a reachability confirmation.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvRetransTimer. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: retransmit-timer
children.short-help: Time between retransmitted Neighbor Solicitations on this link.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvDefaultLifetime. 0 says that Ze
is not a default router, and the prefixes and the resolvers in the
advertisement still apply. Any other value must be at least
maximum-interval, and config verify rejects a smaller one.
children.name: router-lifetime
children.short-help: How long a host keeps Ze in its default router list (AdvDefaultLifetime).

children.description:
Ze advertises prefixes, flags and resolvers on this link, so that a
host autoconfigures. That is the role radvd fills on another system.
Sending is separate from accepting: set forwarding true on an
advertising interface, and leave accept-ra at 0 unless this interface
also learns from another router.
children.name: router-advertisement
children.short-help: Router Advertisement sender (RFC 4861).

children.description:
strict drops a packet whose source address would not be routed back
through this interface. loose drops a packet whose source address has
no route at all. disable performs no source address validation.
children.name: rpf-check
children.short-help: Reverse path filtering mode, on the VPP data plane only for IPv6.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: No source address validation.

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address has no route at all.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address does not route back through this interface.

children.description:
The container holds one unit's IPv6 state. Ze installs the addresses
through netlink. Ze turns autoconf, accept-ra and forwarding into
net.ipv6.conf.<iface> sysctl writes, which it emits on the event bus for
the sysctl plugin to perform.
children.name: ipv6
children.short-help: IPv6 addressing, forwarding, autoconfiguration, and DHCPv6 client for this unit.

children.description:
Ze installs a tc mirred filter that copies each transmitted frame
toward the named interface. Ze resolves the name through the same
selector map as the source, so a capture port bound by mac/match or
aliased by os-name works. An unbound name installs no mirror.
children.name: egress
children.short-help: Mirror egress traffic to this interface

children.description:
Ze installs a tc mirred filter that copies each received frame toward
the named interface. Ze resolves the name through the same selector
map as the source, so a capture port bound by mac/match or aliased by
os-name works. An unbound name installs no mirror.
children.name: ingress
children.short-help: Mirror ingress traffic to this interface

children.description:
The netlink backend mirrors through tc mirred. The vpp backend programs
SPAN, through sw_interface_span_enable_disable, and it maps the ingress
direction and the egress direction onto the RX SPAN state and the TX SPAN
state, as a device-level port mirror.
children.name: mirror
children.short-help: Traffic mirroring for this interface.

children.description:
The leaf sets net.mpls.conf.<iface>.input. net.mpls.platform_labels
sets the size of the global label table.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable MPLS label input on this interface.

children.description:
Ze turns the enable leaf below into a net.mpls.conf.<iface>.input sysctl
write. The size of the global label table is a separate sysctl,
net.mpls.platform_labels, which the sysctl config block sets.
children.name: mpls
children.short-help: MPLS forwarding on this interface (RFC 3031 LSR).

children.description:
A lower value is preferred. On link-down, ze increases the metric by 1024,
which deprioritizes the interface. The default 254 ranks a learned default
below a static default and below a protocol-learned one, the way rib
distance ranks connected 0, static 10 and ebgp 20. Write 0 to put a learned
default on the kernel metric that an operator's static default also uses.
The two then share one kernel route, and the last writer owns it. A value
above 0 also makes ze own the IPv6 default routes of the interface: ze sets
accept_ra_defrtr=0 and installs the ::/0 routes itself.
children.name: route-priority
children.short-help: Route metric for default routes learned on this unit through DHCP or router advertisement.

children.description:
The built-in profiles are dsr, router, hardened, multihomed and proxy. A
user-defined profile comes from a sysctl { profile ... } config block. Ze
applies the profiles in order, and the last one wins on a key that two
profiles both set.
children.name: sysctl-profile
children.short-help: Named sysctl profiles to apply to this unit.

children.description:
The range is 1 to 4094, which is what IEEE 802.1Q allows. Ze creates a
kernel 802.1Q subinterface named <parent>.<vlan-id>. An L3 tunnel refuses
a unit that carries this leaf, because only gretap and ip6gretap carry
Ethernet frames.
children.name: vlan-id
children.short-help: VLAN identifier

children.description:
Ze creates no VRF device and enslaves no interface, so a unit cannot use a
routing table other than the main table. The leaf stays in the schema so
that the refusal can say why. It becomes functional when VRF support ships.
children.name: vrf
children.short-help: Not implemented. Ze refuses a config that sets this leaf.

children.description:
A unit holds the addresses, the VLAN tag and the sysctl settings of one
logical subinterface. A unit with a vlan-id creates a kernel subinterface
named <parent>.<vlan-id>. A unit without one puts its addresses on the parent
device.
children.name: unit
children.short-help: Logical interface unit

children.description:
The choice below selects the encapsulation kind, and each case carries only the
leaves that are valid for that kind. The local endpoint and remote endpoint
pattern matches bgp peer connection { local { ip ... } remote { ip ... } }.
children.name: tunnel
children.short-help: Tunnel interface, in the GRE, GRETAP, IPIP, SIT or IP6TNL family.

children.description:
The value 'none' disables inheritance. When this leaf is set on the
interface, every VLAN unit inherits the profile. A unit that sets its own profile keeps
that one.
children.name: class-of-service
children.short-help: Name of a class-of-service ieee-802.1p profile, or 'none'.

children.description:
Ze keeps the text in the config only, and it makes no kernel call for it. The
kernel link alias IFLA_IFALIAS carries ze's own ownership marker instead, so
a description never reaches it.
children.name: description
children.short-help: Interface description

children.description:
Ze skips a disabled interface at every apply step, so it creates no device
and it installs no address. A device ze created before is deleted, because a
disabled interface leaves the managed set. The config block stays in place.
children.name: disable
children.short-help: Administratively disable this interface

children.description:
An example value is 02:42:ac:11:00:02. Ze applies the value when it creates
the interface. When the leaf is omitted, the kernel assigns a MAC by
itself.
children.name: address
children.short-help: Override the kernel-assigned MAC with a colon-separated hex value.

children.description:
The binding is by MAC rather than by name. The resolver matches the
device's permanent factory address (IFLA_PERM_ADDRESS) when the device
reports one, so the binding survives an operational MAC override. For a
virtual device that reports no permanent address, the resolver matches the
current address. This leaf takes precedence over os-name. It applies to the
ethernet kind only, which is the matched physical kind. Ze identifies the
kinds it creates (dummy, veth, bridge and the rest) by the name ze assigns.
When the matching device is absent, the binding waits until the device
appears.
children.name: match
children.short-help: Bind this logical interface to the kernel device that carries this hardware MAC.

children.description:
address overrides the operational MAC address. match selects the kernel device
by its MAC. The two leaves are independent, so ze can match a NIC by its
permanent factory MAC and override its operational MAC at the same time.
children.name: mac
children.short-help: Hardware MAC settings for this interface.

children.description:
The range is 68 to 16000 bytes and the default is 1500. Ze applies the value
with the netlink call LinkSetMTU after it creates the interface. Ze restores
the previous value when a later step of the same apply fails.
children.name: mtu
children.short-help: Maximum transmission unit

children.description:
GRO aggregates small incoming packets into larger ones before it passes
them up the network stack, which reduces the CPU cost per packet. GRO is
software-based, so it works on all NIC types, including veth and dummy. Ze
applies it through the kernel ioctl ETHTOOL_SGRO. It is equivalent to
'ethtool -K <dev> gro on|off'.
children.name: gro
children.short-help: Generic Receive Offload: aggregate small incoming packets before the network stack.

children.description:
GSO delays the segmentation of a large outgoing packet until just before
the NIC driver transmit path, which reduces CPU work in the upper stack. It
is the software-based counterpart of TSO. Ze applies it through the kernel
ioctl ETHTOOL_SGSO. It is equivalent to 'ethtool -K <dev> gso on|off'.
children.name: gso
children.short-help: Generic Segmentation Offload: delay segmentation until the NIC driver transmit path.

children.description:
The feature lets the NIC run TC flower and u32 filter rules in hardware, so
a matched flow does not reach kernel processing. It needs NIC firmware
support, which is common on mlx5, bnxt and nfp. Ze applies it through the
kernel ioctl ETHTOOL_SFEATURES. It is equivalent to 'ethtool -K <dev> hw-
tc-offload on|off'.
children.name: hw-tc-offload
children.short-help: Hardware Traffic Control Offload: run TC filter rules in the NIC.

children.description:
LRO is the hardware-based counterpart of GRO. It can break forwarding and
bridging, because the coalesced frame no longer matches the original wire
format. Disable it on a router or a bridge that forwards traffic between
interfaces. Ze applies it through the kernel ioctl ETHTOOL_SLRO. It is
equivalent to 'ethtool -K <dev> lro on|off'.
children.name: lro
children.short-help: Large Receive Offload: the NIC coalesces incoming TCP segments before DMA.

children.description:
RFS extends RPS. It steers an incoming packet to the CPU where the
application that consumes the flow runs, which improves cache locality and
reduces cross-CPU cache bounces. When the leaf is true, ze sets
/proc/sys/net/core/rps_sock_flow_entries to 32768, and it distributes per-
queue rps_flow_cnt evenly across the rx queues. Enable RPS as well, because
RFS is only effective with RPS. RFS is not an ethtool feature, so ze uses
sysfs directly.
children.name: rfs
children.short-help: Receive Flow Steering: steer a flow to the CPU that runs its application.

children.description:
RPS hashes the packet header and steers the packet to a target CPU receive
queue. It helps when the NIC has fewer hardware RSS queues than the machine
has CPUs. When the leaf is true, ze writes a bitmask covering all online
CPUs to each rx queue sysfs entry, at
/sys/class/net/<dev>/queues/rx-*/rps_cpus. When the leaf is false, ze
writes 0 to each entry. RPS is not an ethtool feature, so ze uses sysfs
directly.
children.name: rps
children.short-help: Receive Packet Steering: spread incoming packets across CPUs in software.

children.description:
Scatter-Gather I/O lets the NIC assemble a single frame from multiple non-
contiguous memory buffers, which avoids data copies. Most drivers need it
for TSO and GSO. Ze applies it through the kernel ioctl ETHTOOL_SSG. It is
equivalent to 'ethtool -K <dev> sg on|off'.
children.name: sg
children.short-help: Scatter-Gather I/O: build one frame from several memory buffers.

children.description:
TSO moves TCP segmentation to the NIC hardware, so the kernel hands off a
TCP segment of up to 64 KB and the NIC splits it into MTU-sized frames on
the wire. The feature needs NIC hardware support. Disable it when the
interface passes traffic to VPP, or to a virtual switch that cannot handle
an oversized frame. Ze applies it through the kernel ioctl ETHTOOL_STSO. It
is equivalent to 'ethtool -K <dev> tso on|off'.
children.name: tso
children.short-help: TCP Segmentation Offload: the NIC splits large TCP segments into wire frames.

children.description:
Ze applies these features through a kernel ioctl, the ethtool SIOCETHTOOL
interface, or a sysfs write, after it creates the interface. The ethtool(8) CLI
program is not required, because ze talks to the kernel directly. For a boolean
leaf, true enables the feature explicitly, false disables it explicitly, and an
absent leaf preserves the OS default with no kernel call. Offload availability
depends on the NIC driver and the kernel version. Ze logs an unsupported
feature as a warning, and the config commit still succeeds.
children.name: offload
children.short-help: Network offload and packet steering features.

children.description:
When this leaf is omitted, ze uses the logical name as the OS device name, so
every interface whose name already matches its kernel device resolves
unchanged. Set the leaf to alias a readable interface name to a different
kernel device. The iface resolver then maps the logical name to this OS device.
ze init records the discovered OS name here.
children.name: os-name
children.short-help: OS device this logical interface name binds to.

children.description:
Ze validates the peer name with the same rules as name. Ze sets the peer
link state to up right after it creates the pair. The schema gives the
peer end no units, so ze puts no address on it.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: Veth peer name

children.description:
The value is the name of a profile. The value 'none' stops the unit
from inheriting the profile of the parent interface.
children.name: class-of-service
children.short-help: Class-of-service profile of this unit.

children.description:
Ze keeps the text in the config only, and it makes no kernel call for it.
The limit is 255 characters.
children.name: description
children.short-help: Unit description

children.description:
Ze skips a disabled unit at apply, so it installs none of its addresses
and it installs no mirror for the unit. A VLAN subinterface ze created
for the unit is deleted. The config block stays in place.
children.name: disable
children.short-help: Administratively disable this unit

children.description:
IEEE 802.1Q defines the Priority Code Point field, which is
3 bits wide and holds a value from 0 to 7.
children.name: pcp
children.short-help: PCP value Ze stamps in the 802.1Q header.

children.description:
Ze stamps the PCP value in the 802.1Q header. The map needs vlan-id.
Ze sends a priority with no entry as PCP 0.
children.name: egress-qos-map
children.short-help: Map the internal priority of an outgoing packet to the 802.1p PCP value.

children.description: The value runs from 0 to 7.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Internal priority Ze gives to a matching frame.

children.description:
The map needs vlan-id. A frame whose PCP value has no entry keeps
priority 0.
children.name: ingress-qos-map
children.short-help: Map the 802.1p PCP value of a received tagged frame to an internal priority.

children.description:
Ze installs each address on the unit's OS device through netlink. An
address that leaves the list is removed on the next apply, because ze
reconciles the whole set rather than adding to it. A unit with a
vlan-id puts its addresses on <parent>.<vlan-id>.
children.name: address
children.short-help: IPv4 addresses in CIDR notation (e.g., 10.0.0.1/24)

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_accept. It helps a failover,
where a peer announces a new MAC for an existing IP address.
children.name: arp-accept
children.short-help: Accept gratuitous ARP frames and add their entries to the ARP cache.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_announce. Level 0
puts any local address in the ARP request. Level 1 prefers an address
on the target's subnet. Level 2 uses the best local address only,
which the dsr sysctl profile also sets.
children.name: arp-announce
children.short-help: ARP announce level: 0=any, 1=prefer subnet, 2=best only

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_filter. It stops the interface
from answering for an address that is assigned to another interface.
Use it on a multi-homed host.
children.name: arp-filter
children.short-help: Only answer ARP requests for addresses on the receiving interface.

children.description:
0 replies to any request. 1 replies only when the target address is on
the incoming interface. 2 adds a sender subnet check to level 1.
children.name: arp-ignore
children.short-help: ARP ignore level, which selects the ARP requests this interface answers.

children.description:
When the leaf is omitted, ze uses the MAC address. Set it for an
environment where the DHCP server keys a lease on the client-id
rather than on the MAC.
children.name: client-id
children.short-help: DHCP option 61 client identifier, sent in DISCOVER and REQUEST messages.

children.description:
Ze starts one client when this leaf is true, and it stops the
client when the leaf goes false. The client is keyed by the
interface name and the unit name, so two units on one interface
run two clients.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable DHCPv4 client

children.description:
Ze sends the value as DHCP option 12 in the DISCOVER message and
in the REQUEST message. When the leaf is omitted, ze sends no
option 12 at all.
children.name: hostname
children.short-help: Hostname in DHCP requests

children.description:
Ze runs its own DHCPv4 client, so no dhclient process and no udhcpc
process is needed. The client installs the leased address, the
default route and the resolvers that the server sends.
children.name: dhcp
children.short-help: DHCPv4 client configuration

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.forwarding. Routing needs it. When
it is disabled, the kernel drops a packet that is not destined for a
local address.
children.name: forwarding
children.short-help: Allow this interface to forward IPv4 packets between interfaces.

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.proxy_arp. Use it to bridge subnets
that have no L2 connectivity between them, or for an unnumbered
interface.
children.name: proxy-arp
children.short-help: Answer ARP requests for other hosts that are reachable through this router.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.rp_filter, where disable
is 0, strict is 1 and loose is 2. strict drops a packet whose source
address would not route back through this interface. loose drops a
packet whose source address has no route at all.
children.name: rpf-check
children.short-help: Reverse path filtering mode

values.name: disable
values.short-help: No source address check, rp_filter 0.

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address has no route at all, rp_filter 2.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source does not route back through this interface, rp_filter 1.

children.description:
A non-owner Active router accepts packets addressed to
the virtual addresses. The leaf carries version 3
semantics only, and the plugin verifier rejects true
beside version 2.
The dataplane enforces the leaf. With false on a
non-owner, the router still answers ARP and Neighbor
Discovery for the virtual addresses, and still
forwards for the virtual MAC. It does not accept
packets addressed to them, so a ping to a virtual
address gets no reply. The address owner accepts
whatever this leaf says.
children.name: accept-mode
children.short-help: Accept_Mode (RFC 9568 Sections 6.1 and 6.4.3).

children.description:
The native range spans both versions, and the plugin
verifier narrows it per version. Version 3 takes
multiples of 10 ms within 10..40950, and the wire
carries centiseconds (RFC 9568 erratum 8301). Version
2 takes whole seconds within 1000..255000, and the
wire carries seconds.
children.name: advertise-interval-milliseconds
children.short-help: Advertisement interval in milliseconds.

children.description:
A Backup router with a higher priority takes over from
a live Active router with a lower priority.
children.name: preempt
children.short-help: Preempt_Mode (RFC 9568 Section 6.4.2).

children.description:
RFC 9568 does not define this hold-time. Ze arms it on
the first losing advertisement while a local router
with a higher priority waits. It never delays failover
from a dead Active router.
children.name: preempt-delay-seconds
children.short-help: Preemption hold-time, in Junos semantics.

children.description:
255 is reserved for the address owner, and Ze assigns
it automatically. An operator never sets it.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Election priority (RFC 9568 Section 5.2.4).

children.description:
There is no default, because a default
picks the operator's failover policy. RFC
9568 Section 8.3.2 says how far apart two
routers' priorities belong.
children.name: priority-decrement
children.short-help: Priority subtracted from this group while this interface is down.

children.description:
Ze reads the interface's operational state only,
so this interface does not need an address of
the group's family. Two interfaces that are down
cost the sum of their decrements.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: One tracked interface and the priority its loss costs.

children.description:
Ze sums the priority-decrement of every tracked
interface that is down, and subtracts the sum from
the configured priority. The result never falls
below 1 (RFC 9568 Section 5.2.4), and Ze advertises
the new priority at once. Tracking is refused on the
group that owns its virtual address, because that
group advertises 255 whatever a decrement says.
children.name: track
children.short-help: Interfaces whose loss lowers the priority this group advertises.

children.description:
The leaf is present only for an IPv4 group. An IPv6
group is always VRRPv3 (RFC 9568).
children.name: version
children.short-help: Protocol version.

values.short-help: RFC 3768 (VRRPv2), IPv4 only, auth type 0 only.
RFC 9568 (VRRPv3).

children.description:
RFC 9568 Section 5.2.9 sets the wire order, which is
the configuration order. An address equal to a real
address on this unit makes this router the owner. Ze
then forces the priority to 255, and forces
accept-mode to true.
children.name: virtual-address
children.short-help: Virtual IPv4 addresses, encoded on the wire in configuration order.

children.description:
The VRID is unique per interface unit and per address
family. The IPv4 VRID space and the IPv6 VRID space
are independent.
children.name: vrid
children.short-help: Virtual Router Identifier (RFC 9568 Section 5.2.3).

children.description:
The name is a config label only, and Ze never sends it on
the wire. The VRID leaf carries the protocol identity.
children.name: group
children.short-help: One virtual router, identified by an operator-assigned name.

children.description:
Ze runs each group as its own state machine, on a macvlan
device that carries the group's virtual MAC. The device name
starts with zv4 and takes the parent ifindex and the VRID,
inside the 15-character kernel limit. The container carries
ze:backend netlink, so a tree with interface backend vpp is
refused at verify with "VRRP requires the netlink interface
backend". A VRID is unique for one unit and one family, so
the same VRID CAN run on the IPv6 unit beside it.
children.name: vrrp
children.short-help: VRRP virtual routers hosted on this IPv4 unit.

children.description:
The container holds one unit's IPv4 state. Ze installs the addresses
through netlink. Ze turns each other leaf into a net.ipv4.conf.<iface>
sysctl write, which it emits on the event bus for the sysctl plugin to
perform.
children.name: ipv4
children.short-help: IPv4 addressing, forwarding, ARP behavior, and DHCP client for this unit.

children.description:
This leaf needs the netlink backend, for the same reason as autoconf:
the two leaves describe one behavior.
children.name: accept-ra
children.short-help: Accept RA level: 0 disables, 1 accepts when not forwarding, 2 accepts even when forwarding.

children.description:
Ze installs each address on the unit's OS device through netlink. An
address that leaves the list is removed on the next apply, because ze
reconciles the whole set rather than adding to it.
children.name: address
children.short-help: IPv6 addresses in CIDR notation (e.g., fd00::1/64)

children.description:
The kernel learns an address only when a Router Advertisement reaches
the device it owns, so this leaf needs the netlink backend. On the vpp
backend, the NIC belongs to VPP, and no advertisement reaches the Linux
Control Plane tap.
children.name: autoconf
children.short-help: Enable IPv6 stateless autoconfiguration.

children.description:
When the leaf is omitted, ze generates a DUID-LL from the interface
MAC. Set the leaf when the DHCP server binds a lease to a specific
DUID.
children.name: duid
children.short-help: Override the DHCPv6 Unique Identifier (RFC 8415 Section 11).

children.description:
Ze starts a DHCPv6 client on this unit when the leaf is true. The
client sends a Solicit that carries the Rapid Commit option, and
it takes a Reply directly when the server answers with one.
Otherwise it sends a Request after the Advertise.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable DHCPv6 client

children.description:
The prefix length ze asks for, from 48 to 64. Ze reads the
leaf into the DHCP client configuration and then sends no
IA_PD option, so the value reaches no server and changes
nothing. A prefix that a server sends on its own keeps the
length that server assigned.
children.name: length
children.short-help: Requested prefix length

children.description:
Ze sends its DHCPv6 Solicit with no IA_PD option, so it asks no
server for a delegated prefix. Ze does install a prefix that a
server sends on its own in the IA_PD option of a Reply. Ze
publishes that prefix as a lease on this unit. The length leaf
below reaches no message Ze sends.
children.name: pd
children.short-help: Prefix delegation

children.description:
The client requests addresses, delegated prefixes, or both, from a
DHCPv6 server. It runs alongside SLAAC when autoconf is also enabled.
children.name: dhcpv6
children.short-help: DHCPv6 stateful client (RFC 8415).

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv6.conf.<iface>.forwarding. Forwarding disables RA
acceptance, unless accept-ra is set to 2.
children.name: forwarding
children.short-help: Allow this interface to forward IPv6 packets between interfaces.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 requires AdvSendAdvertisements to default to
false, so a node never becomes a router by accident.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Send Router Advertisements on this unit.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 4.2 defines AdvCurHopLimit. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: hop-limit
children.short-help: Value a host places in the Hop Limit field of its outgoing packets.

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x80 of the flags octet in the Router Advertisement.
Set the flag only where a DHCPv6 server answers on this link,
because the flag alone gives a host no address.
children.name: managed
children.short-help:
Set the M flag: hosts get their addresses from DHCPv6
(RFC 4861 Section 4.2).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines MaxRtrAdvInterval. Ze picks each
interval at random between minimum-interval and this value.
children.name: maximum-interval
children.short-help: Longest time between unsolicited Router Advertisements (MaxRtrAdvInterval).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines MinRtrAdvInterval. The value must
not exceed 0.75 x maximum-interval, and config verify rejects a
larger value.
children.name: minimum-interval
children.short-help: Shortest time between unsolicited Router Advertisements (MinRtrAdvInterval).

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x40 of the flags octet in the Router Advertisement.
The flag does not change how a host builds its addresses. Use the
rdnss container instead where no DHCPv6 server runs on this
link.
children.name: other-config
children.short-help:
Set the O flag: hosts get other configuration, such as DNS,
from DHCPv6 (RFC 4861 Section 4.2).

children.description:
With the A flag set, a host builds addresses from this prefix
by stateless autoconfiguration (RFC 4862).
children.name: autonomous
children.short-help: Set the A flag in the Prefix Information option.

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x80 of the flags octet in the Prefix Information
option. With the flag clear, a host sends a packet for an
address in this prefix to the router rather than straight to
the neighbor.
children.name: on-link
children.short-help:
Set the L flag: hosts treat addresses in this prefix as
on-link (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2 defines the preferred lifetime. The
value must not exceed valid-lifetime, and config verify rejects
a larger value. The default is 7 days.
children.name: preferred-lifetime
children.short-help: How long an address built from the prefix stays preferred.

children.description:
4294967295 means that the prefix never expires. The default is
30 days.
children.name: valid-lifetime
children.short-help: How long the prefix stays valid (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description: Ze sends the host bits below the prefix length as zero.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Prefixes advertised in Prefix Information options (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description:
0 tells a host to stop using the resolvers, and an operator can
set it. 4294967295 means that the resolvers never expire. This
leaf has no default: leave it out, and Ze sends 3 x maximum-
interval, the value RFC 8106 Section 5.1 recommends. 0 is not
the default for that reason, because Ze could not then tell an
operator who retires a resolver from one who set nothing.
children.name: lifetime
children.short-help: How long a host can use these resolvers (RFC 8106 Section 5.1).

children.description:
Ze puts every address in ONE RDNSS option, which is why they
share one lifetime. The option carries 8 addresses at most,
and it grows by 16 bytes for each address.
children.name: server
children.short-help: Resolver addresses. All of them share lifetime.

children.description: The option points a link at a resolver without a DHCPv6 server.
children.name: rdnss
children.short-help: Recursive DNS servers advertised to hosts (RFC 8106 Section 5.1).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvReachableTime. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: reachable-time
children.short-help: How long a host treats a neighbor as reachable after a reachability confirmation.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvRetransTimer. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: retransmit-timer
children.short-help: Time between retransmitted Neighbor Solicitations on this link.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvDefaultLifetime. 0 says that Ze
is not a default router, and the prefixes and the resolvers in the
advertisement still apply. Any other value must be at least
maximum-interval, and config verify rejects a smaller one.
children.name: router-lifetime
children.short-help: How long a host keeps Ze in its default router list (AdvDefaultLifetime).

children.description:
Ze advertises prefixes, flags and resolvers on this link, so that a
host autoconfigures. That is the role radvd fills on another system.
Sending is separate from accepting: set forwarding true on an
advertising interface, and leave accept-ra at 0 unless this interface
also learns from another router.
children.name: router-advertisement
children.short-help: Router Advertisement sender (RFC 4861).

children.description:
strict drops a packet whose source address would not be routed back
through this interface. loose drops a packet whose source address has
no route at all. disable performs no source address validation.
children.name: rpf-check
children.short-help: Reverse path filtering mode, on the VPP data plane only for IPv6.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: No source address validation.

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address has no route at all.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address does not route back through this interface.

children.description:
A non-owner Active router accepts packets addressed to
the virtual addresses. Ze enforces the leaf in the
dataplane, with an nftables input chain in the ze_vrrp
table. With false, the chain accepts ICMPv6 types 135
and 136 before it examines any address (RFC 9568
Section 6.1). Neighbor Discovery for the virtual
addresses still answers. The chain drops local delivery
of every other packet to a virtual address, and leaves
forwarding for the virtual MAC untouched. The address
owner accepts whatever this leaf says.
children.name: accept-mode
children.short-help: Accept_Mode (RFC 9568 Section 6.1/6.4.3), v3 semantics.

children.description:
The value is a multiple of 10 ms. The wire carries
centiseconds (RFC 9568 erratum 8301).
children.name: advertise-interval-milliseconds
children.short-help: Advertisement interval in milliseconds.

children.description:
The state machine reads this leaf in the Backup state
only. With true, Ze discards an advertisement whose
priority is lower than its own, so the Master_Down
timer runs out and promotes this router. With false,
Ze accepts that advertisement and re-arms the timer,
so this router stays Backup while the Active router
still sends. The default is true, and
preempt-delay-seconds delays the takeover after the
first losing advertisement.
children.name: preempt
children.short-help: Preempt_Mode (RFC 9568 Section 6.4.2).

children.description:
RFC 9568 does not define this hold-time. Ze takes the
behavior from Junos.
children.name: preempt-delay-seconds
children.short-help: Preemption hold-time, in Junos semantics.

children.description:
255 is reserved for the address owner, and Ze assigns
it automatically.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Election priority (RFC 9568 Section 5.2.4).

children.description:
There is no default, because a default
picks the operator's failover policy. RFC
9568 Section 8.3.2 says how far apart two
routers' priorities belong.
children.name: priority-decrement
children.short-help: Priority subtracted from this group while this interface is down.

children.description:
Ze reads the interface's operational state only,
so this interface does not need an address of
the group's family. Two interfaces that are down
cost the sum of their decrements.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: One tracked interface and the priority its loss costs.

children.description:
Ze sums the priority-decrement of every tracked
interface that is down, and subtracts the sum from
the configured priority. The result never falls
below 1 (RFC 9568 Section 5.2.4), and Ze advertises
the new priority at once. Tracking is refused on the
group that owns its virtual address, because that
group advertises 255 whatever a decrement says.
children.name: track
children.short-help: Interfaces whose loss lowers the priority this group advertises.

children.description:
The FIRST address MUST be an IPv6 link-local address
in fe80::/10, because it is the advertisement source
identity (RFC 9568 Section 5.2.9, erratum 8300). The
plugin verifier enforces it.
children.name: virtual-address
children.short-help: Virtual IPv6 addresses, encoded on the wire in configuration order.

children.description:
The VRID is unique per interface unit and per address
family. The IPv4 VRID space and the IPv6 VRID space
are independent.
children.name: vrid
children.short-help: Virtual Router Identifier (RFC 9568 Section 5.2.3).

children.description:
The name is a config label only, and Ze never sends it on
the wire. The VRID leaf carries the protocol identity.
children.name: group
children.short-help: One virtual router, identified by an operator-assigned name.

children.description:
Ze runs each group as its own state machine, on a macvlan
device that carries the group's virtual MAC. The device name
starts with zv6 and takes the parent ifindex and the VRID,
inside the 15-character kernel limit. Every group here is
VRRPv3, because VRRPv2 is IPv4 only, so this tree carries no
version leaf. The container carries ze:backend netlink, so a
tree with interface backend vpp is refused at verify with
"VRRP requires the netlink interface backend".
children.name: vrrp
children.short-help: VRRP virtual routers hosted on this IPv6 unit.

children.description:
The container holds one unit's IPv6 state. Ze installs the addresses
through netlink. Ze turns autoconf, accept-ra and forwarding into
net.ipv6.conf.<iface> sysctl writes, which it emits on the event bus for
the sysctl plugin to perform.
children.name: ipv6
children.short-help: IPv6 addressing, forwarding, autoconfiguration, and DHCPv6 client for this unit.

children.description:
Ze installs a tc mirred filter that copies each transmitted frame
toward the named interface. Ze resolves the name through the same
selector map as the source, so a capture port bound by mac/match or
aliased by os-name works. An unbound name installs no mirror.
children.name: egress
children.short-help: Mirror egress traffic to this interface

children.description:
Ze installs a tc mirred filter that copies each received frame toward
the named interface. Ze resolves the name through the same selector
map as the source, so a capture port bound by mac/match or aliased by
os-name works. An unbound name installs no mirror.
children.name: ingress
children.short-help: Mirror ingress traffic to this interface

children.description:
The netlink backend mirrors through tc mirred. The vpp backend programs
SPAN, through sw_interface_span_enable_disable, and it maps the ingress
direction and the egress direction onto the RX SPAN state and the TX SPAN
state, as a device-level port mirror.
children.name: mirror
children.short-help: Traffic mirroring for this interface.

children.description:
The leaf sets net.mpls.conf.<iface>.input. net.mpls.platform_labels
sets the size of the global label table.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable MPLS label input on this interface.

children.description:
Ze turns the enable leaf below into a net.mpls.conf.<iface>.input sysctl
write. The size of the global label table is a separate sysctl,
net.mpls.platform_labels, which the sysctl config block sets.
children.name: mpls
children.short-help: MPLS forwarding on this interface (RFC 3031 LSR).

children.description:
A lower value is preferred. On link-down, ze increases the metric by 1024,
which deprioritizes the interface. The default 254 ranks a learned default
below a static default and below a protocol-learned one, the way rib
distance ranks connected 0, static 10 and ebgp 20. Write 0 to put a learned
default on the kernel metric that an operator's static default also uses.
The two then share one kernel route, and the last writer owns it. A value
above 0 also makes ze own the IPv6 default routes of the interface: ze sets
accept_ra_defrtr=0 and installs the ::/0 routes itself.
children.name: route-priority
children.short-help: Route metric for default routes learned on this unit through DHCP or router advertisement.

children.description:
The built-in profiles are dsr, router, hardened, multihomed and proxy. A
user-defined profile comes from a sysctl { profile ... } config block. Ze
applies the profiles in order, and the last one wins on a key that two
profiles both set.
children.name: sysctl-profile
children.short-help: Named sysctl profiles to apply to this unit.

children.description:
The range is 1 to 4094, which is what IEEE 802.1Q allows. Ze creates a
kernel 802.1Q subinterface named <parent>.<vlan-id>. An L3 tunnel refuses
a unit that carries this leaf, because only gretap and ip6gretap carry
Ethernet frames.
children.name: vlan-id
children.short-help: VLAN identifier

children.description:
Ze creates no VRF device and enslaves no interface, so a unit cannot use a
routing table other than the main table. The leaf stays in the schema so
that the refusal can say why. It becomes functional when VRF support ships.
children.name: vrf
children.short-help: Not implemented. Ze refuses a config that sets this leaf.

children.description:
The cos plugin adds the class-of-service leaf and the inline
ingress-qos-map and egress-qos-map lists to the unit. The class-of-service value of the unit
overrides the value of the interface, and 'none' stops the inheritance. Ze refuses a unit that
carries a profile and an inline map together. Both routes need vlan-id on the unit, because the
map reaches the kernel 802.1Q subinterface.
children.name: unit
children.short-help: Logical interface unit.

children.description:
The cos plugin adds the class-of-service leaf to a veth interface. The leaf
names an ieee-802.1p profile, and every unit of the interface inherits it. A unit that sets its
own class-of-service keeps that one, and the value 'none' opts the unit out. Remove the cos
plugin and the leaf disappears from the interface.
children.name: veth
children.short-help: Virtual ethernet pair interface

children.description:
Ze keeps the text in the config only, and it makes no kernel call for it. The
kernel link alias IFLA_IFALIAS carries ze's own ownership marker instead, so
a description never reaches it.
children.name: description
children.short-help: Interface description

children.description:
Ze skips a disabled interface at every apply step, so it creates no device
and it installs no address. A device ze created before is deleted, because a
disabled interface leaves the managed set. The config block stays in place.
children.name: disable
children.short-help: Administratively disable this interface

children.description:
Ze passes the value to the kernel through the wgctrl call
ConfigureDevice. The kernel then sets the mark on each encapsulated UDP
packet, and a policy routing rule or an nftables rule can match it. Ze
always sends the leaf, so a config that clears the mark clears the kernel
state too.
children.name: fwmark
children.short-help:
Firewall mark applied to outgoing encapsulated
packets for policy routing. 0 means unset.

children.description:
When the leaf is unset, the kernel chooses an ephemeral port on the first
outbound handshake.
children.name: listen-port
children.short-help: UDP port WireGuard binds on 0.0.0.0 and :: for handshake and data traffic.

children.description:
The range is 68 to 16000 bytes and the default is 1500. Ze applies the value
with the netlink call LinkSetMTU after it creates the interface. Ze restores
the previous value when a later step of the same apply fails.
children.name: mtu
children.short-help: Maximum transmission unit

children.description:
When this leaf is omitted, ze uses the logical name as the OS device name, so
every interface whose name already matches its kernel device resolves
unchanged. Set the leaf to alias a readable interface name to a different
kernel device. The iface resolver then maps the logical name to this OS device.
ze init records the discovered OS name here.
children.name: os-name
children.short-help: OS device this logical interface name binds to.

children.description:
An inbound packet from this peer must have a source address inside one
of these prefixes. That check is cryptokey routing.
children.name: allowed-ips
children.short-help: CIDR prefixes routed into the tunnel for this peer.

children.description:
Ze removes the peer from the kernel peer set on reload, and the peer
stays in the config.
children.name: disable
children.short-help: Administratively disable this peer.

children.description:
Ze parses the value with net.ParseIP, so a hostname is refused at
apply time. When the endpoint is absent, ze sends no address to
the kernel, and the peer must start the handshake.
children.name: ip
children.short-help:
Remote IPv4 or IPv6 address (numeric, not
a hostname -- DNS resolution is not performed)

children.description:
The value is the listen-port the peer sets on its own side. Ze
combines the port with ip into one UDP address for the kernel, so
a port with no ip reaches nothing.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Remote UDP port

children.description:
Both leaves are required together. The kernel uses this address on the
first outbound handshake, and it updates the address on every inbound
handshake from a new source address.
children.name: endpoint
children.short-help: Remote UDP endpoint for this peer.

children.description: 0 disables the keepalives. A usual value is 25.
children.name: persistent-keepalive
children.short-help: Seconds between unsolicited keepalive packets that maintain NAT state.

children.description:
The key is mixed into the handshake for post-quantum resistance. Ze
stores it $9$-encoded on disk, the same pattern as private-key.
children.name: preshared-key
children.short-help: Optional base64-encoded 32-byte symmetric preshared key.

children.description:
The kernel matches an inbound handshake to a peer by this key. The
key is public, so it carries no ze:sensitive marker, and ze stores it
in plaintext where private-key and preshared-key are $9$-encoded.
children.name: public-key
children.short-help: Base64-encoded 32-byte Curve25519 peer public key

children.description:
Each peer has its own set of allowed-ips, which define the traffic that is
routed through the tunnel.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: WireGuard peer, identified by its public key.

children.description:
Ze stores the key $9$-encoded on disk, through the standard ze sensitive-
leaf pattern, and it decodes the key to plaintext base64 at parse time. 'ze
config show' and 'ze config dump' always emit the $9$ form, never the
plaintext. The $9$ form is obfuscation and not encryption, so protect the
config file at the filesystem level with chmod 600, the same way as a BGP
MD5 password.
children.name: private-key
children.short-help: Base64-encoded 32-byte Curve25519 private key.

children.description:
Ze keeps the text in the config only, and it makes no kernel call for it.
The limit is 255 characters.
children.name: description
children.short-help: Unit description

children.description:
Ze skips a disabled unit at apply, so it installs none of its addresses
and it installs no mirror for the unit. A VLAN subinterface ze created
for the unit is deleted. The config block stays in place.
children.name: disable
children.short-help: Administratively disable this unit

children.description:
Ze installs each address on the unit's OS device through netlink. An
address that leaves the list is removed on the next apply, because ze
reconciles the whole set rather than adding to it. A unit with a
vlan-id puts its addresses on <parent>.<vlan-id>.
children.name: address
children.short-help: IPv4 addresses in CIDR notation (e.g., 10.0.0.1/24)

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_accept. It helps a failover,
where a peer announces a new MAC for an existing IP address.
children.name: arp-accept
children.short-help: Accept gratuitous ARP frames and add their entries to the ARP cache.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_announce. Level 0
puts any local address in the ARP request. Level 1 prefers an address
on the target's subnet. Level 2 uses the best local address only,
which the dsr sysctl profile also sets.
children.name: arp-announce
children.short-help: ARP announce level: 0=any, 1=prefer subnet, 2=best only

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_filter. It stops the interface
from answering for an address that is assigned to another interface.
Use it on a multi-homed host.
children.name: arp-filter
children.short-help: Only answer ARP requests for addresses on the receiving interface.

children.description:
0 replies to any request. 1 replies only when the target address is on
the incoming interface. 2 adds a sender subnet check to level 1.
children.name: arp-ignore
children.short-help: ARP ignore level, which selects the ARP requests this interface answers.

children.description:
When the leaf is omitted, ze uses the MAC address. Set it for an
environment where the DHCP server keys a lease on the client-id
rather than on the MAC.
children.name: client-id
children.short-help: DHCP option 61 client identifier, sent in DISCOVER and REQUEST messages.

children.description:
Ze starts one client when this leaf is true, and it stops the
client when the leaf goes false. The client is keyed by the
interface name and the unit name, so two units on one interface
run two clients.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable DHCPv4 client

children.description:
Ze sends the value as DHCP option 12 in the DISCOVER message and
in the REQUEST message. When the leaf is omitted, ze sends no
option 12 at all.
children.name: hostname
children.short-help: Hostname in DHCP requests

children.description:
Ze runs its own DHCPv4 client, so no dhclient process and no udhcpc
process is needed. The client installs the leased address, the
default route and the resolvers that the server sends.
children.name: dhcp
children.short-help: DHCPv4 client configuration

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.forwarding. Routing needs it. When
it is disabled, the kernel drops a packet that is not destined for a
local address.
children.name: forwarding
children.short-help: Allow this interface to forward IPv4 packets between interfaces.

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.proxy_arp. Use it to bridge subnets
that have no L2 connectivity between them, or for an unnumbered
interface.
children.name: proxy-arp
children.short-help: Answer ARP requests for other hosts that are reachable through this router.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.rp_filter, where disable
is 0, strict is 1 and loose is 2. strict drops a packet whose source
address would not route back through this interface. loose drops a
packet whose source address has no route at all.
children.name: rpf-check
children.short-help: Reverse path filtering mode

values.name: disable
values.short-help: No source address check, rp_filter 0.

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address has no route at all, rp_filter 2.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source does not route back through this interface, rp_filter 1.

children.description:
The container holds one unit's IPv4 state. Ze installs the addresses
through netlink. Ze turns each other leaf into a net.ipv4.conf.<iface>
sysctl write, which it emits on the event bus for the sysctl plugin to
perform.
children.name: ipv4
children.short-help: IPv4 addressing, forwarding, ARP behavior, and DHCP client for this unit.

children.description:
This leaf needs the netlink backend, for the same reason as autoconf:
the two leaves describe one behavior.
children.name: accept-ra
children.short-help: Accept RA level: 0 disables, 1 accepts when not forwarding, 2 accepts even when forwarding.

children.description:
Ze installs each address on the unit's OS device through netlink. An
address that leaves the list is removed on the next apply, because ze
reconciles the whole set rather than adding to it.
children.name: address
children.short-help: IPv6 addresses in CIDR notation (e.g., fd00::1/64)

children.description:
The kernel learns an address only when a Router Advertisement reaches
the device it owns, so this leaf needs the netlink backend. On the vpp
backend, the NIC belongs to VPP, and no advertisement reaches the Linux
Control Plane tap.
children.name: autoconf
children.short-help: Enable IPv6 stateless autoconfiguration.

children.description:
When the leaf is omitted, ze generates a DUID-LL from the interface
MAC. Set the leaf when the DHCP server binds a lease to a specific
DUID.
children.name: duid
children.short-help: Override the DHCPv6 Unique Identifier (RFC 8415 Section 11).

children.description:
Ze starts a DHCPv6 client on this unit when the leaf is true. The
client sends a Solicit that carries the Rapid Commit option, and
it takes a Reply directly when the server answers with one.
Otherwise it sends a Request after the Advertise.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable DHCPv6 client

children.description:
The prefix length ze asks for, from 48 to 64. Ze reads the
leaf into the DHCP client configuration and then sends no
IA_PD option, so the value reaches no server and changes
nothing. A prefix that a server sends on its own keeps the
length that server assigned.
children.name: length
children.short-help: Requested prefix length

children.description:
Ze sends its DHCPv6 Solicit with no IA_PD option, so it asks no
server for a delegated prefix. Ze does install a prefix that a
server sends on its own in the IA_PD option of a Reply. Ze
publishes that prefix as a lease on this unit. The length leaf
below reaches no message Ze sends.
children.name: pd
children.short-help: Prefix delegation

children.description:
The client requests addresses, delegated prefixes, or both, from a
DHCPv6 server. It runs alongside SLAAC when autoconf is also enabled.
children.name: dhcpv6
children.short-help: DHCPv6 stateful client (RFC 8415).

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv6.conf.<iface>.forwarding. Forwarding disables RA
acceptance, unless accept-ra is set to 2.
children.name: forwarding
children.short-help: Allow this interface to forward IPv6 packets between interfaces.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 requires AdvSendAdvertisements to default to
false, so a node never becomes a router by accident.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Send Router Advertisements on this unit.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 4.2 defines AdvCurHopLimit. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: hop-limit
children.short-help: Value a host places in the Hop Limit field of its outgoing packets.

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x80 of the flags octet in the Router Advertisement.
Set the flag only where a DHCPv6 server answers on this link,
because the flag alone gives a host no address.
children.name: managed
children.short-help:
Set the M flag: hosts get their addresses from DHCPv6
(RFC 4861 Section 4.2).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines MaxRtrAdvInterval. Ze picks each
interval at random between minimum-interval and this value.
children.name: maximum-interval
children.short-help: Longest time between unsolicited Router Advertisements (MaxRtrAdvInterval).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines MinRtrAdvInterval. The value must
not exceed 0.75 x maximum-interval, and config verify rejects a
larger value.
children.name: minimum-interval
children.short-help: Shortest time between unsolicited Router Advertisements (MinRtrAdvInterval).

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x40 of the flags octet in the Router Advertisement.
The flag does not change how a host builds its addresses. Use the
rdnss container instead where no DHCPv6 server runs on this
link.
children.name: other-config
children.short-help:
Set the O flag: hosts get other configuration, such as DNS,
from DHCPv6 (RFC 4861 Section 4.2).

children.description:
With the A flag set, a host builds addresses from this prefix
by stateless autoconfiguration (RFC 4862).
children.name: autonomous
children.short-help: Set the A flag in the Prefix Information option.

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x80 of the flags octet in the Prefix Information
option. With the flag clear, a host sends a packet for an
address in this prefix to the router rather than straight to
the neighbor.
children.name: on-link
children.short-help:
Set the L flag: hosts treat addresses in this prefix as
on-link (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2 defines the preferred lifetime. The
value must not exceed valid-lifetime, and config verify rejects
a larger value. The default is 7 days.
children.name: preferred-lifetime
children.short-help: How long an address built from the prefix stays preferred.

children.description:
4294967295 means that the prefix never expires. The default is
30 days.
children.name: valid-lifetime
children.short-help: How long the prefix stays valid (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description: Ze sends the host bits below the prefix length as zero.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Prefixes advertised in Prefix Information options (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description:
0 tells a host to stop using the resolvers, and an operator can
set it. 4294967295 means that the resolvers never expire. This
leaf has no default: leave it out, and Ze sends 3 x maximum-
interval, the value RFC 8106 Section 5.1 recommends. 0 is not
the default for that reason, because Ze could not then tell an
operator who retires a resolver from one who set nothing.
children.name: lifetime
children.short-help: How long a host can use these resolvers (RFC 8106 Section 5.1).

children.description:
Ze puts every address in ONE RDNSS option, which is why they
share one lifetime. The option carries 8 addresses at most,
and it grows by 16 bytes for each address.
children.name: server
children.short-help: Resolver addresses. All of them share lifetime.

children.description: The option points a link at a resolver without a DHCPv6 server.
children.name: rdnss
children.short-help: Recursive DNS servers advertised to hosts (RFC 8106 Section 5.1).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvReachableTime. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: reachable-time
children.short-help: How long a host treats a neighbor as reachable after a reachability confirmation.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvRetransTimer. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: retransmit-timer
children.short-help: Time between retransmitted Neighbor Solicitations on this link.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvDefaultLifetime. 0 says that Ze
is not a default router, and the prefixes and the resolvers in the
advertisement still apply. Any other value must be at least
maximum-interval, and config verify rejects a smaller one.
children.name: router-lifetime
children.short-help: How long a host keeps Ze in its default router list (AdvDefaultLifetime).

children.description:
Ze advertises prefixes, flags and resolvers on this link, so that a
host autoconfigures. That is the role radvd fills on another system.
Sending is separate from accepting: set forwarding true on an
advertising interface, and leave accept-ra at 0 unless this interface
also learns from another router.
children.name: router-advertisement
children.short-help: Router Advertisement sender (RFC 4861).

children.description:
strict drops a packet whose source address would not be routed back
through this interface. loose drops a packet whose source address has
no route at all. disable performs no source address validation.
children.name: rpf-check
children.short-help: Reverse path filtering mode, on the VPP data plane only for IPv6.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: No source address validation.

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address has no route at all.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address does not route back through this interface.

children.description:
The container holds one unit's IPv6 state. Ze installs the addresses
through netlink. Ze turns autoconf, accept-ra and forwarding into
net.ipv6.conf.<iface> sysctl writes, which it emits on the event bus for
the sysctl plugin to perform.
children.name: ipv6
children.short-help: IPv6 addressing, forwarding, autoconfiguration, and DHCPv6 client for this unit.

Ze installs a tc mirred filter that copies each transmitted frame
toward the named interface. Ze resolves the name through the same
selector map as the source, so a capture port bound by mac/match or

children.name: egress
children.short-help: Mirror egress traffic to this interface

children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable MPLS label input on this interface.

children.short-help: MPLS forwarding on this interface (RFC 3031 LSR).

children.short-help: Not implemented. Ze refuses a config that sets this leaf.

children.description:
A unit holds the addresses, the VLAN tag and the sysctl settings of one
logical subinterface. A unit with a vlan-id creates a kernel subinterface
named <parent>.<vlan-id>. A unit without one puts its addresses on the parent
device.
children.name: unit
children.short-help: Logical interface unit

children.description:
The interface level carries listen-port, fwmark and private-key, and a nested
peer list. Each peer carries public-key, endpoint, allowed-ips, preshared-key
and persistent-keepalive. WireGuard is an L3 kind with no MAC address, so it
uses interface-common rather than interface-l2. Ze reconciles each peer in
place, through the wgctrl ConfigureDevice call. Adding a peer, removing one, or
rekeying one does not disturb the netdev or any other peer.
children.name: wireguard
children.short-help: WireGuard interface, configured declaratively.

children.description:
Ze keeps the text in the config only, and it makes no kernel call for it. The
kernel link alias IFLA_IFALIAS carries ze's own ownership marker instead, so
a description never reaches it.
children.name: description
children.short-help: Interface description

children.description:
When the leaf is set, ze binds the XFRM interface to this physical device.
When the leaf is omitted, the interface is unbound, and it uses the routing
table to select the underlay.
children.name: dev
children.short-help: Optional parent device that this XFRM interface binds to.

children.description:
Ze skips a disabled interface at every apply step, so it creates no device
and it installs no address. A device ze created before is deleted, because a
disabled interface leaves the managed set. The config block stays in place.
children.name: disable
children.short-help: Administratively disable this interface

children.description:
A bound security association carries the same if_id. The value must be non-
zero, because 0 means unset in the kernel.
children.name: if-id
children.short-help: XFRM identifier that binds security associations to this interface.

children.description:

children.short-help: OS device this logical interface name binds to.

children.description:
Ze installs each address on the unit's OS device through netlink. An
address that leaves the list is removed on the next apply, because ze
reconciles the whole set rather than adding to it. A unit with a
vlan-id puts its addresses on <parent>.<vlan-id>.
children.name: address
children.short-help: IPv4 addresses in CIDR notation (e.g., 10.0.0.1/24)

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_accept. It helps a failover,
where a peer announces a new MAC for an existing IP address.
children.name: arp-accept
children.short-help: Accept gratuitous ARP frames and add their entries to the ARP cache.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_announce. Level 0
puts any local address in the ARP request. Level 1 prefers an address
on the target's subnet. Level 2 uses the best local address only,
which the dsr sysctl profile also sets.
children.name: arp-announce
children.short-help: ARP announce level: 0=any, 1=prefer subnet, 2=best only

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.arp_filter. It stops the interface
from answering for an address that is assigned to another interface.
Use it on a multi-homed host.
children.name: arp-filter
children.short-help: Only answer ARP requests for addresses on the receiving interface.

children.description:
0 replies to any request. 1 replies only when the target address is on
the incoming interface. 2 adds a sender subnet check to level 1.
children.name: arp-ignore
children.short-help: ARP ignore level, which selects the ARP requests this interface answers.

children.description:
When the leaf is omitted, ze uses the MAC address. Set it for an
environment where the DHCP server keys a lease on the client-id
rather than on the MAC.
children.name: client-id
children.short-help: DHCP option 61 client identifier, sent in DISCOVER and REQUEST messages.

children.description:
Ze starts one client when this leaf is true, and it stops the
client when the leaf goes false. The client is keyed by the
interface name and the unit name, so two units on one interface
run two clients.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable DHCPv4 client

children.description:
Ze sends the value as DHCP option 12 in the DISCOVER message and
in the REQUEST message. When the leaf is omitted, ze sends no
option 12 at all.
children.name: hostname
children.short-help: Hostname in DHCP requests

children.description:
Ze runs its own DHCPv4 client, so no dhclient process and no udhcpc
process is needed. The client installs the leased address, the
default route and the resolvers that the server sends.
children.name: dhcp
children.short-help: DHCPv4 client configuration

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.forwarding. Routing needs it. When
it is disabled, the kernel drops a packet that is not destined for a
local address.
children.name: forwarding
children.short-help: Allow this interface to forward IPv4 packets between interfaces.

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.proxy_arp. Use it to bridge subnets
that have no L2 connectivity between them, or for an unnumbered
interface.
children.name: proxy-arp
children.short-help: Answer ARP requests for other hosts that are reachable through this router.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.ipv4.conf.<iface>.rp_filter, where disable
is 0, strict is 1 and loose is 2. strict drops a packet whose source
address would not route back through this interface. loose drops a
packet whose source address has no route at all.
children.name: rpf-check
children.short-help: Reverse path filtering mode

values.name: disable
values.short-help: No source address check, rp_filter 0.

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address has no route at all, rp_filter 2.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source does not route back through this interface, rp_filter 1.

children.description:
The container holds one unit's IPv4 state. Ze installs the addresses
through netlink. Ze turns each other leaf into a net.ipv4.conf.<iface>
sysctl write, which it emits on the event bus for the sysctl plugin to
perform.
children.name: ipv4
children.short-help: IPv4 addressing, forwarding, ARP behavior, and DHCP client for this unit.

children.description:
This leaf needs the netlink backend, for the same reason as autoconf:
the two leaves describe one behavior.
children.name: accept-ra
children.short-help: Accept RA level: 0 disables, 1 accepts when not forwarding, 2 accepts even when forwarding.

children.description:
Ze installs each address on the unit's OS device through netlink. An
address that leaves the list is removed on the next apply, because ze
reconciles the whole set rather than adding to it.
children.name: address
children.short-help: IPv6 addresses in CIDR notation (e.g., fd00::1/64)

children.description:
The kernel learns an address only when a Router Advertisement reaches
the device it owns, so this leaf needs the netlink backend. On the vpp
backend, the NIC belongs to VPP, and no advertisement reaches the Linux
Control Plane tap.
children.name: autoconf
children.short-help: Enable IPv6 stateless autoconfiguration.

children.description:
When the leaf is omitted, ze generates a DUID-LL from the interface
MAC. Set the leaf when the DHCP server binds a lease to a specific
DUID.
children.name: duid
children.short-help: Override the DHCPv6 Unique Identifier (RFC 8415 Section 11).

children.description:
Ze starts a DHCPv6 client on this unit when the leaf is true. The
client sends a Solicit that carries the Rapid Commit option, and
it takes a Reply directly when the server answers with one.
Otherwise it sends a Request after the Advertise.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable DHCPv6 client

children.description:
The prefix length ze asks for, from 48 to 64. Ze reads the
leaf into the DHCP client configuration and then sends no
IA_PD option, so the value reaches no server and changes
nothing. A prefix that a server sends on its own keeps the
length that server assigned.
children.name: length
children.short-help: Requested prefix length

children.description:
Ze sends its DHCPv6 Solicit with no IA_PD option, so it asks no
server for a delegated prefix. Ze does install a prefix that a
server sends on its own in the IA_PD option of a Reply. Ze
publishes that prefix as a lease on this unit. The length leaf
below reaches no message Ze sends.
children.name: pd
children.short-help: Prefix delegation

children.description:
The client requests addresses, delegated prefixes, or both, from a
DHCPv6 server. It runs alongside SLAAC when autoconf is also enabled.
children.name: dhcpv6
children.short-help: DHCPv6 stateful client (RFC 8415).

children.description:
The leaf sets net.ipv6.conf.<iface>.forwarding. Forwarding disables RA
acceptance, unless accept-ra is set to 2.
children.name: forwarding
children.short-help: Allow this interface to forward IPv6 packets between interfaces.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 requires AdvSendAdvertisements to default to
false, so a node never becomes a router by accident.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Send Router Advertisements on this unit.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 4.2 defines AdvCurHopLimit. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: hop-limit
children.short-help: Value a host places in the Hop Limit field of its outgoing packets.

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x80 of the flags octet in the Router Advertisement.
Set the flag only where a DHCPv6 server answers on this link,
because the flag alone gives a host no address.
children.name: managed
children.short-help:
Set the M flag: hosts get their addresses from DHCPv6
(RFC 4861 Section 4.2).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines MaxRtrAdvInterval. Ze picks each
interval at random between minimum-interval and this value.
children.name: maximum-interval
children.short-help: Longest time between unsolicited Router Advertisements (MaxRtrAdvInterval).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines MinRtrAdvInterval. The value must
not exceed 0.75 x maximum-interval, and config verify rejects a
larger value.
children.name: minimum-interval
children.short-help: Shortest time between unsolicited Router Advertisements (MinRtrAdvInterval).

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x40 of the flags octet in the Router Advertisement.
The flag does not change how a host builds its addresses. Use the
rdnss container instead where no DHCPv6 server runs on this
link.
children.name: other-config
children.short-help:
Set the O flag: hosts get other configuration, such as DNS,
from DHCPv6 (RFC 4861 Section 4.2).

children.description:
With the A flag set, a host builds addresses from this prefix
by stateless autoconfiguration (RFC 4862).
children.name: autonomous
children.short-help: Set the A flag in the Prefix Information option.

children.description:
Ze sets bit 0x80 of the flags octet in the Prefix Information
option. With the flag clear, a host sends a packet for an
address in this prefix to the router rather than straight to
the neighbor.
children.name: on-link
children.short-help:
Set the L flag: hosts treat addresses in this prefix as
on-link (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2 defines the preferred lifetime. The
value must not exceed valid-lifetime, and config verify rejects
a larger value. The default is 7 days.
children.name: preferred-lifetime
children.short-help: How long an address built from the prefix stays preferred.

children.description:
4294967295 means that the prefix never expires. The default is
30 days.
children.name: valid-lifetime
children.short-help: How long the prefix stays valid (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description: Ze sends the host bits below the prefix length as zero.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Prefixes advertised in Prefix Information options (RFC 4861 Section 4.6.2).

children.description:
0 tells a host to stop using the resolvers, and an operator can
set it. 4294967295 means that the resolvers never expire. This
leaf has no default: leave it out, and Ze sends 3 x maximum-
interval, the value RFC 8106 Section 5.1 recommends. 0 is not
the default for that reason, because Ze could not then tell an
operator who retires a resolver from one who set nothing.
children.name: lifetime
children.short-help: How long a host can use these resolvers (RFC 8106 Section 5.1).

children.description:
Ze puts every address in ONE RDNSS option, which is why they
share one lifetime. The option carries 8 addresses at most,
and it grows by 16 bytes for each address.
children.name: server
children.short-help: Resolver addresses. All of them share lifetime.

children.description: The option points a link at a resolver without a DHCPv6 server.
children.name: rdnss
children.short-help: Recursive DNS servers advertised to hosts (RFC 8106 Section 5.1).

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvReachableTime. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: reachable-time
children.short-help: How long a host treats a neighbor as reachable after a reachability confirmation.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvRetransTimer. 0 means that this
router states no value.
children.name: retransmit-timer
children.short-help: Time between retransmitted Neighbor Solicitations on this link.

children.description:
RFC 4861 Section 6.2.1 defines AdvDefaultLifetime. 0 says that Ze
is not a default router, and the prefixes and the resolvers in the
advertisement still apply. Any other value must be at least
maximum-interval, and config verify rejects a smaller one.
children.name: router-lifetime
children.short-help: How long a host keeps Ze in its default router list (AdvDefaultLifetime).

children.description:
Ze advertises prefixes, flags and resolvers on this link, so that a
host autoconfigures. That is the role radvd fills on another system.
Sending is separate from accepting: set forwarding true on an
advertising interface, and leave accept-ra at 0 unless this interface
also learns from another router.
children.name: router-advertisement
children.short-help: Router Advertisement sender (RFC 4861).

children.description:
strict drops a packet whose source address would not be routed back
through this interface. loose drops a packet whose source address has
no route at all. disable performs no source address validation.
children.name: rpf-check
children.short-help: Reverse path filtering mode, on the VPP data plane only for IPv6.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: No source address validation.

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address has no route at all.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Drop a packet whose source address does not route back through this interface.

children.description:
The container holds one unit's IPv6 state. Ze installs the addresses
through netlink. Ze turns autoconf, accept-ra and forwarding into
net.ipv6.conf.<iface> sysctl writes, which it emits on the event bus for
the sysctl plugin to perform.
children.name: ipv6
children.short-help: IPv6 addressing, forwarding, autoconfiguration, and DHCPv6 client for this unit.

children.description:
Ze installs a tc mirred filter that copies each transmitted frame
toward the named interface. Ze resolves the name through the same
selector map as the source, so a capture port bound by mac/match or
aliased by os-name works. An unbound name installs no mirror.
children.name: egress
children.short-help: Mirror egress traffic to this interface

children.description:
Ze installs a tc mirred filter that copies each received frame toward
the named interface. Ze resolves the name through the same selector
map as the source, so a capture port bound by mac/match or aliased by
os-name works. An unbound name installs no mirror.
children.name: ingress
children.short-help: Mirror ingress traffic to this interface

children.description:
The netlink backend mirrors through tc mirred. The vpp backend programs
SPAN, through sw_interface_span_enable_disable, and it maps the ingress
direction and the egress direction onto the RX SPAN state and the TX SPAN
state, as a device-level port mirror.
children.name: mirror
children.short-help: Traffic mirroring for this interface.

children.description:
The leaf sets net.mpls.conf.<iface>.input. net.mpls.platform_labels
sets the size of the global label table.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable MPLS label input on this interface.

children.description:
Ze turns the enable leaf below into a net.mpls.conf.<iface>.input sysctl
write. The size of the global label table is a separate sysctl,
net.mpls.platform_labels, which the sysctl config block sets.
children.name: mpls
children.short-help: MPLS forwarding on this interface (RFC 3031 LSR).

children.description:
A lower value is preferred. On link-down, ze increases the metric by 1024,
which deprioritizes the interface. The default 254 ranks a learned default
below a static default and below a protocol-learned one, the way rib
distance ranks connected 0, static 10 and ebgp 20. Write 0 to put a learned
default on the kernel metric that an operator's static default also uses.
The two then share one kernel route, and the last writer owns it. A value
above 0 also makes ze own the IPv6 default routes of the interface: ze sets
accept_ra_defrtr=0 and installs the ::/0 routes itself.
children.name: route-priority
children.short-help: Route metric for default routes learned on this unit through DHCP or router advertisement.

children.description:
The built-in profiles are dsr, router, hardened, multihomed and proxy. A
user-defined profile comes from a sysctl { profile ... } config block. Ze
applies the profiles in order, and the last one wins on a key that two
profiles both set.
children.name: sysctl-profile
children.short-help: Named sysctl profiles to apply to this unit.

children.description:
The range is 1 to 4094, which is what IEEE 802.1Q allows. Ze creates a
kernel 802.1Q subinterface named <parent>.<vlan-id>. An L3 tunnel refuses
a unit that carries this leaf, because only gretap and ip6gretap carry
Ethernet frames.
children.name: vlan-id
children.short-help: VLAN identifier

children.description:
Ze creates no VRF device and enslaves no interface, so a unit cannot use a
