routing table other than the main table. The leaf stays in the schema so
that the refusal can say why. It becomes functional when VRF support ships.
children.name: vrf
children.short-help: Not implemented. Ze refuses a config that sets this leaf.

children.description:
A unit holds the addresses, the VLAN tag and the sysctl settings of one
logical subinterface. A unit with a vlan-id creates a kernel subinterface
named <parent>.<vlan-id>. A unit without one puts its addresses on the parent
device.
children.name: unit
children.short-help: Logical interface unit

children.description:
The kernel XFRM subsystem encrypts and decrypts the traffic that is routed into
this interface. The if-id binds security associations to the interface. XFRM is
an L3 kind with no MAC address.
children.name: xfrm
children.short-help: XFRM interface, for route-based IPsec (Linux 4.19 and later).

interface.description:
This container merges into ze-iface-conf. Remove the cos plugin and
every QoS leaf disappears from the interfaces.
interface.name: interface
interface.short-help: Interface-level class-of-service bindings and inline QoS maps.

children.description:
Dynamic hostname to advertise (RFC 5301 section 3). Printable 7-bit ASCII only, from space (0x20) to
tilde (0x7e). Each dot-separated label is 1 to 63 octets and the whole name is at most 255 octets,
including the separators (RFC 2181 section 11). One trailing dot is permitted. A non-ASCII name is
refused, not converted.
children.name: hostname
children.short-help: Dynamic hostname this IS-IS instance advertises (RFC 5301 section 3).

children.description:
Ze reads this list for one decision: does the circuit carry
IPv6. An ipv6-unicast entry adds the IPv6 NLPID to TLV 129 and
makes the hello carry TLV 232. TLV 129 carries the IPv4 NLPID
on every circuit. Both families ride one SPF tree, because this
IS-IS is single-topology.
children.name: address-family
children.short-help:
Per-interface address families on this circuit (single-topology;
both ride the shared SPF tree).

children.description:
broadcast, the default, runs the DIS election and sources a pseudo-node LSP when this
IS wins. It advertises the LAN as one TLV 22 entry that points at the pseudo-node. It also
sources a periodic CSNP while this IS is DIS. point-to-point runs no election and no
pseudo-node. It sends a point-to-point hello with TLV 240 and one initial CSNP when the
adjacency reaches Up.
children.name: circuit-type
children.short-help: Circuit type.

values.name: broadcast
values.short-help: LAN broadcast circuit (DIS election).

values.name: point-to-point
values.short-help: Point-to-point circuit.

children.description:
The default is true, so an entry runs IS-IS without this leaf. A false value keeps the
entry in the configuration and opens no circuit. It also stops the connected prefixes of the
interface from reaching the node's own LSP, which a passive interface still advertises.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: IS-IS enabled on this interface.

children.description:
Ze sends an IIH on this circuit at this period. The IIH carries a holding time of this
value multiplied by `hold-multiplier`, clamped into 1 to 65535 seconds. A neighbor drops the
adjacency when no IIH arrives inside the holding time it was told. A shorter interval detects
a dead neighbor faster and costs more packets on the link. `level-1/hello-interval` and
`level-2/hello-interval` replace it at one level.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello interval.

children.description:
Ze advertises `hello-interval` multiplied by this value as the holding time in each IIH,
clamped into 1 to 65535 seconds. The default of 3 lets two hellos be lost before a neighbor
drops the adjacency. The clamp means that no configuration can advertise a holding time of 0,
which would time the adjacency out at once. `level-1/hold-multiplier` and
`level-2/hold-multiplier` replace it at one level.
children.name: hold-multiplier
children.short-help: Hold time = hello-interval * hold-multiplier.

children.description:
This narrows the instance `level` for one circuit. l1 forms only a Level-1 adjacency on
the circuit, l2 only a Level-2 adjacency, and l1-l2 forms both. The circuit floods LSPs and
advertises its reachability only at the levels it forms. A level the instance `level` does
not hold stays off whatever this leaf says.
children.name: level
children.short-help: Per-interface level override.

values.name: l1
values.short-help: Form only a Level-1 adjacency on this circuit.

values.name: l1-l2
values.short-help: Form both adjacencies on this circuit, the default.

values.name: l2
values.short-help: Form only a Level-2 adjacency on this circuit.

children.description:
The value names a `key-chains` entry. Ze then signs and verifies the Level-1 IIH on
this circuit with that chain. RFC 5304 section 2 states that 'IS-IS Hello PDUs SHALL use
the Link Level Authentication String'. This leaf covers the hello only. The LSP, CSNP and
PSNP take the chain that `isis/level-1/auth-key-chain` names.
children.name: auth-key-chain
children.short-help: L1 per-interface (IIH) key-chain reference.

children.description:
Ze sends the Level-1 IIH at this period, in place of the circuit-wide
`hello-interval`. A broadcast circuit runs one Hello timer for each level it forms,
because the Level-1 and the Level-2 LAN IIH are separate PDUs sent to separate multicast
groups. A point-to-point circuit sends one IIH that serves both levels, so it runs one
Hello timer, and that timer takes this pair whenever the circuit forms Level-1. An unset
leaf keeps the circuit-wide value.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: L1 hello-interval override.

children.description:
Ze multiplies the Level-1 hello interval by this value and advertises the product as
the holding time in each Level-1 IIH, clamped into 1 to 65535 seconds. It replaces the
circuit-wide `hold-multiplier` for Level-1. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide value.
children.name: hold-multiplier
children.short-help: L1 hold-multiplier override.

children.description:
Ze advertises this cost for the circuit in the Level-1 LSP, in place of `metric`. An
unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide metric. The value also becomes the metric of the
connected prefixes the circuit contributes at Level-1.
children.name: metric
children.short-help: L1 wide metric override.

children.description:
Ze uses this priority in the Level-1 DIS election, in place of `priority`. An unset
leaf keeps the circuit-wide priority, and so does the value 0: Ze reads an override only
when it is more than 0. To ask for the lowest preference, set the circuit-wide `priority`
to 0.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: L1 DIS priority override.

children.description:
The leaves here replace the circuit-wide value for Level-1 only. One circuit can then
carry a different cost, a different DIS preference, a different Hello period or a different
holding time at each level. A leaf that is not set keeps the circuit-wide value. A circuit
that does not form Level-1 ignores the whole container.
children.name: level-1
children.short-help: Level-1 per-interface overrides.

children.description:
The value names a `key-chains` entry. Ze then signs and verifies the Level-2 IIH on
this circuit with that chain. RFC 5304 section 2 states that 'IS-IS Hello PDUs SHALL use
the Link Level Authentication String'. This leaf covers the hello only. The LSP, CSNP and
PSNP take the chain that `isis/level-2/auth-key-chain` names.
children.name: auth-key-chain
children.short-help: L2 per-interface (IIH) key-chain reference.

children.description:
Ze sends the Level-2 IIH at this period, in place of the circuit-wide
`hello-interval`. A broadcast circuit runs one Hello timer for each level it forms,
because the Level-1 and the Level-2 LAN IIH are separate PDUs sent to separate multicast
groups. A point-to-point circuit sends one IIH that serves both levels, so it runs one
Hello timer, and that timer takes this pair only on a circuit that forms Level-2 alone.
An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide value.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: L2 hello-interval override.

children.description:
Ze multiplies the Level-2 hello interval by this value and advertises the product as
the holding time in each Level-2 IIH, clamped into 1 to 65535 seconds. It replaces the
circuit-wide `hold-multiplier` for Level-2. An unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide value.
children.name: hold-multiplier
children.short-help: L2 hold-multiplier override.

children.description:
Ze advertises this cost for the circuit in the Level-2 LSP, in place of `metric`. An
unset leaf keeps the circuit-wide metric. The value also becomes the metric of the
connected prefixes the circuit contributes at Level-2.
children.name: metric
children.short-help: L2 wide metric override.

children.description:
Ze uses this priority in the Level-2 DIS election, in place of `priority`. An unset
leaf keeps the circuit-wide priority, and so does the value 0: Ze reads an override only
when it is more than 0. To ask for the lowest preference, set the circuit-wide `priority`
to 0.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: L2 DIS priority override.

children.description:
The leaves here replace the circuit-wide value for Level-2 only. One circuit can then
carry a different cost, a different DIS preference, a different Hello period or a different
holding time at each level. A leaf that is not set keeps the circuit-wide value. A circuit
that does not form Level-2 ignores the whole container.
children.name: level-2
children.short-help: Level-2 per-interface overrides.

children.description:
The circuit advertises this cost in TLV 22, and its connected prefixes advertise it in
TLV 135 and TLV 236. RFC 5305 section 3 states that 'The metric octets are encoded as a
24-bit unsigned integer', which is the 1 to 16777215 range here. SPF adds the value once for
each hop, so a lower value makes the circuit preferred. `level-1/metric` and `level-2/metric`
replace it at one level.
children.name: metric
children.short-help: Wide metric (RFC 5305).

children.description:
Ze opens no circuit for a passive interface, so it sends no hello and forms no
adjacency. The connected prefixes of the interface still become TLV 135 and TLV 236 entries
in the node's own LSP, at the metric `metric` sets. Use it on a loopback and on a customer
LAN, where the prefix MUST be reachable and no IS-IS neighbor exists.
children.name: passive
children.short-help: Advertise the interface but form no adjacencies.

children.description:
The value rides in each LAN hello and decides the DIS election on a broadcast circuit.
The highest priority wins, and the highest SNPA MAC address breaks a tie. A priority of 0 is
valid and only lowers the preference, so it does not stop this IS from winning an election it
is alone in. The leaf changes nothing on a point-to-point circuit.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: DIS election priority (broadcast circuits).

children.description:
Ze opens one circuit for each entry that is enabled and not passive. A link that comes up
after start opens its circuit at that moment, and a link that goes down closes it. The connected
prefixes of an enabled entry become TLV 135 and TLV 236 reachability in the node's own LSP.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Per-interface IS-IS configuration.

children.description:
Only an interface with an entry here runs IS-IS. Ze opens no circuit on an interface that this
list omits, so no adjacency forms on it and its connected prefixes reach no LSP.
children.name: interfaces
children.short-help: IS-IS-enabled interfaces.

children.description:
The format is RFC 3339, for example 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z. An empty value leaves the
end open. Keep the accept window of the old key open until every neighbor signs with the
new key.
children.name: end
children.short-help: RFC3339 end timestamp.

children.description:
The format is RFC 3339, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. An empty value leaves the
start open, so the key is accepted from the moment it is committed. A value Ze cannot
parse also leaves the start open.
children.name: start
children.short-help: RFC3339 start timestamp.

children.description:
Ze accepts a received PDU signed with any key whose accept window holds the current
time, up to 16 keys in one chain. Open the accept window of the new key before its send
window. Every neighbor then accepts the new key before any of them signs with it.
children.name: accept-lifetime
children.short-help: When this key is accepted on receive (hitless rotation).

children.description:
cleartext sends the secret in the PDU as auth type 1, so it detects a misconfiguration
and stops no attacker. hmac-md5, the default, is auth type 54 (RFC 5304). The five SHA
choices are auth type 3 (RFC 5310) and range from HMAC-SHA-1 to HMAC-SHA-512. Ze drops a key
whose token it does not know, so a typo here leaves that key out of the chain.
children.name: algorithm
children.short-help: Authentication algorithm.

values.name: cleartext
values.short-help: Cleartext password (auth type 1).

values.name: hmac-md5
values.short-help: HMAC-MD5 (auth type 54, RFC 5304).

values.name: hmac-sha-1
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-1 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).

values.name: hmac-sha-224
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-224 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).

values.name: hmac-sha-256
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-256 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).

values.name: hmac-sha-384
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-384 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).

values.name: hmac-sha-512
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-512 (auth type 3, RFC 5310).

children.description:
The commit encodes the value with the reversible $9$ encoding, the same one PPPoE and
WireGuard use, and the configuration output masks it. Ze decodes it in memory to derive the
HMAC key. A value that does not decode drops the key from the chain. Both ends of an
adjacency MUST hold the same plaintext secret under the same key-id.
children.name: secret
children.short-help: Shared secret, masked and $9$-encoded at rest.

children.description:
The format is RFC 3339, for example 2026-06-01T00:00:00Z. An empty value leaves the
end open, so the key signs forever. Set the end of the old key after the start of the new
one, so the two windows overlap and the rotation loses no adjacency.
children.name: end
children.short-help: RFC3339 end timestamp.

children.description:
The format is RFC 3339, for example 2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. An empty value leaves the
start open. A value Ze cannot parse also leaves the start open, and it does not drop the
key.
children.name: start
children.short-help: RFC3339 start timestamp.

children.description:
Ze signs with the first key in the chain whose send window holds the current time. A key
with no send-lifetime signs from the moment it is committed. When no key in the chain has an
open send window, Ze sends the PDU unsigned, and a neighbor under authentication rejects it.
children.name: send-lifetime
children.short-help: When this key may be used to sign (hitless rotation).

children.description:
Ze reads the keys in configuration order, which is key-id order. The first key whose send
lifetime holds the current time signs a PDU. Every key whose accept lifetime holds that time is
accepted on receive, up to 16 keys, which is what makes a rotation lose no adjacency.
children.name: key
children.short-help: Keys in this chain.

children.description:
A chain holds the keys that sign and verify IS-IS PDUs. Ze authenticates nothing until an
`auth-key-chain` leaf names the chain. A key whose algorithm token Ze does not know, or whose secret
does not decode, is dropped from the chain and signs nothing.
children.name: key-chains
children.short-help: Named authentication key chains for hitless key rotation.

children.description:
l1 holds only the Level-1 database and keeps this IS inside its own area. l2 holds only the
Level-2 database and makes this IS a backbone router. l1-l2, the default, holds both databases and
originates one LSP set at each level. A circuit forms an adjacency only at a level this leaf keeps.
children.name: level
children.short-help: Routing level of this Intermediate System.

values.name: l1
values.short-help: Level-1 (intra-area) only.

values.name: l1-l2
values.short-help: Both Level-1 and Level-2.

values.name: l2
values.short-help: Level-2 (backbone) only.

children.description:
The value names a `key-chains` entry. Ze then signs and verifies every Level-1 LSP, CSNP and
PSNP with that chain. RFC 5304 section 2 states that 'Level 1 Sequence Number PDUs SHALL use the
Area Authentication string as in Level 1 Link State PDUs'. The IIH is separate and takes the
per-interface chain.
children.name: auth-key-chain
children.short-help: L1 per-level (LSP/SNP, area key) key-chain reference.

children.description:
The leaves here apply to Level-1 across the whole instance, and not to one circuit. RFC 5304
section 2 calls the key they select the Area Authentication string.
children.name: level-1
children.short-help: Level-1 (area) per-level configuration.

children.description:
The value names a `key-chains` entry. Ze then signs and verifies every Level-2 LSP, CSNP and
PSNP with that chain. RFC 5304 section 2 states that 'Level 2 Sequence Number PDUs SHALL use the
domain authentication string as in Level 2 Link State PDUs'. The IIH is separate and takes the
per-interface chain.
children.name: auth-key-chain
children.short-help: L2 per-level (LSP/SNP, domain key) key-chain reference.

children.description:
The leaves here apply to Level-2 across the whole instance, and not to one circuit. RFC 5304
section 2 calls the key they select the domain authentication string.
children.name: level-2
children.short-help: Level-2 (domain) per-level configuration.

children.description:
The value stamps the Remaining Lifetime of every LSP this IS originates. A neighbor purges the
LSP when that field reaches 0, so a refresh MUST land first. The default of 1200 seconds pairs with
the 900-second refresh default. This value also bounds the refresh. A refresh of 0, or one
that is not less than this value, falls back to half of it.
children.name: lsp-lifetime
children.short-help: Maximum LSP remaining lifetime.

children.description:
Ze re-originates its own LSP set at this period, which bumps the sequence number and resets the
Remaining Lifetime to `lsp-lifetime`. Without the refresh a quiet node ages out of every neighbor's
database and disappears from the topology. A value of 0, or a value that is not less than
`lsp-lifetime`, falls back to half of `lsp-lifetime`. A refresh then always lands before the purge.
children.name: lsp-refresh-interval
children.short-help: LSP refresh interval.

children.description:
Network Entity Title(s), for example 49.0001.0000.0000.0001.00. At least one is required. The System
ID is the 6 octets before the NSEL.
children.name: net
children.short-help: Network Entity Title(s) of this IS-IS instance, at least one.

children.description:
The bit goes into the type block of this node's own LSP number zero. RFC 3787 section 4 states
that 'Section 7.2.8.1 of ISO 10589 instructs other systems not to use the overloaded IS as a transit
router'. Ze's own SPF obeys the bit the same way. It settles an overloaded node, so the prefixes
that node advertises stay reachable. It expands none of that node's links, so no path runs through
the node. Set the bit to hold transit traffic away while BGP converges after a restart.
children.name: overload
children.short-help: Set the overload bit (RFC 3787).

children.description:
When this leaf is not set, Ze takes the System ID from the 6 octets before the NSEL of the first
`net`. When it is set, the value MUST equal that derived value. A mismatch refuses the commit with
'system-id does not match the system id derived from net'.
children.name: system-id
children.short-help: 6-byte System ID (xxxx.xxxx.xxxx); derived from NET if unset.

isis.description:
The presence of this container starts the IS-IS component. At least one `net` leaf MUST be set for
the engine to run. A commit with no net is accepted, and the engine then stays idle, opens no circuit and
originates no LSP.
isis.name: isis

kernel.description:
The container carries no leaf, so writing it is the whole configuration.
The plugin watches the kernel routing table and emits each route on the
redistribute event bus. A route whose netlink protocol is RTPROT_KERNEL or
RTPROT_REDIRECT is dropped, so a connected subnet route and an ICMP
redirect route never reach BGP. The plugin registers the kernel route
source, and a redistribute statement names that source.
kernel.name: kernel
kernel.short-help: Kernel route redistribution. Presence enables the plugin.

children.description:
Allow PPP LCP authentication negotiation to proceed without an Auth-Protocol. The default is false,
so a peer that rejects all configured authentication methods is disconnected, instead of being
accepted as no-auth.
children.name: allow-no-auth
children.short-help: Allow PPP LCP to finish with no Auth-Protocol, false by default.

children.description:
PAP compares the SHA-256 of the received password with the
SHA-256 of this value, in constant time. CHAP-MD5 computes
MD5 over the identifier, this value and the challenge,
which RFC 1994 Section 4.1 defines. CHAP needs the secret
in clear, so this leaf holds no hash.
children.name: password
children.short-help:
Shared secret for PAP cleartext and
CHAP-MD5/MS-CHAPv2 challenge-response.

children.description:
Ze looks the PPP username up in this list and rejects a
username no entry carries. An empty list rejects every session.
The match is exact, so user and user@example.net are two
accounts.
children.name: user
children.short-help: One subscriber account, keyed by its PPP username.

children.description:
Ze rejects every session while no user is declared here, and it logs
that no user is configured. A session is matched against the list by
its PPP username, and an unknown username is rejected. Local
authentication answers PAP and CHAP-MD5, and it rejects MS-CHAPv2.
children.name: local
children.short-help: Authenticate a subscriber against users declared in this config.

children.description:
RFC 2869 Section 2.1 states that a locally configured value on
the NAS MUST override the value found in an Access-Accept. A leaf that is set pins the
cadence of every session, and the Acct-Interim-Interval attribute (type 85) of an
Access-Accept then changes nothing. This leaf has no default. An unset leaf is the
absent case, and it lets each Access-Accept set the cadence of that session. A session
runs at 300 seconds when neither side states an interval.
children.name: acct-interval
children.short-help: Accounting interim-update interval in seconds.

children.description:
Ze puts Acct-Delay-Time in the three accounting
records and in no other packet, so those three are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf
holds the attribute back from all three.
children.name: packet-type
children.short-help: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.

values.name: accounting-interim
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.

values.name: accounting-start
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.

values.name: accounting-stop
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.

children.description:
RFC 2866 Section 5.2 reports how many seconds the
client has been trying to send this record, and Ze rewrites the value on each
retransmission. A record that carries no Acct-Delay-Time is replayed byte for byte
instead, under the same Identifier, which is what an Access-Request does. accel-ppp ships
this attribute off by default.
children.name: acct-delay-time
children.short-help: Do not send Acct-Delay-Time (attribute 41).

children.description:
RFC 2866 Section 5.10 admits Acct-Terminate-Cause
in a Stop record alone, so accounting-stop is the one value this leaf accepts. An empty
leaf holds the attribute back from the Stop record, which is the same thing said with
fewer words.
children.name: packet-type
children.short-help: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.

values.name: accounting-stop
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.

children.description:
RFC 2866 Section 5.10 states that the attribute 'can
only be present in Accounting-Request records where the Acct-Status-Type is set to Stop',
so the Stop record is the only one this reaches. A pipeline that keys on its own teardown
signal does not need it. FreeRADIUS defaults it to NAS-Reboot in its accounting
queries.
children.name: acct-terminate-cause
children.short-help: Do not send Acct-Terminate-Cause (attribute 49).

children.description:
Ze puts Calling-Station-Id in the three accounting
records and in no other packet, so those three are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf
holds the attribute back from all three.
children.name: packet-type
children.short-help: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.

values.name: accounting-interim
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.

values.name: accounting-start
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.

values.name: accounting-stop
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.

children.description:
RFC 2865 Section 5.31 carries the number the call came
from, which is the L2TP Calling Number of the session, or the subscriber MAC address on
the PPPoE relay path. Some operators do not store it. Check the server first: FreeRADIUS
matches its IP pool queries on this attribute with no fallback value, so a pool it serves
keeps leases that never expire once the attribute stops arriving.
children.name: calling-station-id
children.short-help: Do not send Calling-Station-Id (attribute 31).

children.description:
Ze puts Event-Timestamp in the three accounting
records and in no other packet, so those three are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf
holds the attribute back from all three.
children.name: packet-type
children.short-help: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.

values.name: accounting-interim
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.

values.name: accounting-start
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.

values.name: accounting-stop
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.

children.description:
RFC 2869 Section 5.3 records the second at which the
event happened on the NAS. A server that stamps its own receive time does not need it.
FreeRADIUS falls back to the server clock in its default accounting queries, so a record
without the attribute is still stored with a time.
children.name: event-timestamp
children.short-help: Do not send Event-Timestamp (attribute 55).

children.description:
Ze puts Framed-IP-Address in the three accounting
records and in no other packet, so those three are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf
holds the attribute back from all three.
children.name: packet-type
children.short-help: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.

values.name: accounting-interim
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.

values.name: accounting-start
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.

values.name: accounting-stop
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.

children.description:
RFC 2865 Section 5.8 reports the IPv4 address the
session negotiated, and RFC 2866 Section 4.1 requires that a record which carries the
attribute carries the real address. An operator whose addressing is reported by another
system can hold it back. A session with no IPv4 address sends no attribute either way,
which is a different case and is not configurable.
children.name: framed-ip-address
children.short-help: Do not send Framed-IP-Address (attribute 8).

children.description:
Ze puts NAS-Port-Id in the Access-Request and in
the three accounting records, so all four are what this leaf accepts. An empty leaf holds
the attribute back from all four.
children.name: packet-type
children.short-help: Record types to hold the attribute back from. Name none for all of them.

values.name: access-request
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Access-Request that authenticates the session.

values.name: accounting-interim
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Interim-Update.

values.name: accounting-start
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Start.

values.name: accounting-stop
values.short-help: Hold the attribute back from the Accounting-Request whose Acct-Status-Type is Stop.

children.description:
RFC 2869 Section 5.17 names the access port in text,
and the nas-port-id-format leaf is the template Ze resolves for it. Clearing that leaf
also sends no attribute, on every packet at once. This container is the finer instrument:
it holds the attribute back from the record types you name while the template stays
configured for the rest.
children.name: nas-port-id
children.short-help: Do not send NAS-Port-Id (attribute 87).

children.description:
Name an attribute to hold it back from every record type
that would carry it. Add packet-type under it to hold it back from some record types and
keep it in the others. Each attribute accepts only the record types Ze can put it in, so
a line naming a record type that never carries the attribute is refused when the
configuration is committed rather than ignored at run time.
children.name: exclude
children.short-help: Attributes Ze does not send, each with the record types it is held back from.

children.description:
Ze sends every attribute it can build, which is what a billing
system usually wants, so this container is empty in most deployments. It names the
attributes one deployment does not want on the wire. Nothing here reaches
Acct-Status-Type, Acct-Session-Id or the NAS identity: RFC 2866 Section 5.13 counts the
first two as 'Exactly one instance of this attribute MUST be present', and its Note 1
requires either NAS-IP-Address or NAS-Identifier, so an Accounting-Request without them
is not a conformant record and Ze offers no way to write one.
children.name: attributes
children.short-help: Which optional RADIUS attributes Ze puts in the packets it sends.

children.description:
The listener implements RFC 5176. This leaf has no default on
purpose. An unset leaf keeps the listener off, so an existing deployment does not start
to accept CoA on upgrade. Ze accepts a request only from a configured RADIUS server
address.
children.name: coa-port
children.short-help: UDP port of the RADIUS CoA and Disconnect listener, usually 3799.

children.description:
Ze sends this text as the NAS-Identifier attribute in each
Access-Request and each Accounting-Request. RFC 2865 Section
4.1 requires either NAS-IP-Address or NAS-Identifier in an
Access-Request. With this leaf empty and source-address empty,
Ze sends the hostname, and the plugin name where the host
carries none.
children.name: nas-identifier
children.short-help: NAS-Identifier sent in RADIUS requests.

children.description:
Ze sends the NAS-Port-Id attribute (RFC 2869 Section 5.17) in an
Access-Request packet and in an Accounting-Request packet. The placeholders are
{nas-id}, {tunnel-id} and {session-id}. Ze copies every other character. All three
values are known before the session has an interface. One session therefore sends one
text in its Access-Request and in all its accounting records. A billing system can
join them on it. The 253-octet limit is the largest value a RADIUS attribute can carry (RFC 2865
Section 5). The commit refuses an unknown placeholder, it refuses a {nas-id} when
nas-identifier is unset, and it refuses a template whose widest resolution passes 253
octets because the nas-identifier it expands is long. An unset leaf sends no
attribute.
children.name: nas-port-id-format
children.short-help: Template for the NAS-Port-Id attribute sent in RADIUS requests.

children.description:
RFC 5176 Section 3.4 makes the Message-Authenticator attribute
optional, so the default is false. Ze then processes a request without the attribute
once its Request Authenticator verifies against the shared secret. Set this leaf to
true when every Dynamic Authorization Client sends the attribute. The attribute is an
HMAC-MD5 keyed with the shared secret, and it is the mitigation for the Blast-RADIUS
class of attack (CVE-2024-3596), which forges a RADIUS UDP packet with a chosen-prefix
MD5 collision against the authenticator. A client that sends no attribute gets no
answer while this leaf is true.
children.name: require-message-authenticator
children.short-help: Discard a CoA-Request or a Disconnect-Request that carries no Message-Authenticator.

children.description:
The default is 3 and the range is 1 to 10. Ze sends the request
that many times to one server, then moves to the next entry of
the list. An Access-Request is replayed byte for byte. An
Accounting-Request gets a new identifier and a new
Acct-Delay-Time on each attempt, which RFC 2866 Section 4.1
requires.
children.name: retries
children.short-help: Number of retransmit attempts per server.

children.description:
The leaf is mandatory, and Ze refuses a server entry
without it. Ze joins the value to port to reach the server.
The first entry of the list is the one Ze tries first, so
write the closest server first.
children.name: address
children.short-help: RADIUS server IP address or hostname.

children.description:
The default is 1812 and the range is 1 to 65535. Ze sends
the Access-Request packets and the Accounting-Request
packets of this server to this one port, because a server
entry carries no second port.
children.name: port
children.short-help: RADIUS server UDP port.

children.description:
RFC 2865 Section 3 states that the secret MUST NOT be
empty, that is length 0, because an empty secret makes a forged packet easy to
build.
children.name: shared-key
children.short-help: RADIUS shared secret.

children.description:
The operator orders the list. Ze tries the first entry, and moves to
the next one when that server does not answer. Write the closest
server first.
children.name: server
children.short-help: One RADIUS server Ze sends requests to, tried in the order written.

children.description:
Ze binds the outbound RADIUS socket to this address, so every
request leaves with it. Ze also sends the address as
NAS-IP-Address, which is one of the two attributes RFC 2865
Section 4.1 accepts to name the NAS. With the leaf empty, the
kernel picks the source address and Ze names the NAS with
NAS-Identifier instead.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IPv4 address for outbound RADIUS packets.

children.description:
The default is 3 seconds and the range is 1 to 30. The first
attempt waits this long, and each attempt after it waits twice
the wait before it. With the default of 3 seconds and 3
retries, a server that never answers costs 21 seconds before Ze
tries the next server.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: Per-request timeout in seconds.

children.description:
Authentication and accounting are separate exchanges to the same
server. A session is authorized by an Access-Accept, and the
Accounting-Request packets that follow report its traffic.
children.name: radius
children.short-help: Authenticate and account subscriber sessions against a RADIUS server.

children.description:
The container holds the backend that answers a credential. The
l2tp-auth-local plugin fills the local container under it, and the
l2tp-auth-radius plugin fills the radius container. The timing of the
PPP authentication phase sits under l2tp authentication instead.
children.name: auth
children.short-help: PPP authentication for L2TP subscriber sessions.

children.description:
PPP Auth-Protocol method first advertised in LCP Configure-Request. The default requires CHAP-MD5.
Set the leaf to none only together with allow-no-auth true.
children.name: auth-method
children.short-help: PPP Auth-Protocol method first advertised in LCP Configure-Request.

values.name: chap-md5
values.short-help: Advertise CHAP with the MD5 algorithm (RFC 1994), the default.

values.name: ms-chap-v2
values.short-help: Advertise MS-CHAP-V2 (RFC 2759).

values.name: none
values.short-help: Advertise no Auth-Protocol, so the session opens with no PPP authentication phase.

values.name: pap
values.short-help: Advertise PAP (RFC 1334), which carries the password in clear text.

children.description:
Periodic re-authentication interval in seconds, for CHAP and MS-CHAPv2 only. Zero disables re-auth.
A value of 1 to 4 is rejected, to prevent re-auth storms. The default is 0, which is disabled.
children.name: reauth-interval
children.short-help: Periodic re-authentication interval in seconds, 0 by default.

children.description:
PPP auth-phase timeout in seconds. A session that does not complete authentication within this
window is torn down. The default is 30 seconds.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: PPP auth-phase timeout in seconds, 30 by default.

children.description:
The container holds the timing of the PPP authentication phase, and nothing
else. The backend that answers a credential sits under the auth container, which the
l2tp-auth-local plugin and the l2tp-auth-radius plugin fill. Both leaves here
hot-apply: a new value reaches the next session, and a session that is already up
keeps the value it started with.
children.name: authentication
children.short-help: PPP authentication phase settings for L2TP sessions.

children.description:
Enable the CQM (Customer Quality Monitor) observer. When this leaf is true, Ze pre-allocates
per-session event rings and per-login sample rings at subsystem start. Ze also overrides the PPP
echo interval to 1s for RTT measurement.
children.name: cqm-enabled
children.short-help: Enable the CQM (Customer Quality Monitor) observer.

children.description:
The l2tp block itself starts the subsystem. This leaf stops the subsystem
where the block must stay, and it is filler where no other setting is needed. A
change is restart-only. The reload logs that it ignored the flip and asks for a
restart, and the running state stays as it is.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help:
Enable L2TP subsystem. Defaults to true when the
l2tp block is present; set to false to disable.

children.description:
Ze pre-allocates one ring for each session the subsystem can hold, and each
ring holds this many slots. The value therefore multiplies into the memory the
subsystem takes at startup. A full ring overwrites its oldest event. A session therefore keeps its
most recent events and loses the older ones. A change is restart-only, and the
reload logs that it ignored it.
children.name: event-ring-size-per-session
children.short-help:
Number of events in each per-session event ring.
When full, oldest events are overwritten.

children.description:
Seconds of peer silence before sending HELLO. RFC 2661 recommends 60s. A value more than 3600, which
is one hour, is rejected, because it disables keepalive.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Seconds of peer silence before Ze sends HELLO.

children.description:
Dead-peer detection threshold: consecutive unanswered HELLO keepalive intervals tolerated before an
established tunnel's peer is declared dead and the tunnel is torn down. The effective detection time
is hello-retries x hello-interval, measured from the last proof of peer liveness. That proof is a
delivered control message, or an acknowledgement of one of our messages, including a ZLB ACK of a
HELLO. A value of 0 disables dead-peer detection, and reliable-transport retransmit exhaustion,
about 31s, is then the only teardown signal. The default is 2.
children.name: hello-retries
children.short-help: Unanswered HELLO intervals tolerated before the peer is declared dead.

children.description:
Maximum concurrent PPP logins tracked by the CQM observer. The value controls the size of the
pre-allocated sample ring pool. When the maximum is exceeded, the least recently used login's data
is evicted.
children.name: max-logins
children.short-help: Maximum concurrent PPP logins the CQM observer tracks.

children.description:
Maximum concurrent sessions per tunnel. The default is a finite deployment safety cap. A value of 0
explicitly requests unbounded admission on each tunnel. A new ICRQ or OCRQ beyond a positive limit
is rejected with CDN Result Code 4 (no resources).
children.name: max-sessions
children.short-help: Maximum concurrent sessions per tunnel.

children.description:
Maximum concurrent L2TP tunnels. The default is a finite deployment safety cap. A value of 0
explicitly requests unbounded admission by this leaf. The 65535 ceiling imposed by RFC 2661's 16-bit
Tunnel ID field still applies. A new SCCRQ beyond a positive limit is rejected with StopCCN Result
Code 2.
children.name: max-tunnels
children.short-help: Maximum concurrent L2TP tunnels.

children.description:
IPCP (RFC 1332) is what gives the subscriber an IPv4 address. The default
true offers it on each new session. Set it false and Ze sets DisableIPCP on the
kernel PPP channel of a new session. That session then gets no IPv4 address, and
only IPv6CP can succeed. The leaf hot-applies, and a running session keeps the
address it holds.
children.name: enable-ipcp
children.short-help:
Enable the IPCP NCP (RFC 1332) for new L2TP sessions.
When false, no IPv4 address is negotiated.

children.description:
Enable the IPv6CP NCP (RFC 5072) for new L2TP sessions. When this leaf is false, no IPv6 interface
identifier is negotiated.
children.name: enable-ipv6cp
children.short-help: Enable the IPv6CP NCP (RFC 5072) for a new L2TP session.

children.description:
NCP negotiation timeout in seconds. A session that does not complete NCP within this window is torn
down. The default is 30 seconds.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: NCP negotiation timeout in seconds, 30 by default.

children.description:
NCP is the phase after PPP authentication, where each side negotiates one
network-layer protocol. The two enable leaves choose which protocols Ze offers, and
the timeout leaf bounds the phase. Each leaf hot-applies to a new session, and a
session that is already up keeps what it negotiated.
children.name: ncp
children.short-help: NCP (Network Control Protocol) settings for L2TP sessions.

children.description:
Ze offers the address as the IPCP Primary DNS option, and it offers no such
option while the leaf is absent. A subscriber that asks for another address gets
a Configure-Nak carrying this one. Ze drops the option from its later requests
when the subscriber rejects it.
children.name: dns-primary
children.short-help: Primary DNS server pushed to subscribers.

children.description:
Ze offers the address as the IPCP Secondary DNS option, and it offers no
such option while the leaf is absent. The leaf is independent of dns-primary, so
a pool can name one, both, or neither.
children.name: dns-secondary
children.short-help: Secondary DNS server pushed to subscribers.

children.description:
The range is inclusive, so this address is handed to a session as well. Ze
refuses an end before the start, and it refuses the block that names end without
start. A session that arrives after the last free address is refused with pool
exhausted.
children.name: end
children.short-help: Last address in the pool range (inclusive).

children.description:
Each session sees this address as its IPCP peer, so it is the next hop the
subscriber routes through. Ze refuses an address that falls inside the range
from start to end, and it refuses an address that is not IPv4.
children.name: gateway
children.short-help:
NAS-side IP for all PPP sessions (IPCP local address).
Must not overlap the pool range.

children.description:
Ze refuses the ipv4 block that names start without end, and it refuses a
start after the end. The range is inclusive at both ends, and the bitmap holds
one bit for each address in it. Ze releases an address when the session goes
down, and hands it to the next session that asks.
children.name: start
children.short-help: First address in the pool range.

children.description:
The gateway is the NAS-side address every session sees as its IPCP
peer, and it MUST NOT fall inside the start-to-end range.
children.name: ipv4
children.short-help: The IPv4 range and the DNS servers a PPP session receives.

children.description:
Ze cuts the block into prefixes of the delegated length and hands one to
each subscriber. The block must be native IPv6, so an IPv4-mapped address is
refused. The delegated length can be at most 24 bits longer than the block,
which bounds one pool at 16 million prefixes.
children.name: block
children.short-help: Prefix block to allocate from, for example 2001:db8::/32.

children.description:
Ze cuts the block into prefixes of this length, and delegates one to each
subscriber over DHCPv6 IA_PD (RFC 3633). Ze installs a route to that prefix on the PPP
interface. The length is 48 to 64, and it must be at least as long as the block. It must
be at most 24 bits longer than the block, which caps one pool at 16 million prefixes. The
default is 56, and Ze logs a warning when the leaf is absent. A session RADIUS answers
with a Delegated-IPv6-Prefix takes that prefix and reaches no pool, so this length does
not apply to it.
children.name: delegation-length
children.short-help:
Prefix length delegated to each subscriber
(e.g. 56 for /56 prefixes).

children.description:
The pool allocates one prefix of the configured length to each
subscriber, taken from the configured block, for DHCPv6 prefix
delegation. RFC 3633 defines that delegation.
children.name: ipv6-pd
children.short-help: IPv6 prefix delegation pool for subscribers.

children.description:
The leaf is required here, and the ipv6-pd pool leaves it optional. Ze
refuses a block that is not native IPv6, and names the pool in the error. Ze does
not compare the block of one pool against the block of another, so two blocks
that overlap can delegate one prefix twice.
children.name: block
children.short-help: Prefix block to allocate from, for example 2001:db8::/32.

children.description:
The leaf is required here, and the ipv6-pd pool falls back to 56 when it is
absent. Each named pool cuts its own block into prefixes of its own length, so two pools
can delegate different lengths. The length is 48 to 64, and it must be at least as long
as the block of this pool. It must be at most 24 bits longer than that block, which caps
the pool at 16 million prefixes. A session RADIUS answers with a Delegated-IPv6-Prefix
takes that prefix and reaches no pool.
children.name: delegation-length
children.short-help: Prefix length delegated to each subscriber.

children.description:
The Framed-IPv6-Pool attribute RADIUS returns for a session names one of these
pools. Each pool holds its own block and its own bitmap, and none of them is tied to
the ipv6-pd pool. The name is the list key.
children.name: named-ipv6-pool
children.short-help:
Named IPv6 prefix pools selected by RADIUS
Framed-IPv6-Pool attribute (RFC 6911 attr 100).

children.description:
A session RADIUS sends to this pool receives this address, and not the one
the ipv4 pool holds. Ze offers no Primary DNS option while the leaf is absent,
even when the ipv4 pool names one.
children.name: dns-primary
children.short-help: Primary DNS server pushed to subscribers.

children.description:
A session RADIUS sends to this pool receives this address, and not the one
the ipv4 pool holds. Ze offers no Secondary DNS option while the leaf is absent,
even when the ipv4 pool names one.
children.name: dns-secondary
children.short-help: Secondary DNS server pushed to subscribers.

children.description:
The range is inclusive, so this address is handed to a session as well. A
session that arrives after the last free address of this pool is refused with
pool exhausted. Ze does not move that session to another pool.
children.name: end
children.short-help: Last address in the pool range (inclusive).

children.description:
A session RADIUS sends to this pool sees this address as its IPCP peer, and
not the gateway of the ipv4 pool. Ze refuses an address that falls inside the
range from start to end of this pool.
children.name: gateway
children.short-help: NAS-side IP for sessions using this pool.

children.description:
The leaf is required here, and the ipv4 pool leaves it optional. Ze refuses
a start after the end. Ze does not compare the range of one pool against the
range of another. Two ranges that overlap can therefore hand one address to two
sessions.
children.name: start
children.short-help: First address in the pool range.

children.description:
The Framed-Pool attribute RADIUS returns for a session names one of these
pools. Ze then uses the gateway and the DNS servers of that pool. Ze refuses the
session when the attribute names a pool this list does not hold, and it does not
fall back to the ipv4 pool. The ipv4 pool serves a session with no Framed-Pool.
children.name: named-pool
children.short-help: Named IPv4 pools selected by RADIUS Framed-Pool attribute.

children.description:
A pool is bitmap-backed, so an address is released when the session
goes down and is handed to the next session that asks.
children.name: pool
children.short-help: Address and prefix pools handed to L2TP PPP sessions.

children.description:
Name of the L2TP remote (dial target) that matching subscribers are relayed to. It MUST reference a
remote declared under l2tp/remote, and an unknown name is rejected at config validation.
children.name: remote
children.short-help: Name of the L2TP remote that matching subscribers are relayed to.

children.description:
PPPoE-to-L2TP relay bindings (LAC role). A subscriber whose PADI or PADR carries a matching PPPoE
Service-Name is relayed into an L2TP incoming call toward the named remote, instead of terminating
PPP locally on this box. Removing a binding restores local termination for that service.
children.name: relay
children.short-help: PPPoE-to-L2TP relay bindings for the LAC role.

children.description:
Ze sends the SCCRQ to this address, with the port leaf beside it. The leaf
is mandatory, so a remote without one is refused at commit. Ze parses the
address and the port into one UDP endpoint when it loads the config. A value it
cannot parse is refused there, and not at dial time.
children.name: address
children.short-help:
Remote control-plane IP address to dial. The SCCRQ
destination (RFC 2661 Section 6.1).

children.description:
Permit LNS-side outgoing calls ('request l2tp outgoing-call') toward this remote. The default is
false. The remote must be explicitly enabled for dial-out before an operator can place a call, so a
mistyped remote name is rejected rather than dialed.
children.name: outgoing-calls
children.short-help: Permit LNS-side outgoing calls toward this remote, false by default.

children.description:
Remote UDP port for the control channel. RFC 2661 assigns 1701, and this leaf overrides it for a
non-standard peer.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Remote UDP port for the control channel, 1701 by default.

children.description:
Per-remote CHAP-MD5 tunnel-authentication secret (RFC 2661 Section 5.1.1). It overrides the
subsystem-level shared-secret for tunnels dialed to this remote. When it is empty, this dial carries
no Challenge AVP. The value is masked in CLI output.
children.name: shared-secret
children.short-help: Per-remote CHAP-MD5 tunnel-authentication secret (RFC 2661).

children.description:
L2TP dial targets: remote LNS/LAC endpoints ze initiates tunnels toward, and sends SCCRQ to. They
are referenced by name from 'request l2tp outgoing-call remote <name>' and from PPPoE relay
bindings. Declaring a remote grants no dial by itself. An operator action (RPC) or a relay binding
drives the dial.
children.name: remote
children.short-help: L2TP dial targets, the remote LNS or LAC endpoints Ze dials.

children.description:
Duration of CQM sample retention per login, in seconds. The duration is divided by the 100-second
bucket interval to determine ring capacity. The default of 86400, which is 24 hours, gives 864
buckets.
children.name: sample-retention-seconds
children.short-help: Duration of CQM sample retention per login, in seconds.

children.description:
Default download rate applied to new sessions. The format is a
number followed by a suffix, for example 10mbit or 100kbit. Ze
enforces it with the queueing discipline it installs on the pppN
interface, which shapes what leaves the interface toward the
subscriber.
children.name: default-rate
children.short-help: Default download rate applied to a new session.

children.description:
The default is tbf, and the value reaches every subscriber
interface. With tbf Ze installs one class that carries the rate of
the session. With htb Ze installs one default class whose rate and
ceiling are both that rate, so the class cannot borrow. Ze refuses
a token that is not tbf or htb.
children.name: qdisc-type
children.short-help: Queueing discipline type for subscriber interfaces.

values.name: htb
values.short-help: Hierarchical Token Bucket (classful).

values.name: tbf
values.short-help: Token Bucket Filter (single rate limiter).

children.description:
The format is a number and a suffix, for example 5mbit, and the
suffixes are bit, kbit, mbit, gbit, bps, kbps, mbps and gbps. Ze
enforces it with a policer on the pppN interface ingress hook,
which drops what the subscriber sends above the rate. A queueing
discipline cannot carry this direction, because the ingress hook
holds no queue to delay a packet into. Ze applies default-rate
instead when the leaf is absent. A RADIUS Filter-Id of the form
rate:20mbit/5mbit replaces both this rate and the download rate on
that session, and a RADIUS CoA changes both on a running session.
The 'show l2tp shaper' command reports the rate in force.
children.name: upload-rate
children.short-help: Default upload rate. When omitted, defaults to default-rate.

children.description:
Ze installs the queueing discipline and the ingress policer on the pppN
interface when the session starts. The queueing discipline carries the
download rate and the policer carries the upload rate. A rate changed
here reaches the sessions that start after the change. A running
session keeps the rate it was given, and a RADIUS CoA changes it.
children.name: shaper
children.short-help: Traffic shaping applied to each L2TP subscriber interface.

children.description:
Shared secret used to compute CHAP-MD5 Challenge Responses (RFC 2661 Section 5.1.1, and the AVPs are
defined in Section 4.4.3). When the leaf is unset and a peer sends a Challenge AVP, the subsystem
rejects the tunnel with StopCCN Result Code 4 (Not Authorized). The value is masked in CLI output
and cleared from the process environment after the first read.
children.name: shared-secret
children.short-help: Shared secret that computes CHAP-MD5 Challenge Responses (RFC 2661).

l2tp.description:
L2TPv2 tunnel subsystem settings (RFC 2661). Presence of this block with
any content implies the subsystem is enabled. Use 'enabled false' to
disable it explicitly, or 'enabled true' as a filler when no other settings
are needed.
l2tp.name: l2tp

children.description:
The default is 15 seconds, which is 3 hello intervals. Ze advertises
this value in each Hello, and a neighbor drops the adjacency when no
Hello arrives inside it. Keep it more than hello-interval, because a hold time
under one interval drops the adjacency between two Hellos.
children.name: hello-hold-time
children.short-help: Hello adjacency hold time

children.description:
The default is 5 seconds and the range is 1 to 65535. Ze sends one
Hello for each interface at this period. A shorter interval finds a
neighbor faster and puts more packets on the link.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello message interval

children.description:
Ze runs one discovery listener for each interface of this list. An
empty list runs one listener that the system assigns to an interface
itself. A reload starts discovery on an interface added to the list and
stops it on one removed, and it leaves the other interfaces alone. The
connected prefixes of these interfaces are the FECs this LSR is egress
for.
children.name: interfaces
children.short-help: Interfaces on which LDP discovery is enabled

children.description:
The default is 60 seconds and the range is 1 to 65535. RFC 5036
section 3.5.3 carries the KeepAlive Time in the Common Session
Parameters of the Initialization message. The receiving LSR MUST
calculate the KeepAlive Timer from 'the smaller of its proposed
KeepAlive Time and the KeepAlive Time received in the PDU'.
The lower of the two proposals wins. Ze proposes this value to each
neighbor it opens a session to. Ze sends a KeepAlive every third of
the negotiated value and closes the session when no PDU arrives
inside three times it. The exchange happens one time, at the start
of the session, so a session that is up keeps the value it
negotiated. A change here applies to the sessions that open after
it.
children.name: keepalive-time
children.short-help: Session keepalive interval.

children.description:
Ze refuses a value that is not an IP address, and stays idle while the
leaf is empty. The first 4 bytes of every LDP PDU header carry this
identifier. Ze also originates a label binding for the address itself,
so a neighbor can reach this LSR by its identifier.
children.name: lsr-id
children.short-help: LSR identifier (IPv4 address format)

children.description:
Ze advertises this address in the transport address TLV of each Hello,
which is the address a neighbor connects to. Ze also binds it as the
source address of the TCP connection it opens. With the leaf empty, the
Hello carries no transport address TLV and the kernel picks the source
address.
children.name: transport-address
children.short-help: Transport address for TCP sessions

ldp.description:
The engine stays idle until lsr-id carries an address, and it says so in
the log. Ze then sends Hello messages to 224.0.0.2 port 646 and opens a TCP
session on port 646 to each neighbor it discovers.
ldp.name: ldp

children.description:
The default is false. When the leaf is true, Ze writes the ADD-PATH subtypes
of RFC 8050. A BGP4MP record then carries subtype 9, and a
TABLE_DUMP_V2 dump carries the ADD-PATH RIB subtypes. Ze writes the ADD-PATH subtype whether or not the
session negotiated ADD-PATH, so the record declares a path identifier
that the message can lack.
children.name: add-path
children.short-help:
Force add-path subtypes even when not negotiated
with the peer.

children.description:
The strftime codes in the path decide when Ze opens a new file.
The supported codes are %Y (year), %m (month), %d (day),
%H (hour), %M (minute), %S (second), %s (unix timestamp) and
%N (table name).
children.name: file
children.short-help: Output file path, with strftime patterns for rotation.

children.description:
The value 0 keeps one file open until the daemon stops.
A value of more than 0 makes Ze close the file once it has been open
that many seconds. Ze then opens the next one, and the strftime codes
in file give the new name. A file of -
writes to standard output, which never rotates.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: File rotation interval in seconds. Zero disables rotation.

children.description:
The stream carries every BGP message: OPEN, UPDATE,
NOTIFICATION, KEEPALIVE and ROUTE_REFRESH. It carries the FSM
state transitions too. Ze writes them as BGP4MP records.
children.name: all
children.short-help: All BGP messages and state changes, written as BGP4MP records.

children.description:
The default is both, and both records each direction. received keeps
the messages the peer sent to Ze, and sent keeps the messages Ze sent
to the peer. The filter reaches the BGP messages alone, so a state change record is written
whatever the value.
children.name: direction
children.short-help: Which direction of BGP messages to record.

values.name: both
values.short-help: Record the BGP messages of each direction.

values.name: received
values.short-help: Record the BGP messages the peer sent to Ze alone.

values.name: sent
values.short-help: Record the BGP messages Ze sent to the peer alone.

children.description:
The default is false, so each record header carries type 16, BGP4MP.
RFC 6396 Section 5.3 names type 17 as BGP4MP_ET, and that header
carries 4 more bytes for the microsecond field. The switch reaches all
three streams at once.
children.name: extended-timestamp
children.short-help:
Use BGP4MP_ET (type 17) with microsecond resolution
instead of BGP4MP (type 16).

children.description:
Ze compares each entry with the peer address of the message, so a
message of another peer reaches no file. The filter reaches the BGP
messages alone: Ze writes a state change record for every peer,
whatever this list holds.
children.name: peer-filter
children.short-help:
If set, only record messages from/to these peer addresses.
Empty list means record all peers.

children.description:
The strftime codes in the path name the file Ze opens, exactly as
they do in a dump stream. Ze writes this stream only when the path is set
and interval is more than 0. A path of - writes to standard
output.
children.name: file
children.short-help: Output file path with strftime patterns.

children.description:
The default is 3600 seconds and the range is 60 to 86400. Each dump
writes one PEER_INDEX_TABLE record and then the RIB entries of
every address family, which RFC 6396 Section 4.3.1 requires in that
order.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: RIB dump interval in seconds. Minimum 60.

children.description:
Each dump writes one PEER_INDEX_TABLE record, and then the RIB
entries for every address family. Ze writes them as
TABLE_DUMP_V2 records.
children.name: routes
children.short-help: Periodic RIB snapshots, written as TABLE_DUMP_V2 records.

children.description:
The strftime codes in the path decide when Ze opens a new file.
The supported codes are %Y (year), %m (month), %d (day),
%H (hour), %M (minute), %S (second), %s (unix timestamp) and
%N (table name).
children.name: file
children.short-help: Output file path, with strftime patterns for rotation.

children.description:
The value 0 keeps one file open until the daemon stops.
A value of more than 0 makes Ze close the file once it has been open
that many seconds. Ze then opens the next one, and the strftime codes
in file give the new name. A file of -
writes to standard output, which never rotates.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: File rotation interval in seconds. Zero disables rotation.

children.description:
The stream carries the UPDATE messages alone. The all stream
beside it carries every message type.
children.name: updates
children.short-help: BGP UPDATE message stream (BGP4MP records).

mrt.description:
The container holds the extended-timestamp switch, the add-path
switch, the peer filter, the direction, and the three dump streams.
mrt.name: mrt

children.description:
RFC 5340 Appendix C.2 excludes every AS-external-LSA from a
stub area and from an NSSA. A router inside a stub area reaches an external destination
through the default inter-area route alone. The backbone MUST NOT be a stub area or an
NSSA, and a virtual link MUST NOT cross either one.
children.name: area-type
children.short-help: Area type.

values.name: normal
values.short-help: Flood AS-external-LSAs into this area.

values.name: nssa
values.short-help: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and import external routes as Type 7 LSAs.

values.name: stub
values.short-help: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and reach external destinations through the default route.

children.description:
Ze declares the far endpoint dead after this long with no
Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not
match, so the two endpoints MUST hold the same value.
children.name: dead-interval
children.short-help: Router-dead interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose
HelloInterval does not match the value configured on the receiving interface. The two
endpoints of the virtual link MUST hold the same value.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.4 requires RxmtInterval on a virtual
link. Set it well over the round-trip delay between the two routers. That delay is hard to
estimate across a transit area, so a value that is too large is the safer error.
children.name: retransmit-interval
children.short-help: LSA retransmit interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this
value to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet.
children.name: transmit-delay
children.short-help: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 5340 / RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).

children.description:
RFC 5340 section 4.2 defines the virtual link. The link
belongs to the backbone area. Its cost is the SPF path cost across the transit area, and
it is never configured. The transit area MUST NOT be the backbone, a stub area, or an
NSSA.
children.name: virtual-link
children.short-help: Virtual link across this transit area to a backbone area-border router.

children.description:
The list is keyed by area-id. All routers in an area MUST agree on
the configuration of that area. RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 states that a disagreement stops an
adjacency from forming between two routers.
children.name: area
children.short-help: Per-area OSPFv3 configuration.

children.description:
RFC 5838 section 1 maps each address family to a separate Instance ID
and a separate OSPFv3 instance. Ze starts one engine instance for each configured family.
An area declared here belongs to that instance alone.
children.name: areas
children.short-help: OSPFv3 areas for this address family.

children.description: RFC 5838 §2.1 gives the IPv4-multicast range as 96 to 127.
children.name: instance-id
children.short-help: OSPFv3 Instance ID of this address family.

children.description:
Ze enrolls the interface only when the areas container declares
this area-id. An interface belongs to one area, which RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names Area
ID.
children.name: area
children.short-help: Declared area this interface belongs to.

children.description:
A BFD session that goes Down or AdminDown declares the
OSPFv3 neighbor down at once. Without BFD, Ze waits for the router-dead interval, which is
40 seconds by default.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable single-hop BFD failure detection on this interface.

children.description:
The far system sends no faster than this value. RFC 5880
section 6.8.4 takes the agreed interval as the greater of this value and the Desired Min
TX Interval of the far system.
children.name: min-rx
children.short-help: Required minimum BFD receive interval (RFC 5880 Required Min RX Interval).

children.description:
RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed transmit interval
as the greater of this value and the Required Min RX Interval of the far system.
children.name: min-tx
children.short-help: Desired minimum BFD transmit interval (RFC 5880 Desired Min TX Interval).

children.description:
RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 states that Detect Mult is the
number of packets that have to be missed in a row to declare the session down. The
detection time is this value multiplied by the agreed transmit interval.
children.name: multiplier
children.short-help: BFD detection multiplier (RFC 5880 Detect Mult).

children.description:
RFC 5880 and RFC 5881 define single-hop BFD. When this
container enables it, a Full adjacency opens an IPv6 single-hop BFD session over the
link-local pair. A failure that BFD detects declares the neighbor down much faster than
the router-dead interval does.
children.name: bfd
children.short-help: Single-hop BFD failure detection for this OSPFv3 interface.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 requires an interface output cost of more
than 0, and Ze advertises the value as the cost of this link. An absent leaf takes cost 1,
whatever the speed of the link is.
children.name: cost
children.short-help: Interface output cost.

children.description:
Ze declares the neighbor dead after this long with no Hello.
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match.
Appendix C.3 gives 4 times the hello-interval as the sample value.
children.name: dead-interval
children.short-help: Router-dead interval.

children.description:
A false value drops the interface from the OSPFv3 instance. Ze
then sends no Hello on the link, and this router advertises no link for it.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: OSPFv3 enabled on this interface.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose
HelloInterval does not match the configured value, so every router on the link MUST hold
the same value. A smaller value detects a failure faster and sends more protocol
traffic.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello interval.

children.description:
The value sets the length the key leaf takes: 40 hex
characters for sha1, 64 for sha256, 96 for sha384, and 128 for sha512. Both routers MUST
configure the same algorithm. RFC 4552 section 3 requires the receiver to discard a packet
that fails the check, with no message.
children.name: algorithm
children.short-help: HMAC-SHA integrity algorithm.

values.name: sha1
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-1 with a 40 hex character key.

values.name: sha256
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-256 with a 64 hex character key.

values.name: sha384
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-384 with a 96 hex character key.

values.name: sha512
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-512 with a 128 hex character key.

children.description:
RFC 4552 §4 offers confidentiality with ESP only, never
with AH. Leave this leaf absent, or set it to null, for an ESP that authenticates the
packet and does not encrypt it.
children.name: encryption-algorithm
children.short-help: ESP confidentiality algorithm.

values.name: aes128
values.short-help: Encrypt with AES and a 128-bit key.

values.name: aes256
values.short-help: Encrypt with AES and a 256-bit key.

values.name: null
values.short-help: Authenticate the packet and do not encrypt it.

children.description:
The length MUST match the encryption-algorithm leaf. aes128
takes 32 hex characters, and aes256 takes 64.
children.name: encryption-key
children.short-help: ESP encryption key, written in hex characters.

children.description:

values.short-help: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and reach external destinations through the default route.

children.description:
Ze declares the far endpoint dead after this long with no
Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not
match, so the two endpoints MUST hold the same value.
children.name: dead-interval
children.short-help: Router-dead interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose
HelloInterval does not match the value configured on the receiving interface. The two
endpoints of the virtual link MUST hold the same value.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.4 requires RxmtInterval on a virtual
link. Set it well over the round-trip delay between the two routers. That delay is hard to
estimate across a transit area, so a value that is too large is the safer error.
children.name: retransmit-interval
children.short-help: LSA retransmit interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this
value to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet.
children.name: transmit-delay
children.short-help: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 5340 / RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).

children.description:
RFC 5340 section 4.2 defines the virtual link. The link
belongs to the backbone area. Its cost is the SPF path cost across the transit area, and
it is never configured. The transit area MUST NOT be the backbone, a stub area, or an
NSSA.
children.name: virtual-link
children.short-help: Virtual link across this transit area to a backbone area-border router.

children.description:

the configuration of that area. RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 states that a disagreement stops an
adjacency from forming between two routers.
children.name: area
children.short-help: Per-area OSPFv3 configuration.

children.description:
RFC 5838 section 1 maps each address family to a separate Instance ID
and a separate OSPFv3 instance. Ze starts one engine instance for each configured family.
An area declared here belongs to that instance alone.
children.name: areas
children.short-help: OSPFv3 areas for this address family.

children.description:
RFC 5340 §2.5 defines the Instance ID. RFC 5838 §2.1 gives the
IPv6-unicast range as 0 to 31.
children.name: instance-id
children.short-help: OSPFv3 Instance ID of this address family.

children.description:
Ze enrolls the interface only when the areas container declares
this area-id. An interface belongs to one area, which RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names Area
ID.
children.name: area
children.short-help: Declared area this interface belongs to.

children.description:

OSPFv3 neighbor down at once. Without BFD, Ze waits for the router-dead interval, which is
40 seconds by default.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable single-hop BFD failure detection on this interface.

section 6.8.4 takes the agreed interval as the greater of this value and the Desired Min
TX Interval of the far system.

children.short-help: Required minimum BFD receive interval (RFC 5880 Required Min RX Interval).

as the greater of this value and the Required Min RX Interval of the far system.
children.name: min-tx
children.short-help: Desired minimum BFD transmit interval (RFC 5880 Desired Min TX Interval).

number of packets that have to be missed in a row to declare the session down. The

children.short-help: BFD detection multiplier (RFC 5880 Detect Mult).

container enables it, a Full adjacency opens an IPv6 single-hop BFD session over the

children.short-help: Single-hop BFD failure detection for this OSPFv3 interface.

children.name: holddown
children.short-help: Seconds Ze waits before it declares the link synchronized.

it from the first Hello of the neighbor when this leaf is absent.
children.name: link-local

children.description:
The value 0 makes the neighbor ineligible, so Ze polls it
and never elects it.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Eligibility of this neighbor in the DR election and the BDR election.

children.name: network-type
children.short-help: Network type of this interface.

values.short-help: Multi-access link that elects a DR and a BDR with multicast Hellos.

values.name: nbma
values.short-help: Non-broadcast multi-access link that elects a DR over a configured neighbor list.

values.name: point-to-multipoint
values.short-help: Set of point-to-point links with no DR election.

values.name: point-to-point
values.short-help: Link with one neighbor and no DR election.

and forms no adjacency. The interface stays enrolled in its area, so this router keeps

children.name: passive
children.short-help: Advertise the interface but form no adjacency.

children.description:

that stays silent (RFC 2328 Appendix C.5).
children.name: poll-interval
children.short-help: NBMA poll interval.

children.description: The value 0 makes the interface ineligible.

children.description:

configured SRGB and the configured SRLB.

children.short-help: Enable Segment Routing for this address family.

children.description:

is 0 for IPv4 and 2 for IPv6. This leaf needs no-php.
children.name: explicit-null
children.short-help: Set the E-Flag on the Prefix-SID.

children.description:

MUST be less than the total size of the SRGB.
children.name: index
children.short-help: SID index into the SRGB.

children.description:
The penultimate hop then keeps the label rather than popping
it, so no penultimate-hop-popping happens.
children.name: no-php
children.short-help: Set the NP-Flag on the Prefix-SID.

the advertising router, which is usually a loopback host address. A receiver MUST ignore

children.short-help: Mark this as a node Prefix-SID (sets the N-Flag on the Extended Prefix TLV).

children.short-help: Prefix-SIDs Ze advertises for the local prefixes.

children.short-help: First MPLS label of the SRGB (inclusive).

children.description: The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
children.name: upper-bound
children.short-help: Last MPLS label of the SRGB, inclusive.

children.description:

which a Prefix-SID index maps into (RFC 8665 section 3.2). The SRGB MUST NOT overlap the
SRLB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.

children.short-help: Segment Routing Global Block of this node.

children.description:

both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of

children.name: lower-bound
children.short-help: First MPLS label of the SRLB (inclusive).

children.description: The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
children.name: upper-bound
children.short-help: Last MPLS label of the SRLB, inclusive.

keys an IPv6 neighbor by Router ID.
children.name: nbma-neighbor
children.short-help: A statically configured NBMA neighbor.

children.description:
broadcast and point-to-point are the two common types. nbma
elects a DR and a BDR over a configured neighbor list, with unicast Hellos and poll
Hellos (RFC 5340). point-to-multipoint treats the link as a set of point-to-point links,
with one /128 host route for each neighbor and no DR.
children.name: network-type
children.short-help: Network type of this interface.

values.name: broadcast
values.short-help: Multi-access link that elects a DR and a BDR with multicast Hellos.

values.name: nbma
values.short-help: Non-broadcast multi-access link that elects a DR over a configured neighbor list.

values.name: point-to-multipoint
values.short-help: Set of point-to-point links with no DR election.

values.name: point-to-point
values.short-help: Link with one neighbor and no DR election.

children.description:
Ze gives a passive interface no sender, so it sends no Hello
and forms no adjacency. The interface stays enrolled in its area, so this router keeps
advertising the link.
children.name: passive
children.short-help: Advertise the interface but form no adjacency.

children.description:
Ze sends a Hello at this slower rate to a configured neighbor
that stays silent (RFC 2328 Appendix C.5).
children.name: poll-interval
children.short-help: NBMA poll interval.

children.description: The value 0 makes the interface ineligible.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Priority of this interface in the DR election and the BDR election.

children.description:
The list is keyed by the interface name. The same interface CAN
