appear in the list of another address family, with its own cost and its own
adjacencies.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Per-interface OSPFv3 configuration.

children.description:
RFC 5838 section 2.4 requires a router that takes part in an address
family to discard a Hello whose AF-bit is clear. The base IPv6-unicast family is the one
exception. An interface listed here takes part in this family only.
children.name: interfaces
children.short-help: OSPFv3-enabled interfaces for this address family.

children.description:
When this leaf is true, the RI LSA advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the
configured SRGB and the configured SRLB.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable Segment Routing for this address family.

children.description:
The upstream neighbor then uses the Explicit NULL label, which
is 0 for IPv4 and 2 for IPv6. This leaf needs no-php.
children.name: explicit-null
children.short-help: Set the E-Flag on the Prefix-SID.

children.description:
The MPLS label is the SRGB base plus this index. The index
MUST be less than the total size of the SRGB.
children.name: index
children.short-help: SID index into the SRGB.

children.description:
The penultimate hop then keeps the label rather than popping
it, so no penultimate-hop-popping happens.
children.name: no-php
children.short-help: Set the NP-Flag on the Prefix-SID.

children.description:
RFC 7684 section 2.1 sets the N-Flag when the prefix identifies
the advertising router, which is usually a loopback host address. A receiver MUST ignore
the flag when the prefix length is not a host prefix.
children.name: node-sid
children.short-help: Mark this as a node Prefix-SID (sets the N-Flag on the Extended Prefix TLV).

children.description:
The local prefix is usually the loopback. Each Prefix-SID carries
a SID index into the SRGB of this node (RFC 8665 section 5).
children.name: prefix-sid
children.short-help: Prefix-SIDs Ze advertises for the local prefixes.

children.description:
Ze reads the SRGB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are
both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of
the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
children.name: lower-bound
children.short-help: First MPLS label of the SRGB (inclusive).

children.description: The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
children.name: upper-bound
children.short-help: Last MPLS label of the SRGB, inclusive.

children.description:
The SRGB is the contiguous global MPLS label range this node owns,
which a Prefix-SID index maps into (RFC 8665 section 3.2). The SRGB MUST NOT overlap the
SRLB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
children.name: srgb
children.short-help: Segment Routing Global Block of this node.

children.description:
Ze reads the SRLB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are
both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of
the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
children.name: lower-bound
children.short-help: First MPLS label of the SRLB (inclusive).

children.description: The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
children.name: upper-bound
children.short-help: Last MPLS label of the SRLB, inclusive.

children.description:
The SRLB is the local MPLS label range that Ze allocates an
Adjacency-SID from (RFC 8665 section 3.3). The SRLB MUST NOT overlap the SRGB, the LDP
label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
children.name: srlb
children.short-help: Segment Routing Local Block of this node.

children.description:
Ze advertises the value in the SRMS-Preference TLV (RFC 8665
section 3.4). An unset leaf advertises no TLV.
children.name: srms-preference
children.short-help: SR Mapping-Server preference of this node.

children.description:
RFC 8665 defines Segment Routing for OSPFv2, and RFC 8666 for OSPFv3.
Ze advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the SRGB label range, the SRLB label range, and one
Prefix-SID for each configured prefix. Ze installs label-switched forwarding through the
shared mpls-fib. Segment Routing is off by default.
children.name: segment-routing
children.short-help: Segment Routing over the MPLS dataplane.

children.description:
RFC 5838 §2.1 gives the Instance ID range as 32 to 63. Ze computes
reachability in the unicast shape. Ze does not implement the MOSPF tree computation.
children.name: ipv6-multicast
children.short-help: The IPv6-multicast OSPFv3 address family.

children.description:
RFC 5340 Appendix C.2 excludes every AS-external-LSA from a
stub area and from an NSSA. A router inside a stub area reaches an external destination
through the default inter-area route alone. The backbone MUST NOT be a stub area or an
NSSA, and a virtual link MUST NOT cross either one.
children.name: area-type
children.short-help: Area type.

values.name: normal
values.short-help: Flood AS-external-LSAs into this area.

values.name: nssa
values.short-help: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and import external routes as Type 7 LSAs.

values.name: stub
values.short-help: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and reach external destinations through the default route.

children.description:
Ze declares the far endpoint dead after this long with no
Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not
match, so the two endpoints MUST hold the same value.
children.name: dead-interval
children.short-help: Router-dead interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose
HelloInterval does not match the value configured on the receiving interface. The two
endpoints of the virtual link MUST hold the same value.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.4 requires RxmtInterval on a virtual
link. Set it well over the round-trip delay between the two routers. That delay is hard to
estimate across a transit area, so a value that is too large is the safer error.
children.name: retransmit-interval
children.short-help: LSA retransmit interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this
value to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet.
children.name: transmit-delay
children.short-help: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 5340 / RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).

children.description:
RFC 5340 section 4.2 defines the virtual link. The link
belongs to the backbone area. Its cost is the SPF path cost across the transit area, and
it is never configured. The transit area MUST NOT be the backbone, a stub area, or an
NSSA.
children.name: virtual-link
children.short-help: Virtual link across this transit area to a backbone area-border router.

children.description:
The list is keyed by area-id. All routers in an area MUST agree on
the configuration of that area. RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 states that a disagreement stops an
adjacency from forming between two routers.
children.name: area
children.short-help: Per-area OSPFv3 configuration.

children.description:
RFC 5838 section 1 maps each address family to a separate Instance ID
and a separate OSPFv3 instance. Ze starts one engine instance for each configured family.
An area declared here belongs to that instance alone.
children.name: areas
children.short-help: OSPFv3 areas for this address family.

children.description: RFC 5838 §2.1 gives the IPv6-unicast range as 0 to 31.
children.name: instance-id
children.short-help: OSPFv3 Instance ID of this address family.

children.description:
Ze enrolls the interface only when the areas container declares
this area-id. An interface belongs to one area, which RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names Area
ID.
children.name: area
children.short-help: Declared area this interface belongs to.

children.description:
A BFD session that goes Down or AdminDown declares the
OSPFv3 neighbor down at once. Without BFD, Ze waits for the router-dead interval, which is
40 seconds by default.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable single-hop BFD failure detection on this interface.

children.description:
The far system sends no faster than this value. RFC 5880
section 6.8.4 takes the agreed interval as the greater of this value and the Desired Min
TX Interval of the far system.
children.name: min-rx
children.short-help: Required minimum BFD receive interval (RFC 5880 Required Min RX Interval).

children.description:
RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed transmit interval
as the greater of this value and the Required Min RX Interval of the far system.
children.name: min-tx
children.short-help: Desired minimum BFD transmit interval (RFC 5880 Desired Min TX Interval).

children.description:
RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 states that Detect Mult is the
number of packets that have to be missed in a row to declare the session down. The
detection time is this value multiplied by the agreed transmit interval.
children.name: multiplier
children.short-help: BFD detection multiplier (RFC 5880 Detect Mult).

children.description:
RFC 5880 and RFC 5881 define single-hop BFD. When this
container enables it, a Full adjacency opens an IPv6 single-hop BFD session over the
link-local pair. A failure that BFD detects declares the neighbor down much faster than
the router-dead interval does.
children.name: bfd
children.short-help: Single-hop BFD failure detection for this OSPFv3 interface.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 requires an interface output cost of more
than 0, and Ze advertises the value as the cost of this link. An absent leaf takes cost 1,
whatever the speed of the link is.
children.name: cost
children.short-help: Interface output cost.

children.description:
Ze declares the neighbor dead after this long with no Hello.
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match.
Appendix C.3 gives 4 times the hello-interval as the sample value.
children.name: dead-interval
children.short-help: Router-dead interval.

children.description:
A false value drops the interface from the OSPFv3 instance. Ze
then sends no Hello on the link, and this router advertises no link for it.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: OSPFv3 enabled on this interface.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose
HelloInterval does not match the configured value, so every router on the link MUST hold
the same value. A smaller value detects a failure faster and sends more protocol
traffic.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello interval.

children.description:
The value sets the length the key leaf takes: 40 hex
characters for sha1, 64 for sha256, 96 for sha384, and 128 for sha512. Both routers MUST
configure the same algorithm. RFC 4552 section 3 requires the receiver to discard a packet
that fails the check, with no message.
children.name: algorithm
children.short-help: HMAC-SHA integrity algorithm.

values.name: sha1
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-1 with a 40 hex character key.

values.name: sha256
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-256 with a 64 hex character key.

values.name: sha384
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-384 with a 96 hex character key.

values.name: sha512
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-512 with a 128 hex character key.

children.description:
RFC 4552 §4 offers confidentiality with ESP only, never
with AH. Leave this leaf absent, or set it to null, for an ESP that authenticates the
packet and does not encrypt it.
children.name: encryption-algorithm
children.short-help: ESP confidentiality algorithm.

values.name: aes128
values.short-help: Encrypt with AES and a 128-bit key.

values.name: aes256
values.short-help: Encrypt with AES and a 256-bit key.

values.name: null
values.short-help: Authenticate the packet and do not encrypt it.

children.description:
The length MUST match the encryption-algorithm leaf. aes128
takes 32 hex characters, and aes256 takes 64.
children.name: encryption-key
children.short-help: ESP encryption key, written in hex characters.

children.description:
The length MUST match the algorithm. sha1 takes 40 hex
characters, sha256 takes 64, sha384 takes 96, and sha512 takes 128.
children.name: key
children.short-help: Integrity key, written in hex characters.

children.description:
esp is RFC 4303, and an implementation MUST support
authentication with it. ah is RFC 4302, and an implementation MAY support it.
children.name: protocol
children.short-help: IPsec protocol that protects the OSPFv3 packets.

values.name: ah
values.short-help: Authentication Header (RFC 4302): integrity with no encryption.

values.name: esp
values.short-help: Encapsulating Security Payload (RFC 4303): integrity, with optional encryption.

children.description:
The window applies to ah and to esp alike. RFC 4302 §3.4.3
and RFC 4303 §3.4.3 let the receiver enable or disable anti-replay for each SA, and this
leaf is that switch. The value 0 disables it.

0 is the default because every OSPFv3 SA is manually keyed (RFC 4552 §7), and RFC 4302 §5
says that a compliant implementation SHOULD NOT provide anti-replay with a manually keyed
SA. A non-zero window is 32 or more, which is the minimum RFC 4302 §3.4.3 requires. That
section prefers 64.
children.name: replay-window
children.short-help: Anti-replay window, counted in packets.

children.description:
RFC 4552 section 7 gives the inbound SA and the outbound SA
the same SPI, because a manually keyed group negotiates nothing. Give each protected
interface its own SPI. The kernel identifies the state by the destination, the SPI and the
protocol, so two interfaces that share an SPI collide.
children.name: spi
children.short-help: Security Parameters Index (RFC 4303 §2.1 reserves 0..255).

children.description:
RFC 4552 defines manual IPsec, with AH or with ESP, for an
OSPFv3 interface. When the interface comes up, Ze installs a transport-mode kernel
Security Association and a proto-89 policy. The kernel applies AH or ESP below the
socket. It discards an unprotected OSPF packet, and one whose integrity check fails,
with no message (RFC 4552 §3 and §4).

This authentication path is distinct from the RFC 7166 authentication trailer, and it is
mutually exclusive with a per-interface authentication key-chain. RFC 4552 §7 permits
manual keying only, because IKE cannot key the multicast group. The inbound SA and the
outbound SA share one key.
children.name: ipsec
children.short-help: Manual IPsec that protects the OSPFv3 packets of this interface.

children.description:
RFC 5443 section 1 states that a blackhole exists when one
link on the shortest path carries no LDP session. A false value leaves the cost of the
link unchanged while LDP converges. Traffic can then be lost on a link whose label
bindings do not exist yet.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable LDP-IGP synchronization on this interface.

children.description:
The wait starts when the LDP session is established
(RFC 5443 section 2).
children.name: holddown
children.short-help: Seconds Ze waits before it declares the link synchronized.

children.description:
RFC 5443 and RFC 6138 define LDP-IGP synchronization. The
IPv6 family reuses the address-family-neutral state machine on the shared interface
model.
children.name: ldp-sync
children.short-help: LDP-IGP synchronization of the IPv6 family.

children.description:
The address is the unicast Hello destination. Ze learns
it from the first Hello of the neighbor when this leaf is absent.
children.name: link-local
children.short-help: IPv6 link-local address of the neighbor.

children.description:
The value 0 makes the neighbor ineligible, so Ze polls it
and never elects it.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Eligibility of this neighbor in the DR election and the BDR election.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.6 defines the neighbor list. The list is
required for network-type nbma and for the non-broadcast point-to-multipoint variant. Ze
keys an IPv6 neighbor by Router ID.
children.name: nbma-neighbor
children.short-help: A statically configured NBMA neighbor.

children.description:
broadcast and point-to-point are the two common types. nbma
elects a DR and a BDR over a configured neighbor list, with unicast Hellos and poll
Hellos (RFC 5340). point-to-multipoint treats the link as a set of point-to-point links,
with one /128 host route for each neighbor and no DR.
children.name: network-type
children.short-help: Network type of this interface.

values.name: broadcast
values.short-help: Multi-access link that elects a DR and a BDR with multicast Hellos.

values.name: nbma
values.short-help: Non-broadcast multi-access link that elects a DR over a configured neighbor list.

values.name: point-to-multipoint
values.short-help: Set of point-to-point links with no DR election.

values.name: point-to-point
values.short-help: Link with one neighbor and no DR election.

children.description:
Ze gives a passive interface no sender, so it sends no Hello
and forms no adjacency. The interface stays enrolled in its area, so this router keeps
advertising the link.
children.name: passive
children.short-help: Advertise the interface but form no adjacency.

children.description:
Ze sends a Hello at this slower rate to a configured neighbor
that stays silent (RFC 2328 Appendix C.5).
children.name: poll-interval
children.short-help: NBMA poll interval.

children.description: The value 0 makes the interface ineligible.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Priority of this interface in the DR election and the BDR election.

children.description:
The list is keyed by the interface name. The same interface CAN
appear in the list of another address family, with its own cost and its own
adjacencies.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Per-interface OSPFv3 configuration.

children.description:
RFC 5838 section 2.4 requires a router that takes part in an address
family to discard a Hello whose AF-bit is clear. The base IPv6-unicast family is the one
exception. An interface listed here takes part in this family only.
children.name: interfaces
children.short-help: OSPFv3-enabled interfaces for this address family.

children.description:
When this leaf is true, the RI LSA advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the
configured SRGB and the configured SRLB.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable Segment Routing for this address family.

children.description:
The upstream neighbor then uses the Explicit NULL label, which
is 0 for IPv4 and 2 for IPv6. This leaf needs no-php.
children.name: explicit-null
children.short-help: Set the E-Flag on the Prefix-SID.

children.description:
The MPLS label is the SRGB base plus this index. The index
MUST be less than the total size of the SRGB.
children.name: index
children.short-help: SID index into the SRGB.

children.description:
The penultimate hop then keeps the label rather than popping
it, so no penultimate-hop-popping happens.
children.name: no-php
children.short-help: Set the NP-Flag on the Prefix-SID.

children.description:
RFC 7684 section 2.1 sets the N-Flag when the prefix identifies
the advertising router, which is usually a loopback host address. A receiver MUST ignore
the flag when the prefix length is not a host prefix.
children.name: node-sid
children.short-help: Mark this as a node Prefix-SID (sets the N-Flag on the Extended Prefix TLV).

children.description:
The local prefix is usually the loopback. Each Prefix-SID carries
a SID index into the SRGB of this node (RFC 8665 section 5).
children.name: prefix-sid
children.short-help: Prefix-SIDs Ze advertises for the local prefixes.

children.description:
Ze reads the SRGB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are
both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of
the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
children.name: lower-bound
children.short-help: First MPLS label of the SRGB (inclusive).

children.description: The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
children.name: upper-bound
children.short-help: Last MPLS label of the SRGB, inclusive.

children.description:
The SRGB is the contiguous global MPLS label range this node owns,
which a Prefix-SID index maps into (RFC 8665 section 3.2). The SRGB MUST NOT overlap the
SRLB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
children.name: srgb
children.short-help: Segment Routing Global Block of this node.

children.description:
Ze reads the SRLB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are
both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of
the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
children.name: lower-bound
children.short-help: First MPLS label of the SRLB (inclusive).

children.description: The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
children.name: upper-bound
children.short-help: Last MPLS label of the SRLB, inclusive.

children.description:
The SRLB is the local MPLS label range that Ze allocates an
Adjacency-SID from (RFC 8665 section 3.3). The SRLB MUST NOT overlap the SRGB, the LDP
label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
children.name: srlb
children.short-help: Segment Routing Local Block of this node.

children.description:
Ze advertises the value in the SRMS-Preference TLV (RFC 8665
section 3.4). An unset leaf advertises no TLV.
children.name: srms-preference
children.short-help: SR Mapping-Server preference of this node.

children.description:
RFC 8665 defines Segment Routing for OSPFv2, and RFC 8666 for OSPFv3.
Ze advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the SRGB label range, the SRLB label range, and one
Prefix-SID for each configured prefix. Ze installs label-switched forwarding through the
shared mpls-fib. Segment Routing is off by default.
children.name: segment-routing
children.short-help: Segment Routing over the MPLS dataplane.

children.description:
The ipv6 container is the bare spelling of this same family. Ze
maps both names to the IPv6-unicast family, so configure one of the two.
children.name: ipv6-unicast
children.short-help: IPv6-unicast OSPFv3 address family (RFC 5838 §2.1: Instance ID 0-31).

children.description:
The IPv6 family is OSPFv3 (RFC 5340). It runs as a second engine
instance over the ospfv3 transport, which uses ff02::5 and ff02::6. It shares the FSM,
the flooding and the SPF machinery with the IPv4 family.
children.name: address-family
children.short-help: More OSPF address families.

children.description:
The types are normal, stub and nssa. The stub specification
and the NSSA specification state what each type does.
children.name: area-type
children.short-help: Type of this area.

values.name: normal
values.short-help: Flood AS-external-LSAs into this area.

values.name: nssa
values.short-help: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and import external routes as Type 7 LSAs.

values.name: stub
values.short-help: Keep AS-external-LSAs out and reach external destinations through the default route.

children.description:
The value MUST name an entry of the key-chains list. Ze
leaves the interface unauthenticated when the name matches no entry.
children.name: key-chain
children.short-help: Default key chain inherited by interfaces.

children.description:
An interface whose authentication mode is inherit takes the key
chain of its area. An interface that names its own key chain overrides this default.
children.name: authentication
children.short-help: Area-level authentication defaults.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 names the value StubDefaultCost. It is
the cost of the default summary-LSA this router advertises into the area. The value
applies only when this router is an area border router of a stub area or an NSSA.
children.name: default-cost
children.short-help: Default summary metric for stub/NSSA areas.

children.description:
Ze keeps the default summary the area requires, and suppresses
every other Type 3 summary.
children.name: no-summary
children.short-help: Suppress the Type 3 summaries of a totally-stubby or totally-NSSA area.

children.description:
This leaf applies to an internal NSSA router that has a
usable forwarding address. An NSSA border router always originates the required
default route, so the leaf changes nothing there. It is also inert when the area
sets no-summary true: RFC 3101 section 1.3 makes an internal router's Type 7
default and the no-summary option mutually exclusive.
children.name: default-originate
children.short-help: Originate a Type 7 default route into the NSSA.

children.description:
RFC 3101 section 3.5 defines the interval. A newly elected
translator keeps translating for this long after it loses the role.
children.name: stability-interval
children.short-help: Hysteresis before a translator that lost the role stops translating.

children.description:
candidate enters the election, which the highest router-id
wins. always translates whatever the election decides. never does no translation.
children.name: translate-role
children.short-help: Role of this router in the Type 7 to Type 5 translation.

values.name: always
values.short-help: Translate Type 7 LSAs whatever the election decides.

values.name: candidate
values.short-help: Enter the translator election, which the highest Router ID wins.

values.name: never
values.short-help: Do no Type 7 to Type 5 translation.

children.description:
RFC 3101 section 1.3 lets an NSSA import an external route in a
limited fashion, which a stub area cannot do. The area carries such a route as a Type 7
LSA, and the elected translator rewrites it into a Type 5 LSA.
children.name: nssa
children.short-help: NSSA-specific configuration (applies when area-type is nssa).

children.description:
RFC 2328 section 12.4.3 suppresses the Type 3
summary-LSA when the status is DoNotAdvertise, and the component networks then stay hidden
from the other areas. The value advertise sends one summary-LSA for the range instead.
children.name: advertise
children.short-help: Advertise the aggregate or suppress specifics.

values.name: advertise
values.short-help: Send one summary-LSA for the whole range.

values.name: not-advertise
values.short-help: Send no summary-LSA and hide the component networks from other areas.

children.description:
RFC 2328 section 12.4.3 gives the range the largest
cost of any component network. This leaf replaces that cost with a fixed value.
children.name: cost
children.short-help: Override cost for the aggregate Type 3 LSA.

children.description:
The list is keyed by the prefix. Ze advertises one Type 3
summary-LSA for the range, and it suppresses the summary-LSA of every network the range
covers.
children.name: range
children.short-help: One area summary range.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.2 advertises at most one summary-LSA for
each address range outside the area. A network that no range covers keeps its own
summary-LSA.
children.name: ranges
children.short-help: Inter-area summary ranges.

children.description:
Ze declares the far endpoint dead after this long with no
Hello. RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not
match, so the two endpoints MUST hold the same value.
children.name: dead-interval
children.short-help: Router-dead interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose
HelloInterval does not match the value configured on the receiving interface. The two
endpoints of the virtual link MUST hold the same value.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.4 requires RxmtInterval on a virtual
link. Set it well over the round-trip delay between the two routers. That delay is hard to
estimate across a transit area, so a value that is too large is the safer error.
children.name: retransmit-interval
children.short-help: LSA retransmit interval on the virtual link.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this
value to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet.
children.name: transmit-delay
children.short-help: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).

children.description:
RFC 2328 section 15 defines the virtual link. The link belongs
to the backbone area. Ze computes its output cost from the SPF over the transit area, and
it is never configured. The transit area MUST NOT be the backbone, a stub area, or an
NSSA.
children.name: virtual-link
children.short-help: Virtual link across this transit area to a backbone area-border router.

children.description:
The list is keyed by area-id. Ze holds one link-state database for
each area this router joins. An interface joins the area that its area leaf names.
children.name: area
children.short-help: Per-area configuration.

children.description:
RFC 2328 section 3 states that each area runs a separate copy of the
link-state algorithm, so each area holds its own link-state database. A router connected
to two or more areas is an area border router.
children.name: areas
children.short-help: OSPF areas.

children.description:
Ze then originates the default LSA whatever the Loc-RIB holds. A
false value needs a non-OSPF default in the Loc-RIB first.
children.name: always
children.short-help: Originate even without a default in the RIB.

children.description:
The value is the metric of the Type 5 default LSA, and the field is
24 bits wide. With metric-type type-2, the router that advertises the smallest metric
attracts the traffic of the whole AS.
children.name: metric
children.short-help: Default LSA metric.

children.description:
RFC 2328 section 2.3 adds the distance to the ASBR for a Type 1
metric. A Type 2 metric is compared alone, and the internal distance only breaks a tie.
children.name: metric-type
children.short-help: External metric type for the default route.

values.name: type-1
values.short-help: Add the internal distance to the ASBR to the external metric.

values.name: type-2
values.short-help: Compare the external metric alone and break a tie on the internal distance.

children.description:
Ze originates the LSA only while the Loc-RIB holds a default route
that OSPF did not learn. Ze purges the LSA when that route goes away. The always leaf
removes the condition.
children.name: originate
children.short-help: Originate a default Type 5 LSA.

children.description:
Ze originates one Type 5 AS-external LSA for 0.0.0.0/0 (RFC 2328
section 12.4.4). The origination makes this router an AS boundary router, which sets the
E-bit in its Router-LSA.
children.name: default-information
children.short-help: Default-route origination as an AS-external LSA.

children.description:
RFC 7684 defines the Extended Link Opaque LSA, which is Opaque Type 8.
The LSA associates attributes with the links of this router, one LSA for each
point-to-point link and each transit link, which mirrors the Router-LSA link. The leaf
needs opaque true.

The LSA is a container that a link-attribute application fills with sub-TLVs, for example
Segment Routing. It is off by default until such a producer needs it. Ze decodes and
shows a received Extended Link LSA whatever this leaf holds.
children.name: extended-link
children.short-help: Originate Extended Link Opaque LSAs for the local links.

children.description:
RFC 7684 defines the Extended Prefix Opaque LSA, which is Opaque
Type 7. The LSA associates attributes with the prefixes this router advertises. The leaf
needs opaque true.

The LSA is a container that a prefix-attribute application fills with sub-TLVs, for
example Segment Routing. It is off by default until such a producer needs it. Ze decodes
and shows a received Extended Prefix LSA whatever this leaf holds.
children.name: extended-prefix
children.short-help: Originate Extended Prefix Opaque LSAs for the local prefixes.

children.description:
RFC 5286 section 3.6 selects at most one alternate next-hop for
each primary next-hop. A false leaf computes no alternate, so a link failure waits for the
SPF run and the FIB update.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable LFA / TI-LFA fast-reroute backup computation and install.

children.description:
ti-lfa builds a repair list from the Prefix-SID and the
Adjacency-SID of the repair path, so it needs segment-routing. lfa uses a directly
connected loop-free neighbor alone, and it protects no prefix that has none.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Backup computation mode: base LFA, or LFA with a TI-LFA SR-repair fallback.

values.name: lfa
values.short-help: Base loop-free alternates only (RFC 5286).

values.name: ti-lfa
values.short-help: Add the Segment-Routing repair-list fallback (TI-LFA).

children.description:
RFC 5286 section 3.2 gives Inequality 3 for a node-protecting
alternate N against a primary neighbor E for destination D. Distance_opt(N, D) MUST be
less than Distance_opt(N, E) plus Distance_opt(E, D). Section 3.6 takes a link-protecting
alternate when no node-protecting one exists.
children.name: node-protection
children.short-help: Prefer node-protecting alternates over link-only alternates (RFC 5286 Section 3.6).

children.description:
RFC 5286 defines the Loop-Free Alternate. When this container enables
fast reroute, SPF pre-computes a loop-free backup next-hop beside each primary next-hop
and programs it into the FIB. Ze then repairs a single local link failure, or a single
node failure, before the IGP reconverges.

TI-LFA mode adds a Segment-Routing repair-list fallback where no directly connected LFA
exists, and it needs segment-routing. The container applies to OSPFv2 and to OSPFv3.
OSPFv3 gets base-LFA next-hop selection only, because an SR repair label is IPv4 only.
children.name: fast-reroute
children.short-help: Loop-Free Alternate and TI-LFA IP fast reroute.

children.description:
RFC 3623 Appendix B.2 names this value
RestartHelperStrictLSAChecking, and section 3.2 states the rule. Ze stops helper mode
when it installs a changed LSA that would flood to the restarting router.
children.name: strict-lsa-checking
children.short-help: Stop helper mode when a changed LSA would flood to the restarting router.

children.description:
RFC 3623 section 3.1 enters helper mode on two conditions. This
router MUST hold a Full adjacency with the restarting router. The database MUST NOT have
changed since that router restarted. A false value refuses helper mode, so the restart
drops the adjacency.
children.name: support
children.short-help: RFC 3623 Appendix B.2 RestartHelperSupport: act as a helper for a restarting neighbor.

children.description:
In this role Ze holds the adjacency to a restarting neighbor and
stops LSDB churn for the grace period of that neighbor.
children.name: helper
children.short-help: Helper role of this router.

children.description:
RFC 3623 Appendix B.1 names this value RestartInterval. Keep
it at or under LSRefreshTime, which is 1800 seconds. A longer interval lets the LSAs of
this router age out during the restart.
children.name: restart-interval
children.short-help: Grace period during which a neighbor advertises this router as fully adjacent.

children.description:
planned names a restart the operator triggered.
planned-and-unplanned covers a cold restart too (RFC 3623 section 5), and Ze restricts
the unplanned reason to unknown and to redundant-cp.
children.name: support
children.short-help: RFC 3623 Appendix B.1 RestartSupport.

values.name: disabled
values.short-help: Never originate a Grace-LSA, and restart normally.

values.name: planned
values.short-help: Originate a Grace-LSA on a planned restart only.

values.name: planned-and-unplanned
values.short-help: Originate a Grace-LSA on a planned restart and on an unplanned restart.

children.description:
In this role Ze originates a Grace-LSA and keeps the FIB across a
restart.
children.name: restarter
children.short-help: Restarting-router role of this router.

children.description:
RFC 3623 defines Graceful Restart for OSPFv2, and RFC 5187 for
OSPFv3. The container is family-neutral and drives both address families. The OSPFv3
family inherits it unless that family configures its own.
children.name: graceful-restart
children.short-help: Graceful Restart, which keeps forwarding across a control-plane restart.

children.description:
Ze enrolls the interface only when the areas container declares
this area-id. An interface belongs to one area, which RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names Area
ID.
children.name: area
children.short-help: Declared area this interface belongs to.

children.description:
The value MUST name an entry of the key-chains list. Ze
takes the area chain instead when the mode leaf is inherit, even when this leaf names a
chain.
children.name: key-chain
children.short-help: Key chain reference.

children.description: The value inherit takes the area default.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Authentication mode of this interface.

values.name: hmac-sha-1
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-1 digest (AuType 2).

values.name: hmac-sha-256
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-256 digest (AuType 2).

values.name: hmac-sha-384
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-384 digest (AuType 2).

values.name: hmac-sha-512
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-512 digest (AuType 2).

values.name: inherit
values.short-help: Take the authentication key chain of the area.

values.name: md5
values.short-help: Keyed MD5 digest (AuType 2).

values.name: none
values.short-help: No authentication (AuType 0).

values.name: simple
values.short-help: Cleartext password (AuType 1).

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 states that the AuType MUST be the same
for all routers attached to the network. Ze takes the AuType from the algorithm of the
keys in the resolved chain.
children.name: authentication
children.short-help: Per-interface authentication settings.

children.description:
A BFD session that goes Down or AdminDown declares the OSPF
neighbor down at once. Without BFD, Ze waits for the router-dead interval, which is 40
seconds by default.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable single-hop BFD failure detection on this interface.

children.description:
The far system sends no faster than this value. RFC 5880
section 6.8.4 takes the agreed interval as the greater of this value and the Desired Min
TX Interval of the far system.
children.name: min-rx
children.short-help: Required minimum BFD receive interval (RFC 5880 Required Min RX Interval).

children.description:
RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 takes the agreed transmit interval
as the greater of this value and the Required Min RX Interval of the far system.
children.name: min-tx
children.short-help: Desired minimum BFD transmit interval (RFC 5880 Desired Min TX Interval).

children.description:
RFC 5880 section 6.8.4 states that Detect Mult is the
number of packets that have to be missed in a row to declare the session down. The
detection time is this value multiplied by the agreed transmit interval.
children.name: multiplier
children.short-help: BFD detection multiplier (RFC 5880 Detect Mult).

children.description:
RFC 5880 and RFC 5881 define single-hop BFD. When this
container enables it, a Full adjacency opens a single-hop BFD session. A failure that BFD
detects declares the neighbor down much faster than the router-dead interval does.
children.name: bfd
children.short-help: Single-hop BFD failure detection for this OSPF interface.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 requires an interface output cost of
more than 0. Ze advertises the value as the cost of this link in its Router-LSA. An absent
leaf takes cost 1, whatever the speed of the link is.
children.name: cost
children.short-help: Interface output cost.

children.description:
Ze declares the neighbor dead after this long with no Hello.
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose RouterDeadInterval does not match.
Appendix C.3 gives 4 times the hello-interval as the sample value.
children.name: dead-interval
children.short-help: Router-dead interval.

children.description:
A false value drops the interface from the OSPF instance. Ze
then sends no Hello on the link, and this router advertises no link for it.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: OSPF enabled on this interface.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Section 10.5 drops a received Hello whose
HelloInterval does not match the configured value, so every router on the link MUST hold
the same value. A smaller value detects a failure faster and sends more protocol
traffic.
children.name: hello-interval
children.short-help: Hello interval.

children.description:
RFC 6549 section 3 defines OSPFv2 Multi-Instance. An absent
leaf-list runs the base instance 0 only, which is bit-for-bit compatible with base
OSPFv2.

Each listed value runs a separate OSPFv2 instance, which Ze demultiplexes on this subnet.
Ze discards a received packet whose Instance ID matches none of the listed values
(RFC 6549 sections 2 and 3.1).
children.name: instance-id
children.short-help: Multi-Instance Instance IDs this interface takes part in.

children.description:
RFC 5443 section 1 states that a blackhole exists when one
link on the shortest path carries no LDP session. A false value leaves the cost of the
link unchanged while LDP converges. Traffic can then be lost on a link whose label
bindings do not exist yet.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable LDP-IGP synchronization on this interface.

children.description:
The wait starts when the LDP session is established.
RFC 5443 section 2 estimates that every label binding is exchanged by then, and it defines
no universal default. The value 0 restores the cost as soon as the session is up, which is
permitted and not advised.
children.name: holddown
children.short-help: Seconds Ze waits before it declares the link synchronized.

children.description:
RFC 5443 and RFC 6138 define LDP-IGP synchronization. Ze holds
a point-to-point link at maximum cost, and withholds the transit link of a broadcast link
that is not a cut edge, until LDP is synchronized. Transit traffic is then not
black-holed before the label bindings exist.
children.name: ldp-sync
children.short-help: LDP-IGP synchronization of this interface.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Section 10.6 rejects a Database Description packet
whose Interface MTU is larger than the receiving interface accepts without fragmentation.
A true value skips that check, so the adjacency reaches Full across an MTU mismatch.
children.name: mtu-ignore
children.short-help: Skip DD MTU mismatch rejection.

children.description:
The value 0 makes the neighbor ineligible, so Ze polls it
and never elects it.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Eligibility of this neighbor in the DR election and the BDR election.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.6 defines the neighbor list. The list is
required for network-type nbma and for the non-broadcast point-to-multipoint variant.
children.name: nbma-neighbor
children.short-help: A statically configured NBMA neighbor.

children.description:
broadcast and point-to-point are the two common types. nbma
elects a DR and a BDR over a configured neighbor list, with unicast Hellos and poll
Hellos (RFC 2328). point-to-multipoint treats the link as a set of point-to-point links,
with one host route for each neighbor and no DR.
children.name: network-type
children.short-help: Network type of this interface.

values.name: broadcast
values.short-help: Multi-access link that elects a DR and a BDR with multicast Hellos.

values.name: loopback
values.short-help: Send no Hellos and advertise the interface address as a host route.

values.name: nbma
values.short-help: Non-broadcast multi-access link that elects a DR over a configured neighbor list.

values.name: point-to-multipoint
values.short-help: Set of point-to-point links with no DR election.

values.name: point-to-point
values.short-help: Link with one neighbor and no DR election.

children.description:
Ze gives a passive interface no sender, so it sends no Hello
and forms no adjacency. The interface stays enrolled in its area, so this router keeps
advertising the link.
children.name: passive
children.short-help: Advertise the interface but form no adjacency.

children.description:
Ze sends a Hello at this slower rate to a configured neighbor
that stays silent (RFC 2328 Appendix C.5).
children.name: poll-interval
children.short-help: NBMA poll interval.

children.description: The value 0 makes the interface ineligible.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Priority of this interface in the DR election and the BDR election.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 names the value RxmtInterval, and it also
paces the retransmission of a Database Description packet and a Link State Request. Set it
well over the round-trip delay on the link, or needless retransmissions result.
children.name: retransmit-interval
children.short-help: LSA retransmit interval.

children.description:
RFC 3630 section 2.5.9 defines the Administrative Group,
which is also named Resource Class or Color. The mask is 32 bits wide, and the least
significant bit is group 0.
children.name: admin-group
children.short-help: Administrative Group mask of this link.

children.description:
Ze originates one Type 10 opaque LSA for each active TE
link, and that LSA carries one Link TLV (RFC 3630 section 2.4.2). Ze skips a link with no
usable Link Type and Link ID, for example a broadcast link with no DR yet.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Advertise a TE Link LSA for this interface.

children.description:
RFC 5392 section 3.3.1 makes the Remote AS Number
sub-TLV REQUIRED in a Link TLV that advertises an inter-AS TE link. The sub-TLV is type 21
and four octets wide, so it carries a 4-byte AS number.
children.name: remote-as
children.short-help: RFC 5392 sec 3.3.1 Remote AS Number of the neighboring AS the link connects to.

children.description:
RFC 5392 section 3.3.2 defines the value, which
travels in sub-TLV 22. The RFC recommends the remote TE Router ID.
children.name: remote-asbr-ipv4
children.short-help: IPv4 Remote ASBR ID of the inter-AS link.

children.description:
RFC 5392 section 3.3.3 defines the value, which
travels in sub-TLV 24 and not in sub-TLV 23. Use a stable global IPv6 address.
children.name: remote-asbr-ipv6
children.short-help: IPv6 Remote ASBR ID of the inter-AS link.

children.description:
RFC 5392 section 3.1.1 defines the policy. area is a
Type 10 LSA, held inside the area of the ASBR. as is a Type 11 LSA, flooded across the
AS.
children.name: scope
children.short-help: Flooding scope of the inter-AS TE LSA.

values.name: area
values.short-help: Type 10 LSA, held inside the area of the ASBR.

values.name: as
values.short-help: Type 11 LSA, flooded across the AS.

children.description:
RFC 5392 defines the inter-AS TE link. Ze forms no OSPF
adjacency on the link (RFC 5392 section 4), and the ASBR proxies the link into its own AS.
The container needs remote-as, and at least one remote-asbr address.
children.name: inter-as
children.short-help: Inter-AS Traffic Engineering link.

children.description:
RFC 3630 section 2.5.6 carries the value in IEEE floating
point form, in a four-octet sub-TLV of type 6. An unset max-reservable-bandwidth takes
this value (section 2.5.7).
children.name: max-bandwidth
children.short-help: RFC 3630 sec 2.5.6 Maximum Bandwidth (true link capacity) in bytes/second.

children.description:
RFC 3630 section 2.5.7 defines the value, in bytes per
second. An unset leaf takes max-bandwidth.
children.name: max-reservable-bandwidth
children.short-help: Maximum Reservable Bandwidth of this link.

children.description:
RFC 3630 section 2.5.5 defines the metric. It is
independent of the OSPF cost, and an unset leaf takes the cost.
children.name: te-metric
children.short-help: Traffic Engineering metric of this link.

children.description:
RFC 3630 and RFC 5392 define the attributes. Ze advertises
them in a Type 10 opaque TE LSA, and in a Type 10 or a Type 11 LSA for an inter-as link.
The container needs the top-level opaque leaf. The TE metric is independent of the
cost.
children.name: traffic-engineering
children.short-help: Traffic Engineering link attributes of this interface.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 defines InfTransDelay. Ze adds this value
to the age of every LSA in a Link State Update before it sends the packet on this link.
children.name: transmit-delay
children.short-help: Estimated LSA transmission delay (RFC 2328 InfTransDelay must be > 0).

children.description:
The list is keyed by the interface name. Ze enrolls an entry only
when its enabled leaf is true and the areas container declares its area.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Per-interface OSPF configuration.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 states that some of these parameters describe the
attached network, so they MUST be consistent across every router on that network. The
hello-interval, the dead-interval and the authentication are the three that stop an
adjacency when they differ.
children.name: interfaces
children.short-help: OSPF-enabled interfaces.

children.description:
RFC 7474 defines AuType 3, which carries an extended cryptographic
sequence number of 64 bits. The leaf applies to the HMAC-SHA algorithms.
children.name: extended-sequence
children.short-help: Use AuType 3 rather than AuType 2 for this key chain.

children.description:
The value is an RFC 3339 timestamp. RFC 5709 section 3.2
calls this bound Key Stop Accept, the time at which this router stops accepting a packet made
with this key. Keep it later than the `send-lifetime` end, because RFC 5709 section 3.2
states that 'KeyStopGenerate SHOULD be less than KeyStopAccept'. An absent leaf leaves the
window open with no end bound.
children.name: end
children.short-help: RFC3339 end timestamp.

children.description:
The value is an RFC 3339 timestamp, for example
2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. RFC 5709 section 3.2 calls this bound Key Start Accept, the time from
which this router accepts a packet made with this key. An absent leaf leaves the window open
with no start bound.
children.name: start
children.short-help: RFC3339 start timestamp.

children.description:
RFC 5709 section 3.2 names the two bounds Key Start Accept and
Key Stop Accept. RFC 7474 section 4 requires that, for packet reception, 'the key validity
interval as defined by AcceptLifetimeStart and AcceptLifetimeEnd must include the current
time'. Ze checks that both timestamps parse as RFC 3339 and refuses the configuration when
one does not. On receive Ze tries only the keys whose window covers the current time, so a
packet made with a key outside its window is dropped and counted under the accept-lifetime
reason. A key with no accept-lifetime is accepted at every time. When no key of the chain is
in its window, every packet on the interface is dropped. Use `send-lifetime` to control
which key signs.
children.name: accept-lifetime
children.short-help: When this key is accepted on receive.

children.description:
simple is AuType 1, which sends a cleartext password. The md5
value and the hmac-sha values are AuType 2, which sends a digest. The extended-sequence
leaf turns AuType 2 into AuType 3.
children.name: algorithm
children.short-help: Authentication algorithm.

values.name: hmac-sha-1
values.short-help: AuType 2, an HMAC-SHA-1 digest of 20 octets.

values.name: hmac-sha-256
values.short-help: AuType 2, an HMAC-SHA-256 digest of 32 octets.

values.name: hmac-sha-384
values.short-help: AuType 2, an HMAC-SHA-384 digest of 48 octets.

values.name: hmac-sha-512
values.short-help: AuType 2, an HMAC-SHA-512 digest of 64 octets.

values.name: md5
values.short-help: AuType 2, a keyed MD5 digest of 16 octets.

values.name: simple
values.short-help: AuType 1, a cleartext password.

children.description:
Ze masks the value in every output, and it stores the $9$ form
at rest. A simple-password secret is at most 8 octets, which RFC 2328 Appendix D sets as
the width of the authentication field.
children.name: secret
children.short-help: Shared secret, masked and $9$-encoded at rest.

children.description:
The value is an RFC 3339 timestamp. An absent leaf leaves
the window open with no end bound, so this key signs until a later key starts.
children.name: end
children.short-help: RFC3339 end timestamp.

children.description:
The value is an RFC 3339 timestamp, for example
2026-01-01T00:00:00Z. An absent leaf leaves the window open with no start bound.
children.name: start
children.short-help: RFC3339 start timestamp.

children.description:
Ze signs with the key whose window covers the current time.
When two windows cover it, the latest-starting key wins. When every window has expired, Ze
keeps the most-recently-starting key rather than sending an unauthenticated packet.
children.name: send-lifetime
children.short-help: Window in which Ze can use this key to sign a packet.

children.description:
The list is keyed by key-id. Ze picks the key that signs from the
send-lifetime windows, and it verifies a received packet against every key of the chain.
children.name: key
children.short-help: Keys in this chain.

children.description:
A chain rotates the signing key and the adjacency stays up. Ze refuses
a chain whose send-lifetime windows leave a gap, because the signing coverage would then
lapse.
children.name: key-chains
children.short-help: Named authentication key chains for hitless rotation.

children.description:
Ze sets every non-stub link of its Router-LSA to MaxLinkMetric,
which RFC 6987 section 3 defines as 0xffff. A stub link keeps its cost, so a directly
connected prefix of this router stays reachable.
children.name: always
children.short-help: Always advertise as a stub router.

children.description:
The unit is seconds, the range is 0 to 86400, and 0 is the
default. RFC 6987 defines the MaxLinkMetric advertisement and defines no shutdown timer for
it. Ze stores this value and reports it as `on-shutdown-seconds` in `show ospf`. Ze raises
the stub-router bit in the Router Information LSA of RFC 7770 when the value is more than 0.
Ze starts no timed window: only `always` makes Ze originate the Router-LSA with
MaxLinkMetric.
children.name: on-shutdown
children.short-help: Advertise as a stub router for N seconds during a graceful shutdown (0 disables).

children.description:
The unit is seconds, the range is 0 to 86400, and 0 is the
default. RFC 6987 defines the MaxLinkMetric advertisement and defines no startup timer for
it. Ze stores this value and reports it as `on-startup-seconds` in `show ospf`. Ze raises the
stub-router bit in the Router Information LSA of RFC 7770 when the value is more than 0. Ze
starts no timed window: only `always` makes Ze originate the Router-LSA with
MaxLinkMetric.
children.name: on-startup
children.short-help: Advertise as a stub router for N seconds after startup (0 disables).

children.description:
RFC 6987 section 2 has the stub router announce its Router-LSA with
the cost of all non-stub links set to MaxLinkMetric. Section 3 defines MaxLinkMetric as the
16-bit value 0xffff. A stub link keeps its cost, so a directly connected prefix of this
router stays reachable. The `always` leaf originates that Router-LSA. The `on-startup` and
`on-shutdown` leaves are stored and reported by `show ospf`, and they originate nothing. Any
of the three set to a value other than the default raises the stub-router bit in the Router
Information LSA of RFC 7770.
children.name: router-lsa
children.short-help: Stub-router control of the Router-LSA link costs.

children.description:
RFC 6987 defines the stub router. Ze originates the Router-LSA with
MaxLinkMetric, so transit traffic avoids this router.
children.name: max-metric
children.short-help: Stub-router advertisement of this router.

children.description:
SPF keeps at most this many equal-cost next-hops for one prefix, and it
drops the rest. Ze uses 8 when the leaf is absent.
children.name: maximum-paths
children.short-help: Maximum ECMP paths per prefix.

children.description:
RFC 5250 defines the opaque LSA. When this leaf is true, the router
sets the O-bit in its Database Description packets, which advertises that it will receive
and forward an opaque LSA, and it originates an opaque LSA for each registered consumer.

Ze stores a received opaque LSA and refloods it by its scope whatever this leaf holds. A
false leaf stops the capability advertisement and the origination only.
children.name: opaque
children.short-help: Enable the opaque-LSA capability.

children.description:
Ze writes the value into the metric field of the AS-external LSA,
which is 24 bits wide. A source with no entry in this list takes 20.
children.name: metric
children.short-help: Injected metric.

children.description:
RFC 2328 section 2.3 states that a Type 1 external metric is in the
same units as the OSPF cost. A Type 2 metric is an order of magnitude larger than any
internal path. A Type 1 route always wins over a Type 2 route.
children.name: metric-type
children.short-help: External metric type.

values.name: type-1
values.short-help: External metric in OSPF cost units, added to the internal distance.

values.name: type-2
values.short-help: External metric larger than any internal path, compared alone.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix A.4.5 states that the External Route Tag is not
used by the OSPF protocol itself. It carries information between AS boundary routers, and
a policy on another router CAN match it.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: External route tag.

children.description:
This list starts no import. The generic redistribute container enables
the import, with a rule of the shape destination ospf import <source>. A source with no
entry here takes metric 20 and metric-type type-2.
children.name: redistribute
children.short-help: Per-source metric, metric type and tag for redistribution into OSPF.

children.description:
The unit is Mbps, the range is 1 to 4294967, and the default is 100000.
Ze divides this bandwidth by the speed of a link to derive the cost of that link, so under
the default a 10 Gbit/s link costs 10 and a 1 Gbit/s link costs 100. An interface that sets
`interfaces/interface/cost` keeps that cost and is not derived. The quotient is clamped to
the range a Router-LSA link metric carries, 1 to 65535, because RFC 2328 Appendix C.3 states
that the interface output cost 'must always be greater than 0' and the wire field is two
octets wide. A link whose speed the kernel does not report costs 1, which covers a loopback,
a dummy, a tunnel and a link with no carrier; a veth reports 10000 and is derived like a real
NIC. The speed is read again on each origination pass, so a link that renegotiates re-prices
itself. The value is router-wide: every OSPFv3 address family prices a link exactly as the
IPv4 family does. A change to this leaf drops no adjacency: Ze re-prices each interface in
place and originates the new Router-LSA at the commit.
children.name: reference-bandwidth
children.short-help: Auto-cost reference bandwidth in Mbps.

children.description:
RFC 3630 section 2.4.1 defines the Router Address. The value is a
stable IPv4 address that is always reachable, usually a loopback, and the router
advertises it once in its Router-Address TE LSA. An unset leaf takes the Router ID. The
leaf needs opaque, and at least one traffic-engineering interface, to take effect.
children.name: router-address
children.short-help: Traffic Engineering Router Address of this router.

children.description:
Ze derives the Router ID when this leaf is absent. It reads the
highest loopback IPv4 address first, then the highest interface IPv4 address.
children.name: router-id
children.short-help: OSPF Router ID of this instance, in dotted-quad form.

children.description:
The LSA advertises the informational capabilities of this router.
OSPFv2 also needs opaque true, because the RI LSA is an opaque LSA.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Originate the Router Information LSA.

children.description:
RFC 7770 section 2.7 defines the scopes. An enabled RI LSA with no
scope listed takes area and as.
children.name: scope
children.short-help: Flooding scopes at which Ze advertises the RI LSA.

values.name: area
values.short-help: Area (OSPFv2 opaque type 10, OSPFv3 0xA00C).

values.name: as
values.short-help: AS-wide (OSPFv2 opaque type 11, OSPFv3 0xC00C).

values.name: link
values.short-help: Link-local (OSPFv2 opaque type 9).

children.description:
RFC 7770 defines the Router Information LSA, which advertises the
optional capabilities of this router. It is opaque type 4 in OSPFv2 and function code 12
in OSPFv3. The container applies to both address families. A top-level container drives
the OSPFv3 family unless that family configures its own.
children.name: router-information
children.short-help: Router Information LSA of this router.

children.description:
When this leaf is true, the RI LSA advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the
configured SRGB and the configured SRLB.
children.name: enable
children.short-help: Enable Segment Routing for this address family.

children.description:
The upstream neighbor then uses the Explicit NULL label, which
is 0 for IPv4 and 2 for IPv6. This leaf needs no-php.
children.name: explicit-null
children.short-help: Set the E-Flag on the Prefix-SID.

children.description:
The MPLS label is the SRGB base plus this index. The index
MUST be less than the total size of the SRGB.
children.name: index
children.short-help: SID index into the SRGB.

children.description:
The penultimate hop then keeps the label rather than popping
it, so no penultimate-hop-popping happens.
children.name: no-php
children.short-help: Set the NP-Flag on the Prefix-SID.

children.description:
RFC 7684 section 2.1 sets the N-Flag when the prefix identifies
the advertising router, which is usually a loopback host address. A receiver MUST ignore
the flag when the prefix length is not a host prefix.
children.name: node-sid
children.short-help: Mark this as a node Prefix-SID (sets the N-Flag on the Extended Prefix TLV).

children.description:
The local prefix is usually the loopback. Each Prefix-SID carries
a SID index into the SRGB of this node (RFC 8665 section 5).
children.name: prefix-sid
children.short-help: Prefix-SIDs Ze advertises for the local prefixes.

children.description:
Ze reads the SRGB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are
both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of
the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
children.name: lower-bound
children.short-help: First MPLS label of the SRGB (inclusive).

children.description: The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
children.name: upper-bound
children.short-help: Last MPLS label of the SRGB, inclusive.

children.description:
The SRGB is the contiguous global MPLS label range this node owns,
which a Prefix-SID index maps into (RFC 8665 section 3.2). The SRGB MUST NOT overlap the
SRLB, the LDP label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
children.name: srgb
children.short-help: Segment Routing Global Block of this node.

children.description:
Ze reads the SRLB only when lower-bound and upper-bound are
both set, and it drops the range when upper-bound is less than lower-bound. The size of
the block is upper-bound minus lower-bound plus one.
children.name: lower-bound
children.short-help: First MPLS label of the SRLB (inclusive).

children.description: The value MUST be equal to or more than lower-bound.
children.name: upper-bound
children.short-help: Last MPLS label of the SRLB, inclusive.

children.description:
The SRLB is the local MPLS label range that Ze allocates an
Adjacency-SID from (RFC 8665 section 3.3). The SRLB MUST NOT overlap the SRGB, the LDP
label space, or the RSVP-TE label space.
children.name: srlb
children.short-help: Segment Routing Local Block of this node.

children.description:
Ze advertises the value in the SRMS-Preference TLV (RFC 8665
section 3.4). An unset leaf advertises no TLV.
children.name: srms-preference
children.short-help: SR Mapping-Server preference of this node.

children.description:
RFC 8665 defines Segment Routing for OSPFv2, and RFC 8666 for OSPFv3.
Ze advertises SR-Algorithm 0, the SRGB label range, the SRLB label range, and one
Prefix-SID for each configured prefix. Ze installs label-switched forwarding through the
shared mpls-fib. Segment Routing is off by default.
children.name: segment-routing
children.short-help: Segment Routing over the MPLS dataplane.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix B names the value MinLSArrival and sets it to 1
second. Ze discards a new instance of one LSA that arrives sooner than this after the last
accepted instance.
children.name: min-ls-arrival-ms
children.short-help: Minimum arrival interval for accepting a new LSA instance.

children.description:
RFC 2328 Appendix B names the value MinLSInterval and sets it to 5
seconds. It is the minimum time between two distinct originations of one LSA.
children.name: min-ls-interval-ms
children.short-help: Minimum interval between LSA reoriginations.

children.description:
Ze waits this long after the first change before it runs SPF. The
delay returns to this value when no change arrived for spf-max-hold-ms.
children.name: spf-delay-ms
children.short-help: Initial SPF delay.

children.description:
A second change inside the backoff window raises the delay to this
floor. Each further change doubles the delay, up to spf-max-hold-ms.
children.name: spf-hold-ms
children.short-help: SPF hold floor.

children.description:
The doubling stops at this value. A gap longer than this value
between two changes resets the delay to spf-delay-ms.
children.name: spf-max-hold-ms
children.short-help: SPF max hold.

children.description:
Ze holds the SPF run back after a topology change, so one burst of LSAs
costs one run. The three spf leaves shape that backoff. The two ls leaves bound how often
one LSA is originated and accepted.
children.name: timers
children.short-help: SPF and LSA throttle timers.

ospf.description:
The presence of this container starts the OSPFv2 engine, which RFC 2328
defines. The address-family container adds the OSPFv3 families of RFC 5340, and each one
runs as a separate engine instance.
ospf.name: ospf

children.description:
The trust anchor itself, with no private key. Paste the PEM as it is printed, headers and
line breaks included, which is what 'ze show pki local-ca pem' gives you and what a .crt file
holds. Base64-encoded DER with no headers is also read, for a config written before PEM was
accepted.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: X.509 CA certificate, as a PEM document or as base64-encoded DER.

children.description:
Certificate revocation lists this CA issued, each an 'X509 CRL' PEM document or
base64-encoded DER. EAP-TLS on TLS 1.3 checks the revocation status of every certificate on a
peer's chain except the trust anchor. RFC 9190 Section 5.4 makes that check mandatory. An
EAP-TLS peer that validates against this CA and finds no current list here is refused. Publish
a fresh list before the nextUpdate of the one here passes: an expired list answers nothing
about the present and refuses the same peers. A list that revokes nothing is a valid answer
and is what a CA publishes while it has withdrawn no certificate.
children.name: crl
children.short-help: Certificate revocation lists this CA issued, each a PEM document or base64-encoded DER.

children.description:
Trusted CA certificate. The certificate leaf takes a PEM document, headers and line breaks
included, which is what 'ze show pki local-ca pem' prints and what a .crt file holds. Base64-encoded
DER with no PEM headers is also read.
children.name: ca
children.short-help: Trusted CA certificate.

children.description:
The certificate this node presents. Paste the PEM as it is printed, headers and line
breaks included, which is what a .crt file holds. Base64-encoded DER with no headers is also
read, for a config written before PEM was accepted. The matching key goes in private key.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: X.509 device certificate, as a PEM document or as base64-encoded DER.

children.description:
Intermediate CA certificates, each a PEM document or base64-encoded DER. Give them in order, from the one that issued this
certificate toward the trust anchor. Ze stores them beside the device certificate for chain
building, and sends them after it in the IKE_AUTH chain. RFC 7296 Section 3.6 requires an
implementation be capable of being configured to send up to four X.509 certificates. This device
certificate plus three intermediates is that maximum. A single value is still valid.
children.name: intermediate
children.short-help: Intermediate CA certificates, from the issuer toward the trust anchor.

children.description:
An OCSP response the certificate's issuer signed about this certificate, as base64-encoded
DER or as an 'OCSP RESPONSE' PEM document. Ze sends it in the certificate message when a peer
asks for a Certificate Status Request, which RFC 9190 Section 5.4 makes mandatory for an EAP-TLS
server on TLS 1.3. Fetch it from the responder your CA publishes, with 'openssl ocsp -respout'.
Ze refuses a response about another certificate. A response carries a nextUpdate: a peer that
checks the status refuses this certificate once that time passes, so replace the value before
it does. An entry with no response answers a Certificate Status Request with no status, which
RFC 6066 Section 8 permits, and the peer then checks revocation against the crl of the ca that
issued this certificate.
children.name: ocsp-response
children.short-help: OCSP response about this certificate, stapled to a peer that asks for it.

children.description:
Private key, as a PEM document or as base64-encoded DER. The config file stores it as $9$, and Ze
decodes it on load. The supported encodings are PKCS8, SEC1 (ECDSA), and PKCS1 (RSA).
children.name: key
children.short-help: Private key, as a PEM document or as base64-encoded DER.

children.description:
The container holds one leaf, key, and the container is optional. An entry with no private
key holds a certificate Ze sends and verifies against, and cannot sign with. Ze checks when it
loads the config that the key matches the public key of the certificate beside it. Ze refuses
the config when it does not, so a mismatched pair never reaches a handshake. The key leaf is
marked sensitive. The config file stores it as $9$, Ze decodes it on load, and a display path
prints a placeholder in its place.
children.name: private
children.short-help: Private key associated with this certificate.

children.description:
One entry holds the certificate this device presents, the intermediate certificates that lead
toward its trust anchor, and the private key that signs with it. The certificate leaf is mandatory
and the private container is not, so an entry can hold a certificate Ze sends and cannot sign with.
A TLS listener that asks for the key of such an entry is refused, and is never served another
certificate in its place. Ze validates every entry when it loads the config. An expired certificate
refuses the commit and stops the daemon from starting. A certificate that builds no chain to a ca
entry in this block does the same.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help:
Device certificate with optional private key and
intermediate certificates.

pki.description:
PKI certificate and key store. Presence of this block enables certificate-based authentication for
IPsec VPN, TLS, and other subsystems.
pki.name: pki

children.description:
Chooses how the engine encodes the events it sends this plugin: 'json' for JSON objects,
'text' for the line format ExaBGP plugins read. 'text' also makes the engine forward every
received BGP UPDATE to the plugin. A peer's 'attach process' binding can set an encoding of its
own, and that value wins over this one. With no value here and none on the binding, the engine
uses 'text'.
children.name: encoder
children.short-help: Event encoding format

values.name: json
values.short-help: JSON encoding

values.name: text
values.short-help: Human-readable text encoding

children.description:
States what you expect ze to do when this plugin's process exits. The plugin itself declares
whether it may be started again, and this leaf is a request inside that declaration. With no leaf
here the plugin's own declaration decides. With 'false' the plugin is left stopped even when it
would have been started again. With 'true' against a plugin that declares it must not be
restarted, ze refuses to start, and the error names the plugin and the policy it declared: ze
honors neither side in silence. The spelling comes from ExaBGP, whose process block carries the
same leaf. A restart is bounded at 5 in 60 seconds and 20 in the life of the daemon, after which
the plugin is disabled and 'show health' reports plugin-down.
children.name: respawn
children.short-help: Respawn on exit

children.description:
The command line that starts the plugin. The engine runs it with '/bin/sh -c', so arguments,
quoting and a PATH lookup work as they do in a shell. The directory of the running ze binary is
added to PATH as a fallback, so 'ze plugin <name>' finds the binary in a development tree. The
child reads ZE_PLUGIN_HUB_HOST, ZE_PLUGIN_HUB_PORT, ZE_PLUGIN_HUB_TOKEN, ZE_PLUGIN_CA_PEM and
ZE_PLUGIN_NAME from its environment, and connects back over TLS. A value of the form 'ze.<plugin>'
names a built-in plugin, which the engine then runs in this process rather than as a fork. run and
use are mutually exclusive, and a block that sets both is refused.
children.name: run
children.short-help: Command to execute plugin as external process (with args)

children.description:
Bounds a stall in the plugin startup handshake, and does not bound the handshake itself. The
handshake runs in stages across every plugin that starts together. The timer expires only when no
plugin of that group completes a stage for this long. Write a duration with a unit, such as 10s or
1m: a value with no unit is refused, and so is a negative value. With no value the engine uses the
ze.plugin.stage.timeout environment variable, which defaults to 5s. Raise it for a plugin that
needs longer to reach its first stage.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: Startup timeout (e.g., 10s, 1m)

children.description:
Names a built-in plugin to run in this process instead of a command. The block then behaves
like an internal block: no fork, no TLS connect-back, and an in-memory pipe between the engine and
the plugin. run and use are mutually exclusive, and a block that sets both is refused. The use
leaf of an internal block is checked against the registered plugin names, and this one is not. An
unknown name here fails at startup with 'unknown internal plugin'.
children.name: use
children.short-help: Name of a built-in plugin to run in-process (mutually exclusive with run)

children.description:
Runs a plugin as a separate process. The engine starts the run command with '/bin/sh -c'. The
child connects back to the hub listener over TLS. It reads the address, the certificate authority root
and its token from its environment. A block that sets use instead of run runs a built-in plugin in
this process, with no fork. The block name is the name a peer's 'attach process' binding refers to,
and the name the hub binds the connect-back token to.
children.name: external
children.short-help: External plugin process

children.description:
Name of a pki ca entry holding the certificate authority root of the hub this client connects to.
The client validates the hub certificate chain against that root and refuses any other chain, so it
sends no token to a hub it did not authenticate. Export the root from the hub and paste it into a
pki ca block on this client. A leaf the hub reissues still validates, because the root is the anchor
and not the certificate.
children.name: ca
children.short-help: Name of the pki ca entry holding the hub certificate authority root.

children.description:
The address of the remote hub, as an IP address or a hostname. It joins the port leaf
into the dial address, and it also sets the TLS server name the client verifies. The value
MUST therefore appear in the hub certificate. A certificate that names a different host is
refused, and the client sends its secret to no such hub.
children.name: host
children.short-help: Remote hub address

children.description:
The TCP port of the remote hub. It MUST equal the port of the hub server block that
carries this client's entry. There is no default: a block with no port dials port 0, and no
hub listens there.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Remote hub port

children.description:
The token this daemon sends to the hub at authentication. It holds at least 32 characters
and the config is refused below that length. It MUST equal the secret of the matching client
entry in the hub's server block, so rotate both sides in one change. The CLI masks the value
on display, and the committed config file holds it in the clear.
children.name: secret
children.short-help: Auth token (min 32 chars)

children.description:
Binds the outbound hub connection to this local IP address. Set it when the route to the
hub leaves an interface whose address the hub does not expect. One example is a hub that
accepts one management address only. The address MUST exist on this host, because the
connection fails when the kernel cannot bind it. With no value the kernel picks the source
address of the outgoing route. 'ze doctor' probes the hub through the same source address, so
its verdict matches what the daemon does.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IP address for outbound hub connections.

children.description:
Each block is an outbound connection to the hub that holds this daemon's config. The daemon
dials the first block only, and never dials a second block. The client validates the hub
certificate, sends its name and secret, then fetches its config and commits it. A heartbeat every
30 seconds holds the connection open. It reconnects with a delay that grows from 1 second to 60
seconds, and it stops when this instance is no longer marked as managed. The daemon dials nothing
here unless it runs as a managed instance with blob-backed config storage.
children.name: client
children.short-help: Outbound hub connections (managed client mode)

children.description:
Name of a pki certificate the managed-client listener on this block serves. An empty name serves a
certificate this daemon's own certificate authority issues, and reissues as it ages. Export that
authority root with 'show pki local-ca pem' and name it in each client's pki ca block, so a client
validates the chain rather than one certificate.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: Name of the pki certificate the managed-client listener on this block serves.

children.description:
The token this named client presents at authentication. It holds at least 32
characters, and the config is refused below that length with the client name in the error.
An entry with no secret is refused as well. Write the same value in the secret leaf of the
client block on the remote daemon. This per-client token is checked before the block
secret. The CLI masks the value on display, and the committed config file holds it in the
clear.
children.name: secret
children.short-help: Per-client auth token (min 32 chars)

children.description:
Each entry names a managed client this hub accepts, and the token that client presents.
One entry turns the block into a managed config listener. That listener answers a config
fetch. It pushes a change notice when the client's stored config is written. The config it
serves is the stored file 'client-<name>.conf', so the entry name is what routes a config to a
client. Every server block that carries client entries serves one certificate, and a config
that names two different ones is refused.
children.name: client
