children.short-help: Accepted remote managed clients

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:
The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a
free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
The token this listener accepts from a connection whose name matches no plugin this
daemon started and no client entry in this block. A plugin the daemon starts receives a random
per-name token in its environment instead, so no operator copies this value into a plugin. It
holds at least 32 characters and the config is refused below that length. With no server block
the daemon generates a random secret at each start, which no process outside it can know. The
CLI masks the value on display, and the committed config file holds it in the clear.
children.name: secret
children.short-help: Auth token for plugin connections (min 32 chars)

children.description:
Each block is one TLS listener. The plugin acceptor binds the first block in configuration
order and no other, so a second block exists for the managed clients it names. Every block that
carries client entries also starts the managed config server, which needs blob-backed config
storage. Give such a block a port of its own. A block whose address the plugin acceptor already
binds fails to listen, and 'ze doctor' reports that collision. Set ip and port to the listen
address, and secret to the token a connection presents.
children.name: server
children.short-help: Named hub server instances (TLS listeners)

children.description:
Sets the TLS listener that plugin processes connect back to, and the outbound connection this
daemon makes to a remote hub for its config. With no server block the daemon opens one on 127.0.0.1,
with a kernel-chosen port and a random secret. Each plugin process reads that address and a per-plugin
token from its environment. Declare a server block when a process the daemon did not start must
connect, such as the plugin CLI or a remote managed client. Declare a client block when this daemon
takes its config from a remote hub.
children.name: hub
children.short-help: Plugin transport and auth configuration

children.description:
Names the built-in plugin this block runs. The value MUST be a plugin registered in this
binary. A value that is not registered is refused, and the error prints the registered names.
Command completion offers that same list. The leaf is required, and a block with no use is refused
with 'internal plugin requires use'.
children.name: use
children.short-help: Name of a built-in plugin to run in-process

children.description:
Runs a plugin that ships inside the ze binary as a goroutine of this process. There is no fork,
no TLS connect-back and no shell command: the engine and the plugin exchange messages over an
in-memory pipe. Each block needs a use leaf naming the built-in plugin, and a block that also sets run
is refused. Declare a block here to bind a built-in plugin to a peer with 'attach process', or to run
one under a name of your own. A plugin that claims a configured address family loads without a block.
children.name: internal
children.short-help: Built-in plugin running in-process

plugin.description:
Declares the plugins this daemon runs, and the hub transport they connect back over. A built-in
plugin that claims a configured address family starts with no block here, because the engine loads it for
that family. Declare an internal block to run a built-in plugin under a name you choose. Declare an
external block to run a program of your own. Declare a hub block to set the TLS listener and its secrets.
The name of an internal or external block is the name a peer's 'attach process' binding refers to.
plugin.name: plugin

children.description:
Name one interface, or several. The entries are an OR: Ze
installs one nftables rule for each entry, and a packet that
arrives on any one of them matches. A trailing * matches by
prefix, so the entry l2tp* matches l2tp0 and l2tp1. Each
entry keeps its own wildcard state, so one list holds eth0
and l2tp* together. With no interface named, the policy
matches every ingress interface.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Ingress interfaces to match, where a trailing '*' matches by prefix.

children.description:
A value that starts with @ names a firewall set, and
Ze matches the destination address of the packet
against the elements of that set. Any other value
MUST carry a prefix length, because Ze parses it as
a prefix. 10.0.0.1 is refused at commit, and
10.0.0.1/32 matches one host.
children.name: destination-address
children.short-help: Destination IP prefix or @set reference.

children.description:
The syntax is the syntax of source-port: one port, a
range written with a hyphen, or a comma-separated
list of both, at most 128 entries. Ze reads the
destination port at offset 2 of the transport
header, so write the protocol leaf beside it.
children.name: destination-port
children.short-help: Destination port or port range.

children.description:
The value set is the one every firewall backend can
lower, so a spelling outside it is refused at commit
rather than at the next firewall reconcile.
children.name: protocol
children.short-help: L4 protocol to match.

values.name: ah
values.short-help: Match IPsec AH, IP protocol 51.

values.name: esp
values.short-help: Match IPsec ESP, IP protocol 50.

values.name: gre
values.short-help: Match GRE, IP protocol 47.

values.name: icmp
values.short-help: Match ICMP, IP protocol 1.

values.name: icmpv6
values.short-help: Match ICMPv6, IP protocol 58.

values.name: ospf
values.short-help: Match OSPF, IP protocol 89.

values.name: sctp
values.short-help: Match SCTP, IP protocol 132.

values.name: tcp
values.short-help: Match TCP, IP protocol 6.

values.name: udp
values.short-help: Match UDP, IP protocol 17.

values.name: vrrp
values.short-help: Match VRRP, IP protocol 112.

children.description:
A value that starts with @ names a firewall set, and
Ze matches the source address of the packet against
the elements of that set. Any other value MUST carry
a prefix length, because Ze parses it as a prefix.
10.0.0.1 is refused at commit, and 10.0.0.1/32
matches one host.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IP prefix or @set reference.

children.description:
Ze accepts one port, a range written with a hyphen,
or a comma-separated list of both, and it holds at
most 128 entries. Two entries that overlap or touch
are refused at commit, and so is port 0. Ze compiles
more than one entry into an anonymous nftables
interval set.
children.name: source-port
children.short-help: Source port or port range (e.g. '80,443').

children.description:
Every flag you list MUST be set in the packet. Ze
builds the nftables mask from the same list, so a
flag you do not list is not read and its value does
not matter. Write syn,ack to match a packet that
carries both. A name outside the six is refused at
commit, and an empty list is refused too.
children.name: tcp-flags
children.short-help:
Comma-separated TCP flags to match
(fin, syn, rst, psh, ack, urg).

children.description:
Ze puts every leaf of this block into one nftables rule,
so a packet MUST match all of them. An empty from block
matches every packet on the interfaces of the policy.
Write the protocol leaf beside a port leaf. Ze reads a
port from the transport header at a fixed offset and
adds no protocol guard. A port leaf alone also reads
those two bytes of another L4 header.
children.name: from
children.short-help: Packet match criteria.

children.description:
Evaluation order (lower values first). Rules with
equal order are sorted by name. If omitted,
defaults to 0.
children.name: order
children.short-help: Evaluation order of this rule, lower values first.

children.description:
Ze emits the nftables accept verdict and sets no
fwmark, so the packet keeps the routing decision of
the main table. The verdict ends the ze_pr chain, so
no later rule of any policy reads that packet. Put
an accept rule in front of a table rule to carve an
exception out of it.
children.name: accept
children.short-help: Skip this policy (packet routes normally).

children.description:
Ze emits the nftables drop verdict in the ze_pr
chain, which runs at the prerouting hook with
priority -150. The kernel discards the packet before
it makes a routing decision, and it sends the source
no ICMP answer.
children.name: drop
children.short-help: Drop matching packets.

children.description:
Ze allocates a kernel routing table from range
2000-2999 for this next-hop. Ze then manages the
default route, the fwmark, and the ip rule in that
table internally.
children.name: next-hop
children.short-help: Redirect matching packets to this next-hop.

children.description:
Ze routes each matching packet through the kernel
routing table with this number. Range 1000-2999 is
reserved for ze internal use, which covers the VRF
tables and the policy-routing tables Ze allocates.
children.name: table
children.short-help: Route matching packets through this kernel routing table.

children.description:
Ze writes this value into the TCP MSS option, kind
2, of every matching packet, and it does not read
the value already there. A packet that carries no
MSS option is not changed. The range is 1 to 65535,
and 0 is refused at commit. This action is not
terminal, so it combines with accept, drop, table,
or next-hop in the same rule.
children.name: tcp-mss
children.short-help: Rewrite the TCP MSS option to this value in bytes.

children.description:
The block carries one terminal action: accept, drop,
table, or next-hop. Two terminal actions in one rule are
refused at commit, and the error names both. tcp-mss is
not terminal, so it combines with one of the four. A
then block with no terminal action sets no fwmark, so
the packet keeps the main table.
children.name: then
children.short-help: Action for matching packets.

children.description:
Ze sorts the rules by the order leaf, lowest first, and it
breaks a tie by name. The position of a rule in the config
file does not decide its position in the chain. A rule with
no order leaf takes 0 and runs first. Each rule becomes one
nftables term for each interface the policy names, and one
term when it names none. The terms of one rule stay
together, so the order leaf still decides which rule the
kernel reads first.
children.name: rule
children.short-help: Ordered list of match/action rules.

children.description:
Ze applies the rules of this policy to packets that arrive on
the listed interfaces. A policy that lists no interface matches
on any ingress interface. Each rule that selects a table or a
next-hop gets its own fwmark from range 0x50000 to 0x5FFFF. An
ip rule then maps that mark to the table.
children.name: route
children.short-help: A named policy route applied to ingress interfaces.

policy.description:
Ze merges every policy into one nftables table named ze_pr. The
chain of that table attaches to the prerouting hook at priority
-150. A rule marks the packet, and an ip rule then selects the
kernel routing table for that mark. A packet that matches no rule
keeps the routing decision of the main table.
policy.name: policy

children.description:
The default is ze. Ze writes the value into the AC-Name tag, 0x0102, of
each discovery reply it builds. A client that hears several
concentrators reads this name to pick one.
children.name: ac-name
children.short-help: Access Concentrator Name advertised in PADO (RFC 2516 Section 5.2).

children.description:
The default is false. A client that rejects the configured
method is then disconnected, and it is never admitted
unauthenticated.
children.name: allow-no-auth
children.short-help: Accept a subscriber whose LCP negotiation ends with no Auth-Protocol option.

children.description:
The access concentrator advertises the method in its LCP
Configure-Request (RFC 1661 Section 6.2), for every subscriber
that completes PPPoE discovery. The auth handler verifies the
credential (l2tp-auth-local or l2tp-auth-radius). The default
requires CHAP-MD5 (RFC 1994). Set it to none only together
with allow-no-auth true.
children.name: auth-method
children.short-help: PPP Auth-Protocol method the access concentrator advertises in LCP.

values.name: chap-md5
values.short-help: Advertise CHAP with the MD5 algorithm (RFC 1994), the default.

values.name: ms-chap-v2
values.short-help: Advertise MS-CHAP-V2 (RFC 2759).

values.name: none
values.short-help: Advertise no Auth-Protocol, so the session opens with no PPP authentication phase.

values.name: pap
values.short-help: Advertise PAP (RFC 1334), which carries the password in clear text.

children.description:
The default is 5 seconds and the range is 1 to 300. The cookie is 20
bytes: 16 bytes of a truncated HMAC-SHA256 over the two MAC addresses,
and 4 bytes of Unix timestamp. Each interface holds its own random key,
so a cookie of one interface never verifies on another.
children.name: cookie-timeout
children.short-help:
AC-Cookie validity duration in seconds. Cookies older
than this are rejected in PADR validation.

children.description:
The default is true when the pppoe block is present.
Set it to false to disable the subsystem.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the PPPoE subsystem.

children.description:
Ze takes the global max-sessions when this leaf is absent or 0. The
session identifiers come from a bitmap over the 16-bit space, and
identifier 0 is reserved. A PADR that arrives at the limit gets no
session, and Ze reports that the maximum is reached.
children.name: max-sessions
children.short-help:
Per-interface session limit. Defaults to the global
max-sessions when unset.

children.description:
Ze takes the global max-sessions-per-mac when this leaf is absent
or 0. A PADR from a MAC already at the cap gets a PADS carrying an
error tag and session ID 0x0000 instead of a new session.
children.name: max-sessions-per-mac
children.short-help:
Per-interface override for max-sessions-per-mac.
Defaults to the global value when unset.

children.description:
Ze answers a PADI whose Service-Name tag holds a value of this
list, and it answers a PADI whose tag is empty. A PADI naming any
other service gets no PADO. An empty list here takes the global
list, and an empty global list accepts every Service-Name.
children.name: service-name
children.short-help:
Per-interface Service-Name filter. Overrides the
global service-name list when set.

children.description: Each interface has an independent session ID space.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Access interfaces on which PPPoE discovery listens.

children.description:
The 16-bit session ID range limits the count to 1 through
65535.
children.name: max-sessions
children.short-help: Maximum concurrent PPPoE sessions per interface.

children.description:
The default is 8 and the range is 1 to 65535. RFC 2516
places no limit on concurrent sessions from one peer MAC,
so this bounds replay rather than a legitimate
multi-session client: a PADR from a MAC already at the
cap gets a PADS carrying an error tag and session ID
0x0000 instead of a new session. The per-interface
max-sessions-per-mac overrides this value.
children.name: max-sessions-per-mac
children.short-help:
Maximum concurrent sessions one subscriber MAC
address may hold.

children.description:
The default is 100 and the range is 1 to 10000. Ze counts the PADI
packets of one interface inside a one-second window and discards
every packet over the count. Ze also discards a second PADI from one
source MAC address inside the same second. The range starts at 1, so
no configuration turns the limiter off.
children.name: padi-rate-limit
children.short-help: Maximum PADI packets accepted per second on one interface.

children.description:
An empty list accepts any Service-Name. The per-interface
service-name list overrides this global list.
children.name: service-name
children.short-help: Accepted Service-Name values (RFC 2516 Section 5.1).

pppoe.description:
This block with any content in it enables the subsystem.
Use 'enabled false' to disable it explicitly. Use
'enabled true' as a filler when no other settings are
needed.
pppoe.name: pppoe

children.description: An empty leaf-list imports every family.
children.name: family
children.short-help: Address families Ze imports from this source.

children.description:
The route tag is the value the source protocol attached to the route, for
example the tag leaf of a static route. A rule that names a tag imports the routes carrying exactly that
value and rejects the others. A rule with no tag leaf imports every route from the source, whatever tag
it carries. The value 0 is a tag like any other: a route with no tag carries 0, so tag 0 imports the
untagged routes alone.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: Import only the routes that carry this route tag.

children.description: If the family leaf-list is empty, Ze imports every family.
children.name: import
children.short-help: Import routes from a source into this destination.

children.description:
Each entry names a consumer that registered itself, for example bgp
or ospf.
children.name: destination
children.short-help: Destination protocol for redistributed routes.

redistribute.description:
Each destination protocol has its own container that holds the import
rules. To add a destination protocol, add a key here.
redistribute.name: redistribute

children.description:
A connected route is the prefix an interface address
covers. The default 0 is the best distance a route can
hold, so a connected route wins the prefix against every
protocol that carries a higher value. This is the only
distance leaf whose range starts at 0. The other five
start at 1. Raise it above another protocol's distance to let
that protocol win the same prefix. The value applies
whether or not you write the rib block, because sysrib
resolves every protocol from these schema defaults when it
starts.
children.name: connected
children.short-help: Directly connected networks.

children.description:
An eBGP route comes from a peer in another autonomous
system. The default 20 ranks eBGP above every IGP declared
here and below a static route. The range is 1 to 255. The
BGP RIB plugin stamps this value on each path it inserts.
The Loc-RIB ranks the paths on what it stamped, so the
value decides selection before sysrib sees the route. The
seam that carries it is process-global: a BGP RIB running
in a forked plugin process keeps its own bootstrap 20 and
nothing reports that.
children.name: ebgp
children.short-help: External BGP routes.

children.description:
An iBGP route comes from a peer in the same autonomous
system. The default 200 is the highest of the six declared
here, so an iBGP route loses the prefix to any other
protocol that holds it. The range is 1 to 255. The BGP RIB
plugin stamps this value on each path it inserts, and its
bootstrap 200 applies until sysrib publishes the
declaration. The eBGP distance is a separate leaf, so the
two BGP classes rank apart.
children.name: ibgp
children.short-help: Internal BGP routes.

children.description:
The default 115 ranks IS-IS below OSPF and above iBGP. The
range is 1 to 255. The IS-IS SPF installer stamps this
value on each path it puts in the Loc-RIB, and its
bootstrap 115 applies until sysrib publishes the
declaration. One value covers level 1 and level 2: Ze
declares no separate distance for each level.
children.name: isis
children.short-help: IS-IS routes.

children.description:
The default 110 ranks OSPF below eBGP and above IS-IS. The
range is 1 to 255. The OSPF SPF installer stamps this value
on each path it puts in the Loc-RIB, and its bootstrap 110
applies until sysrib publishes the declaration. One value
covers every OSPF route: Ze declares no separate distance
for an external LSA.
children.name: ospf
children.short-help: OSPF routes.

children.description:
A static route is one the operator wrote under the static
configuration. The default 10 ranks a static route above
every dynamic protocol declared here and below a connected
route. The range is 1 to 255. sysrib applies the value to
each route that arrives under the protocol name static.
Raise it to more than 20 to let an eBGP route win the
same prefix.
children.name: static
children.short-help: Static routes.

children.description:
Administrative distance ranks one protocol against another for the same prefix, and the lower
value wins. It is NOT an IGP metric and NOT the IGP distance to a next hop: those measure a path,
this ranks the protocol that offered it. RFC 4271 mandates no values; these follow the Cisco and
Juniper convention. This container is the only place any protocol's distance is declared, and every
protocol takes its value from here whether or not you write the block.
children.name: distance
children.short-help: Administrative distance per protocol.

children.description:
This list names the protocols Ze does not program. Selection is
unchanged: the system RIB ranks the candidates for each prefix
on administrative distance and picks one winner. A winner from
a protocol named here stays in the RIB, `show rib` reports it,
redistribution can offer it to another protocol, and the
protocol's own event stream still carries it. Ze declines the
write to the kernel, to VPP or to a P4 switch. It holds the
prefix off `system-rib/best-change`, the stream every FIB
writer reads, so the list applies to every FIB. Ze also
releases the next-hop tracking for the prefix, so
`show nexthop-table` stops listing it under its next-hop.
An empty list withholds nothing, which is the behavior of a
router that says nothing here. Withholding is one of the
reasons a selected route is not programmed: a route the
operating system installs, and a route whose SRv6 SID reaches
nothing, are not written either. The values are the protocol
names this build registered: the editor completes them, and a
name nothing registered is refused at commit.
children.name: fib-withhold
children.short-help:
Protocols whose selected routes are not programmed into the
FIB. An empty list programs all.

rib.description:
The system RIB takes the best route each protocol offers and
selects one system best for each prefix. The FIB plugins program
that winner into the kernel with netlink, into VPP, or into a P4
switch. The kernel FIB carries no administrative distance field, so
the ranking happens here and only the winner reaches netlink. The
distance container below is the one declaration of every protocol's
administrative distance. The fib-withhold leaf-list beside it names
the protocols whose winners are not programmed. Routes reach the
system RIB from the protocols, never from this block.
rib.name: rib

children.description:
The leaf is mandatory. The range refuses 0 and 253 to 255, because
253 is the kernel default table, 254 is the main table and 255 is
the local table. Ze also refuses an identifier this build cannot
program through netlink without truncation.
children.name: id
children.short-help:
Kernel routing table ID. Reserved IDs
excluded: 0 (use 'default'), 253-255
(kernel reserved).

children.description:
One entry maps one name to one kernel table identifier. Ze refuses an
entry named default, and refuses an entry with no id. Two entries CAN
carry the same identifier, because the registry keys on the name.
children.name: table
children.short-help: A named routing table.

routing-table.description:
Ze builds one registry from these entries, and a static route or a policy
route resolves its table name against that registry. The name default is
built-in and resolves to table 0, so no entry can carry that name.
routing-table.name: routing-table
routing-table.short-help:
Named routing table definitions. Each entry maps
a name to a kernel routing table ID.

children.description:
Hop address, given as an IPv4 prefix such as 10.0.0.8/30. A commit that gives a bare
address with no prefix length is rejected. The address and the prefix length both go into
the ERO IPv4 prefix subobject of the bypass PATH.
children.name: address
children.short-help: Hop address (IPv4 prefix)

children.description:
Hop type. strict is the default and asks that the previous hop reaches this one directly.
loose sets the L bit of the ERO subobject and permits other hops between them. Ze reads any
value other than loose as strict.
children.name: type
children.short-help: Hop type (strict or loose)

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Set the L bit of the ERO subobject and permit other hops between them.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: The previous hop must reach this one directly, with no hop between them.

children.description:
Bypass path hops. The route has to avoid the link or the node this bypass protects, because a
backup that crosses the protected resource fails with it. Ze has no IGP and no CSPF, so the
operator gives the hops. The hops are ordered by the numeric index key.
children.name: explicit-route
children.short-help: Bypass path hops (must avoid the protected resource)

children.description:
Merge point address (IPv4). The address is the protected LSPs' next hop (link protection) or
next-next hop (node protection), where this bypass rejoins them.
children.name: merge-point
children.short-help: Merge point address (IPv4) where this bypass rejoins the protected LSPs.

children.description:
This bypass merges at a next-next hop, so it gives node protection. A protected LSP that asked
for node protection is armed onto a bypass only when this leaf is true. Left false, the bypass
protects the link alone, and a node-protection request finds no bypass at this PLR.
children.name: node-protection
children.short-help: This bypass merges at a next-next hop, so it gives node protection

children.description:
Facility-backup bypass LSP (RFC 4090 Section 3.2): an LSP from this PLR to a merge point, explicitly
routed to avoid the protected resource. A protected transit LSP is redirected onto this bypass on a
local failure. The redirected LSP is one whose next hop (link protection) or next-next hop (node
protection) is this bypass's merge point. The route is explicit because Ze has no IGP and no CSPF to
compute a backup path.
children.name: bypass
children.short-help: Facility-backup bypass LSP from this PLR to a merge point (RFC 4090 Section 3.2).

children.description:
Local link prefix (IPv4 CIDR, for example 10.0.0.4/30). When more than one interface is configured,
admission control maps an LSP to this interface. The map applies when the neighbor address falls
within the prefix.
children.name: address
children.short-help: Local link prefix in IPv4 CIDR form, for example 10.0.0.4/30.

children.description:
Maximum link bandwidth. The value is reported by 'show rsvp-te interface' and it is not an
admission limit. Only max-reservable-bandwidth bounds what admission control accepts.
children.name: max-bandwidth
children.short-help: Maximum link bandwidth (bps)

children.description:
Maximum reservable bandwidth. Admission control denies a reservation when the accounted total
plus the new request is more than this value. A shared-explicit session counts its largest LSP
once rather than the sum, so a make-before-break reroute is not double-counted. Left unset, the
limit is 0 and every tunnel that requests bandwidth on this interface is denied.
children.name: max-reservable-bandwidth
children.short-help: Maximum reservable bandwidth (bps)

children.description:
Per-interface RSVP-TE configuration. Bandwidth admission control accounts each reservation against
one entry of this list. An interface that no entry names carries no limit, so every reservation
that resolves onto it is admitted.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Per-interface RSVP-TE configuration

children.description:
Number of missed refreshes before state cleanup, 1 to 255, default 3. State expires when the last
refresh is older than refresh-period multiplied by this number, which is 90 seconds at the
defaults. Expiry releases the reserved bandwidth, the MPLS forwarding entry and the label, then
sends an lsp-down event.
children.name: refresh-multiplier
children.short-help: Number of missed refreshes before state cleanup

children.description:
PATH and RESV refresh interval, 1 to 65535 seconds, default 30. The same 65535-second ceiling caps
the period a neighbor advertises in TIME_VALUES. A neighbor therefore cannot hold state alive for
years. A
reload reaches the running LSPs at the next refresh tick.
children.name: refresh-period
children.short-help: PATH/RESV refresh interval (RFC 2205 soft-state)

children.description:
Router identifier, in IPv4 address format. A commit that gives an IPv6 address is rejected. The
address is the PATH sender address, the address the transport socket binds, and the seed of the
session key each tunnel and bypass derives. A change after startup is logged and refused, and the
running router-id stays in use until the daemon restarts.
children.name: router-id
children.short-help: Router identifier (IPv4 address format)

children.description:
Requested bandwidth. The value fills the SENDER_TSPEC token rate, token bucket and peak rate.
Admission control charges it against the interface entry the LSP neighbor resolves onto, and it
denies the LSP when the charge is more than max-reservable-bandwidth.
children.name: bandwidth
children.short-help: Requested bandwidth (bps)

children.description:
Tunnel endpoint, an IPv4 address. The address is the SESSION tunnel endpoint the PATH carries.
A node whose own router-id equals this address acts as the egress and answers with a RESV. Every
other node on the path acts as a transit node.
children.name: destination
children.short-help: Tunnel endpoint (IPv4 address)

children.description:
Hop address, given as an IPv4 prefix such as 10.0.0.4/30. A commit that gives a bare
address with no prefix length is rejected. The address and the prefix length both go into
the ERO IPv4 prefix subobject.
children.name: address
children.short-help: Hop address (IPv4 prefix)

children.description:
Hop type. strict is the default and asks that the previous hop reaches this one directly.
loose sets the L bit of the ERO subobject and permits other hops between them. Ze reads any
value other than loose as strict.
children.name: type
children.short-help: Hop type (strict or loose)

values.name: loose
values.short-help: Set the L bit of the ERO subobject and permit other hops between them.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: The previous hop must reach this one directly, with no hop between them.

children.description:
Explicit route hops. The list becomes the ERO object the PATH carries (RFC 3209 Section 4.3).
Ze has no IGP and no CSPF, so the operator gives every hop. A tunnel with no hop here is signaled
with no ERO object. A commit that changes the list starts a make-before-break reroute.
children.name: explicit-route
children.short-help: Explicit route hops

children.description:
Backup method. facility is the default and asks each PLR for one bypass LSP that protects
many LSPs (RFC 4090 Section 3.2). one-to-one asks for one detour per LSP (Section 3.1). As a
PLR, Ze arms only a facility bypass from its own bypass list. Ze signals a one-to-one request
and builds no detour for it.
children.name: backup
children.short-help: Backup method: facility (one bypass protects many LSPs) or one-to-one (a detour per LSP)

values.name: facility
values.short-help: Ask each PLR for one bypass LSP that protects many LSPs (RFC 4090 Section 3.2).

values.name: one-to-one
values.short-help: Ask for one detour per LSP (RFC 4090 Section 3.1), which Ze signals and never builds.

children.description:
Request a backup that guarantees the reserved bandwidth. Ze sets the bandwidth-protection
flag in SESSION_ATTRIBUTE (RFC 4090 Section 4.3) and records it in the RESV route object. Ze's
own bypass selection does not compare the bypass bandwidth, so the flag is a request to the
PLR downstream.
children.name: bandwidth-protection
children.short-help: Request a backup that guarantees the reserved bandwidth

children.description:
Maximum number of hops the backup path can take, 0 to 255, default 16. The value goes into
the FAST_REROUTE object (RFC 4090 Section 4.1) for the PLR that computes the backup. A Ze
facility bypass is routed by its own explicit-route list, so this limit does not shorten
it.
children.name: hop-limit
children.short-help: Maximum number of hops the backup path can take

children.description:
Request NNHOP (node) protection rather than NHOP (link) protection. Ze sets the
node-protection flag in SESSION_ATTRIBUTE (RFC 4090 Section 4.3). As a PLR, Ze then arms only
a bypass whose merge point is the next-next hop of the explicit route. That bypass also has
to set its own node-protection leaf. With no such bypass, the LSP gets no protection.
children.name: node-protection
children.short-help: Request NNHOP (node) protection rather than NHOP (link) protection

children.description:
Fast Reroute (RFC 4090) local protection for this LSP. The container has presence. Absent, the
head-end PATH carries no SESSION_ATTRIBUTE and no FAST_REROUTE object, and no transit PLR arms a
backup. Present, it also puts setup-priority, hold-priority and the tunnel name on the wire.
children.name: fast-reroute
children.short-help: Fast Reroute (RFC 4090) local protection for this LSP

children.description:
Hold priority, where 0 is the highest and 7 is the default. It states how hard this LSP holds
its reservation against a setup of higher priority. Ze signals it beside setup-priority, and
only for a tunnel that declares fast-reroute.
children.name: hold-priority
children.short-help: Hold priority (0 = highest)

children.description:
Setup priority, where 0 is the highest and 7 is the default. Ze signals the value in the
SESSION_ATTRIBUTE and FAST_REROUTE objects, and it adds both objects only for a tunnel that
declares fast-reroute. Ze preempts no LSP of its own, so the priority acts on the routers
downstream.
children.name: setup-priority
children.short-help: Setup priority (0 = highest)

children.description:
Tunnel identifier, the part of the SESSION that separates this LSP from another to the same
endpoint. Ze reserves 61440 to 65535 for the bypass LSPs it derives from a bypass name, and a
commit that puts a tunnel in that range is rejected.
children.name: tunnel-id
children.short-help: Tunnel identifier

children.description:
RSVP-TE LSP tunnel definition. Each entry signals a PATH from the local router-id toward
destination. A commit that changes only the explicit route starts a make-before-break reroute (RFC
3209 Section 6.1) and leaves the live tunnel in place.
children.name: tunnel
children.short-help: RSVP-TE LSP tunnel definition

rsvp-te.description:
RSVP-TE traffic engineering configuration. Signaling is IPv4 only. Without a router-id the engine stays
idle, and no tunnel and no bypass signals. Ze has no IGP and no CSPF, so every path is given as an
explicit route.
rsvp-te.name: rsvp-te

children.description:
RFC 7534 Section 3.4 and RFC 7535 Section 3.1 give the
single-stack option. The anycast addresses themselves are
fixed constants, and an operator never types one.
children.name: address-family
children.short-help: Restrict the service to one address family.

values.name: both
values.short-help: Serve on both IPv4 and IPv6 anycast addresses. This is the default.

values.name: ipv4-only
values.short-help: Serve on the two IPv4 anycast addresses only.

values.name: ipv6-only
values.short-help: Serve on the two IPv6 anycast addresses only.

children.description:
An empty list, which is the default, answers every source and
matches the standard AS112 public-sink behavior. With one
prefix or more, the node answers a query only when its source
IP is inside one of those prefixes. It drops every other query
and sends no response.
A loopback source and an on-box source are always permitted,
whatever this list holds, so the 'request as112 healthcheck'
probe is never blocked.
A set list makes the node non-public. That is correct for a
local-use mirror, and wrong for an AS112 contributor the whole
internet reaches.
children.name: allow-from
children.short-help: Client-source access list of the queries the node answers.

children.description:
The redistribute statement is `redistribute { destination bgp
{ import as112 } }`. The default is the well-known AS112
number 112 (RFC 7534 Section 3.2), because the redistribute
source models an AS112 virtual router. Set an operator ASN, or
an RFC 6996 private-use ASN, to originate under a coordinated
AS or a local-use AS instead. Ze ignores this leaf unless
'import as112' is configured under redistribute.
children.name: asn
children.short-help: Origin AS the AS112 covering prefixes carry when redistributed into BGP.

children.description:
The leaf takes an AA:NN standard community (RFC 1997) and a
well-known name such as no-export or nopeer (RFC 3765). Those
are the values RFC 7534 Section 3.4 recommends to restrict
AS112 route propagation.
The type is 'string' rather than the AA:NN-only ze-types
community pattern, so a well-known name is accepted. The
canonical community parser validates every value at config
time. Ze ignores this leaf unless 'import as112' is configured
under redistribute.
children.name: community
children.short-help: BGP communities attached to the redistributed AS112 covering prefixes.

children.description:
The default is false. Ze binds DoH on every IP the cleartext
listeners use, on listen-port, at path. The listener drives the
same handler as cleartext DNS, so allow-from answers a DoH
client exactly as it answers a UDP client. A query the handler
refuses gets HTTP 403.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the DNS-over-HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).

children.description:
The default is 443, and the range is 1 to 65535. Ze refuses a
port of 0. A GET carries the query base64url-encoded in the dns
parameter, and a POST carries it in an application/dns-message
body of 65535 bytes at most.
children.name: listen-port
children.short-help: TCP port for the DoH HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).

children.description:
RFC 8484 defines the URI Template. The default path is
/dns-query.
children.name: path
children.short-help: HTTP request path the DoH endpoint answers on.

children.description:
The listener reuses the certificate material of the tls
container. It binds the fixed anycast addresses and the
loopback address on 'listen-port', at 'path'.
children.name: doh
children.short-help: DNS-over-HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).

children.description:
The AS112 node does not start while this leaf is false, and
false is the default.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the AS112 anycast DNS node.

children.description:
The facility name is the name of the site, for example
'Example Datacenter'. It is surfaced beside the location.
children.name: facility
children.short-help: Facility name in the HOSTNAME.AS112.NET/ARPA TXT answers.

children.description:
RFC 7534 Section 3.5 defines those answers. The string tells
an operator which anycast instance answered a query. An empty
value omits the TXT string.
children.name: hostname
children.short-help: Node identification string in the HOSTNAME.AS112.NET/ARPA TXT answers.

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:
The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a
free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
as112 always occupies port 53 on its fixed IPv4 anycast
addresses while it is enabled. The Go-level default,
RegisterListenerDefault, fills in the representative address,
because no operator-facing command populates this list.
children.name: ipv4-anycast-listener
children.short-help: Presence-only anchor for port 53 on the fixed IPv4 anycast addresses.

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:
The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a
free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
as112 always occupies port 53 on its fixed IPv6 anycast
addresses while it is enabled.
children.name: ipv6-anycast-listener
children.short-help: Presence-only anchor for port 53 on the fixed IPv6 anycast addresses.

children.description:
The location is surfaced beside the facility, for example
'London, UK'.
children.name: location
children.short-help: City and country in the HOSTNAME.AS112.NET/ARPA TXT answers.

children.description:
When this leaf and key-file are both unset, Ze uses an
ephemeral self-signed certificate.
children.name: cert-file
children.short-help: Path to the PEM server certificate presented on DoT and DoH.

children.description:
The listeners send the leaf certificate and every
intermediate certificate the store entry holds.
This leaf excludes cert-file and key-file. Setting both is
a configuration error.
The PKI store lives in the hub process, so a geodns plugin
or an as112 plugin started as an external process cannot
resolve the name. The secure listeners then do not start,
and Ze logs the error. Cleartext DNS still runs.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: Name of the PKI store certificate served on DoT and DoH.

children.description:
The default is false. Ze binds DoT on every IP the cleartext
listeners use, on listen-port. DoT is TCP only, because RFC
7858 Section 3.1 defines no UDP counterpart. When the TLS
material fails to load, Ze starts no secure listener and the
cleartext listeners keep running.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the DNS-over-TLS listener (RFC 7858).

children.description:
Ze reads cert-file and key-file on each apply, so a rotated
pair reaches the listener without a restart. One of the two
alone stops the secure listeners with an error, and the
cleartext listeners keep running. The certificate leaf names a
PKI store entry instead, and Ze refuses a config that writes
both sources.
children.name: key-file
children.short-help:
Path to the PEM private key matching cert-file. Must be
set together with cert-file.

children.description: The RFC 7858 well-known 'domain-s' port is 853.
children.name: listen-port
children.short-help: TCP port for the DoT listener.

children.description:
RFC 7858 defines DNS-over-TLS (DoT). When it is enabled, the
DoT listener binds the fixed anycast addresses and the
loopback address on 'listen-port'.
When cert-file and key-file are both unset, Ze uses an
ephemeral self-signed certificate, which a strict client
cannot validate. Supply an operator PEM file for a node the
public trusts.
children.name: tls
children.short-help: DNS-over-TLS listener, and the certificate material it shares with DoH.

children.description:
RFC 7534 Section 3.3 states that a node does not advertise the
service prefix while the name server is not running. With true,
which is the default, Ze announces the covering prefixes only
while the as112 node serves. Ze withdraws them when serving is
lost, when the service is disabled, and when the node shuts
down. With false, Ze announces as soon as the node is enabled
and imported, with no serving-state gate. Ze ignores this leaf
unless 'import as112' is configured under redistribute.
children.name: watchdog
children.short-help: Announce the covering prefixes only while the node serves DNS.

children.description:
The container holds the enable switch, the address family, the
node identification strings, the access list, the BGP settings
and the secure listeners.
children.name: as112
children.short-help: AS112 anycast DNS node.

children.description:
Enable the DHCP server. Left false, the plugin still parses and validates the config, and it
binds no socket and builds no handler. A commit that sets it true rebuilds one handler for each
subnet and binds the listeners again.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable DHCP server

children.description:
Interfaces to serve DHCP on. Ze binds one UDP listener for each name in the list. A name that
fails to bind is logged as an error and skipped. When no name binds, the server logs that it is
not serving and answers nothing.
children.name: listen-interface
children.short-help: Interfaces to serve DHCP on

children.description:
HTTP URL for the iPXE boot script. Ze sends it as option 67 only to a client whose user
class in option 77 starts with iPXE. That reply carries option 60 and option 67 alone, so
the iPXE client receives no option 66, no option 43 and no siaddr. A commit rejects a URL
that does not start with http:// or https://, and one longer than 255 characters.
children.name: boot-script-url
children.short-help: HTTP URL for iPXE boot script (sent as option 67 to iPXE clients)

children.description:
Boot file path for BIOS clients, sent as option 67. Ze sends it whenever the first client
architecture in option 93 is any value other than 7 (RFC 4578 Section 2.1). An absent or
malformed option 93 reads as architecture 0, which is BIOS, so this path is the fallback.
children.name: bootfile-bios
children.short-help: Boot file path for BIOS clients (option 67)

children.description:
Boot file path for UEFI clients, sent as option 67. Ze sends it only when the first client
architecture in option 93 is 7, which is UEFI x64 (RFC 4578 Section 2.1). Every other
architecture receives bootfile-bios.
children.name: bootfile-uefi
children.short-help: Boot file path for UEFI clients (option 67)

children.description:
Enable PXE boot option injection. Set true, a commit also requires tftp-server,
bootfile-bios and bootfile-uefi, and it names the missing one. Left false, Ze adds no PXE
option even for a client that identifies itself as PXEClient.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable PXE boot option injection

children.description:
TFTP server IP address for PXE boot. Ze writes the address into the siaddr field of the
reply (RFC 2131 Section 4.3.1) and its text form into option 66 (RFC 2132 Section 9.9). The
address has to be IPv4. An iPXE client receives neither, because boot-script-url answers it
instead.
children.name: tftp-server
children.short-help: TFTP server IP address for PXE boot (option 66, siaddr)

children.description:
PXE boot server settings (RFC 4578). Ze adds these options only when the client vendor class
in option 60 starts with PXEClient:. An ordinary DHCP client sees none of them. With pxe
enabled, a commit also requires tftp-server, bootfile-bios and bootfile-uefi.
children.name: pxe
children.short-help: PXE boot server settings (RFC 4578)

children.description:
Default gateway address, sent as option 3. Ze also uses it as the DHCP server
identifier of this subnet, in option 54. With no default-router the identifier falls
back to the start address of the first range, and then to the network address of the
prefix. A REQUEST that names a different server identifier is left unanswered.
children.name: default-router
children.short-help: Default gateway address (option 3)

children.description:
DNS server addresses, sent as option 6. Write them in preference order, because Ze
sends them in the order it reads them. A commit rejects more than 63 addresses, which is
what one DHCP option holds, and it rejects an address that is not IPv4.
children.name: dns-server
children.short-help: DNS server addresses (option 6)

children.description:
Domain name for clients, sent as option 15. Ze sends the string as it is written. A
commit rejects a value longer than 255 characters, which is the most one DHCP option
holds.
children.name: domain-name
children.short-help: Domain name for clients (option 15)

children.description:
Lease duration in seconds, 60 to 604800, default 86400. Ze sends it as option 51. It
also sends the renewal time T1 as half of it, and the rebinding time T2 as seven
eighths of it. RFC 2131 Section 4.4.5 states those two fractions. The lease table drops
a binding after the same time.
children.name: lease-time
children.short-help: Lease duration in seconds

children.description:
First allocatable address, and the address is allocatable. It has to fall inside
the subnet prefix, and it has to be less than or equal to stop. A commit names which
of the two rules it broke.
children.name: start
children.short-help: First allocatable address

children.description:
Last allocatable address, and the address is allocatable. It has to fall inside the
subnet prefix. A range of one address is written with the same value in start and
stop.
children.name: stop
children.short-help: Last allocatable address

children.description:
Named dynamic address pool range. A subnet holds 10 ranges at most. Ze sorts them by
start address and rejects a commit where two of them overlap. Ze allocates in that
order.
children.name: range
children.short-help: Named dynamic address pool range

children.description:
Fixed IP address for this client. It has to fall inside the subnet prefix, and a
commit rejects an address outside it. The address does not have to fall inside a
range. When it does, Ze marks it allocated so the dynamic pool never offers it to
another client.
children.name: ip-address
children.short-help: Fixed IP address for this client

children.description:
Client MAC address. Ze reads the colon form aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff, the hyphen form and
the dotted form. Ze matches the value against the client hardware address of the
request. A mapping with no mac-address is rejected at commit.
children.name: mac-address
children.short-help: Client MAC address (xx:xx:xx:xx:xx:xx)

children.description:
Static MAC-to-IP binding. Ze answers a client whose MAC address matches with the mapped
address, and it never consults the dynamic pool for that client. A mapped address that
falls inside a range is marked in the pool, so no other client is offered it.
children.name: static-mapping
children.short-help: Static MAC-to-IP binding

children.description:
Subnet with address pool and options. Each subnet becomes one handler with its own address
pool and lease table. A request that carries no relay address, no client address and no
requested address matches every subnet. The first handler with a free address answers it.
children.name: subnet
children.short-help: Subnet with address pool and options

children.description:
Named network grouping of subnets. The name is a label for the operator, and Ze puts it on no
packet. Ze sorts the groups by name and builds one handler for each subnet in that order. A
request is answered by the first handler that accepts it.
children.name: shared-network
children.short-help: Named network grouping of subnets

children.description:
DHCP server settings. Ze speaks DHCPv4 only (RFC 2131 and RFC 2132), so every address leaf under
this container is IPv4. The server binds one listener for each name in listen-interface, and
every listener answers for every configured subnet.
children.name: dhcp-server
children.short-help: DHCP server settings

children.description:
edns0-then-packet, the default, reads the address from the EDNS0 client-subnet option (RFC
7871) and falls back to the packet source address. packet ignores the option and always reads the
packet source. edns0 reads only the option. A query with no option then matches no `source`
prefix, so a name the zone owns draws an empty NOERROR answer.
children.name: client-ip-source
children.short-help: Where the client IP used for source selection is read from

values.name: edns0
values.short-help: Use only the EDNS0 client-subnet option (RFC 7871); no answer without it

values.name: edns0-then-packet
values.short-help: Prefer EDNS0 client-subnet, fall back to the packet source IP

values.name: packet
values.short-help: Use the UDP/TCP packet source IP

children.description:
Default record TTL (seconds) when a host omits its own. The range is 1 to 2147483647 (RFC 2181
section 8). A zero default is not allowed.
children.name: default-ttl
children.short-help: Default record TTL in seconds when a host omits its own.

children.description:
The default is false, so geodns binds no DNS-over-HTTPS listener. A true value binds
every `listener` IP on `listen-port` at `path`. DoH takes the certificate material of the
`tls` container, so it needs no `tls/enabled`. A certificate that does not load starts no
secure listener, and the cleartext listeners stay bound.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the DNS-over-HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).

children.description:
The DoH listener binds this TCP port on every `listener` IP. A commit with the value 0
is refused. Move the port when a web server already holds 443 on the same address, because
the second bind of one address and port fails.
children.name: listen-port
children.short-help: TCP port for the DoH HTTPS listener (RFC 8484).

children.description:
The DoH endpoint answers this path alone. An empty value keeps the default /dns-query.
RFC 8484 section 3 states that 'The DoH client is configured with a URI Template [RFC6570]'.
A client MUST therefore be told a path that is not the default.
children.name: path
children.short-help:
HTTP request path the DoH endpoint answers on (RFC 8484
URI Template); defaults to /dns-query.

children.description:
DNS-over-HTTPS (DoH, RFC 8484) listener. It reuses the tls container's certificate material. It
binds the configured listener IPs on 'listen-port' at 'path'.
children.name: doh
children.short-help: DNS-over-HTTPS listener (DoH, RFC 8484).

children.description:
The default is false, so geodns binds no listener and answers no query. A true value binds
each `listener` entry for UDP and TCP, and it binds the DoT and DoH listeners that are enabled.
A false value unbinds every listener.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the GeoDNS server

children.description:
Each entry becomes one A record or one AAAA record for the host, and one query
answers all of them. Ze refuses the commit for a host with no entry here, unless `type`
is SRV.
children.name: address
children.short-help: One or more A/AAAA addresses (v4 => A, v6 => AAAA when type omitted)

children.description:
The value is the TCP or UDP port the service listens on at `target`. The range
is 0 to 65535. Ze copies the number into the record and checks nothing about it.
children.name: port
children.short-help: SRV port

children.description:
RFC 2782 states that 'A client MUST attempt to contact the target host with the
lowest-numbered priority it can reach'. That text is in the section 'The format of
the SRV RR'. Targets that share a priority are ordered by `weight`. The range is 0
to 65535.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: SRV priority

children.description:
The value is the hostname that runs the service. Ze adds the trailing dot when
the value has none. A commit is refused when the name breaks the length bounds RFC
1035 sets. Ze adds no address record for the target, so a client resolves that name
in a second query.
children.name: target
children.short-help: SRV target hostname

children.description:
RFC 2782, 'The format of the SRV RR', calls the weight 'a relative weight for
entries with the same priority'. The same text states that 'Larger weights SHOULD be
given a proportionately higher probability of being selected'. Use 0 when one target
has no selection to do. The range is 0 to 65535.
children.name: weight
children.short-help: SRV weight

children.description:
Ze reads this container only when `type` is SRV. All four leaves are then required,
and a commit that omits one is refused with 'need priority weight port target'. An SRV
host answers one record, and `address` on it is ignored.
children.name: srv
children.short-help: SRV record fields (when type is SRV)

children.description:
The value is the TTL in seconds of every record of this host. An unset leaf takes
`default-ttl`. 0 is permitted here and refused on `default-ttl`, and it asks a resolver
to cache the answer for no time. The range is the TTL range RFC 2181 section 8 sets.
children.name: ttl
children.short-help: Record TTL; defaults to default-ttl when unset

children.description:
An unset leaf reads each `address` entry on its own, and answers A for an IPv4
address and AAAA for an IPv6 address. A refuses the commit for an IPv6 address, and AAAA
refuses it for an IPv4 address. SRV reads the `srv` container and ignores `address`.
children.name: type
children.short-help: Record type; omit to auto-detect A vs AAAA per address

values.name: A
values.short-help: Answer an A record for each address, and refuse an IPv6 address at commit.

values.name: AAAA
values.short-help: Answer an AAAA record for each address, and refuse an IPv4 address at commit.

values.name: SRV
values.short-help: Answer an SRV record from the srv container, and ignore the address list.

children.description:
One entry holds one name and the records Ze answers for it inside this set. A commit is
refused when the entry carries no address and `type` is not SRV. It is also refused when
`type` and the address family disagree.
children.name: host
children.short-help: A hostname and its records

children.description:
A host set is one answer set. Ze picks the set for a query from the client address, through
the `source` prefix that matches it. One set can serve several source prefixes. The same
hostname can appear in several sets with a different address in each. That is what makes the
answer depend on the client.
children.name: host-set
children.short-help: Named, reusable set of host records; referenced by source entries

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:
The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a
free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
UDP+TCP listen endpoints. Each named entry binds one IP (IPv4 or IPv6) and one port. Repeat the same
port for a dual-stack pair. Ze defaults to 127.0.0.1:5300 and ::1:5300 when no entry is configured.
The ze:listener marking enables config-time port-conflict detection across services.
children.name: listener
children.short-help: UDP and TCP listen endpoints for geodns.

children.description:
Ze builds one NS record for each entry, named ns1.<zone> to nsN.<zone> in list order, and
one A glue record beside it. The glue name is synthesized and never configured. A commit is
refused when a zone is long enough to make nsN.<zone> break the length bounds RFC 1035 sets.
The records go in the Answer of an NS query and in the Authority of every other answer.
children.name: nameserver
children.short-help: Nameserver IPv4 addresses; ns1..nsN.<zone> A glue is synthesised (max 9)

children.description:
The value becomes the RNAME field of the SOA record. A value with no dot is read as the
mailbox local part under the zone, so the default builds hostmaster.<zone>. A value that
holds a dot is used as a whole domain name, with the trailing dot added.
children.name: contact
children.short-help: Responsible-party mailbox label (SOA RNAME), e.g. hostmaster

children.description:
The value goes into the EXPIRE field of the SOA record, in seconds. It tells a secondary
when to stop the service of a zone it can no longer refresh. geodns serves no AXFR, so no
secondary acts on it, and the value changes no answer Ze gives.
children.name: expire
children.short-help: SOA expire seconds

children.description:
SOA minimum, the negative-cache TTL in seconds. The range is 0 to 2147483647. The field is stamped
as the SOA record's own TTL, so the RFC 2181 section 8 TTL range bounds it.
children.name: minimum
children.short-help: SOA minimum, the negative-cache TTL in seconds.

children.description:
The value becomes the MNAME field of the SOA record. Ze adds the trailing dot when the
value has none. An unset leaf makes Ze build ns1.<zone> for each zone it serves, so the
name follows the zone the query asked for. A commit is refused when the name breaks the
length bounds RFC 1035 sets.
children.name: mname
children.short-help: Primary nameserver (SOA MNAME). Defaults to ns1.<first-zone> when unset.

children.description:
The value goes into the REFRESH field of the SOA record, in seconds. It tells a
secondary how long to wait before it checks the serial again. geodns serves no AXFR, so no
secondary acts on it, and the value changes no answer Ze gives.
children.name: refresh
children.short-help: SOA refresh seconds

children.description:
The value goes into the RETRY field of the SOA record, in seconds. It tells a secondary
how long to wait after a failed refresh. geodns serves no AXFR, so no secondary acts on it,
and the value changes no answer Ze gives.
children.name: retry
children.short-help: SOA retry seconds

children.description:
Ze reads this leaf only when `serial-mode` is fixed, and it then serves the value
unchanged. The other two modes compute the serial and ignore the leaf. In fixed mode you own
the increase after each change, under the serial arithmetic RFC 1982 defines.
children.name: serial
children.short-help: SOA serial used when serial-mode is fixed

children.description:
auto-epoch, the default, takes the Unix time in seconds at commit. It raises that by one
when the result is not more than the previous serial, so two commits in one second still
increase. auto-datetime builds YYYYMMDDnn (RFC 1912), and the 32-bit field leaves two counter
digits, so it holds 100 revisions in one day. fixed serves the `serial` leaf unchanged.
children.name: serial-mode
children.short-help: How the 32-bit SOA serial is generated

values.name: auto-datetime
values.short-help: YYYYMMDDnn (RFC 1912); capped at 100 revisions/day by the 32-bit serial

values.name: auto-epoch
values.short-help: max(Unix seconds at commit, previous serial + 1); strictly increases at any rate

values.name: fixed
values.short-help: Use the serial leaf verbatim

children.description:
Ze builds the SOA record of each zone from these leaves. It serves no AXFR, so no secondary
acts on `refresh`, `retry` and `expire`, and those three only carry their value in the record.
`minimum` is the one field an answer depends on, because Ze stamps it as the TTL of the SOA
record and as its MINTTL.
children.name: soa
children.short-help: SOA record fields (synthesised; geodns serves no AXFR)

children.description:
The value names a `host-set` entry. A commit that names an unknown set is refused with
'references unknown host-set', and a source with no value here is refused as well. A client
this prefix matches is answered from that set alone.
children.name: host-set
children.short-help: Name of the host-set to answer for clients matching this prefix

children.description:
Maps a client-IP prefix to a host-set. The longest prefix wins. 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 are the catch-all
external default.
children.name: source
children.short-help: Maps a client-IP prefix to a host-set.

children.description:
Path to the PEM server certificate presented on DoT and DoH. Leave this leaf and key-file unset to
select an ephemeral self-signed certificate.
children.name: cert-file
children.short-help: Path to the PEM server certificate presented on DoT and DoH.

children.description:
Name of the certificate in the PKI store to serve on DoT and DoH. The listeners send the leaf
certificate and every intermediate certificate the store entry holds. This leaf and
cert-file/key-file are mutually exclusive, and setting both is a configuration error. The PKI store
lives in the hub process, so a geodns plugin started as an external process cannot resolve the name.
The secure listeners then do not start, and Ze logs the error. Cleartext DNS is unaffected.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: Name of the PKI store certificate to serve on DoT and DoH.

children.description:
The default is false, so geodns binds no DNS-over-TLS listener. A true value binds every
`listener` IP on `listen-port`, beside the cleartext endpoints. When the certificate material
does not load, Ze logs the error and starts no secure listener. The cleartext listeners stay
bound.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the DNS-over-TLS listener (RFC 7858).

children.description:
The value is the path to the PEM private key of `cert-file`, and the two go together.
Ze re-reads the pair on each commit, so a rotated key is picked up with no restart. This
leaf and `certificate` are mutually exclusive, and a commit that sets both is refused. Leave
both this leaf and `cert-file` unset to select an ephemeral self-signed certificate.
children.name: key-file
children.short-help:
Path to the PEM private key matching cert-file. Must be
set together with cert-file.

children.description:
The DoT listener binds this TCP port on every `listener` IP, and it uses no UDP. A
commit with the value 0 is refused. Move the port off 853 only when a client can be told the
new one, because a DoT client uses 853 by default.
children.name: listen-port
children.short-help:
TCP port for the DoT listener; the RFC 7858 well-known
'domain-s' port is 853.

children.description:
DNS-over-TLS (DoT, RFC 7858) listener and the certificate material shared with DoH. When the
listener is enabled, DoT binds the configured listener IPs on 'listen-port'. When cert-file and
key-file are unset, Ze uses an ephemeral self-signed certificate, which a strict client cannot
validate.
children.name: tls
children.short-help: DNS-over-TLS listener and the certificate material shared with DoH.

children.description:
Zones served (FQDN). A query name must be one of these, or a name inside one, compared label by
label. A name outside every zone draws REFUSED.
children.name: zone
children.short-help: Zones served, as fully qualified domain names.

children.description:
GeoDNS answers a query from the client address rather than from the name alone. A `source`
entry maps a client prefix to a `host-set`, and the longest prefix that holds the client address
wins. The same name can then answer a different address to each client. Ze is authoritative for the
`zone` entries only, and it serves no AXFR.
children.name: geodns
children.short-help: GeoDNS server: per-source-IP DNS answers

children.description:
Ze serves the files of this directory under /install/boot/. An
empty leaf registers no such path, and a client then gets 404. Ze
builds /install/boot/boot.ipxe itself, and only when
listen-interface names an interface whose address it can resolve.
children.name: boot-directory
children.short-help: Directory containing installer kernel, initrd, iPXE config

children.description:
The default is false. When the leaf is true, Ze refuses the
configuration unless image-directory or boot-directory names a
directory. The plugin binds the port when the configuration is
applied, and a bind that fails is reported in the log.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable image server

children.description:
Ze serves the files of this directory under /install/image/. An
empty leaf registers no such path, and a client then gets 404. A
request that reaches the path while the directory holds no image
gets 503.
children.name: image-directory
children.short-help: Directory containing gokrazy disk images

children.description:
Ze resolves the IPv4 address of EVERY interface named here and binds
listen-port on each one, as the TFTP server and the DHCP server do with the same
leaf. With no interface named, Ze binds the port on every address of the host. An
interface that does not resolve is named in the log and skipped, and the interfaces
that do resolve still serve. When no interface binds at all, Ze logs 'no interfaces
bound' and the image server serves nothing. Ze builds /install/boot/boot.ipxe only
for a listener bound to an interface address, and the script names the address the
client reached.
children.name: listen-interface
children.short-help: Interfaces to serve on

children.description:
The default is 80 and the range is 1 to 65535. Ze binds this port
on the IPv4 address of each listen-interface. With no interface
named, Ze binds the port on every address of the host.
children.name: listen-port
children.short-help: HTTP listen port

children.description:
Ze emits the value on the installer kernel cmdline, as
ze.rescue-auth, and the installer checks it before it
opens the rescue shell. An empty value makes the
installer fail closed, so a fatal error opens no shell.
The PXE network carries this value unauthenticated,
so it MUST commit only to a dedicated rescue token, and
never to the admin password.
children.name: rescue-auth
children.short-help: Salted argon2id of the installer rescue token, as '<saltHex>:<digestHex>'.

children.description:
Ze refuses a value that bcrypt cannot read, so the target never
gets a database with an unusable password. Only the hash reaches
the served zefs database, so the cleartext password does not cross
the PXE network.
children.name: ssh-password-hash
children.short-help: Bcrypt hash of admin password (written to served zefs)

children.description:
Ze writes this name and the password hash into a zefs database, and
serves that database at /install/database.zefs. The target reads it
and gets its first administrator. Write ssh-username and
ssh-password-hash together, because Ze refuses one without the
other.
children.name: ssh-username
children.short-help: Admin username for installed target (written to served zefs)

children.description:
The server answers three paths under /install: the disk image, the boot
files of the installer, and the zefs database the target starts with.
Ze registers a path only when the leaves that feed it are set, so a
path with nothing behind it answers 404.
children.name: image-server
children.short-help: HTTP image server for PXE provisioning

children.description:
The default is false. When the leaf is true, Ze refuses the
configuration unless root-directory names a directory. A
configuration that names no listen-interface binds no socket, and
Ze then logs that the server does not serve.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable TFTP server

children.description:
Ze opens one UDP socket for each interface of this list and binds
the socket to that interface with SO_BINDTODEVICE. A logical
interface name is resolved to its kernel device first. An interface
that fails to bind is logged, and the others keep their socket.
children.name: listen-interface
children.short-help: Interfaces to serve TFTP on

children.description:
The default is 10 and the range is 1 to 1000. The count is shared
by every listener of the server. Over the limit Ze answers the read
request with a TFTP error that carries the text service
unavailable, and the transfers already open keep running.
children.name: max-transfers
children.short-help: Maximum concurrent TFTP transfers

children.description:
Ze resolves each requested file under this directory and follows
every symbolic link first. A file that lands outside the directory
gets an access violation error, so a client cannot read the rest of
the disk. The leaf is required when enabled is true.
children.name: root-directory
children.short-help: Directory to serve files from

children.description:
The server answers a read request on UDP port 69 and refuses every
write request, so no client can put a file on this host. Ze accepts
octet mode alone, and answers any other mode with an illegal operation
error. Ze negotiates the blksize option of RFC 2348 and the tsize
option of RFC 2349, and it does not support the windowsize option.
children.name: tftp-server
children.short-help: Read-only TFTP server (RFC 1350)

service.description:
The container holds the settings of each service Ze runs, and the
as112 container under it configures the AS112 node.
service.name: service

children.description:
The sender sees a timeout rather than a refusal, so a traceroute
stops at this hop with no reply. Use reject when the sender
SHOULD learn the destination is unreachable.
children.name: blackhole
children.short-help: Drop the packet and send no ICMP message to the sender.

children.description:
The case holds the blackhole container, and the presence of that
container selects the action. Ze installs the route with the kernel blackhole
type, so the kernel drops the packet and answers nothing.
children.name: discard
children.short-help: Drop the packet and tell the sender nothing.

children.description:
BFD profile name (from bfd/profile list). When the BFD session to this next-hop goes down, Ze
removes the next-hop from the ECMP group. Ze then reprograms the route with the remaining active
next-hops.
children.name: bfd-profile
children.short-help: BFD profile name for this next-hop, from the bfd/profile list.

children.description:
Ze resolves the name to a kernel interface index and sets it
on the route. A link-local IPv6 gateway needs it, because the
same address can exist on every link. A name that resolves to no
interface skips this one route, which show static routes then
reports with its reason.
children.name: interface
children.short-help:
Outgoing interface. Required when the
next-hop is a link-local IPv6 address.

children.description:
ECMP weight. A higher value receives proportionally more traffic. The default of 1 gives equal
distribution.
children.name: weight
children.short-help: ECMP weight of this next-hop, 1 by default.

children.description:
The gateway address is the key, so one route holds one entry for
each gateway. Ze shares the traffic between the entries in proportion
to their weights. An entry can name its own BFD profile, and a next
hop whose BFD session goes down leaves the group.
children.name: hop
children.short-help:
Forward via gateway. Multiple entries produce
ECMP with traffic distributed by weight.

children.description:
The range is 1 to 65535, and Ze reads 0 as 1. The weight
counts only against the other next hops of the same route. A
route with one next hop ignores it.
children.name: weight
children.short-help:
ECMP weight. Higher values receive
proportionally more traffic.

children.description:
Forward through the interface only, with no gateway address. This form serves point-to-point links,
such as PPPoE and GRE tunnels, where the next-hop is implicit. Multiple entries can coexist with
gateway next-hops for mixed ECMP.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Forward through the interface only, with no gateway address.

children.description:
Ze reads the hop list and the interface list, and joins the two into
one set of next hops. A route whose next container holds neither one
stops the config load. One next hop becomes a plain route, and two or
more become a multipath route.
children.name: next
children.short-help:
Forward action. Contains gateway and interface
next-hops that may be combined for ECMP.

children.description:
The case holds the next container, which carries gateway next hops and
interface next hops. Two or more next hops of either kind become one ECMP
route. A redistribute consumer sees this case alone.
children.name: forward
children.short-help: Send the packet on toward a next hop.

children.description:
The sender learns at once rather than waiting for a timeout, which
is what separates this from blackhole. The reply itself costs a
packet per dropped packet.
children.name: reject
children.short-help: Drop the packet and send an ICMP unreachable to the sender.

children.description:
The case holds the reject container, and the presence of that container
selects the action. Ze installs the route with the kernel unreachable type,
so the kernel answers with ICMP destination unreachable.
children.name: unreachable
children.short-help: Drop the packet and answer the sender.

children.description:
One case is required. Ze stops the load for a route that names none of next,
blackhole and reject, and it names the prefix in the error. Only the forward case
reaches the redistribute bus.
children.name: action
children.short-help: What to do with matching packets.

children.description:
The note reaches show static routes and nothing else. It is not sent to the
kernel, and no filter reads it. Ze compares the note at a reload, so a change to
the note alone reprograms the route. The length is 0 to 255 characters.
children.name: description
children.short-help: Operator note for this route.

children.description:
Ze writes the value into the netlink route priority. The kernel prefers the
lower priority when two routes cover the same prefix. 0 leaves the attribute
out, so the kernel applies its own default. The redistribute event carries the
same value.
children.name: metric
children.short-help:
Route metric. Used as kernel route priority
(lower is preferred) and carried in redistribute.

children.description:
Ze prints the value in the tag field of show static route and in the config
diff. A redistribute import rule can select routes by tag: write the same value in
a tag leaf under redistribute destination <proto> import static. When Ze
redistributes the route into OSPF, it writes the value into the External Route Tag
of the AS-external LSA, and the tag on the route wins over the tag configured for
the source. Ze writes the value into no kernel route, because Linux has no route
tag attribute. A change to tag alone re-applies the route, because the config diff
compares the field.
children.name: tag
children.short-help: Opaque tag Ze attaches to this route for policy and redistribution.

children.description:
The prefix is the key, so one table holds one entry for each prefix. Ze compares
every leaf of the entry at a reload, the description included, and reprograms the
route when one of them changed.
children.name: route
children.short-help: A static route entry.

children.description:
A named routing table grouping. The table name is resolved to a kernel table ID through the
