routing-table registry. Use 'default' for the main routing table.
children.name: table
children.short-help: A named routing table that holds static routes.

static.description:
Ze programs each route into the kernel through netlink, or into the VPP dataplane, and
marks it with the static protocol number. A route the backend cannot program is skipped and
logged, and the rest of the section still applies. Only a forward route in the default table
reaches the redistribute bus, where BGP can announce it.
static.name: static

children.description:
1800 seconds, which is 30 minutes, is the default, and the range is 60 to 86400
seconds. Ze polls once when the manager starts, and then at each interval. Every
temperature test and every self-test decision happens on that poll, so this
interval bounds how late an alert can arrive.
children.name: check-interval
children.short-help: Health poll interval in seconds

children.description:
false is the default, and nothing else under this container is read while the
leaf holds false. Ze reads the leaf as false unless it holds exactly true. A change
to false at a reload stops the poll loop, and clears every warning and error this
component raised.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable SMART monitoring on all detected ATA/NVMe devices

children.description:
The seven weekday names are the accepted values, and sunday is the
default. Ze reads the weekday from the local time of the appliance. The
extended test starts on that day alone, whatever the interval leaf holds.
children.name: day
children.short-help: Preferred day of week for extended self-tests

values.name: friday
values.short-help: Run the extended self-test on a Friday.

values.name: monday
values.short-help: Run the extended self-test on a Monday.

values.name: saturday
values.short-help: Run the extended self-test on a Saturday.

values.name: sunday
values.short-help: Run the extended self-test on a Sunday, the default.

values.name: thursday
values.short-help: Run the extended self-test on a Thursday.

values.name: tuesday
values.short-help: Run the extended self-test on a Tuesday.

values.name: wednesday
values.short-help: Run the extended self-test on a Wednesday.

children.description:
The last letter names the unit: h for hours, d for days, m for minutes
and s for seconds. A bare number is read as seconds. 7d is the default. A
shorter interval still waits for the day leaf, so the test runs once in
that week.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Interval between extended self-tests, for example 7d

children.description:
Ze starts the test at the first poll at or after this time on the named
day. The clock is the local time of the appliance. 03:00 is the default. Ze
skips the extended test while a short test is still running, and tries again
at the next poll.
children.name: time
children.short-help: Preferred time of day for extended self-tests (HH:MM)

children.description:
Ze starts the extended test at a poll where three conditions hold. The
weekday matches the day leaf, the time of day has passed, and the interval since
the last test has passed. The extended test takes a weekday of its own, and the
short test does not.
children.name: long
children.short-help: Extended self-test schedule

children.description:
The last letter names the unit: h for hours, d for days, m for minutes
and s for seconds. A bare number is read as seconds. 24h is the default, and
Ze keeps the default and logs a warning for a value it cannot read.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Interval between short self-tests, for example 24h

children.description:
Ze starts the test at the first poll of the day at or after this time,
and only when the interval has also passed. The clock is the local time of
the appliance. 02:00 is the default.
children.name: time
children.short-help: Preferred time of day for short self-tests (HH:MM)

children.description:
Ze starts the short test at a poll where two conditions hold. The interval
since the last test has passed, and the time of day has passed. The short test
needs no weekday, and the extended test does.
children.name: short
children.short-help: Short self-test schedule

children.description:
Ze decides at each health poll whether a test is due, so check-interval bounds
how close to the wanted time a test can start. Ze starts no test on a device that is
already running one, and tries again at the next poll.
children.name: self-test
children.short-help: Periodic SMART self-test scheduling

children.description:
A reading at or above this value raises the temp-critical error, and clears
the temp-high warning. 55 degrees is the default. Ze does not check that critical
is more than informational, so a critical value at or under informational hides
the informational warning completely.
children.name: critical
children.short-help: Temperature above which a critical error is raised

children.description:
Ze compares the reading against the reading of the previous poll. A rise of
this many degrees or more raises the temp-rising warning, and a smaller rise
clears it. The first poll of a device raises nothing, because no previous
reading exists. The range is 1 to 50 degrees, and 4 is the default.
children.name: difference
children.short-help: Temperature change threshold for rate-of-change alerts

children.description:
A reading at or above this value raises the temp-high warning, and a lower
reading clears it. 45 degrees is the default. Ze tests the critical value first,
so this warning never appears while the reading is also at or above critical.
children.name: informational
children.short-help: Temperature above which an informational warning is raised

children.description:
Ze reads the temperature at each poll and compares it against the three leaves.
A device that reports 0 degrees is read as having no reading, and Ze then raises
nothing for it.
children.name: temperature
children.short-help: Temperature alert thresholds in degrees Celsius

children.description:
Ze polls each ATA and NVMe device it finds, and turns SMART on for a device that
has it off. A reading past a threshold raises a warning or an error on the report bus,
and a reading back under the threshold clears it. show storage smart prints the last
reading of each device.
children.name: smart
children.short-help: SMART disk health monitoring and self-test scheduling

storage.description:
The container holds the smart block alone. Ze reads it at config load and at each
reload, and starts or stops the health manager to match.
storage.name: storage

children.description:
The leaf is mandatory, so Ze refuses a profile setting with no
value. Every interface unit that names this profile gets the
same value, because only the key carries the <iface>
placeholder.
children.name: value
children.short-help: Value to set for this key.

children.description:
The list holds 50 entries at most. Ze applies these settings to
each interface unit that names the profile, and it replaces <iface>
in each key with the name of that unit. One profile therefore
serves every interface.
children.name: setting
children.short-help: Kernel tunables in this profile.

children.description: A user-defined profile overrides a built-in profile that has the same name.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: A named collection of kernel tunables that Ze applies together to interface units.

children.description:
The leaf is mandatory, so Ze refuses a setting with no value. Ze
writes the text into the /proc/sys file of the key. A key Ze knows
is checked first: a bool key takes 0 or 1, and a range key takes an
integer inside its own bounds.
children.name: value
children.short-help: Value to set for this key.

children.description: The name uses kernel-native naming, for example net.ipv4.conf.all.forwarding.
children.name: setting
children.short-help: A kernel tunable that Ze sets persistently.

sysctl.description:
A setting entry applies to the host, and a profile entry applies to the
interface units that name the profile. Ze validates a key it knows against the type and the
range of that key. Ze accepts a key it does not know, and the kernel then
refuses a value it cannot take.
sysctl.name: sysctl

children.description:
The tokens are {name} for the config basename, {host},
{domain}, {date} as YYYYMMDD, {time} as HHMMSS, and
{archive} for the block name. Ze appends .conf.
children.name: filename
children.short-help: Filename format with token substitution.

children.description:
A file:// URL writes to the local filesystem. An http:// or
https:// URL uploads the config with an HTTP request.
children.name: location
children.short-help: Archive destination URL (file://, http://, https://).

children.description:
With true, Ze skips a daily or hourly archive when the
config did not change since the last one. The leaf changes
nothing for the commit trigger and the manual trigger.
children.name: on-change
children.short-help: Time-based only: skip if config unchanged since last archive.

children.description:
Ze gives up on an upload that passes this timeout. The
format is the Go duration format, such as 30s or 2m.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: HTTP upload timeout, in Go duration format, for example 30s.

children.description: The triggers are commit, manual, daily and hourly.
children.name: trigger
children.short-help: When to archive.

values.name: commit
values.short-help: Archive on every config commit.

values.name: daily
values.short-help: Archive once per day.

values.name: hourly
values.short-help: Archive once per hour.

values.name: manual
values.short-help: Archive only on explicit request.

children.description:
Each entry names one destination, and Ze writes a copy of the
config to every entry its trigger fires for.
children.name: archive
children.short-help: Named config archive destinations.

children.description:
RFC 2865 Section 4.1 and RFC 3579 Section 3.3 Note 1
permit one credential and never two, so ze sends
exactly one. Select chap only when the RADIUS server
holds the operator password in cleartext. RFC 2865
Section 2.2 states that 'CHAP requires that the user's
password be available in cleartext to the server so
that it can encrypt the CHAP challenge and compare that
to the CHAP response. If the password is not available
in cleartext to the RADIUS server then the server MUST
send an Access-Reject to the client.' A server that
stores password hashes cannot verify CHAP and rejects
every login. With pap the password is recoverable from
a captured request by anyone who holds the shared
secret, because Section 5.2 hides it with a reversible
XOR.
The two eap values run a full RADIUS/EAP conversation:
ze answers EAP itself, as the peer, with the password
the operator typed, and the server drives it through
Access-Challenge packets. eap-md5 carries the same
cleartext-password requirement as chap. eap-mschapv2
needs the server to hold the NT hash instead, which is
what an Active Directory backed server holds.
children.name: auth-method
children.short-help: Credential the Access-Request carries for an operator login.

values.name: chap
values.short-help: Send a CHAP-Password digest with the challenge in CHAP-Challenge.

values.name: eap-md5
values.short-help: Run an EAP MD5-Challenge conversation inside EAP-Message attributes.

values.name: eap-mschapv2
values.short-help: Run an EAP MS-CHAPv2 conversation inside EAP-Message attributes.

values.name: pap
values.short-help: Send the password in a User-Password attribute, hidden with the shared secret.

children.description:
This leaf is optional. Leave it unset when the RADIUS
server always names a profile through
profile-attribute. When the server does not name one,
and no default is set here, the login names no profile
and is denied. Ze never authorizes a user it cannot
attach a profile to.
children.name: default-profile
children.short-help: Ze authorization profiles used when the Access-Accept carries no profile-attribute.

children.description:
Filter-Id is the only value. RFC 2865 Section 5.25 says
of Class that 'the client MUST NOT interpret the
attribute locally', so ze cannot read a profile name
out of Class.
children.name: profile-attribute
children.short-help: Access-Accept reply attribute that names the user's ze authorization profiles.

values.name: filter-id
values.short-help: RADIUS Filter-Id (11), RFC 2865 Section 5.11

children.description:
The value counts the transmissions Ze sends to one
server, and not the retransmissions after the first.
With the default 3, Ze sends the Access-Request and
retransmits it twice before it moves to the next
server. The range is 0 to 10, and a configured 0 reaches
the client as 3, because the client reads 0 as unset.
The budget that bounds one login can then cancel the
exchange partway through those transmissions. The login
falls through to the local accounts, which is the answer
a slow server gets too. Read timeout for the wait
between the transmissions.
children.name: retries
children.short-help: Transmit attempts per server before failover

children.description:
RFC 2865 Section 3 states that the secret MUST NOT
be empty (length 0). An empty secret lets an
attacker forge packets.
children.name: key
children.short-help: RADIUS shared secret (RFC 2865).

children.description:
1812 is the port officially assigned to RADIUS.
RFC 2865 Section 3 states that 'Exactly one RADIUS
packet is encapsulated in the UDP Data field, where
the UDP Destination Port field indicates 1812
(decimal).' The range is 1 to 65535. Ze joins this
port to the server address and resolves the pair as
udp4. This block sends Access-Requests only, so it
addresses the authentication port, and no
accounting port is configured here.
children.name: port
children.short-help: UDP authentication port (default 1812)

children.description:
Ze sends the Access-Request to the first server, and it
moves to the next one when that server does not answer.
The order is the config order, because the list is
ordered-by user. Each server gets a new Identifier, a new
Request Authenticator, and the User-Password hidden again
under the key of that server. RFC 2865 Section 4.1
requires the new Request Authenticator: 'The Request
Authenticator value MUST be changed each time a new
Identifier is used.' Where every server fails, the AAA
chain moves on to the local accounts, so an unreachable
server never locks the operator out. A row that carries
no key builds no RADIUS backend at all, rather than a
shorter server list.
children.name: server
children.short-help: RADIUS servers, tried in configured order

children.description:
Ze binds the outbound udp4 socket to this address, so
every Access-Request leaves with it as the source. An
IPv4 address here is also sent as NAS-IP-Address
(RFC 2865 Section 4.1). Where the leaf is absent, the
kernel picks the address of the outgoing interface and
no NAS-IP-Address is sent. NAS-Identifier carries the
hostname of this device either way, so the request
meets Section 4.1 with the leaf unset. An address this
host does not hold refuses the bind, and Ze logs the
failure. The RADIUS backend then contributes nothing,
and login falls through to the local accounts.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IP for outbound RADIUS requests

children.description:
The value bounds the wait for one answer from one
server. Each wait after a miss doubles the one before
it. The default 3 therefore waits 3 seconds, then 6,
then 12, across the three transmissions the default
retries allows. The range is 1 to 60 seconds. The time
one login spends on RADIUS is capped at 2 minutes,
whatever timeout and retries hold. The login then falls
through to the local accounts.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: Per-server request timeout in seconds

children.description:
This block is separate from the L2TP subscriber RADIUS
path, which lives under the l2tp root.
children.name: radius
children.short-help: RADIUS servers for operator login over SSH, web and MCP (RFC 2865).

children.description:
Set it true and Ze sends an accounting record for each
command a user runs. One background worker sends the
records, so a slow server does not delay the command.
The queue holds 64 records, and Ze counts each record it
drops because the queue is full. That count is what
shows a server which cannot keep up.
children.name: accounting
children.short-help: Enable command execution accounting

children.description:
The default false authorizes each command from the local
profiles alone and sends the server nothing. Set it true
and Ze sends an AUTHOR REQUEST for each command, with
service=shell, cmd=<verb> and one cmd-arg for each
argument (RFC 8907 Section 6). PASS_ADD and PASS_REPL
run the command, and FAIL refuses it. Ze sends privilege
level 1 on every one of these requests.
children.name: authorization
children.short-help: Enable per-command TACACS+ authorization

children.description:
The key is the shared secret RFC 8907 Section 4.5
builds the MD5 pseudo-pad from, and both ends must
hold the same value. A client with no secret has no
conformant packet to send. Section 10.5.2 requires
a shared secret and forbids a client to set
TAC_PLUS_UNENCRYPTED_FLAG. Omitting the key refuses
a commit, through the AAA rebuild rather than
through the schema: a missing mandatory field is
only a warning. At BOOT the same failure is logged
and this backend is DROPPED from the chain. A user
who exists locally still logs in, and the local
profiles still govern the command. The leaf is
marked
sensitive, so every display path prints a
placeholder. A $9$-encoded value written by hand is
decoded on read, and the commit path writes back
what you typed.
children.name: key
children.short-help: Shared secret this server obfuscates its packets with

children.description:
Port 49 is the port IANA assigns to TACACS+, and
RFC 8907 Section 3.4 names it. Ze opens one TCP
connection to this port and reuses it where the
server agrees to the single-connect flag. The type
sets no lower bound, so a commit takes 0 and every
connection to that server then fails.
children.name: port
children.short-help: TCP port (default 49)

children.description:
Ze tries the servers in the order you write them and
moves to the next one when a connection or an exchange
fails. The order is the config order, because the list
is ordered-by user. Where every server fails, the AAA
chain moves on to the local backend, so the local
accounts still answer.
children.name: server
children.short-help: TACACS+ servers, tried in configured order

children.description:
Ze binds the local end of the outbound TCP connection to
this address. Use it where the TACACS+ server accepts
one address for this device, for example a loopback
address. Where the leaf is absent, the kernel picks the
address of the outgoing interface.
children.name: source-address
children.short-help: Source IP for outbound TACACS+ connections

children.description:
The leaf decides one case: the server did not answer, or
it answered ERROR or a status Ze does not know. The
default false then authorizes the command from the local
profiles, so a server outage does not lock the operator
out. Set it true and Ze refuses the command instead.
Neither value changes a FAIL from the server, which
always refuses the command. The leaf reaches nothing
while authorization is false.
children.name: strict-fallback
children.short-help: Deny authorization when TACACS+ is unavailable instead of falling back to local RBAC

children.description:
The value bounds two things for each server: the TCP
connect, and the read of one exchange. Ze gives it to
net.Dialer.Timeout and to the deadline of the
connection. With four servers and the default 5, a full
failover takes at most 20 seconds before the AAA chain
reaches the local backend.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: Per-server connection timeout in seconds

children.description:
The TACACS+ backend joins the AAA chain at priority 100, in
front of the local backend at priority 200. Ze builds the
backend only where the server list holds one entry or more,
so a container with no server leaves the chain unchanged.
Authentication runs as soon as one server exists. The
authorization leaf and the accounting leaf each turn on
their own half.
children.name: tacacs
children.short-help: TACACS+ server configuration (RFC 8907)

children.description:
A level mapped to no profiles would authenticate the
user and grant nothing. Authorization reads an empty
profile set as 'no opinion' rather than 'deny'. To
deny a privilege level, leave the level out of the
mapping.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: Ze authorization profiles for this privilege level. At least one is required.

children.description:
The list turns the privilege level Ze resolves for a
session into the ze authorization profiles of that session.
A level with no entry here denies the login, so this mapping
is what grants access, and not the PASS from the server. Ze
also removes a reserved profile name from the set, and a
level that then resolves to nothing denies the login too.
children.name: tacacs-profile
children.short-help: Maps TACACS+ privilege level to ze authorization profile

children.description:
The canonical form carries a cost prefix, for
example $2a$10$ before the salt and the digest.
Write the plaintext password to plaintext-password.
On commit, ze hashes that value into this leaf and
then discards the plaintext.
children.name: password
children.short-help: Bcrypt-hashed password, in canonical form.

children.description:
On commit, the config system hashes this value with
bcrypt into the canonical password leaf, and it
removes this leaf from the tree. Ze never writes the
value to the config file. A display path renders the
secret placeholder in its place.
children.name: plaintext-password
children.short-help: Write-only plaintext password.

children.description:
Authorization profile names assigned to this user. A commit rejects a name that no profile
under system authorization defines, and it rejects a reserved name. Once one profile
exists, a user with no name here authenticates and is then denied every command.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: Authorization profile name(s) assigned to this user

children.description:
The value is the middle field of an SSH public key line.
It carries no type prefix and no comment suffix.
children.name: key
children.short-help: Base64-encoded public key data.

children.description:
The algorithm is the first field of an SSH public key line,
such as ssh-ed25519.
children.name: type
children.short-help: SSH public key algorithm.

values.name: ecdsa-sha2-nistp256
values.short-help: An ECDSA key on the NIST P-256 curve.

values.name: ecdsa-sha2-nistp384
values.short-help: An ECDSA key on the NIST P-384 curve.

values.name: ecdsa-sha2-nistp521
values.short-help: An ECDSA key on the NIST P-521 curve.

values.name: ssh-ed25519
values.short-help: An Ed25519 key.

values.name: ssh-rsa
values.short-help: An RSA key.

children.description:
Ze joins the type and the key of each entry into one authorized_keys
line. A client key that equals any entry of this user authenticates
that user. A key that does not parse is logged and skipped, and the
other keys of the user still match. A user that carries a key and no
profile authenticates, and the authorizer then decides what they can
run.
children.name: public-keys
children.short-help:
SSH public keys for key-based authentication.
Each entry is a named key (e.g. user@host).

children.description:
Authenticated user (local). Each entry is one local account. password carries the bcrypt hash
the login compares against, and profile names the authorization profiles the account carries.
A commit rejects an entry whose name is reserved for a built-in identity.
children.name: user
children.short-help: Authenticated user (local)

children.description:
System authentication settings. The user list under it holds the local accounts, which the local
AAA backend reads. That backend runs after TACACS+ in the chain, so it answers when the remote
server is unreachable. A configuration with no user rejects every local login.
children.name: authentication
children.short-help: System authentication settings

children.description:
Action when no entry of this section matches the command. Ze reads the value allow,
and it leaves the section at deny for every other state, the absent leaf included. A
user who carries several profiles falls back to the default of the first profile whose
section was reached.
children.name: default-action
children.short-help: Action when no entry matches

values.name: allow
values.short-help: Permit a command that no entry of this section matches.

values.name: deny
values.short-help: Refuse a command that no entry of this section matches.

children.description:
Authorization action for a command this entry matches. Ze reads the value allow, and
it leaves the entry at deny for every other state, the absent leaf included. The
first matching entry decides, so a deny stops the search even where a later entry
allows.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Authorization action

values.name: allow
values.short-help: Permit the command this entry matches and stop the search.

values.name: deny
values.short-help: Refuse the command this entry matches and stop the search.

children.description:
Command path prefix, or a regular expression when regex is true. A prefix
comparison ignores case and stops at a word boundary. 'show bgp' therefore matches
'show bgp' and 'show bgp summary', and it does not match 'show bgpx'. An empty match
is rejected at commit. A match that names no command Ze knows is logged as a
warning and kept, because a plugin can register its commands later.
children.name: match
children.short-help: Command path prefix or regex pattern

children.description:
If true, match is a regular expression. Ze compiles the pattern at commit and
rejects one it cannot compile. The pattern is not anchored, so it matches anywhere
inside the command text. Write ^ and $ where the whole command has to match. A regex
entry is case sensitive, unlike a prefix entry.
children.name: regex
children.short-help: If true, match is a regular expression

children.description:
Ordered authorization entry. Ze sorts the entries of the section by number and takes
the action of the first one that matches. A command that matches no entry falls to
default-action. An entry with an empty match is rejected at commit.
children.name: entry
children.short-help: Ordered authorization entry

children.description: Configuration command authorization, which is the set of commands that change the config. Ze evaluates this section for every command the dispatcher does not mark read-only.
children.name: edit
children.short-help: Configuration command authorization (write commands)

children.description:
Action when no entry of this section matches the command. Ze reads the value allow,
and it leaves the section at deny for every other state, the absent leaf included. A
user who carries several profiles falls back to the default of the first profile whose
section was reached.
children.name: default-action
children.short-help: Action when no entry matches

Ordered authorization entry. Ze sorts the entries of the section by number and takes

children.name: entry
children.short-help: Ordered authorization entry

children.description: Operational command authorization, which is the set of read-only commands. Ze evaluates this section when the dispatcher marks the command read-only, and the edit section for every other command.
children.name: run
children.short-help: Operational command authorization (read-only commands)

children.description:
Named authorization profile with a run section and an edit section. A user can carry several
profiles. Ze takes the action of the first profile that holds a matching entry. When no entry
of any profile matches, the section default of the first profile applies.
children.name: profile
children.short-help: Named authorization profile with run and edit sections

children.description:
Profile-based command authorization. Ze builds the authorization store only when this container
holds at least one profile. With no profile written, no store exists and every authenticated
user runs every command. The first profile therefore changes the answer for every user, and a
user with no profile assigned is denied from that point.

A backend that FAILS TO BUILD is dropped and the chain composes without it, so these
profiles still govern where the local backend survived. Where every backend fails,
nothing authenticates and every command is refused.
children.name: authorization
children.short-help: Profile-based command authorization

children.description:
After each archive write, Ze prunes the files beyond this
count, oldest first. 0 disables the pruning and keeps every
file. The count applies to a file:// archive only, and Ze
never prunes an HTTP archive.
children.name: commit-revisions
children.short-help: Maximum number of config archive files kept per file:// location.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_acct. The
counters cost memory per flow, so the kernel keeps them off
until they are asked for.
children.name: accounting
children.short-help: Enable per-connection byte/packet counters (nf_conntrack_acct).

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_checksum.
The kernel then drops a packet whose checksum is wrong
before it tracks the flow.
children.name: checksum
children.short-help: Enable conntrack checksum verification (nf_conntrack_checksum).

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_expect_max. An expectation is the
second flow a helper predicts, such as an FTP data
connection.
children.name: expect-max
children.short-help: Maximum expected connections (nf_conntrack_expect_max).

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_buckets.
More buckets shorten each hash chain, and cost more memory.
children.name: hash-size
children.short-help: Conntrack hash table buckets (nf_conntrack_buckets).

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_log_invalid. The values are all,
tcp, udp, icmp and icmpv6.
children.name: log-invalid
children.short-help: Log invalid packets for the specified protocol (nf_conntrack_log_invalid).

The leaf-list only loads a module. Removing a module from

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max. The
table holds no more flows than this, and a new flow past the
bound is dropped.
children.name: table-size
children.short-help: Maximum conntrack table entries (nf_conntrack_max).

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_be_liberal. With true the
kernel tracks a packet outside the window rather than
marking it INVALID.
children.name: be-liberal
children.short-help: Accept out-of-window packets for established connections.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_ignore_invalid_rst. With
true the kernel drops such a RST rather than closing the
flow on it.
children.name: ignore-invalid-rst
children.short-help: Ignore RST packets with invalid sequence numbers.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_loose. With true the
kernel picks up a flow whose handshake it never saw.
children.name: loose
children.short-help: Allow tracking connections started before conntrack loaded.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_tcp_max_retrans. The kernel
marks the flow INVALID past this many retransmissions.
children.name: max-retrans
children.short-help: Maximum retransmissions before marking connection invalid.

children.description:
The container holds the four TCP flags, and Ze writes each
one to its net.netfilter key.
children.name: tcp
children.short-help: TCP connection tracking behavior flags.

children.description:

net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_dccp_timeout_closereq. It

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_dccp_timeout_closing. It
bounds a connection that is closing.

children.short-help: Closing timeout (seconds).

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_dccp_timeout_open. An
idle open connection leaves the table after this

children.description:
Ze writes the value to

bounds a connection that is half open.

directions.
children.name: stream
children.short-help: Stream timeout (seconds).

children.description:
Ze writes the value to
net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_udp_timeout. It bounds a
UDP flow that has seen traffic in one direction.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: Default timeout (seconds).

children.description:
The container holds the two UDP timeouts, and Ze writes
each one to its net.netfilter key.
children.name: udp
children.short-help: UDP connection tracking timeouts.

children.description:
The container holds one sub-container per protocol. Ze
writes each leaf to its own net.netfilter timeout key.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: Connection tracking timeouts per protocol.

children.description:
Ze writes the value to net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_timestamp.
The kernel then records the start time of each flow.
children.name: timestamp
children.short-help: Enable per-connection timestamps (nf_conntrack_timestamp).

children.description:
The container holds the helper modules to load, the table
bounds, the protocol timeouts and the TCP behavior flags. Ze
writes each one to its net.netfilter sysctl key.
children.name: conntrack
children.short-help: Connection tracking (conntrack) module loading, table tuning, and timeout configuration.

children.description:
The rates are 9600, 19200, 38400, 57600 and 115200 baud.
The default is 115200.
children.name: speed
children.short-help: Baud rate (default 115200).

values.short-help: 19200 baud.
38400 baud.
57600 baud.
9600 baud.

children.description:
Each entry names one serial device, and it carries the baud
rate of that device.
children.name: device
children.short-help: Serial device to configure as console.

children.description:
The container holds the serial devices Ze runs a console on. A
headless device has no other way in when the network is down.
children.name: console
children.short-help: Serial console configuration for headless CPE devices.

children.description:
Ze reads the record the kernel left, writes it into the crash
directory as a kernel-kind report, and clears the region so
the next fault has room. Run 'show crashes' to read whether
the running kernel is armed as well as configured.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Store the kernel panic record as a crash report at the next boot.

children.description:
Refused on a build that cannot stage a capture kernel,
which today means anything other than amd64. Reported as
configured but not armed when the crash directory has
less free space than the image needs, with the shortfall
in bytes.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Capture a full memory image as well as the panic backtrace.

children.description:
The capture kernel runs after the fault and needs its own
memory, separate from the region holding the backtrace.
The range is 64 to 1024 megabytes. It is a floor on the
space estimate: the image itself is sized to RAM.
children.name: reserve
children.short-help: Memory reserved for the capture kernel that writes the image.

children.description:
A backtrace names the faulting subsystem, which is what a bug
report needs. A memory image is sized to RAM and costs the
write time while the router is down, so it is off by default
and reported as unarmed until the target has room for it.
children.name: memory-image
children.short-help: Full memory image capture, for a fault a backtrace does not explain.

children.description:
The region is taken from RAM on every boot, so it is sized for
a backtrace rather than for a memory image. The range is 4 to
256 megabytes and the default of 16 holds a full backtrace.
The appliance build renders the size onto the kernel command
line, so a change takes effect at the next image build.
children.name: reserve
children.short-help: Memory the kernel reserves to write its panic record into.

children.description:
A Go panic is already captured. This container covers the kernel
panic, which leaves no process behind to write a report. The
kernel writes its own record into a reserved memory region, and
Ze reads it on the next boot. The reservation is a kernel boot
argument, so it is armed by the next boot of an image built with
image.crash-dump, not by the commit.
children.name: crash-dump
children.short-help: Kernel crash capture, kept across a reboot and listed by show crashes.

children.description:
The cache holds this many answers at most, and 0 disables
it. The range is 0 to 1000000, and the default is 10000.
children.name: cache-size
children.short-help: Maximum cached entries (0 disables caching).

children.description:
Ze holds an answer for the TTL the response carries, and
never longer than this value. 0 keeps the response TTL
alone. The default is 86400 seconds.
children.name: cache-ttl
children.short-help: Maximum cache TTL in seconds (0 uses response TTL only).

children.description:
RFC 4035 defines the stub model. off leaves resolution
unchanged. permissive and strict set the EDNS0 DO bit, and
rely on a validating upstream (CD=0) to answer SERVFAIL on a
broken chain. strict rejects such an answer as an error.
permissive logs it and returns the empty result. An insecure
zone and an unsigned zone (NOERROR, AD=0) are always
accepted.
children.name: dnssec-validation
children.short-help: Upstream-answer DNSSEC validation for the stub resolver.

values.name: off
values.short-help: No DNSSEC handling, and no DO bit. This is the default.

values.name: permissive
values.short-help: Request DNSSEC, and log a broken chain without failing.

values.name: strict
values.short-help: Request DNSSEC, and reject an answer on a broken chain.

children.description:
The default /tmp/resolv.conf suits gokrazy, whose rootfs is
read-only. Set /etc/resolv.conf on standard Linux. An empty
string stops Ze writing the file.
children.name: resolv-conf-path
children.short-help: Path Ze writes the DNS servers to, as a resolv.conf file.

children.description:
Ze waits this long for an answer before it gives up on a
query. The range is 1 to 60 seconds, and the default is 5.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: Query timeout in seconds.

children.description:
The container holds the resolv.conf path, the query timeout, the
cache bounds and the DNSSEC validation mode.
children.name: dns
children.short-help: DNS resolver tuning and resolv.conf settings.

children.description:
Ze expands a $ENV_VAR reference in the value when it reads the
config.
children.name: domain
children.short-help: System domain, supports $ENV_VAR expansion.

children.description:
Ze expands a $ENV_VAR reference in the value when it reads the
config.
children.name: host
children.short-help: System hostname, supports $ENV_VAR expansion.

children.description:
Ze writes each address to the resolv.conf file named by
dns/resolv-conf-path, and its own resolver asks these servers.
children.name: name-server
children.short-help: Static DNS name servers, written to resolv.conf and used by ze internal resolver.

children.description:
Ze multiplies the PeeringDB prefix count by this margin, in
percent, and uses the result as the prefix limit. The range
is 0 to 100, and the default is 10.
children.name: margin
children.short-help: Percentage margin above PeeringDB count for prefix maximum (0-100).

children.description:
Ze sends each query to this base URL. The default is
https://www.peeringdb.com. Set another URL to reach a mirror
or a test server.
children.name: url
children.short-help: PeeringDB-compatible API base URL.

children.description:
The container holds the API base URL and the prefix-limit
margin. Ze asks PeeringDB for the prefix counts of a peer.
children.name: peeringdb
children.short-help: PeeringDB API configuration for prefix data lookups.

children.description:
Ze reads the file with one GET, and the URL carries the
scheme, the host and the path of that one file. A
mirror publishes five files, so it takes five blocks.
children.name: url
children.short-help: URL Ze reads this registry's delegation file from.

children.description:
One block names one registry and the URL its delegation
file is read from. A registry with no block is read from
the file that registry publishes, so mirroring one
registry takes one block.
children.name: delegation-source
children.short-help: Per-registry source of the delegation file.

children.description:
The container holds one delegation-source block per registry.
`update resolve rir` reads the delegation file of every
registry, and a block names where one of the five is read
from.
children.name: rir
children.short-help: Regional Internet Registry delegation table settings.

children.description:
Ze writes the governor to every core. The values are
performance, powersave, ondemand, conservative and
schedutil.
children.name: governor
children.short-help: CPU scaling governor applied to all cores.

values.name: conservative
values.short-help: Gradual frequency scaling.

values.name: ondemand
values.short-help: Dynamic frequency scaling.

values.name: performance
values.short-help: Maximum frequency.

values.name: powersave
values.short-help: Minimum frequency.

values.name: schedutil
values.short-help: Scheduler-driven frequency scaling.

children.description:
The container holds the scaling governor Ze writes to each
core.
children.name: cpu
children.short-help: CPU frequency scaling tuning.

children.description:
Ze asks the driver for a receive ring of this many
descriptors. The range is 1 to 65535, and a driver
refuses a size it cannot serve.
children.name: rx
children.short-help: Receive ring buffer size.

children.description:
Ze asks the driver for a transmit ring of this many
descriptors. The range is 1 to 65535, and a driver
refuses a size it cannot serve.
children.name: tx
children.short-help: Transmit ring buffer size.

children.description:
The container holds the receive ring size and the
transmit ring size of the interface.
children.name: ring
children.short-help: Ring buffer sizes.

children.description:
Each entry names one interface and holds the ethtool
settings Ze applies to it.
children.name: ethtool
children.short-help: Per-interface ethtool settings.

children.description:
The list takes a single CPU, a comma-separated set, and
a range with a hyphen.
children.name: cpus
children.short-help: CPU list, for example 0,2,4-7.

children.description:
Each entry names one interface, and Ze pins the IRQs of that
interface to the CPUs the entry lists.
children.name: irq-affinity
children.short-help: Pin NIC IRQs to specific CPUs.

children.description:
The container holds the CPU governor, the IRQ affinity list and
the ethtool settings. The tuning runs on Linux, and it needs
root or CAP_SYS_ADMIN.
children.name: tuning
children.short-help: Runtime hardware tuning applied at startup and on config commit.

children.description:
With true, Ze downloads, verifies and stages a binary
update on a platform Ze manages. With false, Ze only
checks the version and reports it.
children.name: auto-apply
children.short-help: Download, verify, and stage a Ze binary update without an operator.

children.description:
Ze checks the version once in this interval. The range is 60
to 604800 seconds, and the default is 86400, which is one
day.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Check interval in seconds (default 86400 = daily, minimum 60).

children.description:
The end is not part of the window: Ze stages at start and at
every minute up to end, and not at end itself. Ze refuses a
value that is not HH:MM.
children.name: end
children.short-help: End time HH:MM in local time.

children.description:
Ze refuses a value that is not HH:MM, with an hour of 0 to 23
and a minute of 0 to 59. A start later than end makes the
window cross midnight, so 22:00 to 02:00 is four hours.
children.name: start
children.short-help: Start time HH:MM in local time.

children.description:
Ze reads the window only when start and end both carry a time. Ze
downloads and verifies at any hour, and it waits for the window
before it replaces the binary. Outside the window Ze reports that
the update waits, and it keeps the verified file.
children.name: maintenance-window
children.short-help: Time window when binary replacement may occur. Download and verification proceed at any time.

children.description:
The leaf is empty, so writing it is the whole instruction. Ze
waits 5 seconds after it stages the binary and then runs the
new one. Ze refuses a configuration that carries both immediate
and time.
children.name: immediate
children.short-help: Restart automatically after staging (5s drain delay). Mutually exclusive with time.

children.description:
Ze stages the binary as soon as the maintenance window permits,
then waits for this time of day to run it. A time outside the
maintenance window is permitted, and Ze logs a warning that
names both. Ze refuses a configuration that carries both
immediate and time.
children.name: time
children.short-help: Daily restart time, HH:MM in local time. Mutually exclusive with immediate.

children.description:
An absent container leaves the restart to the operator.
The container with immediate restarts after a short drain.
The container with time restarts at that time each day.
children.name: restart
children.short-help: What Ze does after it stages an update.

children.description:
Ze waits for the delay after it detects a new version, so
that many routers do not download at the same second. 0
disables the spread.
children.name: spread
children.short-help: Maximum random delay in seconds before the download starts.

children.description:
One answer is {"version":"26.05.17"}. Ze compares that
value against its own release version, in lexicographic
order.
children.name: url
children.short-help: HTTPS URL that serves a JSON object with a 'version' field.

children.description: On gokrazy, gokrazy manages the image updates.
children.name: update-check
children.short-help: System version check and platform update settings.

system.description:
The container holds the system-wide settings. This module attaches the local user accounts under
authentication, and the command authorization profiles under authorization.
system.name: system

children.description:
Ze asks for no credentials while this leaf is false, and
false is the default.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Require HTTP Basic Authentication on the metrics and health endpoints.

children.description:
Ze compares the password of each request with this hash, and it
compares the username in constant time. A value that is not a
bcrypt hash stops the metrics server with an error, and the
config check warns about it at commit. With basic-auth enabled,
a username and this password are both required.
children.name: password
children.short-help: Bcrypt-hashed HTTP Basic Authentication password. Write plaintext via plaintext-password.

children.description:
On commit, the config system hashes this value into
password and removes this leaf. The value is never
written to the config file, and a display path renders
the secret placeholder for it.
children.name: plaintext-password
children.short-help: Write-only password.

children.description:
A client shows the realm to the user when it asks for
the credentials. The default is 'ze prometheus'.
children.name: realm
children.short-help: HTTP Basic Authentication realm.

children.description: The username pairs with the password leaf beside it.
children.name: username
children.short-help: HTTP Basic Authentication username.

children.description:
The container holds the enable switch, the realm, the
username and the two password leaves.
children.name: basic-auth
children.short-help: HTTP Basic Authentication for the Prometheus service.

children.description:
With false, Ze runs every other collector and stops this
one. The default is true.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable or disable this collector.

children.description:
The range is 1 to 60 seconds. An absent leaf gives the
collector the interval of the netdata container. The leaf lives
under a deprecated list, so write netdata/collector/interval
instead.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Override sampling interval for this collector (seconds). Inherits global interval if not set.

children.description:
Write netdata/collector instead. Ze reads this list only when the
netdata container carries no collector list, and it then logs the
deprecated path it read. A netdata collector list replaces this one
whole, and the two are never merged.
children.name: collector
children.short-help: Deprecated: use netdata/collector. Per-Netdata-collector overrides (enable/disable, interval).

children.description:
Ze serves no metrics endpoint while this leaf is false, and
false is the default.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the Prometheus metrics endpoint.

children.description:
Write netdata/interval instead. Ze reads this leaf only when the
netdata container carries no interval leaf, and it then logs the
deprecated path it read. The range is 1 to 60 seconds and the
default is 1.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Deprecated: use netdata/interval. Netdata-compatible OS collector sampling interval in seconds.

children.description:
With false, Ze runs every other collector and stops this
one. The default is true.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable or disable this Netdata-compatible OS collector.

children.description:
When this leaf is not set, the collector uses the global
Netdata interval.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Override the sampling interval of this collector, in seconds.

children.description:
Each entry names one collector, and it overrides the settings of
that collector alone.
children.name: collector
children.short-help: Per-Netdata-collector overrides of the enable state and the interval.

children.description:
With false, Ze exports the Ze-native metrics alone. The
default is true.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable the Netdata-compatible OS collectors.

children.description:
Each Netdata-compatible OS collector samples the operating
system once in this interval. The range is 1 to 60 seconds, and
the default is 1.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Netdata-compatible OS collector sampling interval in seconds.

children.description:
Ze puts the prefix in front of each Netdata-compatible OS
collector metric name. It does not change a Ze-native metric
name. The default is netdata.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Metric name prefix for Netdata-compatible OS collector metrics only.

children.description:
The default of enabled is true, so an absent container still runs
the collectors. The three settings under it replace the deprecated
prefix, interval and collector leaves beside this container. Ze
reads a deprecated leaf only when the matching leaf here is absent,
and it logs the path it read.
children.name: netdata
children.short-help: Netdata-compatible OS collector metrics. These settings do not affect Ze-native metrics.

children.description:
A scraper reads the metrics at this path on each listen
endpoint. The default path is /metrics.
children.name: path
children.short-help: HTTP path of the metrics endpoint.

children.description:
The leaf sets the metric name prefix for Netdata-compatible
OS collector metrics only.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Deprecated: use netdata/prefix.

children.description:
The listener binds this address. 0.0.0.0 binds every IPv4 address of
the host, and :: binds every IPv6 address. Config validation refuses
two listeners that share a protocol and a port when their addresses
overlap. A wildcard address overlaps every address of its own family,
and an IPv4 address never overlaps an IPv6 address.
children.name: ip
children.short-help: Listen IP address

children.description:
The port range is 0 to 65535. Port 0 makes the operating system pick a
free port at bind time, so no client can know the port before the
listener starts. ze doctor tries to bind each configured endpoint and
reports the one the host refuses.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Listen TCP port; 0 means OS-assigned

children.description:
Each entry names one listen endpoint. The default endpoint
is 127.0.0.1 on port 9273.
children.name: server
children.short-help: Prometheus listen endpoints.

children.description:
The container holds the enable switch, the listen endpoints, the
metrics path, the HTTP Basic Authentication settings and the
collector settings.
children.name: prometheus
children.short-help: Prometheus metrics HTTP export.

telemetry.description:
The container holds the Prometheus export settings and the Netdata-
compatible collector settings.
telemetry.name: telemetry

children.description:
The default backend is tc, the queueing disciplines of Linux iproute2.
Another backend declares itself through traffic.RegisterBackend. The ze:backend YANG
extension on a feature node declares which backend supports that feature. The
commit-time gate reads that extension and rejects a config that names a qdisc or a
filter type the backend does not support.
children.name: backend
children.short-help: Traffic control backend that programs the queueing disciplines.

children.description: An absent leaf takes the value of the rate leaf.
children.name: ceil
children.short-help: Largest rate this class can reach.

children.description:
A mark filter takes a hex value. A dscp filter
takes a DSCP name. A protocol filter takes a protocol name.
children.name: value
children.short-help: Value the filter matches.

children.description:
The list key is the match type, so one class carries at
most one match of each type.
children.name: match
children.short-help: A filter that classifies a packet into this class.

children.description: The value 0 is the highest priority.
children.name: priority
children.short-help: Scheduling priority of this class.

children.description:
The value is a number and a unit, for example 10mbit
or 100kbps.
children.name: rate
children.short-help: Rate this class is guaranteed.

children.description:
The list key is the class name. A class carries a rate, a
ceil, a priority, and the filters that select its traffic.
children.name: class
children.short-help: One traffic class of the queueing discipline.

children.description:
The value is the name of a class in the class list of this
qdisc.
children.name: default-class
children.short-help: Name of the class that takes the unclassified traffic.

children.description:
The commit-time gate rejects a type the configured backend
does not support.
children.name: type
children.short-help: Type of the queueing discipline.

values.name: fq
values.short-help: The Fair Queue qdisc.

values.name: fq_codel
values.short-help: The Fair Queue Controlled Delay qdisc.

values.name: hfsc
values.short-help: The Hierarchical Fair Service Curve qdisc.

values.name: htb
values.short-help: The Hierarchical Token Bucket qdisc.

values.name: netem
values.short-help: The Network Emulator qdisc.

values.name: prio
values.short-help: The Priority qdisc.

values.name: sfq
values.short-help: The Stochastic Fair Queue qdisc.

values.name: tbf
values.short-help: The Token Bucket Filter qdisc.

children.description:
Ze attaches this qdisc at the root of the interface, and every
class hangs beneath it.
children.name: qdisc
children.short-help: The root queueing discipline of the interface.

children.description: The list key is the interface name.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Traffic control of one named interface.

children.description:
One entry exists for each interface Ze programs. The backend leaf
names the program that applies the entries.
children.name: control
children.short-help: Traffic control configuration of each interface.

children.description:
The default false attaches nothing and starts no poll loop. Set it true and
the config also needs one enabled interface or more under interfaces. Without
one, the commit is refused and the error names the missing interface list. An accounting
that would report nothing never reaches the kernel.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable traffic-usage accounting.

children.description:
The default true accounts on the interface, so an entry with no
body needs nothing more. Set it false and Ze drops the entry before it
attaches anything. The accounting on that interface stops, and the rest
of the list is not touched. To stop the whole feature, use the enabled
leaf under usage.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Account traffic on this interface.

children.description:
The leaf overrides the max-entries leaf under usage for this
interface alone, and an unset leaf takes the global value. The value is
the capacity of each LRU map of the interface, so it also sets the
memory the interface costs. An effective value of 0 is refused at
commit. A change makes Ze attach the eBPF programs again, because a map
takes its capacity at creation.
children.name: max-entries
children.short-help: Override the global max-entries (per-map LRU capacity) for this interface (inherits when unset).

children.description:
0 disables the cleanup for this interface. When the leaf is unset, this interface inherits the
global stale-timeout.
children.name: stale-timeout
children.short-help: Override the global stale-timeout for this interface, in milliseconds.

children.description:
The leaf overrides the track-ip leaf under usage for this interface
alone, and an unset leaf takes the global value. True adds two more LRU
maps to this interface, one for ingress and one for egress, keyed by
IPv4 address. A change makes Ze attach the eBPF programs again, because
the map set changes.
children.name: track-ip
children.short-help: Override the global track-ip for this interface (inherits the global value when unset).

children.description:
The entry names one interface and can override three leaves of the
usage container: track-ip, stale-timeout and max-entries. What the entry
does not set, it takes from the leaf of the same name under usage. An entry
with a name and no body is accounted with every global value. A change to
track-ip or to max-entries makes Ze detach the eBPF programs and attach them
again, because both decide the shape of the maps.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: Per-interface traffic-usage accounting.

children.description:
Ze accounts on the interfaces listed here and on no other. An interface
with no entry is not accounted, and an entry whose enabled leaf is false is
dropped before the attach. With usage enabled and this list empty, the commit is
refused.
children.name: interfaces
children.short-help: Interfaces to account on.

children.description:
One poll loop reads every map of every accounted interface at this period,
so the value sets how fresh a metric series is. The default 1000 reads once a
second. A value outside 100 milliseconds to 1 hour is refused at commit. The
eBPF programs count at line rate whatever this value is, so a longer interval
loses no bytes.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: Map poll interval in milliseconds (100ms..1h).

children.description:
The value is the capacity of each LRU map, and an interface takes it unless
its own max-entries leaf overrides it. Ze creates two maps for each accounted
interface, and two more where track-ip is true, so the value sets the memory the
accounting costs. Beyond the capacity the kernel evicts the least recently used
entry, which keeps the top talkers and loses the quiet ones.
children.name: max-entries
children.short-help: Per-map LRU capacity; least-recently-used entries are evicted beyond this, keeping top talkers.

children.description:
Ze removes a metric series it has not seen within this time, which stops
the series of a talker that left from staying forever. The value 0 disables the
cleanup, so every series stays until the plugin stops. An interface can
override the value with its own stale-timeout leaf. An interface value that is
not 0 and less than 1 second is refused at commit.
children.name: stale-timeout
children.short-help: Remove a metric series unseen within this many milliseconds; 0 disables cleanup.

children.description:
The address is the source address on ingress and the destination address on egress. The default is
false, which limits the number of metric series.
children.name: track-ip
children.short-help: Account bytes per IPv4 address as well as per interface.

children.description:
Ze attaches two eBPF programs to each accounted interface with TCX, one on
ingress and one on egress. They count bytes into per-interface LRU hash maps, keyed
by L4 port and protocol. Where track-ip is true they also key by IPv4 address. One
poll loop reads the maps and publishes the counts as metric series. The programs
count only: they drop no packet and they change none.
children.name: usage
children.short-help: Per-interface eBPF TCX byte accounting (port/protocol always; per-IP via track-ip).

traffic.description:
Two subtrees sit under it, and they are independent. control programs the
queueing disciplines of each interface, which decides which packet leaves first. usage
counts bytes with an eBPF program, and it changes no packet. Each subtree comes from its
own plugin, so removing one plugin removes that subtree alone.
traffic.name: traffic
traffic.short-help: Traffic subsystem: QoS control and byte-usage accounting.

children.description:
Number of half-open IKE SAs tolerated before an inbound
IKE_SA_INIT must answer a COOKIE challenge. RFC 7296
Section 2.6 makes the challenge the answer to state and CPU
exhaustion from forged source addresses. The default of 0
challenges every inbound initiation, which costs one extra
round trip and stops a single spoofed datagram taking a
peer's only half-open handshake slot. Raise it to tolerate
that many half-open handshakes before challenging.
children.name: cookie-threshold
children.short-help: Number of half-open IKE SAs tolerated before a COOKIE challenge.

children.description:
The Child SA rekey trigger sits ahead of the lifetime by the larger of a
random 10 percent and one retransmit budget. That lead is capped at half the
lifetime. RFC 7296 Section 2.8 states the rule. 'When the lifetime of a
Security Association expires, the Security Association MUST NOT be used.' Ze
therefore tears the SA down at that point, even when a rekey is still in
flight. The value 0 starts no rekey and no expiry.
children.name: lifetime
children.short-help: SA lifetime in seconds. 0 disables expiry.

children.description:
With enable, Ze puts a KEi payload in the CREATE_CHILD_SA request, and the
replacement Child SA is keyed from a fresh Diffie-Hellman secret. With disable,
Ze sends no KEi, and the replacement is keyed from SK_d alone, so one leaked
SK_d reads every replacement Child SA. RFC 7296 Section 2.17 gives both KEYMAT
forms. An ESP proposal carries no Diffie-Hellman group of its own, so Ze offers
the group the IKE SA already negotiated. The default is enable, and Ze refuses a
response that disagrees with what its request carried.
children.name: pfs
children.short-help: Perfect Forward Secrecy for Child SA rekeying.

values.name: disable
values.short-help: Send no KEi and key each replacement Child SA from SK_d alone.

values.name: enable
values.short-help: Send a KEi payload and key each replacement Child SA from a fresh Diffie-Hellman secret.

children.description:
No build carries a transform for chacha20poly1305
or 3des, so a proposal that names one is refused at
commit. The refusal lists the algorithms the build does
implement.
children.name: encryption
children.short-help: Encryption algorithm.

values.name: 3des
values.short-help: Triple-DES-CBC (RFC 2451), deprecated. No build implements it.

values.name: aes128
values.short-help: AES-CBC-128 (RFC 3602).

values.name: aes128ccm12
values.short-help: AES-CCM-128, 12-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes128ccm16
values.short-help: AES-CCM-128, 16-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes128ccm8
values.short-help: AES-CCM-128, 8-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes128gcm
values.short-help: AES-GCM-128, 16-byte ICV (RFC 4106).

values.name: aes256
values.short-help: AES-CBC-256 (RFC 3602).

values.name: aes256ccm12
values.short-help: AES-CCM-256, 12-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes256ccm16
values.short-help: AES-CCM-256, 16-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes256ccm8
values.short-help: AES-CCM-256, 8-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes256gcm
values.short-help: AES-GCM-256, 16-byte ICV (RFC 4106).

values.name: chacha20poly1305
values.short-help: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 7634). No build implements it.

children.description:
Integrity algorithm. It is required beside a
non-AEAD cipher, and refused beside an AEAD cipher. RFC 7296
Section 3.3 gives an AEAD cipher its own integrity, so an ESP
proposal offers the integrity transform NONE. An ESP proposal
carries no PRF transform, so this leaf never names one.
No build carries a transform for sha1, so a proposal that
names it is refused at commit. The refusal lists the
algorithms the build does implement.
children.name: hash
children.short-help: Integrity algorithm.

values.name: sha1
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-1-96 (RFC 2404). No build implements it.

children.description:
ESP proposal. Lower number = higher priority. One group
offers at most 255 proposals, because RFC 7296 Section 3.3.1
numbers them in one octet.
children.name: proposal
children.short-help: ESP proposal, where a lower number is a higher priority.

children.description:
The group carries the ESP proposals a peer offers for its Child SAs and the lifetime
those SAs run under. A group MUST hold at least one proposal, and commit refuses an
empty one. One group holds at most 255 proposals.
children.name: esp-group
children.short-help: ESP (Encapsulating Security Payload) group.

children.description:
The default is none. The parser stores the value and no other code reads it,
so none, start and restart leave the daemon with the same behavior. A session
whose IKE SA the peer deletes tears its Child SA down and reconnects on a growing
backoff. The session loop does this after every failure.
children.name: close-action
children.short-help: Action when peer closes the IKE SA.

values.name: none
values.short-help: The default: the session reconnects on a growing backoff.

values.name: restart
values.short-help: Accepted and not read: the session reconnects on a growing backoff.

values.name: start
values.short-help: Accepted and not read: the session reconnects on a growing backoff.

children.description:
The default is hold. One log line reads the value when the peer is
declared dead, and no other code reads it. The three values restart, hold
and clear leave the same behavior. Ze deletes the Child SA, ends the
session, and reconnects on a growing backoff.
children.name: action
children.short-help: Action when DPD detects a dead peer.

values.name: clear
values.short-help: Log clear when the peer is dead, then reconnect on a growing backoff.

values.name: hold
values.short-help: Log hold when the peer is dead, then reconnect on a growing backoff.

values.name: restart
values.short-help: Log restart when the peer is dead, then reconnect on a growing backoff.

children.description:
Ze sends the next probe this long after the last one, and it sends none
while a probe is outstanding. The default is 30 seconds.
children.name: interval
children.short-help: DPD probe interval in seconds.

children.description:
The value bounds the whole liveness budget, so it covers the first probe and
every repeat of it. RFC 7296 Section 2.4 allows the verdict only when
'repeated attempts to contact it have gone unanswered for a timeout period'.
Ze repeats the probe on a growing backoff inside the budget and tears the SA
down when the budget runs out. The default is 120 seconds.
children.name: timeout
children.short-help: DPD timeout in seconds before declaring peer dead.

children.description:
The timers run whether or not this container is present. A peer with no DPD
block probes every 30 seconds and waits 120 seconds for the answer. The probe is
an empty INFORMATIONAL request, which is the liveness check of RFC 7296 Sections
1.4 and 2.4.
children.name: dead-peer-detection
children.short-help: Dead Peer Detection (DPD) settings (RFC 3706).

children.description:
The default is ikev2 and the engine writes major version 2 into every header
it sends. The parser stores the value and no other code reads it, so a group that
names ikev1 commits and still runs IKEv2.
children.name: key-exchange
children.short-help: IKE protocol version.

values.name: ikev1
values.short-help: Accepted and not read: the group still runs IKEv2.

values.name: ikev2
values.short-help: IKEv2 (RFC 7296), the version the engine speaks.

children.description:
Ze rekeys the IKE SA before the lifetime runs out, on the trigger the ESP group
lifetime describes. It also rekeys the SA as the message id space nears its
ceiling. RFC 7296 Section 2.2 requires that. 'In the unlikely event that Message
IDs grow too large to fit in 32 bits, the IKE SA MUST be closed or rekeyed.' The
value 0 starts no rekey, so the SA runs until the peer or the operator ends
it.
children.name: lifetime
children.short-help: IKE SA lifetime in seconds, where 0 starts no rekey.

children.description:
The number is Transform Type 4 of RFC 7296 Section 3.3.2. That section lists
the values current at publication, up to 18, and sends the reader to the
IANA registry for later ones. Ze takes 1 to 31 and refuses a group this
build carries no transform for. The refusal lists the numbers the build does
carry, which stops the reserved Transform ID 0 reaching the wire.
children.name: dh-group
children.short-help: Diffie-Hellman group number (RFC 7296 Section 3.3.2).

children.description:
No build carries a transform for chacha20poly1305
or 3des, so a proposal that names one is refused at
commit. The refusal lists the algorithms the build does
implement.
children.name: encryption
children.short-help: Encryption algorithm.

values.name: 3des
values.short-help: Triple-DES-CBC (RFC 2451), deprecated. No build implements it.

values.name: aes128
values.short-help: AES-CBC-128 (RFC 3602).

values.name: aes128ccm12
values.short-help: AES-CCM-128, 12-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes128ccm16
values.short-help: AES-CCM-128, 16-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes128ccm8
values.short-help: AES-CCM-128, 8-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes128gcm
values.short-help: AES-GCM-128, 16-byte ICV (RFC 4106).

values.name: aes256
values.short-help: AES-CBC-256 (RFC 3602).

values.name: aes256ccm12
values.short-help: AES-CCM-256, 12-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes256ccm16
values.short-help: AES-CCM-256, 16-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes256ccm8
values.short-help: AES-CCM-256, 8-byte ICV (RFC 4309, RFC 5282). IKE SA only.

values.name: aes256gcm
values.short-help: AES-GCM-256, 16-byte ICV (RFC 4106).

values.name: chacha20poly1305
values.short-help: ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD (RFC 7634). No build implements it.

children.description:
It is required beside
every cipher, and an AEAD cipher is no exception. RFC 7296
Section 3.3.3 makes the PRF a mandatory transform for an IKE
proposal, and this leaf names it. An ESP proposal reads the
same leaf as integrity alone, and refuses it beside an AEAD
cipher.
No build carries a transform for sha1, so a proposal that
names it is refused at commit. The refusal lists the
algorithms the build does implement.
children.name: hash
children.short-help: PRF and integrity algorithm.

values.name: sha1
values.short-help: HMAC-SHA-1-96 (RFC 2404). No build implements it.

children.description:
IKE proposal. Lower number = higher priority. One group
offers at most 255 proposals, because RFC 7296 Section 3.3.1
numbers them in one octet.
children.name: proposal
children.short-help: IKE proposal, where a lower number is a higher priority.

children.description:
The group carries the IKE proposals, the IKE SA lifetime and the Dead Peer Detection
timers. A group MUST hold at least one proposal, and commit refuses an empty one.
One group holds at most 255 proposals.
children.name: ike-group
children.short-help: IKE (Internet Key Exchange) group.

children.description:
Commit refuses a name no interface on the host carries. The first IPv4 address of
the interface fills the local-address of every peer that names none. It is also the
address the IKE socket on port 500 and the NAT-T socket on port 4500 bind to. A
reload whose interface holds no IPv4 address is refused, and the same case at
startup runs and writes a warning.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: WAN interface for IPsec traffic.

children.description:
RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1 defines bypass as 'to allow the packet to pass
without IPsec protection' and discard as 'to discard the traffic, i.e.,
not to let the traffic traverse the IPsec boundary'.

There is no protect here on purpose. A protect entry names an ESP
transform, a mode and a peer to negotiate keys with, and those live
under site-to-site peer. Offering the word in both places would put one
concept in two grammars.

The leaf is mandatory rather than defaulted. A defaulted disposition is
the one field of this entry whose wrong value is silent: a bypass
written where a discard was meant passes exactly the traffic the
operator wrote the entry to stop.
children.name: action
children.short-help: What the entry does with the traffic its selector matches.

values.name: bypass
values.short-help: Let matching traffic cross the boundary unprotected.

values.name: discard
values.short-help: Drop matching traffic at the boundary.

children.description:
RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1 splits the database by direction: SPD-O holds
the outbound bypass and discard entries and SPD-I holds the inbound
ones. A policy is one-way, so a Ze entry is one-way too.

both installs the mirrored pair: the outbound entry keeps local and
remote as written, and the inbound entry swaps them, because the local
side of a flow is the DESTINATION of an inbound packet. It is the
default because a one-way discard leaves the return traffic crossing
the boundary, which almost never expresses what the operator meant.
children.name: direction
children.short-help: Which side of the boundary the entry acts on.

values.name: both
values.short-help: Both directions, as a mirrored pair of entries.

values.name: in
values.short-help: Traffic arriving from the unprotected side.

values.name: out
values.short-help: Traffic leaving for the unprotected side.

children.description:
One exact port, or any for every port. RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1.1 defines
the selector as a list of ranges; the kernel selector Ze programs carries a
port and a mask, which expresses every port or one exact port and no
range between them. A range is refused rather than widened to any,
because widening would bypass or discard traffic the operator did not
name.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Local port of the selector.

values.name: any
values.short-help: Every port.

children.description:
The value is a CIDR prefix and Ze installs it as the local selector of
the policy. Use 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 for every address. The two prefixes of
one entry MUST share an address family, and commit refuses a mixed pair
because a kernel selector carries one family.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Local traffic the entry matches.

children.description:
Local is Ze's own side of the IPsec boundary. It is the source of an
outbound packet and the destination of an inbound one, which is the swap
direction both performs.
children.name: local
children.short-help: The local side of the selector.

children.description:
Where this entry sits in the operator's ordering of the Security
Policy Database. A LOWER value is searched FIRST, in Ze and in the
Linux kernel, and it carries the same meaning as policy-priority
under a site-to-site peer.

RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: the management interface 'MUST support
(total) ordering of these entries, as seen via this interface'.

The default of 1000 sits between the IKE control-plane bypass at 100
and a peer's default rank of 2000, so an entry written with no order
outranks the tunnels and carves its hole out of them. Raise it above
2000 to let a tunnel win instead.

The range starts above 100 for the reason policy-priority states: an
entry at or above the IKE bypass captures the IKE exchange that
builds and rekeys every tunnel on the node.
children.name: order
children.short-help: Rank of this entry, lowest searched first.

children.description:
The next-layer protocol of RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1.1, such as 6 for TCP
and 17 for UDP. Zero is that section's ANY, which matches every
protocol.

A local-port or remote-port other than any needs this leaf to name a
protocol that carries ports. Commit refuses the pair otherwise,
because a port selector under protocol 0 would match on a field the
classifier cannot read.
children.name: protocol
children.short-help: IP protocol number the selector matches, 0 for every protocol.

children.description:
It follows the rule the local port states: one exact port or any, and a
value other than any needs the protocol leaf.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Remote port of the selector.

values.name: any
values.short-help: Every port.

children.description:
It follows the rules the local prefix states, including the shared
address family.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Remote traffic the entry matches.

children.description:
Remote is the far side of the IPsec boundary. It is the destination of an
outbound packet and the source of an inbound one.
children.name: remote
children.short-help: The remote side of the selector.

children.description:
An entry of the Security Policy Database that Ze installs directly,
rather than one a Child SA negotiation produces.

RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1 gives the database three dispositions:
'PROTECT, BYPASS, or DISCARD'. A peer under site-to-site produces
the PROTECT entries, because those name a transform and a peer to
negotiate it with. The other two name neither, so they are written
here: BYPASS lets traffic cross the IPsec boundary in the clear,
and DISCARD stops it at the boundary.

Section 7.4 makes the discard disposition an obligation: 'All
implementations MUST support DISCARDing of fragments using the
normal SPD packet classification mechanisms.' This list is the
management interface that Section 4.4.1 requires for it.

Ze installs every entry when the configuration is applied and
removes it when the entry leaves the configuration. An entry needs
no peer, no key and no negotiation, so it is in force whether or
not any tunnel is up.
children.name: policy
children.short-help: Operator-authored Security Policy Database entry.

children.description:
eap-md5 establishes no shared key, and RFC 7296
Section 2.16 discourages such a method: EAP methods that do
not establish a shared key SHOULD NOT be used, as they are
subject to a number of man-in-the-middle attacks. The IKEv2
AUTH payloads are then keyed by SK_pi and SK_pr instead of
