by an EAP MSK. The method authenticates the client to Ze and
tells the client nothing about Ze. The daemon writes one
warning when this mode is adopted. Use eap-tls or
eap-mschapv2 unless the client runs no other method.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: EAP authentication method.

values.name: eap-md5
values.short-help: EAP MD5-Challenge, Type 4 (RFC 3748 Section 5.4).

values.name: eap-mschapv2
values.short-help: EAP-MSCHAPv2: the client proves its password by challenge and response.

values.name: eap-tls
values.short-help: EAP-TLS, Type 13 (RFC 5216): the client authenticates with a certificate.

children.description:
Ze compares the name against nothing, so a name no PKI store entry
carries still commits. The trust anchor of a handshake comes from the
ca-certificate leaf of the site-to-site peer.
children.name: ca-certificate
children.short-help:
Name of the CA certificate in the PKI store.
It has no effect today.

children.description:
Ze compares the name against nothing, so a name no PKI store entry
carries still commits. The certificate a handshake presents comes from
the certificate leaf of the site-to-site peer.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help:
Name of the server certificate in the PKI store.
It has no effect today.

children.description:
Server certificate references for EAP. Ze parses
both leaves and no component reads them today, so neither
takes effect. Ze also leaves both unchecked, so a name that
no PKI store entry carries still commits here. The enforced
leaves of these names are the site-to-site peer ones.
children.name: x509
children.short-help: Server certificate references for EAP.

children.description:
Ze reads this block with the same parser as the site-to-site peer
authentication block, so mode is mandatory here too. A handshake takes its EAP
server credentials from the peer block instead, so the mode named here selects no
method. The one effect it carries is the warning the daemon writes when it names
eap-md5.
children.name: authentication
children.short-help: EAP authentication settings for remote access.

children.description:
Ze reads the leaf when the mode of the authentication block is eap-tls,
and ignores it under every other mode. Commit refuses an empty value under
eap-tls. The name is compared against nothing, so a name the PKI store does
not hold still commits.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: Client certificate name in PKI store. Required for eap-tls.

children.description:
Ze reads the leaf when the mode of the authentication block is
eap-mschapv2 or eap-md5, and ignores it under every other mode. The $9$
wrapper is removed and what is left is the password. Commit refuses an empty
value under those two modes, because an empty password authenticates every
client that guesses the name. The CLI writes the value back $9$-encoded and
masks it in the configuration output.
children.name: password
children.short-help: User password ($9$-encoded). Required for eap-mschapv2.

children.description:
One entry holds the credential of one client. Which leaf carries that
credential follows the mode of the authentication block: password for
eap-mschapv2 and eap-md5, certificate for eap-tls. Ze validates every entry and
no handshake reads one, because EAP runs against the credentials of the
site-to-site peer.
children.name: eap-user
children.short-help: EAP user entry for remote access authentication.

children.description:
The group MUST be declared under vpn ipsec esp-group, and commit refuses a
name no group carries. No other code reads the reference, because no remote
access session runs.
children.name: esp-group
children.short-help: Reference to an ESP group name.

children.description:
The group MUST be declared under vpn ipsec ike-group, and commit refuses a
name no group carries. No other code reads the reference, because no remote
access session runs.
children.name: ike-group
children.short-help: Reference to an IKE group name.

children.description:
The leaf carries one address, and the pool sorts it into its IPv4 list or
its IPv6 list from the family of that address. RFC 7296 Section 3.15.1 names
the attribute that carries it INTERNAL_IP4_DNS or INTERNAL_IP6_DNS. Ze sends
no Configuration payload today, so no client receives the address.
children.name: dns
children.short-help: DNS server pushed to clients via IKEv2 Configuration Payload.

children.description:
The pool carries the domain beside the addresses it leases. Ze sends no
Configuration payload today, so no client receives the domain.
children.name: domain
children.short-help: Search domain pushed to clients.

children.description:
Commit refuses a value that is not a CIDR prefix, and a prefix length
outside /8 to /30. The pool leases the addresses of the prefix without the
network address and the broadcast address, so a /30 carries two clients. An
empty leaf leases no IPv4 address. No code reads the pool today, so no client
receives an address.
children.name: range
children.short-help: IPv4 CIDR for client addresses (e.g. 10.10.0.0/24). Prefix length /8-/30.

children.description:
Commit refuses a value that is not a CIDR prefix, and a prefix length
outside /48 to /126. An empty leaf leases no IPv6 address. No code reads the
pool today, so no client receives an address.
children.name: range6
children.short-help: IPv6 CIDR for client addresses (e.g. fd00::/64). Prefix length /48-/126.

children.description: Virtual IP pool for client address assignment (IKEv2 Configuration Payload, RFC 7296 Section 2.19).
children.name: pool
children.short-help: Virtual IP pool for client address assignment.

children.description:
The subtree parses and no session reads it, so a pool assigns no address and an
eap-user authenticates nobody. The engine builds the address pool at each apply and
then discards it. Configure a road warrior as a site-to-site peer with an EAP mode
until the service exists. plan/immediate/spec-ipsec-remote-access.md owns the work.
children.name: remote-access
children.short-help: Remote access VPN for road warrior clients (EAP).

children.description:
Name of the CA certificate in the PKI store. Required for
every EAP mode and for X.509. It is the trust anchor the remote
certificate must chain to, through any intermediate certificates the
peer sends. Without it any self-signed certificate would
authenticate. The remote certificate must also carry the remote-id
identity in a subject alternative name. Ze reads the subject common
name only when the certificate has no such extension.
children.name: ca-certificate
children.short-help: Name of the CA certificate in the PKI store.

children.description:
Name of the device certificate in the PKI store. Required for
every EAP mode, because RFC 7296 Section 2.16 makes the responder sign
its AUTH with a public key. Also used by X.509 mode. Ze sends this
certificate first, then the intermediate certificate the PKI entry
carries.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: Name of the device certificate in the PKI store.

children.description:
The most X.509 certificates Ze sends for this peer, and the most it
accepts from it. RFC 7296 Section 3.6 requires an implementation be
capable of being configured to send and accept up to four. The
default is that figure, so an operator who never sets this leaf
gets the conformant behavior.

A peer that sends more than this is REFUSED, never truncated. A
silent trim would pass a count check and hide from the operator
that the limit was reached. It would also make which certificates
survive depend on the order the peer chose.
children.name: certificate-count
children.short-help: The most X.509 certificates Ze sends to this peer and accepts from it.

children.description:
RFC 9190 Section 5.4 recommends OCSP stapling for checking an
EAP-TLS server's certificate chain, and puts a MUST on the peer
that uses it: 'it MUST treat a CertificateEntry (but not the trust
anchor) without a valid CertificateStatus extension as invalid and
abort the handshake with an appropriate alert'. This leaf is what
makes Ze such a peer.

With it true, Ze refuses an authenticator that staples nothing,
staples a response about another certificate, staples an expired
one, or staples one that reports the certificate revoked or
unknown. It also refuses a chain carrying an intermediate below
the trust anchor, because Ze reads a stapled status for the leaf
certificate alone and Section 5.4 makes an entry whose status it
cannot read invalid.

With it false, which is the default, Ze checks the same chain
against the crl of the ca it validates against. Section 5.4
requires that check on TLS 1.3 either way.

It governs the peer role. As the authenticator Ze answers a
Certificate Status Request whenever the pki certificate it
presents carries an ocsp-response, whatever this leaf says.
children.name: certificate-status-request
children.short-help: Check this peer's EAP-TLS certificate chain by the OCSP response it staples.

children.description:
The http URL at which this device's own certificate is published,
sent beside the SHA-1 hash when hash-and-url is true. RFC 7296
Section 3.6 requires support for the http scheme.
children.name: certificate-url
children.short-help: The http URL at which this device publishes its own certificate.

children.description:
Destinations a certificate URL received from this peer CAN resolve
to, beyond the fetcher's defaults. The fetcher refuses loopback,
private, link-local and multicast addresses, and the cloud metadata
address. It refuses them because the daemon runs on a router and
holds routes an internet host does not. Naming a prefix here
permits it.
children.name: certificate-url-allow
children.short-help: Extra destinations a certificate URL from this peer CAN resolve to.

children.description:
When it is true Ze sends its certificate as a SHA-1 hash plus
certificate-url, advertises HTTP_CERT_LOOKUP_SUPPORTED, and
resolves a peer's Hash and URL payload.

It defaults to false, and that default is a security property.
Resolving a peer's payload fetches a URL that peer chose, and Ze
must do that before it CAN authenticate the peer. With this leaf
false Ze advertises nothing, a conforming peer sends no such
payload, a non-conforming one is dropped, and no fetch is reachable.

The enabled fetch takes the http scheme only, a 64 KiB cap, a
5 second timeout, no redirects, denied destinations, and SHA-1
verification before any parser.
children.name: hash-and-url
children.short-help: Use the Hash and URL certificate encodings of RFC 7296 Section 3.6.

children.description:
Ze derives the ID type it sends from the shape of the value. An IP
address literal goes out as ID_IPV4_ADDR or ID_IPV6_ADDR, and every
other value as ID_FQDN. There is no ID_DER_ASN1_DN form, so commit
refuses a distinguished name. Commit also refuses a subtree or an
address range, because this leaf names the one identity Ze asserts. An
empty leaf sends the peer name.
children.name: local-id
children.short-help: Local identity for IKE negotiation.

children.description:
eap-md5 establishes no shared key, and RFC 7296
Section 2.16 discourages such a method: EAP methods that
do not establish a shared key SHOULD NOT be used, as
they are subject to a number of man-in-the-middle
attacks. The IKEv2 AUTH payloads are then keyed by SK_pi
and SK_pr instead of by an EAP MSK. The method
authenticates this peer to the far end and tells this
peer nothing about the far end. The daemon writes one
warning when this mode is adopted. Use eap-tls or
eap-mschapv2 unless the far end runs no other method.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Authentication mode.

values.name: eap-md5
values.short-help: EAP MD5-Challenge, Type 4 (RFC 3748 Section 5.4).

values.name: eap-mschapv2
values.short-help: EAP-MSCHAPv2: this peer proves its password by challenge and response.

values.name: eap-tls
values.short-help: EAP-TLS, Type 13 (RFC 5216): this peer authenticates with a certificate.

values.name: pre-shared-secret
values.short-help: Both ends prove the same secret, taken from the pre-shared-secret leaf.

values.name: x509
values.short-help: Sign AUTH with the named certificate and validate the remote one against ca-certificate.

children.description:
Ze reads the leaf when the mode is pre-shared-secret, and when the mode
is an EAP method that carries a password. The $9$ wrapper is removed
first, and the pre-shared-secret-encoding leaf then decides whether the
result is ASCII text or hexadecimal digit pairs.
children.name: pre-shared-secret
children.short-help: Pre-shared key ($9$-encoded).

children.description:
RFC 7296
Section 2.15 requires the management interface to
accept both an ASCII string and a hex encoding of
the shared secret. Set this to hex to supply the
secret as hexadecimal digit pairs, which is the way
to configure a secret holding non-printable octets.

The encoding is stated here and is never guessed from
the value. A secret such as abcdef0123456789 is both
valid ASCII and valid hex, so reading it as hex would
silently change an existing secret. A hex value with
an odd length or a non-hexadecimal character is
refused at commit rather than read as ASCII.
children.name: pre-shared-secret-encoding
children.short-help: How to read the pre-shared-secret value.

values.name: ascii
values.short-help: Read the secret as ASCII text, one octet for each character.

values.name: hex
values.short-help: Read the secret as hexadecimal digit pairs, two digits for each octet.

children.description:
When it is set,
Ze refuses an IKE_AUTH whose ID payload names another identity.
Comparable types are ID_IPV4_ADDR, ID_IPV6_ADDR, ID_FQDN,
ID_RFC822_ADDR, ID_KEY_ID, and ID_DER_ASN1_DN, and an address value
accepts the two address types alone. A distinguished name is
compared in RFC 4514 string form, and it binds against the
certificate subject exactly, octet for octet.

A value can name ONE peer or a SET of peers. RFC 4301 Section
4.4.3.1 requires both forms of Peer Authorization Database entry.
A set is written with the hierarchy separator in front, and it
admits the identities BELOW it and not the value itself:
'.example.com' admits vpn.example.com, '@example.com' admits
gateway@example.com, and ',ST=MA,C=US' admits every distinguished
name whose top relative distinguished names are ST=MA,C=US. An
address entry takes the same CIDR prefix the traffic-selector
leaves take, so '10.0.0.0/24' admits every address in that block.
ID_KEY_ID is always compared exactly, because an opaque octet
string has no hierarchy to cut.

The certificate binding stays per peer whichever form is used. A
peer admitted by a set must still assert an identity its own
certificate carries, so a set never widens what one certificate
proves.

When it is empty Ze checks no identity, so every certificate the
ca-certificate issued authenticates as this peer. Set it whenever
that authority issues to more than one client.
children.name: remote-id
children.short-help: Identity the remote endpoint must assert.

children.description:
The one IKE ID type the remote endpoint CAN assert, and when
absent any type Ze CAN compare, which is the historical behavior.
When it is set Ze refuses every other type, so a peer asserting
ID_FQDN with the text of a configured mail address is refused.

RFC 7296 Section 4 requires that it be possible to configure Ze to
accept a PKIX certificate where the identity passed is ID_KEY_ID.
An opaque key id corresponds to no certificate field, so Ze cannot
derive that binding and refuses it by default. Setting this leaf to
key-id is the operator stating that a chain to ca-certificate plus
the exact key id IS the intended binding.

It governs what Ze ACCEPTS, and the type Ze sends still follows
the shape of local-id.
children.name: remote-id-type
children.short-help: The one IKE ID type the remote endpoint CAN assert.

values.name: der-asn1-dn
values.short-help: ID_DER_ASN1_DN, the DER-encoded subject name of a certificate.

values.name: fqdn
values.short-help: ID_FQDN, a fully qualified domain name.

values.name: ipv4-address
values.short-help: ID_IPV4_ADDR, an IPv4 address in four octets.

values.name: ipv6-address
values.short-help: ID_IPV6_ADDR, an IPv6 address in sixteen octets.

values.name: key-id
values.short-help: ID_KEY_ID, an opaque octet string no certificate field can bind.

values.name: rfc822-address
values.short-help: ID_RFC822_ADDR, a mail address such as user@example.com.

children.description:
RFC 9190 Section 2.1.3 leaves resumption to each end: 'It is up
to the EAP-TLS peer to use resumption', and 'the EAP-TLS server
MAY choose to require a full handshake'. This leaf is that
choice, and it covers both roles of this peer.

With it true, an authentication that follows an earlier one
skips the certificate exchange and reuses the session the ticket
carries. Ze still checks the cached chain against the current
ca-certificate and crl before it accepts the session, on both
roles, so a revoked or expired certificate is refused on a
resumed authentication as it is on a full one.

With it false every authentication runs a full handshake. Ze
still SENDS a session ticket, because RFC 9190 Section 2.1.2
makes that a MUST with no condition on it; the ticket is simply
never accepted back.

Changing this leaf, the certificate, the ca-certificate or the
crl discards every ticket ze holds for this peer.
children.name: session-resumption
children.short-help: Let an EAP-TLS exchange with this peer resume an earlier one.

children.description:
Ze reads it only when the direct ca-certificate
leaf is empty. It then satisfies the trust anchor that
every EAP mode and X.509 require.
children.name: ca-certificate
children.short-help: Name of the CA certificate in the PKI store.

children.description:
Ze reads it only when the direct certificate
leaf is empty. It then satisfies the certificate that
every EAP mode and X.509 require.
children.name: certificate
children.short-help: Name of the device certificate in the PKI store.

children.description:
X.509 certificate references (deprecated, use
the direct leaves). Ze reads a leaf here only when the
direct leaf of the same name is empty. A name set here
therefore meets the same requirement the direct leaf
meets, and it is checked against the PKI store the same
way.
children.name: x509
children.short-help: X.509 certificate references, deprecated in favor of the direct leaves.

children.description:
The mode leaf decides which leaf below it Ze reads. A pre-shared-secret peer
and an EAP password mode read pre-shared-secret. X.509 and every EAP mode
read certificate and ca-certificate, and commit refuses a peer that leaves
either of those empty.
children.name: authentication
children.short-help: Peer authentication settings.

children.description:
With `initiate` Ze starts the IKE_SA_INIT exchange toward remote-address.
With respond Ze starts nothing and waits. Ze matches an unsolicited
IKE_SA_INIT to a respond peer when the source address of the datagram
equals its remote-address. A respond peer that names no remote-address
therefore matches nothing.
children.name: connection-type
children.short-help: Whether to initiate or wait for the remote peer.

values.name: initiate
values.short-help: Start the IKE_SA_INIT exchange toward remote-address.

values.name: respond
values.short-help: Start nothing and wait for an IKE_SA_INIT whose source is remote-address.

children.description:
The group MUST be declared under vpn ipsec esp-group, and commit refuses a
name no group carries. It supplies the ESP proposals Ze offers for this
peer's Child SAs and the lifetime those SAs run under.
children.name: esp-group
children.short-help: Reference to an ESP group name.

children.description:
The group MUST be declared under vpn ipsec ike-group, and commit refuses a
name no group carries. It supplies the IKE proposals, the IKE SA lifetime
and the Dead Peer Detection timers of this peer.
children.name: ike-group
children.short-help: Reference to an IKE group name.

children.description:
The value is an IP address literal. Ze reads it with net.ParseIP, so an
interface name here resolves to nothing and the peer cannot build a Child
SA. Name the interface under vpn ipsec interface instead, and Ze fills this
leaf from the first IPv4 address of that interface.
children.name: local-address
children.short-help: Local endpoint IP address.

children.description:
Encapsulation mode for this peer's Child SAs.

RFC 7296 Section 1.3.1 states the default itself: 'Except when
using this option to negotiate transport mode, all Child SAs will
use tunnel mode.' Ze asks for transport mode by sending
USE_TRANSPORT_MODE with the Child SA request, and the peer can
decline. A declined request establishes a tunnel-mode Child SA
unless transport-required is set.

Transport mode constrains the traffic selectors. RFC 7296 Section
2.23.1 requires exactly one IP address in TSi and in TSr, so every
traffic-selector prefix under this peer must be a single host, and
a vti binding is refused because an XFRM interface carries tunnel
encapsulation.
children.name: mode
children.short-help: Encapsulation mode for this peer's Child SAs.

values.name: transport
values.short-help: Protect the payload and keep the outer IP header (RFC 4301 transport mode).

values.name: tunnel
values.short-help: Encapsulate the whole packet (RFC 4301 tunnel mode).

children.description:
Where this peer's Security Policy Database entries sit in the
operator's ordering of that database. A LOWER value is searched
FIRST, in Ze and in the Linux kernel.

RFC 4301 Section 4.4.1: 'The ordering requirement arises because
entries often will overlap due to the presence of (non-trivial)
ranges as values for selectors. Thus, a user or administrator MUST
be able to order the entries to express a desired access control
policy.' The same section binds this interface: it 'MUST support
(total) ordering of these entries, as seen via this interface'.

Two peers whose traffic selectors overlap, 0.0.0.0/0 on both for
example, describe the same traffic. Give the one that must win the
lower value. Peers that share a value are ordered by whichever
established last, which is what every peer did before this leaf
existed, so the default 2000 keeps an unordered configuration
installing exactly what it installed before.

The range starts above 100, which is where the IKE control-plane
bypass sits. A peer entry at or above that rank captures the IKE
exchange that builds and rekeys the very SA it protects, and the
tunnel could then never renegotiate. It ends at 2147483647, the
largest rank Ze can carry to a dataplane.
children.name: policy-priority
children.short-help: Rank of this peer's Security Policy Database entries, lowest searched first.

children.description:
Ze resolves the value with net.ResolveUDPAddr over udp4 and sends IKE to
port 500 there, so an IPv6 literal is refused with "ike: resolve remote".
Ze builds the NAT detection hashes of RFC 7296 Section 2.23 from this value.
It sends none when the value is not an address literal. An unsolicited
IKE_SA_INIT reaches a respond peer only when its source address equals this
leaf, character for character.
children.name: remote-address
children.short-help: Remote endpoint IPv4 address or DNS hostname.

children.description:
Local port of the selector.

RFC 7296 Section 3.13.1 requires the port fields to be 0 and
65535 whenever the protocol is 0 or defines no port, so a
value other than any needs the protocol leaf to name a
protocol that has ports.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Local port of the selector.

values.name: any
values.short-help: Every port. RFC 7296 Section 3.13.1 encodes it as start 0, end 65535.

children.description:
The value is a CIDR prefix, and Ze installs it as the local selector
of the kernel policy. Under mode transport the prefix MUST cover
exactly one address, a /32 or a /128. RFC 7296 Section 2.23.1
requires one IP address in TSi and in TSr, so commit refuses
anything wider there.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Local traffic the Child SA carries.

children.description:
The prefix under it is mandatory once a traffic-selector entry exists,
and commit refuses an entry that leaves it out. The port under it takes
any unless the protocol leaf names a protocol that carries ports.
children.name: local
children.short-help:
The local side of the selector pair (TSi when Ze
initiates, TSr when Ze responds).

children.description:
IP protocol number the selector matches, such as 6 for TCP and
17 for UDP. Zero matches every protocol, which is RFC 7296
Section 3.13.1's 'protocol 0'.
children.name: protocol
children.short-help: IP protocol number the selector matches.

children.description:
It follows the same rule as the local port: a value other
than any needs the protocol leaf.
children.name: port
children.short-help: Remote port of the selector.

values.name: any
values.short-help: Every port. RFC 7296 Section 3.13.1 encodes it as start 0, end 65535.

children.description:
The value is a CIDR prefix, and Ze installs it as the remote
selector of the kernel policy. The single-address rule the local
prefix states applies here as well under mode transport.
children.name: prefix
children.short-help: Remote traffic the Child SA carries.

children.description:
It obeys the rules the local container states. Ze narrows the peer's
proposal against the pair of prefixes, and it answers TS_UNACCEPTABLE
when no non-empty subset remains.
children.name: remote
children.short-help:
The remote side of the selector pair (TSr when Ze
initiates, TSi when Ze responds).

children.description:
The traffic this peer's Child SAs carry, and the policy RFC 7296
Section 2.9 narrows a peer's proposal against.

When no entry is present the peer accepts whatever the remote
endpoint proposes, which is the behavior of every configuration
written before this list existed. Adding an entry restricts the
peer: a proposal Ze cannot narrow to a non-empty subset of these
entries is answered with TS_UNACCEPTABLE.

RFC 7296 Section 2.9 permits several selectors, so this is a list.
children.name: traffic-selector
children.short-help: The traffic this peer's Child SAs carry.

children.description:
Whether a peer that declines transport mode is unacceptable.

RFC 7296 Section 1.3.1: 'If the responder declines the request, the
Child SA will be established in tunnel mode. If this is unacceptable
to the initiator, the initiator MUST delete the SA.' Only the
operator knows whether it is unacceptable, so this leaf carries that
decision. When it is true and the response omits USE_TRANSPORT_MODE,
Ze deletes the SA rather than run a tunnel-mode Child SA the
operator did not ask for. When it is false the SA stays up in
tunnel mode, which is the safe default.

It applies only when mode is transport.
children.name: transport-required
children.short-help: Delete the SA when the peer declines transport mode.

children.description:
Route-based IPsec encrypts the traffic the routing table forwards
into the named XFRM interface. Commit refuses a name beside mode
transport, because an XFRM interface carries tunnel-mode encapsulation.
No code maps the name to the if-id of that interface today. The Child
SA is installed with if_id 0, and the binding carries no traffic.
children.name: bind
children.short-help: VTI interface name to bind this peer's traffic to.

children.description:
The interface itself is declared under interfaces xfrm, where the if-id
leaf carries the identifier a bound security association must match. Ze joins
the two nowhere, so every Child SA is installed with if_id 0.
children.name: vti
children.short-help: Virtual Tunnel Interface binding.

children.description:
Ze runs one session for each peer. A configuration reload stops and restarts
only the peers whose own configuration changed, so a peer left untouched keeps
its Child SAs up. A peer MUST reference one IKE group and one ESP group.
children.name: peer
children.short-help: Remote VPN peer.

children.description:
Each peer under it is one tunnel to one remote gateway. A peer carries its own
algorithms, its own identity, its own traffic selectors and its own rank in the
Security Policy Database.
children.name: site-to-site
children.short-help: Site-to-site VPN peers.

children.description:
Ze speaks IKEv2 (RFC 7296) and installs each negotiated Child SA into the Linux XFRM
stack. A peer references one ESP group and one IKE group, and those two carry the
algorithms and the timers of the tunnel.
children.name: ipsec
children.short-help: IPsec VPN configuration.

vpn.description:
Ze declares one subsystem under it today, which is ipsec. That subsystem holds the ESP
groups, the IKE groups and the site-to-site peers.
vpn.name: vpn

children.description:
Ze writes this path into the socksvr section of startup.conf and then connects to it through GoVPP.
The path MUST be absolute, MUST NOT contain "..", and MUST be 108 characters or less, which is the
Unix socket path limit. Under external true Ze writes no startup.conf, so this leaf is the only
setting Ze needs to reach a VPP process another supervisor started. Ze retries the connection 10
times, one second apart, inside a 30-second budget.
children.name: api-socket
children.short-help: GoVPP binary API Unix socket path.

children.description:
Ze writes this core number into the cpu section of startup.conf as main-core. The core is excluded
from the worker set, so the main thread and a worker never share a CPU. Omit the leaf and VPP picks
the main core itself, and Ze still counts the worker list from core 1. A core the host does not hold
online is refused at commit.
children.name: main-core
children.short-help:
CPU core for VPP main thread.
Omit for automatic assignment.

children.description:
Fixed sleep between VPP main-loop polls, expressed in whole milliseconds, which is the only accepted
unit, for example 10ms. Ze emits it as unix { poll-sleep-usec N } in startup.conf, where 1ms is 1000
microseconds. Omit the leaf for VPP's default, where the workers busy-poll at 100% CPU with no
sleep, and the latency is lowest. Set a non-zero value up to 100ms on a shared or dev host, to trade
latency for idle CPU. An explicit 0ms is emitted and equals the default.
children.name: poll-sleep
children.short-help: Fixed sleep between VPP main-loop polls, in whole milliseconds.

children.description:
Ze writes these cores into the corelist-workers line of the cpu section in startup.conf,
and writes no line when neither leaf is set. The syntax is the one the kernel uses for
isolcpus: single cores, ranges, or both, as in 2-4 or 2,4,6. Set this leaf when the isolated
set holds cores to keep for something else, and omit it to derive the cores from workers. It
MUST NOT be set beside workers, because the two are separate answers to the same question,
and Ze refuses a config that carries both. A core the host does not hold online, a core that
is also main-core, and a core listed twice are each refused at commit. Cores outside the
kernel's isolated set are accepted, and the vpp-cpu-isolation doctor check reports them.
children.name: worker-cores
children.short-help: Explicit CPU core list for the VPP worker threads.

children.description:
Ze turns this count into the corelist-workers line of the cpu section in startup.conf, and
the worker-cores leaf names those cores instead. Ze takes the cores from the set the kernel
isolated at boot, lowest first, with main-core excluded. Isolated 2-4 with main-core 2 and
workers 2 therefore emits corelist-workers 3-4. When the kernel isolated no core, the list is
contiguous and starts one core after main-core, so 4 workers with main-core 1 emits
corelist-workers 2-5. The vpp-cpu-isolation doctor check then reports that the workers share
their CPUs with Linux. A count the host cannot satisfy is refused at commit, and a value of 0
emits no line, which is what an absent leaf does.
children.name: workers
children.short-help:
Number of VPP worker threads.
Omit for automatic (one per available core).

children.description:
These leaves write the cpu section of startup.conf, and the main-core leaf pins the VPP main
thread. The workers leaf asks for a count, and Ze takes those cores from the set the kernel
isolated, which it reads from /sys/devices/system/cpu/isolated. The worker-cores leaf names the
cores instead, and it MUST NOT be set beside workers. The poll-sleep leaf sits here for the
operator, and Ze emits it in the unix section, because that is where VPP reads poll-sleep-usec.
Omit every leaf to let VPP place its own threads, and Ze checks a placement leaf you set at
commit. Ze refuses a core the host does not hold, a worker core that is also main-core, and a
worker count the host cannot satisfy.
children.name: cpu
children.short-help: VPP CPU pinning configuration.

children.description:
Ze writes this name into the dev entry of the dpdk section in startup.conf, so VPP calls the
interface by it. The name is 1 to 15 characters of letters, digits, underscore, hyphen and dot,
and a hyphen or a dot MUST NOT come first. Omit the leaf and Ze writes no name line, so VPP
picks the interface name itself.
children.name: name
children.short-help:
Short interface name (e.g. xe0, e1).
Used in ze CLI and config.

children.description:
Ze writes this count into the dev entry of the dpdk section as num-rx-queues. An explicit 0 is
written out, so it is not the same as an absent leaf. Omit the leaf and the line is absent,
which leaves VPP on its own default. Ze does not compare the count against the queues the NIC
holds.
children.name: rx-queues
children.short-help:
Number of receive queues.
Omit for VPP default.

children.description:
Ze writes this count into the dev entry of the dpdk section as num-tx-queues. An explicit 0 is
written out, so it is not the same as an absent leaf. Omit the leaf and the line is absent,
which leaves VPP on its own default. Ze does not compare the count against the queues the NIC
holds.
children.name: tx-queues
children.short-help:
Number of transmit queues.
Omit for VPP default.

children.description:
The list key is the PCI address, so this list holds one entry for each NIC. Ze loads the vfio, vfio_pci
and vfio_iommu_type1 kernel modules, then binds each listed address to vfio-pci. A bind failure on
one NIC unbinds every NIC Ze bound in the same pass, and VPP does not start.
children.name: interface
children.short-help: DPDK-managed network interface.

children.description:
Every NIC listed here is unbound from its kernel driver and bound to vfio-pci before VPP starts, so
Linux loses the interface. Ze saves the original driver name and rebinds it when the daemon stops.
Under external true Ze binds nothing, because the external supervisor owns that step. An empty list
emits no dpdk section in startup.conf.
children.name: dpdk
children.short-help: DPDK NIC configuration.

children.description:
Enable VPP integration. When this leaf is true, Ze manages the VPP lifecycle. Ze generates
startup.conf, binds the DPDK NICs, starts the VPP process, and connects through GoVPP.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable VPP integration, so Ze manages the VPP lifecycle.

children.description:
When this leaf is true, Ze does not exec or supervise the VPP process, generate startup.conf, or
bind DPDK NICs. The external supervisor owns all of that. Ze only connects through GoVPP to
api-socket. Use this leaf for systemd-managed VPP, for a container sidecar deployment, or for the
`le test vpp` stub harness. The default is false, where Ze owns the VPP lifecycle.
children.name: external
children.short-help: Let an external supervisor own the VPP process, false by default.

children.description:
When this leaf is true, Ze writes lcp-auto-subint into the linux-cp section of startup.conf. A dot1q
or QinQ sub-interface created in VPP then gets its own Linux sub-TAP. When it is false, Ze omits the
line, so a sub-interface has no mirror in Linux and only its parent interface does. The default is
true, and lcp enabled MUST also be true before Ze writes the line.
children.name: auto-subint
children.short-help:
Auto-create sub-TAPs for dot1q/QinQ
sub-interfaces.

children.description:
When this leaf is true, Ze enables linux_cp_plugin.so and linux_nl_plugin.so in startup.conf, and writes
the linux-cp and linux-nl sections. When it is false, no other lcp leaf reaches startup.conf and
the netns leaf is not validated. The default is true. LCP gives each VPP interface a TAP mirror in
Linux, so a routing daemon binds an ordinary Linux socket.
children.name: enabled
children.short-help: Enable LCP plugin in VPP.

children.description:
Ze writes this name into the linux-cp section of startup.conf as default netns. VPP then creates the
TAP mirrors under /var/run/netns/NAME. An EMPTY value is valid, and Ze then omits the line. It is
the one value that leaves the TAPs in the namespace Ze runs in. An absent leaf is not
the same as an empty one, because Ze seeds the default "dataplane" when the leaf is absent. With
any name, Ze binds BGP in its own namespace and cannot bind on an LCP TAP address, which the
doctor check vpp-lcp-netns reports. A name with a path separator, a space or an unprintable
character is refused at commit. VPP truncates a name at a space, so the namespace it then opens
under /var/run/netns/ does not exist.
children.name: netns
children.short-help:
Network namespace for LCP TAP interfaces.
Routing daemons run in this namespace.

children.description:
When this leaf is true, Ze writes lcp-sync into the linux-cp section of startup.conf. A link, MTU or
address change made in VPP then reaches the Linux TAP mirror. When it is false, Ze omits the line and
the two sides drift apart. The default is true, and lcp enabled MUST also be true before Ze writes
the line.
children.name: sync
children.short-help:
Sync VPP state changes (link, MTU, IP)
to Linux TAP mirrors.

children.description:
Linux Control Plane plugin. The plugin creates TAP mirrors in Linux for VPP interfaces. A routing
daemon such as ze BGP can then use Linux TCP on a VPP-managed NIC.
children.name: lcp
children.short-help: Linux Control Plane plugin settings.

children.description:
Ze writes this count into the buffers section of startup.conf as buffers-per-numa, beside a fixed
default-data-size of 2048 bytes. So the pool costs the count multiplied by 2048 bytes on each NUMA
node, and the default 128000 costs 250 MiB. A value of 0 is refused at commit with "vpp: memory
buffers must be > 0".
children.name: buffers
children.short-help:
Number of packet buffers per NUMA node.
128000 is proven for full DFZ at 10G.

children.description:
The two accepted values are 2M and 1G. For 1G Ze writes page-size 1G into both the buffers section and
the statseg section of startup.conf. For 2M Ze writes page-size default-hugepage-size instead,
which takes whatever the kernel holds as its default hugepage size. The ze doctor check warns when
you select 1G on an amd64 CPU with no pdpe1gb flag, because the kernel then reserves no 1G page.
children.name: hugepage-size
children.short-help: Hugepage size for VPP buffers.

values.name: 1G
values.short-help: Write page-size 1G into the buffers and statseg sections of startup.conf.

values.name: 2M
values.short-help: Write page-size default-hugepage-size, which takes the kernel's default hugepage size.

children.description:
Ze writes this size into the heapsize section of startup.conf as main-heap-size. The value MUST be
digits followed by M or G, so 1536M is accepted and 1.5G is refused at commit. The ze doctor check
counts this size toward the hugepage memory it expects the host to have reserved.
children.name: main-heap
children.short-help:
VPP main heap size (e.g. 512M, 1G, 1536M).
Production with full DFZ: 1536M.

children.description:
These three leaves decide how much hugepage memory VPP asks the host for. The ze doctor check adds the
main heap, the buffer memory and the stats segment together. It warns when the host reserved less
hugepage memory than that sum. The hugepage-size leaf decides which page size VPP asks for, and it
also governs the stats segment.
children.name: memory
children.short-help: VPP memory and buffer configuration.

children.description:
Load wireguard_plugin.so so the vpp interface backend can program WireGuard tunnels. The tunnels are
configured as interface wireguard under backend vpp.
children.name: wireguard
children.short-help: Load wireguard_plugin.so for the vpp interface backend.

children.description:
Optional VPP plugin enablement. startup.conf uses 'plugin default { disable }', so Ze loads only the
always-on plugins and the plugins toggled on here. The always-on plugins are dpdk, plus linux-cp
when lcp is enabled.
children.name: plugins
children.short-help: Optional VPP plugins to load.

children.description:
Stats polling interval in seconds. The interval controls how often Ze reads VPP's stats segment for
Prometheus metrics.
children.name: poll-interval
children.short-help: Stats polling interval in seconds.

children.description:
Ze writes this size into the statseg section of startup.conf as size. The value MUST be digits followed
by M or G, so 512M and 1G are accepted and 512MB is refused at commit. The page size of the
segment comes from memory hugepage-size and not from this leaf. The ze doctor check counts this
size toward the hugepage memory it expects the host to have reserved.
children.name: segment-size
children.short-help: Stats segment shared memory size.

children.description:
Ze writes this path into the statseg section of startup.conf as socket-name, and the telemetry poller
connects to it to read VPP's counters. The path MUST be absolute, MUST NOT contain "..", and MUST
be 108 characters or less, which is the Unix socket path limit. This is a different socket from
api-socket, which carries the binary API.
children.name: socket-path
children.short-help: Stats segment Unix socket path.

children.description:
The stats segment is the shared memory area VPP writes its counters into. Ze connects to it separately
from the binary API and reads it for Prometheus metrics, at the interval poll-interval sets. A failed
stats connection logs "vpp: stats connection failed, telemetry disabled" and leaves the rest of the
VPP integration running.
children.name: stats
children.short-help: VPP stats segment configuration.

vpp.description:
Ze reads this subtree at startup and writes /etc/vpp/startup.conf from it, then starts /usr/bin/vpp.
A change committed later logs "config reload requires daemon restart to take effect" and does not reach
VPP until the daemon restarts. The enabled leaf is false by default, so every other leaf here changes
nothing until you set it to true.
vpp.name: vpp
